title: About
text: About Alto is an open-source desktop app for learning music theory. Explore the roadmap, see what changed in each release, and find the licenses and credits for the software, fonts, and recordings that come with Alto. Roadmap Release notes License and credits

title: alto.audio
text: alto.audio Note playback: recorded instrument samples (University of Iowa), with pitch-shifting for missing notes. Sounds plays notes through Qt’s QSoundEffect , one effect per note, created the first time it is needed. A note with no recording is made by shifting the nearest recording (or, for the piano outside its sampled range, by synthesis). Instrument previews render the phrase as one cached clip to preserve its rhythm from the first playback. The module-level sounds is the one the interface uses. Examples >>> [ inst . label for inst in INSTRUMENTS ][: 2 ] ['Piano', 'Flute'] >>> Sounds (). instrument 'piano'

title: alto.audio
text: synth_piano def synth_piano ( midi : int , * , duration : float = 1.6 , ) -> list [ float ] [Source] Synthesize a piano note, for notes outside the recorded range. An additive model: stretched partials, a decay for each partial, a detuned string pair, and a hammer thump. Each partial is a decaying sine made by rotating a complex number one sample at a time, which needs no sine or exponential per sample. Parameters midi ( int ): The MIDI note number. The same number always gives the same sound. duration ( float, default 1.6 ): How long the note lasts, in seconds. Keyword-only. Returns list of float : Mono samples at SAMPLE_RATE , scaled so the loudest is 0.8. Examples >>> samples = synth_piano ( 60 , duration = 0.1 ) >>> len ( samples ) 4410 >>> round ( max ( abs ( s ) for s in samples ), 1 ) 0.8

title: alto.audio
text: Instrument Instrument ( key : str , * , label : str , folder : str , gain : float = 1.0 , sustained : bool = False , family : str = '' , variant : str = '' , damped : bool = False , samples : tuple [ tuple [ int , Path ], ...] = (), pack_name : str = '' , kind : str = '' , ) [Source] An instrument that notes can be played on, and where its recordings are. Attributes key ( str ): A short identifier used in settings and file names. label ( str ): The name shown in the interface. Keyword-only. folder ( str ): Under assets/ : “piano” or “samples/ ". File names are MIDI note numbers. Keyword-only. gain ( float, default 1.0 ): The level relative to the piano. Keyword-only. sustained ( bool, default False ): True for bowed and blown instruments, whose notes end when the next one begins; struck and plucked ones ring on. Keyword-only. damped ( bool, default False ): True for an instrument whose notes are stopped by a damper when the key is let go, played without the pedal: the piano. Each note ends as the next one begins, as it does when the fingers move from key to key, instead of ringing on over the following notes as if the pedal were down. Keyword-only. family ( str, default ““ ): Instruments that are ways of playing the same instrument share a family (the viola: arco and pizzicato). Keyword-only. variant ( str, default ““ ): Which way of playing it, within the family. Keyword-only. samples ( tuple of (int, Path), default () ): Pairs of MIDI pitches and local recording paths supplied by an installed instrument pack. Keyword-only. pack_name ( str, default ““ ): Display name of the plugin that supplies the recordings. Keyword-only. kind ( str, default ““ ): What sort of instrument it is, such as “harpsichord”, so that other sounds of the same sort can be offered together. Built-in instruments use their family or name. Keyword-only. Examples >>> Instrument ( ... "flute" , ... label = "Flute" , ... folder = "samples/flute" , ... sustained = True , ... ). gain 1.0 >>> ( ... INSTRUMENT_BY_KEY [ "piano" ]. damped , ... INSTRUMENT_BY_KEY [ "marimba" ]. damped , ... ) (True, False)

title: alto.audio
text: Instrument.kind_name @ property def kind_name () -> str [Source] Name what sort of instrument this is, in lowercase. Returns str : The plugin’s kind , or the built-in family, or the instrument’s label. Examples >>> ( ... INSTRUMENT_BY_KEY [ ... "viola_bowed" ... ]. kind_name , ... INSTRUMENT_BY_KEY [ "flute" ]. kind_name , ... ) ('viola', 'flute')

title: alto.audio
text: Instrument.picker_group @ property def picker_group () -> str [Source] Identify the instrument’s entry in the sound picker. Returns str : The pack-qualified key for a plugin sound, or the built-in family or label. Examples >>> INSTRUMENT_BY_KEY [ ... "viola_bowed" ... ]. picker_group 'Viola'

title: alto.audio
text: Instrument.playback_volume def playback_volume ( level : float = 1.0 ) -> float [Source] Return the output volume for a note or clip played on this instrument. Parameters level ( float, default 1.0 ): Relative amplitude. Simultaneous notes can request a lower level for each voice. Returns float : Linear Qt volume between zero and one, including the instrument’s gain. Examples >>> INSTRUMENT_BY_KEY [ "flute" ]. playback_volume () 0.85

title: alto.audio
text: instrument_groups def instrument_groups () -> list [ tuple [ str , list [ Instrument ]]] [Source] Return the instruments as they are listed for choosing. Ways of playing one instrument share a single entry. Returns list of tuple of (str, list of Instrument) : Each entry’s picker group and its instruments, in the order listed. Examples >>> [ name for name , _ in instrument_groups ()] ['Piano', 'Flute', 'French Horn', 'Viola', 'Marimba', 'Vibraphone'] >>> [ ... inst_ . variant ... for inst_ in dict ( instrument_groups ())[ ... "Viola" ... ] ... ] ['Arco', 'Pizzicato']

title: alto.audio
text: read_wav def read_wav ( path : Path ) -> tuple [ list [ float ], int ] [Source] Read a mono 16-bit WAV file. Parameters path ( Path ): The file. Returns tuple of (list of float, int) : The samples as floats from -1 to 1, and the sample rate in hertz. Examples >>> import tempfile >>> path_ = ( ... Path ( tempfile . mkdtemp ()) / "silence.wav" ... ) >>> _ = path_ . write_bytes ( ... to_wav_bytes ([ 0.0 ] * 10 ) ... ) >>> samples , rate = read_wav ( path_ ) >>> len ( samples ), rate (10, 44100)

title: alto.audio
text: shift_pitch def shift_pitch ( samples : Sequence [ float ], * , semitones : float , ) -> list [ float ] [Source] Change the pitch of samples by resampling them. It also changes the length, which is fine for a few semitones. Parameters samples ( sequence of float ): Mono samples. semitones ( float ): How far to shift; positive is higher. Keyword-only. Returns list of float : The resampled samples, shorter when shifted up and longer when shifted down. Examples >>> len ( ... shift_pitch ([ 0.0 ] * 100 , semitones = 12 ) ... ) # an octave up: half as long 50

title: alto.audio
text: to_wav_bytes def to_wav_bytes ( samples : Iterable [ float ], * , rate : int = SAMPLE_RATE , ) -> bytes [Source] Encode samples as a mono 16-bit WAV file in memory. Parameters samples ( iterable of float ): Mono samples from -1 to 1; anything beyond is clipped. rate ( int, default SAMPLE_RATE ): The sample rate in hertz. Keyword-only. Returns bytes : The contents of a WAV file. Examples >>> to_wav_bytes ([ 0.0 ] * 10 )[: 4 ] b'RIFF' >>> import tempfile >>> clipped = ( ... Path ( tempfile . mkdtemp ()) / "clipped.wav" ... ) >>> _ = clipped . write_bytes ( ... to_wav_bytes ([ 2.0 , - 3.0 , 0.5 ]) ... ) >>> [ ... round ( value , 3 ) ... for value in read_wav ( clipped )[ 0 ] ... ] # beyond full scale is clipped [1.0, -1.0, 0.5]

title: alto.audio
text: write_file_atomically def write_file_atomically ( path : Path , * , data : bytes , ) -> None [Source] Write a file so that nothing ever reads it half written, even another copy of Alto writing the same file. The bytes go to a file of the writer’s own first and then replace the file in one step. Parameters path ( Path ): The file. data ( bytes ): What it holds. Keyword-only. Examples >>> folder = Path ( tempfile . mkdtemp ()) >>> write_file_atomically ( ... folder / "note.wav" , data = b "RIFF" ... ) >>> ( ... ( folder / "note.wav" ). read_bytes (), ... [ p . name for p in folder . iterdir ()], ... ) (b'RIFF', ['note.wav'])

title: alto.audio
text: metronome_preview_pcm @ lru_cache ( maxsize = len ( METRONOME_CLICKS )) def metronome_preview_pcm ( key : str ) -> tuple [ bytes , int ] [Source] Return the four beats used for playback and the spectrum display. Parameters key ( str ): The bundled click to repeat at 120 BPM. Returns tuple of bytes and int : Mono 16-bit PCM frames and their sample rate in hertz. Examples >>> pcm , rate = metronome_preview_pcm ( "high-pip" ) >>> len ( pcm ) > 3 * rate True

title: alto.audio
text: Sounds Sounds () [Source] Bases: QObject A lazy cache of notes played through QSoundEffect , in the chosen instrument. Attributes enabled ( bool ): False while the app is muted. instrument ( str ): The key of the instrument in use, a key of INSTRUMENT_BY_KEY . FADE_MS ( int ): How quickly a sustained note dies away when the next one begins, in milliseconds. Examples >>> s = Sounds () >>> s . enabled , s . instrument (True, 'piano') >>> s . enabled = False # muted: nothing below makes a sound >>> s . play_midi ( 60 ) Constructor Create a player with the piano chosen and sound on. Constructor examples >>> Sounds (). instrument 'piano'

title: alto.audio
text: Sounds.recordings def recordings ( inst : Instrument ) -> dict [ int , Path ] [Source] Return the notes an instrument has a recording for on disk. Parameters inst ( Instrument ): The instrument. Returns dict of int to Path : MIDI note number to its sample file. Examples >>> 60 in Sounds (). recordings ( ... INSTRUMENT_BY_KEY [ "piano" ] ... ) True

title: alto.audio
text: Sounds.unrecorded def unrecorded ( instrument : str | None = None ) -> list [ int ] [Source] List the notes within an instrument’s recorded range that have no recording of their own, nearest middle C first. Each is made the first time it plays, by shifting the nearest recording. alto.ui.warmup makes them ahead of time with prepare , so that even a first play is quick. Parameters instrument ( str or None, default None ): The instrument’s key, or None for the current one. Returns list of int : MIDI note numbers. Examples >>> notes = Sounds (). unrecorded ( ... "piano" ... ) # the piano is recorded every third semitone >>> notes [: 2 ], 60 in notes , len ( notes ) ([61, 59], False, 58)

title: alto.audio
text: Sounds.prepare def prepare ( midi : int , * , instrument : str | None = None , ) -> None [Source] Make the file a note plays, if it has no recording and was not made before, so that its first play is quick. Parameters midi ( int ): The MIDI note number. instrument ( str or None, default None ): The instrument’s key, or None for the current one. Keyword-only. Examples >>> Sounds (). prepare ( 61 , instrument = "piano" )

title: alto.audio
text: Sounds.note_duration_ms def note_duration_ms ( midi : int , * , instrument : str | None = None , ) -> int [Source] Read the playback length of a note for synchronized instrument animations. Parameters midi ( int ): Sounding MIDI pitch. instrument ( str or None ): Pack sound key, or None for the learner’s selected sound. Returns int : Duration in milliseconds, using the usual feedback interval if the WAV is unavailable. Examples A one-second sample has the same 1000 ms feedback interval when muted.

title: alto.audio
text: Sounds.play_midi def play_midi ( midi : int , * , volume : float = 1.0 , instrument : str | None = None , force : bool = False , release_previous : bool = True , ) -> None [Source] Play a note in the chosen instrument (or another one). A sustained instrument (bowed or blown) ends the notes still sounding first, as a player would, and so does a damped one (the piano, played without the pedal), unless release_previous is False, which is for the notes of a chord that start together. Nothing plays while muted unless force is set. A failure to play is reported but never raised, so audio can never break an exercise. Parameters midi ( int ): The MIDI note number. volume ( float, default 1.0 ): The level from 0 to 1, before the instrument’s own gain. Keyword-only. instrument ( str or None, default None ): The key of the instrument to use instead of the chosen one. Keyword-only. force ( bool, default False ): Play even while muted, for previews. Keyword-only. release_previous ( bool, default True ): End the sustained or damped notes still ringing first. Keyword-only. Examples >>> s = Sounds () >>> s . enabled = False >>> s . play_midi ( 60 ) # muted: returns at once >>> Sounds (). play_midi ( 60 ) # doctest: +SKIP

title: alto.audio
text: Sounds.play_metronome_click def play_metronome_click ( * , force : bool = False , ) -> None [Source] Play one beat with the selected click sound. Parameters force ( bool, default False ): Play even when muted for an explicit settings preview. Examples >>> player = Sounds () >>> player . enabled = False >>> player . play_metronome_click ()

title: alto.audio
text: Sounds.preview_metronome def preview_metronome ( key : str ) -> None [Source] Play four evenly spaced clicks at 120 BPM, even while muted. Render one clip so loading the sound cannot delay later beats. Parameters key ( str ): The bundled click to audition. Examples >>> sounds . preview_metronome ( "low-pip" ) # doctest: +SKIP

title: alto.audio
text: Sounds.stop_metronome_preview def stop_metronome_preview () -> None [Source] End the four-click audition when leaving the preview. Examples >>> sounds . stop_metronome_preview ()

title: alto.audio
text: Sounds.stop_all def stop_all () -> None [Source] Silence every note at once, and cancel any fade-outs underway. Examples >>> Sounds (). stop_all ()

title: alto.audio
text: Sounds.preview def preview ( key : str , * , midis : Iterable [ int | None ], step_ms : int | tuple [ int , ...] = 300 , beat_ms : int | None = None , force : bool = True , on_step : Callable [[ int | None ], object ] | None = None , ) -> None [Source] Play notes one after another in an instrument, even while muted, to hear what it sounds like. The phrase is rendered as one audio clip, so first-use loading cannot change the spacing between notes. Starting a preview silences the one before it. Parameters key ( str ): The key of the instrument. midis ( iterable of int or None ): MIDI pitches in order, with None for a rest. Keyword-only. step_ms ( int or tuple of int, default 300 ): Duration in milliseconds for every note, or one per note. beat_ms ( int or None ): Add the selected metronome sound at this interval in milliseconds. Omit for an unaccompanied preview. force ( bool, default True ): Play even when muted. False follows the sound setting while keeping the visual timing. on_step ( callable or None ): Highlight each onset. Clear on completion or interruption. Examples >>> sounds . preview ( ... "flute" , midis = [ 60 , 64 , 67 ] ... ) # doctest: +SKIP

title: alto.audio
text: Sounds.play_rhythm def play_rhythm ( step_ms : tuple [ int , ...], * , levels : tuple [ float , ...], force : bool = False , on_step : Callable [[ int | None ], object ], ) -> None [Source] Play one metronome click per written onset, observing rests. Parameters step_ms ( tuple of int ): Length of each note or rest in milliseconds. levels ( tuple of float ): Click volume from zero (rest) to one for each step. force ( bool ): Allow an explicit audition while muted. on_step ( callable ): Highlight notes and rests, then clear after the last step. Examples >>> sounds . play_rhythm ( ... ( 600 , 600 ), levels = ( 1.0 , 0.0 ), on_step = print , ... ) # doctest: +SKIP

title: alto.audio
text: Sounds.play_notes def play_notes ( columns : Iterable [ Sequence [ Note ]], * , gap_ms : int = DEFAULT_NOTE_GAP_MS , warmup : bool = False , force : bool = False , instrument : str | None = None , on_step : Callable [[ int | None ], object ] | None = None , ) -> None [Source] Play staff columns left to right, evenly spaced. The notes within a column sound together, a little quieter the more there are. Parameters instrument ( str or None ): Instrument key for this playback, or None for the learner’s selection. force ( bool ): Play even when exercise audio is muted. warmup ( bool ): Silently initialize audio streams before starting playback. columns ( iterable of sequence of Note ): The columns of notes, as drawn on a staff. gap_ms ( int, default 450 ): The time between columns, in milliseconds. Keyword-only. on_step ( callable or None, default None ): Called with the index of each column as it starts, and with None when the last has had its time. It is called while muted too, so a display can follow the music with the sound off. Keyword-only. Examples >>> s = Sounds () >>> s . enabled = False >>> s . play_notes ( ... [ ... [ ... Note . parse ( "C4" ), ... Note . parse ( "E4" ), ... Note . parse ( "G4" ), ... ] ... ] ... ) # muted: nothing sounds

title: alto.audio
text: Sounds.stop_sample def stop_sample ( on_step : Callable [[ int | None ], object ]) -> None [Source] Stop a displayed sample if it still owns playback. Parameters on_step ( callable ): The display callback originally passed to play_sample. Examples >>> Sounds (). stop_sample ( print )

title: alto.audio
text: Sounds.play_sample def play_sample ( columns : Sequence [ Sequence [ Note ]], * , gap_ms : int , on_step : Callable [[ int | None ], object ], force : bool = False , instrument : str | None = None , warmup : bool = False , ) -> None [Source] Play a displayed sample and report the sounding column until it ends or is interrupted. Parameters columns ( sequence of sequence of Note ): Written notes in playback order, with simultaneous notes grouped together. gap_ms ( int ): Time between column onsets in milliseconds. on_step ( callable ): Receives each sounding column index and None to clear the display. instrument ( str or None ): Instrument key for this playback, or None for the learner’s selection. force ( bool ): Audition the sample even when exercise audio is muted. warmup ( bool ): Prepare the audio streams before the first note. Examples >>> player = Sounds () >>> player . enabled = False >>> player . play_sample ( ... [[ Note . parse ( "C4" )]], ... gap_ms = 300 , ... on_step = print , ... ) 0 >>> player . stop_sample ( print ) None

title: alto.audio
text: Sounds.play_correct def play_correct ( streak : int ) -> None [Source] Play a note that climbs the C major scale (C5 to C6) as the streak grows, then wraps. Parameters streak ( int ): How many right answers in a row; 1 plays C5. Examples >>> s = Sounds () >>> s . enabled = False >>> s . play_correct ( 3 ) # muted: nothing sounds

title: alto.circle_schemes
text: alto.circle_schemes The color schemes of the circle of fifths: the presets, and the schemes a user makes. A scheme says what color each of the 24 cells of the circle is when it is quiet and when it is lit, and whether its wedges are light, with dark names. The circle blends between the two as a cell brightens. The disc in the middle is not part of a scheme: it takes the colors of the app’s theme. Nothing here needs Qt, so the schemes can be tested, saved and shown anywhere; alto.ui.circle turns them into pictures. A color is a hue (0 to 360), a saturation and a lightness (both 0 to 1). Examples >>> scheme = preset ( "cyan-indigo" ) >>> scheme . name , scheme . light ('Cyan to indigo', False) >>> round ( ... scheme . color ( ... "outer" , place = 0 , lift = 1.0 ... )[ 2 ], ... 2 , ... ) > round ( ... scheme . color ( ... "outer" , place = 0 , lift = 0.0 ... )[ 2 ], ... 2 , ... ) True

title: alto.circle_schemes
text: CellMaker class CellMaker ( Protocol ) [Source] A function that gives the cell at a place on a ring its quiet and lit colors.

title: alto.circle_schemes
text: CustomRecord class CustomRecord ( TypedDict ) [Source] A scheme of the user’s own, as it is saved. Attributes id ( str ): Its key, such as “custom-1”. name ( str ): What the user called it. mode ( str ): How its colors are made: a key of MODES . colors ( list of str ): The colors the mode takes, as “#rrggbb”: what a cell looks like when it is lit. light ( bool ): Whether the wedges are light, with dark names.

title: alto.circle_schemes
text: Scheme Scheme ( key : str , name : str , description : str , light : bool , cells : dict [ str , tuple [ Cell , ...]], ) [Source] A color scheme for the circle. Attributes key ( str ): Its identifier, used to save the choice. name ( str ): Its name, as the settings show it. description ( str ): A sentence about it. light ( bool ): Whether the wedges are light, with dark names, instead of dark with white names. cells ( dict of str to tuple of (tuple of float, tuple of float) ): For each ring (“outer” and “inner”), the 12 cells’ quiet and lit colors, clockwise from the top.

title: alto.circle_schemes
text: Scheme.color def color ( ring : str , * , place : int , lift : float , ) -> tuple [ float , float , float ] [Source] Return the color of a cell as it is lit. Parameters ring ( str ): “outer” or “inner”. place ( int ): The cell’s place, clockwise from the top. Keyword-only. lift ( float ): How lit it is, from 0 (quiet) to 1 (fully lit). Keyword-only. Returns tuple of float : Its red, green and blue, each from 0 to 1. Examples >>> red , green , blue = preset ( "spectrum" ). color ( ... "outer" , place = 0 , lift = 1.0 ... ) >>> red > green and red > blue True >>> preset ( "spectrum" ). color ( ... "outer" , place = 6 , lift = 0.0 ... )[ 0 ] < 0.2 True

title: alto.circle_schemes
text: Scheme.names def names () -> dict [ str , str ] [Source] Return the colors of the names written on the wedges. Returns dict of str to str : “ink” (a key’s name) and “muted” (its other name and its numeral), as “#rrggbb”. Examples >>> ( ... preset ( "paper" ). names ()[ "ink" ], ... preset ( "spectrum" ). names ()[ "ink" ], ... ) ('#1b2030', '#f5f5f5')

title: alto.circle_schemes
text: rgb_of def rgb_of ( color : Hsl , * , capped : bool , ) -> tuple [ float , float , float ] [Source] Turn a color into red, green and blue, keeping a dark circle’s cells from getting too bright. Yellows and greens look far brighter than blues of the same lightness, so on dark wedges a color that is brighter than white names can stand is brought down to the limit. Parameters color ( tuple of float ): The hue, saturation and lightness. capped ( bool ): Whether to bring a too bright color down. Keyword-only. Returns tuple of float : Red, green and blue, each from 0 to 1. Examples >>> r , g , b = rgb_of ( ... ( 60.0 , 0.9 , 0.5 ), capped = True ... ) >>> 0.299 * r + 0.587 * g + 0.114 * b <= MAX_BRIGHTNESS + 1e-9 True >>> rgb_of (( 0.0 , 0.0 , 1.0 ), capped = False ) (1.0, 1.0, 1.0)

title: alto.circle_schemes
text: hex_of def hex_of ( rgb : tuple [ float , float , float ]) -> str [Source] Write a color as “#rrggbb”. Parameters rgb ( tuple of float ): Red, green and blue, each from 0 to 1. Returns str : The color as hexadecimal. Examples >>> hex_of (( 1.0 , 0.5 , 0.0 )) '#ff8000'

title: alto.circle_schemes
text: hsl_of def hsl_of ( text : str ) -> Hsl [Source] Read a color written as “#rrggbb”. Parameters text ( str ): The color. Returns tuple of float : Its hue (0 to 360), saturation and lightness. Examples >>> hsl_of ( "#ff0000" ) (0.0, 1.0, 0.5)

title: alto.circle_schemes
text: signature_of def signature_of ( place : int ) -> int [Source] Return how far a place is from C, with flats as negative: the key signature of the major key there. Parameters place ( int ): The place clockwise from the top, 0 to 11. Returns int : From -5 (five flats) to 6 (six sharps). Examples >>> [ ... signature_of ( at ) ... for at in ( 0 , 1 , 6 , 7 , 11 ) ... ] [0, 1, 6, -5, -1]

title: alto.circle_schemes
text: preset def preset ( key : str ) -> Scheme [Source] Return a preset by its key. Parameters key ( str ): A key of PRESETS . Returns Scheme : The preset. Raises KeyError : If there is no such preset. Examples >>> preset ( "midnight" ). name 'Midnight' >>> len ( PRESETS ) 14

title: alto.circle_schemes
text: record_of def record_of ( key : str , * , name : str , mode : str , colors : list [ str ], light : bool = False , ) -> CustomRecord [Source] Make the record of a scheme of the user’s own. Parameters key ( str ): Its key, such as “custom-1”. name ( str ): Its name. Keyword-only. mode ( str ): How its colors are made: a key of MODES . Keyword-only. colors ( list of str ): The colors the mode takes, as “#rrggbb”. Keyword-only. light ( bool, default False ): Whether the wedges are light. Keyword-only. Returns CustomRecord : The record. Nothing is checked: clean_record does that. Examples >>> record_of ( ... "custom-1" , ... name = "Mine" , ... mode = "single" , ... colors = [ "#2f6bd0" ], ... )[ "light" ] False

title: alto.circle_schemes
text: clean_record def clean_record ( raw : object ) -> CustomRecord | None [Source] Check one saved scheme of the user’s own, and tidy it. Parameters raw ( object ): What was read back from the saved data. Returns CustomRecord or None : The record, with a name of at most 40 characters, or None if anything in it is missing or wrong: an unknown mode, a color that is not “#rrggbb”, or the wrong number of colors for the mode. Examples >>> good = record_of ( ... "custom-1" , ... name = "Mine" , ... mode = "rings" , ... colors = [ "#2f6bd0" , "#18a0c0" ], ... ) >>> clean_record ( good ) == good True >>> few = record_of ( ... "custom-1" , ... name = "Mine" , ... mode = "rings" , ... colors = [ "#2f6bd0" ], ... ) >>> unknown = record_of ( ... "custom-1" , ... name = "Mine" , ... mode = "nope" , ... colors = [ "#2f6bd0" , "#18a0c0" ], ... ) >>> ( ... clean_record ( few ) is None , ... clean_record ( unknown ) is None , ... ) (True, True) >>> clean_record ( "not a record" ) is None True

title: alto.circle_schemes
text: custom_scheme def custom_scheme ( record : CustomRecord ) -> Scheme [Source] Make a scheme from one of the user’s own records. The colors in a record are what a cell looks like when lit; the quiet cells are the same hue, calmer and darker (or, on a light wedges, paler). Parameters record ( CustomRecord ): A record that clean_record accepted. Returns Scheme : The scheme, with the key and name of the record. Examples >>> scheme = custom_scheme ( ... record_of ( ... "custom-1" , ... name = "Mine" , ... mode = "rings" , ... colors = [ "#2f6bd0" , "#18a0c0" ], ... ) ... ) >>> scheme . key , scheme . name , scheme . light ('custom-1', 'Mine', False) >>> scheme . cells [ "outer" ][ 0 ][ 1 ][ ... 0 ... ] != scheme . cells [ "inner" ][ 0 ][ 1 ][ ... 0 ... ] # two rings, two hues True

title: alto.circle_schemes
text: dump_customs def dump_customs ( records : list [ CustomRecord ]) -> str [Source] Write the user’s own schemes as text to save. Parameters records ( list of CustomRecord ): The schemes. Returns str : JSON. Examples >>> dump_customs ([]) '[]'

title: alto.circle_schemes
text: load_customs def load_customs ( text : str ) -> list [ CustomRecord ] [Source] Read the user’s own schemes back, leaving out any that are not valid and any beyond the limit. Parameters text ( str ): What dump_customs wrote. Returns list of CustomRecord : The valid schemes, each with its own key. Examples >>> ( ... load_customs ( "not json" ), ... load_customs ( "[1, 2]" ), ... ) ([], []) >>> one = record_of ( ... "custom-1" , ... name = "A" , ... mode = "single" , ... colors = [ "#2f6bd0" ], ... ) >>> [ ... r [ "id" ] ... for r in load_customs ( ... dump_customs ([ one , one ]) ... ) ... ] # a repeated key is dropped ['custom-1']

title: alto.circle_schemes
text: resolve def resolve ( key : str , * , customs : list [ CustomRecord ], ) -> Scheme [Source] Find a scheme by its key, among the presets and the user’s own, falling back to the default. Parameters key ( str ): The saved choice. customs ( list of CustomRecord ): The user’s own schemes. Keyword-only. Returns Scheme : The scheme, or the default one if the key is unknown (for instance after the scheme was deleted). Examples >>> ( ... resolve ( "midnight" , customs = []). name , ... resolve ( "gone" , customs = []). key , ... ) ('Midnight', 'cyan-indigo')

title: alto.circle_schemes
text: next_custom_key def next_custom_key ( customs : list [ CustomRecord ]) -> str [Source] Return a key that none of the user’s schemes has. Parameters customs ( list of CustomRecord ): The user’s own schemes. Returns str : “custom-“ and the smallest number that is free. Examples >>> taken = [ ... record_of ( ... "custom-1" , ... name = "" , ... mode = "single" , ... colors = [], ... ) ... ] >>> next_custom_key ([]), next_custom_key ( taken ) ('custom-1', 'custom-2')

title: alto.exercises.base
text: alto.exercises.base Exercise framework. Register a ChoiceExercise for button answers or an Exercise for construction tasks. An Exercise makes Question objects. The Question says what to show (a staff, a keyboard or only text), which buttons to offer and which answer is right. The exercise screen and the scheduler work with those two classes only, so a new exercise needs no new interface code. Examples >>> question = Question ( ... "Name this note." , ... choices = [ "C" , "D" , "E" ], ... answer = "D" , ... ) >>> question . check ( "D" ), question . check ( "E" ) (True, False)

title: alto.exercises.base
text: FingerboardPosition FingerboardPosition ( strings : tuple [ str , ...], string : int , note : str , instrument : str = '' , ) [Source] A written pitch on one string, with the tuning needed to redraw it. Examples >>> FingerboardPosition ( ... ( "C3" , "G3" , "D4" , "A4" ), 2 , "E4" ... ). string 2

title: alto.exercises.base
text: PicturePosition PicturePosition ( instrument : str , point : tuple [ float , float ], note : str = '' , size : float = 0.0 , focus : tuple [ float , ...] = (), marker : bool = True , view : str = '' , keys : tuple [ tuple [ str , str ], ...] = (), notes : tuple [ str , ...] = (), span : tuple [ str , ...] = (), ) [Source] A pack-owned image and a marked location in its original pixels. Attributes instrument ( str ): The pack-qualified instrument whose picture is shown. point ( tuple of float ): The marked location, in the picture’s own pixels. note ( str, default ““ ): A pitch to play when the answer is right, or an empty string for a silent question. size ( float, default 0.0 ): The marker’s diameter in the picture’s own pixels. Zero asks for Alto’s default size, which suits a large part. focus ( tuple of float, default () ): The region to show, as left, top, width and height in the picture’s own pixels, so a small part is easy to see. Empty shows the whole picture. marker ( bool, default True ): False shows the picture without a dot, for a lesson that introduces the whole instrument. view ( str, default ““ ): The instrument’s extra picture to use, such as “back”, with the point and focus in that picture’s pixels. Empty uses the instrument’s main picture. keys ( tuple of tuple of str, default () ): Keys to highlight on the instrument’s keyboards, which Alto draws instead of the picture. Each is the name of a keyboard and the pitch of a key on it, such as ("Lower manual", "C4") . notes ( tuple of str, default () ): Pitches to play one after another when the answer is right, such as the two keys of an interval. They take the place of note . span ( tuple of str, default () ): The lowest and highest key to draw on each keyboard, such as ("C3", "C5") . Empty draws each keyboard’s whole range. Examples >>> PicturePosition ( ... "pack.studio.drum" , ( 80 , 50 ) ... ). point (80, 50) >>> PicturePosition ( ... "pack.studio.organ" , ... ( 0 , 0 ), ... keys = (( "Great" , "C4" ), ( "Swell" , "E4" )), ... ). keys [ 1 ] ('Swell', 'E4')

title: alto.exercises.base
text: Question Question ( prompt : str , * , choices : list [ str ], answer : str , staff : list [ list [ Note ]] = field ( default_factory = list ), clef : str = 'treble' , explanation : str = '' , key : int = 0 , staff_signature : int | None = None , minor : bool = False , value : str = 'whole' , grid : dict [ str , tuple [ int , int ]] | None = None , keyboard : Note | None = None , keyboard_notes : list [ Note ] = field ( default_factory = list ), key_staff : bool = False , keyboard_range : tuple [ int , int ] | None = None , octaves : list [ str ] | None = None , second_label : str = 'Octave' , joiner : str = '' , construct : Note | None = None , accidentals : bool = False , accept : tuple [ str , ...] = (), show_staff : bool = False , caption : str = '' , build_key : bool = False , place_signature : bool = False , starting_slots : list [ int ] = field ( default_factory = list ), construct_scale : list [ Note ] | None = None , construct_steps : list [ str ] | None = None , notes_only : bool = False , any_octave : bool = False , exact_octave : bool = False , circle : int | None = None , circle_kind : str = '' , circle_ring : str = 'outer' , circle_key : int | None = None , required : tuple [ str , ...] = (), place_clef : str = '' , picture : PicturePosition | None = None , fingerboard : FingerboardPosition | None = None , notation_target : tuple [ str , int ] | None = None , notation_excerpt : str | None = None , ) [Source] One question, with what to show for it and which answer is right. Attributes prompt ( str ): The text shown above the question; may be empty. choices ( list of str ): The answer buttons, in the order they should be offered. Keyword-only. answer ( str ): The right answer, one of choices (or the note name for a “place this note” question). Keyword-only. staff ( list of list of Note ): What to draw on the staff: each inner list is one chord or note. Keyword-only. clef ( str, default “treble” ): The clef to draw on. Keyword-only. explanation ( str, default ““ ): Text shown after the answer to say why it is right. Keyword-only. key ( int, default 0 ): The key signature to draw: that many sharps if positive, flats if negative. Keyword-only. value ( str, default “whole” ): The written duration for single notes and interval voices. Keyword-only. staff_signature ( int or None ): Override the signature shown on the staff while retaining the key for scale degrees. Keyword-only. minor ( bool, default False ): Use the signature’s relative minor for scale degree naming. Keyword-only. grid ( dict of str to tuple of (int, int) or None ): Where to put each answer button, as (row, column). Without it the choices form one row. Keyword-only. picture ( PicturePosition or None ): Pack image, marker coordinates and optional sounding pitch. Keyword-only. fingerboard ( FingerboardPosition or None ): Tuning, string index, and marked pitch for a four-string identification question. Keyword-only. keyboard ( Note or None ): A piano key to highlight, instead of drawing a staff. Keyword-only. keyboard_notes ( list of Note ): Multiple piano keys to highlight together instead of drawing a staff. Keyword-only. key_staff ( bool, default False ): Draw key as a small key-signature staff above the keyboard. Keyword-only. keyboard_range ( tuple of (int, int) or None ): The keys (MIDI numbers, inclusive) the keyboard picture should show. Keyword-only. octaves ( list of str or None ): When set, the answer is a choice button plus one of these second-row buttons. Keyword-only. second_label ( str, default “Octave” ): What the second row of buttons is called. Keyword-only. joiner ( str, default ““ ): Put between the two parts to make the answer (“” for a note and its octave: C + 4 gives C4). Keyword-only. construct ( Note or None ): The note to place on the staff: the answer is a position, not a button. Keyword-only. accidentals ( bool, default False ): Show the sharp, natural and flat buttons for a construct question. Keyword-only. accept ( tuple of str ): Other answers that count as right, such as the enharmonic name of a black key. Keyword-only. show_staff ( bool, default False ): Draw the staff even with no notes on it, to show only its clef and key signature. Keyword-only. caption ( str, default ““ ): Text written on the staff itself, under the music, in place of the prompt above it. Keyword-only. build_key ( bool, default False ): The learner builds the key signature key on a blank staff with the fork widget, instead of pressing a button. Keyword-only. place_signature ( bool, default False ): Place each accidental of the named key on the staff. Keyword-only. starting_slots ( list of int ): Zero-based positions of the accidentals already printed in an Order of Keys question. construct_scale ( list of Note or None ): The notes of a scale to place on the staff one after another, left to right: the answer is the whole row. Keyword-only. construct_steps ( list of str or None ): The steps between the notes of construct_scale , each “W” (whole) or “H” (half), to mark once the notes are placed; None if the steps are not asked. Keyword-only. notes_only ( bool, default False ): Show note names without a scale degree context. Keyword-only. any_octave ( bool, default False ): Accept a single constructed note with the right spelling in any octave. Keyword-only. exact_octave ( bool, default False ): The scale has to be placed in the octave asked, not in any octave. Keyword-only. circle ( int or None ): A question on the circle of fifths: the place asked about, clockwise from C at 0. Keyword-only. circle_kind ( str, default ““ ): What the circle asks: “major” (the relative major of a minor key), “minor” (the relative minor of a major key) or “numeral” (the Roman numeral of a chord of a key). Keyword-only. circle_ring ( str, default “outer” ): Which ring the cell asked about is in: “outer” for the major keys or “inner” for the minor ones. Keyword-only. circle_key ( int or None ): For a Roman numeral question, the place of the key whose chords they are. Keyword-only. required ( tuple of str ): Answers that must all be given, one after another in any order, such as both names of a key with two: B and C♭. Empty for an ordinary question with one answer. Keyword-only. notation_target ( tuple of (str, int) or None ): Notation part and zero-based note column or staff line to highlight. Keyword-only. notation_excerpt ( str or None ): Versioned score containing the target. Its position is an index into the excerpt manifest. Keyword-only. place_clef ( str, default ““ ): The clef to put on a blank staff: the answer is a clef symbol (G, C or F) and a place on the staff, not a button. Empty for any other question. Keyword-only. Examples >>> q = Question ( ... "Which note is this?" , ... choices = [ "C" , "D" , "E" ], ... answer = "D" , ... staff = [[ Note . parse ( "D4" )]], ... ) >>> q . check ( "D" ) True >>> Question . from_dict ( ... q . to_dict () ... ) == q # a question can be stored and asked again True

title: alto.exercises.base
text: Question.check_placed def check_placed ( note : Note ) -> bool [Source] Report whether a note placed on the staff is the one asked for. The spelling must match exactly. The octave must also match unless any_octave is set. Parameters note ( Note ): The note the learner placed. Returns bool : True if it matches the requested note spelling and any required octave. Examples >>> q = Question ( ... "Place C4" , ... choices = [], ... answer = "C4" , ... construct = Note . parse ( "C4" ), ... ) >>> q . check_placed ( Note . parse ( "C4" )) True >>> q . check_placed ( ... Note . parse ( "B#3" ) ... ) # sounds the same, but is spelled differently False

title: alto.exercises.base
text: Question.sounding_columns def sounding_columns () -> list [ list [ Note ]] [Source] Return pitches from the staff or keyboard in playback order. Returns list of list of Note : Each column contains the pitches sounding together. Examples A keyboard interval plays both of its highlighted pitches.

title: alto.exercises.base
text: Question.placement_columns def placement_columns ( note : Note | None ) -> list [ list [ Note ]] [Source] Return the given and placed notes grouped by onset, omitting the answer until it is placed. Parameters note ( Note or None ): Pitch under the pointer or submitted by the learner. Returns list of list of Note : Visible notes in playback order. Examples >>> q = Question ( ... "Place a major third." , ... choices = [], ... answer = "E4" , ... staff = [ ... [ Note . parse ( "C4" ), Note . parse ( "E4" )] ... ], ... ) >>> q . placement_columns ( None ) == [ ... [ Note . parse ( "C4" )] ... ] True

title: alto.exercises.base
text: Question.check_scale def check_scale ( notes : list [ Note ]) -> bool [Source] Report whether the notes placed on the staff are the scale asked for. The spelling and the order of the notes must match, so a G♯ is not an A♭. Unless exact_octave is set the octave does not matter, as long as the whole scale is in the same one: the same scale an octave higher or lower is right, but a scale with one note in the wrong octave is not. With exact_octave the scale has to be in the octave asked. Parameters notes ( list of Note ): The notes the learner placed, left to right. Returns bool : True if they are the notes of construct_scale , all moved by the same whole number of octaves (or, with exact_octave , not moved at all). Examples >>> asked = [ Note . parse ( "C4" ), Note . parse ( "D4" )] >>> q = Question ( ... "Place C D." , ... choices = [], ... answer = "C4 D4" , ... construct_scale = asked , ... ) >>> q . check_scale ( ... [ Note . parse ( "C4" ), Note . parse ( "D4" )] ... ) True >>> q . check_scale ( ... [ Note . parse ( "C5" ), Note . parse ( "D5" )] ... ) # the same scale, an octave higher True >>> q . check_scale ( ... [ Note . parse ( "C4" ), Note . parse ( "D5" )] ... ) # one note in another octave False >>> q . check_scale ( ... [ ... Note . parse ( "C4" ), ... Note . parse ( "D4" ), ... Note . parse ( "E4" ), ... ] ... ) False >>> exact = Question ( ... "Place C D." , ... choices = [], ... answer = "C4 D4" , ... construct_scale = asked , ... exact_octave = True , ... ) >>> ( ... exact . check_scale ( ... [ Note . parse ( "C4" ), Note . parse ( "D4" )] ... ), ... exact . check_scale ( ... [ Note . parse ( "C5" ), Note . parse ( "D5" )] ... ), ... ) (True, False)

title: alto.exercises.base
text: Question.check_steps def check_steps ( steps : list [ str ]) -> bool [Source] Report whether the steps marked between the notes of a scale are the right ones. Parameters steps ( list of str ): The steps the learner marked, left to right, each “W” or “H”. Returns bool : True if the steps are not asked, or if they are those of construct_steps . Examples >>> q = Question ( ... "Mark the steps." , ... choices = [], ... answer = "W H" , ... construct_steps = [ "W" , "H" ], ... ) >>> ( ... q . check_steps ([ "W" , "H" ]), ... q . check_steps ([ "H" , "W" ]), ... q . check_steps ([ "W" ]), ... ) (True, False, False) >>> Question ( ... "No steps." , choices = [], answer = "" ... ). check_steps ([]) True

title: alto.exercises.base
text: Question.check_built def check_built ( count : int ) -> bool [Source] Report whether a key signature built with the fork is the one asked for. Parameters count ( int ): The signature the learner built: that many sharps if positive, flats if negative. Returns bool : True if it equals key . Examples >>> q = Question ( ... "Build D major." , ... choices = [], ... answer = "2 sharps" , ... key = 2 , ... show_staff = True , ... build_key = True , ... ) >>> q . check_built ( 2 ), q . check_built ( - 2 ) (True, False)

title: alto.exercises.base
text: Question.places_sequence @ property def places_sequence () -> bool [Source] Report whether the learner enters successive positions on the staff. Returns bool : True for scales and handwritten key signatures. Examples >>> Question ( ... "D major" , ... choices = [], ... answer = "F♯5 C♯5" , ... place_signature = True , ... ). places_sequence True

title: alto.exercises.base
text: Question.check def check ( choice : str ) -> bool [Source] Report whether a chosen answer is right. Parameters choice ( str ): The text of the button that was pressed. Returns bool : True if it is the answer or one of the other accepted answers. Examples >>> q = Question ( ... "" , ... choices = [ "F♯" , "G♭" ], ... answer = "F♯" , ... accept = ( "G♭" ,), ... ) >>> q . check ( "F♯" ), q . check ( "G♭" ), q . check ( "A" ) (True, True, False) >>> both = Question ( ... "" , ... choices = [ "B" , "C♭" , "D" ], ... answer = "B" , ... required = ( "B" , "C♭" ), ... ) >>> ( ... both . check ( "B" ), ... both . check ( "C♭" ), ... both . check ( "D" ), ... ) # each is right, but both are needed: see `complete` (True, True, False)

title: alto.exercises.base
text: Question.complete def complete ( given : set [ str ]) -> bool [Source] Report whether the answers given so far are all of those needed. Parameters given ( set of str ): The right answers given so far. Returns bool : For an ordinary question, whether the answer has been given; for one with several required , whether all have. Examples >>> both = Question ( ... "" , ... choices = [ "B" , "C♭" ], ... answer = "B" , ... required = ( "B" , "C♭" ), ... ) >>> ( ... both . complete ({ "B" }), ... both . complete ({ "C♭" , "B" }), ... ) (False, True) >>> Question ( ... "" , choices = [ "C" ], answer = "C" ... ). complete ({ "C" }) True

title: alto.exercises.base
text: Question.item_key def item_key () -> str [Source] Return a stable identity for the question, so the same one can be recognized when it comes around again. It covers what is asked and where it is drawn, but not the note value or the order of the buttons. Returns str : A 20-character hexadecimal string. Examples >>> a = Question ( ... "Name it." , ... choices = [ "C" , "D" ], ... answer = "C" , ... ) >>> b = Question ( ... "Name it." , ... choices = [ "D" , "C" ], ... answer = "C" , ... ) # the same question, buttons in another order >>> a . item_key () == b . item_key () True >>> len ( a . item_key ()) 20

title: alto.exercises.base
text: Question.to_dict def to_dict () -> dict [Source] Return the question as plain data, so it can be stored and asked again. Returns dict : The fields of the question, with notes as dictionaries and tuples as lists. Examples >>> data = Question ( ... "Name it." , ... choices = [ "C" ], ... answer = "C" , ... staff = [[ Note . parse ( "C4" )]], ... ). to_dict () >>> data [ "answer" ], data [ "staff" ] ('C', [[{'octave': 4, 'letter': 0, 'accidental': 0}]])

title: alto.exercises.base
text: Question.from_dict @ classmethod def from_dict ( d : dict ) -> Question [Source] Rebuild a question from the data that to_dict made. Parameters d ( dict ): The stored data. Questions saved by older versions, which may carry a play field, are accepted. Returns Question : The question. Examples >>> q = Question ( ... "Name it." , ... choices = [ "C" , "D" ], ... answer = "C" , ... key = 2 , ... accept = ( "D" ,), ... ) >>> Question . from_dict ( q . to_dict ()) == q True

title: alto.exercises.base
text: note_from def note_from ( v : dict | None ) -> Note | None [Source] Rebuild a note from stored data. Parameters v ( dict or None ): A note as the dictionary to_dict stores, or None. Returns Note or None : The note, or None if v was None. Examples >>> note_from ( ... { ... "octave" : 4 , ... "letter" : 0 , ... "accidental" : 0 , ... } ... ) Note(octave=4, letter=0, accidental=0) >>> note_from ( None ) is None True

title: alto.exercises.base
text: signature def signature ( * parts : object ) -> str [Source] Describe the exercise settings in force, so a stored question is only asked again under the settings it was made for. Parameters *parts ( object ): The settings to describe: dataclasses, dictionaries, lists, sets and plain values, nested as needed. Returns str : A JSON string that is the same for equal settings, however their sets and dictionaries happen to be ordered. Examples >>> signature ({ "clefs" : { "bass" , "treble" }}, 3 ) '[{"clefs": ["bass", "treble"]}, 3]' >>> signature ( ... { "clefs" : { "treble" , "bass" }}, 3 ... ) == signature ( ... { "clefs" : { "bass" , "treble" }}, 3 ... ) True

title: alto.exercises.base
text: Exercise class Exercise ( ABC ) [Source] What every exercise provides: its name, how it makes questions and how long a good answer takes. Attributes name ( str ): The title shown on the home screen and in the exercise list. category ( str ): The heading it is listed under. description ( str ): One line saying what the exercise is for. par_seconds ( float, default 5.0 ): How long a good first answer takes; much quicker earns credit and much slower counts against the question. icon ( str, default ““ ): SVG shapes for the exercise’s tile, in a 24 by 24 box with COLOR where the theme’s ink goes. Plugins supply one; empty uses Alto’s own icon for the exercise. has_sound ( bool, default True ): False for an exercise that makes no sound at all, whatever the sound button says. interval_voices ( bool, default False ): True when two notes on the staff are an interval: they keep the question’s note value, with the stems apart, and are played one after the other when they are melodic. Examples >>> class Demo ( Exercise ): ... name = "Demo" ... ... def generate ( self , rng ): ... return Question ( ... "Pick A." , ... choices = [ "A" , "B" ], ... answer = "A" , ... ) >>> Demo (). generate ( random . Random ( 0 )). answer 'A'

title: alto.exercises.base
text: Exercise.sound_instrument def sound_instrument ( key : str | None ) -> str | None [Source] Choose the instrument that plays this exercise’s notes. Parameters key ( str or None ): The key of the instrument the question’s picture asks for, or None when it asks for none. Returns str or None : The key to play with, or None for the learner’s own choice of sound. Exercises return the picture’s instrument unless a setting says otherwise. Examples >>> from alto.exercises.library import NoteNames >>> NoteNames (). sound_instrument ( ... "pack.viola.bowed-viola" ... ) 'pack.viola.bowed-viola'

title: alto.exercises.base
text: Exercise.settings_signature def settings_signature () -> str [Source] Return what identifies the settings that shape the questions. A stored question is only asked again while this is unchanged. Exercises with settings override it. Returns str : An identifier; empty for an exercise with no settings. Examples >>> class Demo ( Exercise ): ... def generate ( self , rng ): ... return Question ( ... "?" , choices = [ "A" ], answer = "A" ... ) >>> Demo (). settings_signature () ''

title: alto.exercises.base
text: Exercise.card_prompt def card_prompt ( question : Question ) -> str [Source] Say what to do on a flashcard made from a question, where nothing on screen explains the task. Exercises whose on-screen prompt depends on the screen (buttons to press, a staff to click) override this. Parameters question ( Question ): The question on the card. Returns str : The instruction, shown above the card’s picture. Examples >>> class Demo ( Exercise ): ... name = "Demo" ... ... def generate ( self , rng ): ... return Question ( ... "Pick A." , ... choices = [ "A" ], ... answer = "A" , ... ) >>> Demo (). card_prompt ( ... Question ( "" , choices = [ "A" ], answer = "A" ) ... ) 'Demo' >>> Demo (). card_prompt ( ... Question ( ... "Click the fermata." , ... choices = [], ... answer = "fermata" , ... notation_target = ( "fermata" , 0 ), ... ) ... ) 'Locate the fermata.'

title: alto.exercises.base
text: Exercise.card_groups def card_groups () -> dict [ str , str ] | None [Source] Map playable examples to the skills that share a calendar review date. Returns dict of str to str or None : Example item keys mapped to skill names, or None when every example has its own schedule. Examples >>> from alto.exercises.library import ( ... KeyboardNotes , ... ) >>> KeyboardNotes (). card_groups () is None True

title: alto.exercises.base
text: Exercise.card_count def card_count () -> int | None [Source] Count distinct cards possible with the current settings when the exercise has an exact catalog. Returns int or None : Catalog size, or None for an exercise that prepares a bounded daily sample. Examples >>> from alto.exercises.library import ( ... KeyboardNotes , ... ) >>> KeyboardNotes (). card_count () is None True

title: alto.exercises.base
text: Exercise.daily_candidates def daily_candidates ( rng : random . Random ) -> Iterator [ Question ] [Source] Yield distinct questions until 100 consecutive draws find no new playable item. Parameters rng ( random.Random ): The generator for this day’s sample. Yields Question : A playable question. Finite exercises can override this to visit every eligible item. Examples >>> from alto.exercises.library import ( ... KeyboardNotes , ... ) >>> isinstance ( ... next ( ... KeyboardNotes (). daily_candidates ( ... random . Random ( 1 ) ... ) ... ), ... Question , ... ) True

title: alto.exercises.base
text: Exercise.review_question def review_question ( question : Question , * , same_settings : bool , ) -> Question | None [Source] Adapt a stored question for review under the active settings. Parameters question ( Question ): Previously introduced card. same_settings ( bool ): Whether the saved presentation matches the active settings. Returns Question or None : A playable question when the exercise recognizes this presentation. Examples >>> from alto.exercises.library import ( ... KeyboardNotes , ... ) >>> ex = KeyboardNotes () >>> q = ex . generate ( random . Random ( 1 )) >>> ex . review_question ( ... q , same_settings = True ... ) == q True

title: alto.exercises.base
text: Exercise.refresh def refresh ( question : Question ) -> Question [Source] Bring a stored question up to date with how the exercise draws its questions now. A question that is asked again comes from the copy stored when it was first asked, which an older version may have drawn differently. The default leaves it as it is. Parameters question ( Question ): The question as it was stored. Returns Question : The question as the exercise would draw it today. Examples >>> class Demo ( Exercise ): ... def generate ( self , rng ): ... return Question ( ... "?" , choices = [ "A" ], answer = "A" ... ) >>> q = Question ( "?" , choices = [ "A" ], answer = "A" ) >>> Demo (). refresh ( q ) is q True

title: alto.exercises.base
text: Exercise.instructions def instructions () -> str [Source] Return the help text shown from the exercise’s help button. Exercises override it to describe themselves. Returns str : Simple HTML; by default the one-line description. Examples >>> class Demo ( Exercise ): ... description = "Spot the note." ... ... def generate ( self , rng ): ... return Question ( ... "?" , choices = [ "A" ], answer = "A" ... ) >>> Demo (). instructions () 'Spot the note.'

title: alto.exercises.base
text: Exercise.generate @ abstractmethod def generate ( rng : random . Random ) -> Question [Source] Make one new question. Parameters rng ( random.Random ): The random number generator to use, so tests can ask for a repeatable question. Returns Question : The question. Examples >>> from alto.exercises.library import NoteNames >>> q = NoteNames (). generate ( random . Random ( 1 )) >>> q . answer in q . choices True

title: alto.exercises.base
text: ButtonSettings ButtonSettings ( button_mode : str = 'all' , button_count : int = 6 , ) [Source] An exercise’s choice of answer layout and maximum number of buttons per group. Examples >>> ButtonSettings (). button_mode 'all'

ChordQualities , ... ) >>> ChordQualities (). settings_signature () ''

title: alto.exercises.base
text: ChoiceExercise.generate def generate ( rng : random . Random ) -> Question [Source] Generate the musical task and apply the selected button count. Parameters rng ( random.Random ): Source for the exercise and the distractor sample. Returns Question : A question with its answer buttons ready for practice. Examples >>> from alto.exercises.library import ( ... ChordQualities , ... ) >>> len ( ... ChordQualities () ... . generate ( random . Random ( 0 )) ... . choices ... ) 5

title: alto.exercises.base
text: ChoiceExercise.limit_buttons def limit_buttons ( question : Question , * , rng : random . Random , ) -> Question [Source] Limit each answer group while keeping all the buttons needed to complete the question. Parameters question ( Question ): The task and its eligible answer choices. rng ( random.Random ): Source for sampling distractors. Returns Question : The question with its chosen layout. Examples A note and octave question keeps the correct name and octave in their respective groups.

title: alto.exercises.base
text: ChoiceExercise.make_question @ abstractmethod def make_question ( rng : random . Random ) -> Question [Source] Generate the task and eligible answer choices before the button limit is applied. Parameters rng ( random.Random ): The exercise’s random source. Returns Question : The musical task. Examples Note Identification supplies the note names appropriate to the active clef and key settings.

title: alto.exercises.base
text: register def register () -> type [ Exercise ] [Source] Add an exercise to REGISTRY , next to the others of its category. The categories come in the order they first appear, so the home screen and the exercise list can show each category once, with all its exercises under it. Used as a class decorator. Parameters cls ( type of Exercise ): The exercise class. Returns type of Exercise : The same class, so the decorator can be applied to a class definition. Examples >>> @ register ... class Demo ( Exercise ): ... name = "Demo" ... category = ( ... "A category no other exercise has" ... ) ... ... def generate ( self , rng ): ... return Question ( ... "?" , choices = [ "A" ], answer = "A" ... ) >>> REGISTRY [ - 1 ] is Demo True >>> REGISTRY . remove ( Demo )

title: alto.exercises.base
text: pick_distractors def pick_distractors ( correct : str , * , pool : list [ str ], n : int , rng : random . Random , ) -> list [ str ] [Source] Choose wrong answers to offer alongside the right one, and shuffle them all. Parameters correct ( str ): The right answer. It is always in the result. pool ( list of str ): Where the wrong answers come from; repeats and the right answer are ignored. Keyword-only. n ( int ): How many wrong answers to include (fewer if the pool has fewer). Keyword-only. rng ( random.Random ): The random number generator used to choose and shuffle. Keyword-only. Returns list of str : The right answer and up to n others, in a random order. Examples >>> choices_ = pick_distractors ( ... "C" , ... pool = [ "C" , "D" , "E" , "F" ], ... n = 2 , ... rng = random . Random ( 0 ), ... ) >>> len ( choices_ ), "C" in choices_ (3, True)

title: alto.exercises.library
text: alto.exercises.library The exercises: note names, intervals, key signatures, scales, chords, arpeggios, keyboard keys and note construction. Each class makes one kind of Question and registers itself with @register , so importing this module is what adds the exercises to the home screen. Examples >>> from alto.exercises import REGISTRY >>> [ cls . name for cls in REGISTRY ][: 3 ] ['Note Identification', 'Keyboard Note Identification', 'Note Construction']

Parameters accidentals ( bool, default False ): Ask notes with explicit sharps, flats and naturals, whatever the settings say.
