Random ( 14 ) ... ) >>> # noinspection PyUnresolvedReferences >>> q . keyboard_range [ ... 0 ... ] <= q . keyboard . midi <= q . keyboard_range [ 1 ] True

title: alto.exercises.library
text: NoteConstruction class NoteConstruction ( Exercise ) [Source] Place a named note on the staff. Examples >>> q = NoteConstruction (). generate ( ... random . Random ( 15 ) ... ) >>> q . construct is not None and q . prompt . startswith ( ... "Place " ... ) True

title: alto.exercises.library
text: NoteConstruction.card_prompt def card_prompt ( question : Question ) -> str [Source] Say which note to place, whichever way the on-screen prompt words it. Parameters question ( Question ): The question on the card. Returns str : The instruction. Examples >>> NoteConstruction (). card_prompt ( ... Question ( ... "Place F♯4 on the staff." , ... choices = [], ... answer = "F♯4" , ... ) ... ) 'Place F♯4 on the staff.' >>> NoteConstruction (). card_prompt ( ... Question ( "" , choices = [], answer = "B♭3" ) ... ) 'Place B♭3 on the staff.'

title: alto.exercises.library
text: NoteConstruction.settings_signature def settings_signature () -> str [Source] Return what identifies the settings that shape these questions. Returns str : The clefs, accidentals and key signature settings, and the naming in force. Examples >>> NoteConstruction (). settings_signature (). startswith ( ... "[" ... ) True

title: alto.exercises.library
text: NoteConstruction.instructions def instructions () -> str [Source] Return the help text for the exercise. Returns str : Simple HTML, with paragraphs added for the key signature and accidental settings that are on. Examples >>> "Click the staff" in NoteConstruction (). instructions () True

title: alto.exercises.library
text: NoteConstruction.generate def generate ( rng : random . Random ) -> Question [Source] Make a note name to be placed on the staff. Parameters rng ( random.Random ): The random number generator. Returns Question : A prompt such as ‘Place F♯4 on the staff.’; the answer is the note’s name, and construct is the note to place. Examples >>> q = NoteConstruction (). generate ( ... random . Random ( 16 ) ... ) >>> q . answer in q . prompt True

title: alto.exercises.library
text: NoteConstruction.card_count def card_count () -> int [Source] Count distinct construction cards without rendering them. Returns int : Number of eligible written placements under the current settings. Examples >>> NoteConstruction (). card_count () > 0 True

title: alto.exercises.library
text: NoteConstruction.daily_candidates def daily_candidates ( rng : random . Random ) -> Iterator [ Question ] [Source] Visit all eligible placements in a randomized order. Parameters rng ( random.Random ): Source for the order of the signatures and placements. Yields Question : One playable placement for each combination. Examples >>> next ( ... NoteConstruction (). daily_candidates ( ... random . Random ( 5 ) ... ) ... ). construct is not None True

title: alto.exercises.library
text: NoteConstruction.review_question def review_question ( question : Question , * , same_settings : bool , ) -> Question | None [Source] Determine whether an introduced placement belongs to the current construction catalog. Parameters question ( Question ): Stored construction card. same_settings ( bool ): Whether its original settings are still active. Returns Question or None : The playable card if its placement and prompt remain eligible. Examples >>> ex = NoteConstruction () >>> q = ex . generate ( random . Random ( 3 )) >>> ex . review_question ( ... q , same_settings = True ... ) == q True

title: alto.exercises.library
text: ClefBasics class ClefBasics ( ChoiceExercise ) [Source] Put a named clef on a blank staff: choose the G, C or F symbol and put it on the line that makes the clef asked for. Examples >>> q = ClefBasics (). generate ( random . Random ( 1 )) >>> ( ... q . answer == q . place_clef ... and q . place_clef in settings . CLEF_BASICS_CLEFS ... ) True

title: alto.exercises.library
text: ClefBasics.settings_signature def settings_signature () -> str [Source] Use button preferences for reviews only when the learner answers with buttons. Returns str : The signature for the active question type. Examples Changing Button count leaves staff-placement reviews available.

title: alto.exercises.library
text: ClefBasics.practice_signature def practice_signature () -> str [Source] Return what identifies the settings that shape these questions. Returns str : The clefs asked for. Examples >>> ClefBasics (). settings_signature (). startswith ( ... "[" ... ) True

title: alto.exercises.library
text: ClefBasics.instructions def instructions () -> str [Source] Return the help text for the exercise, for the kind of question that is being asked. Returns str : Simple HTML. Examples >>> "Clef Basics" in ClefBasics (). instructions () True

title: alto.exercises.library
text: ClefBasics.make_question def make_question ( rng : random . Random ) -> Question [Source] Name a clef to place, or draw a clef to name. Parameters rng ( random.Random ): The random number generator. Returns Question : For construction, a blank staff and the name of the clef, which is the question written under the staff. For identification, a staff with the clef drawn on it, and a button for each clef that can be asked for. Examples >>> q = ClefBasics (). generate ( random . Random ( 3 )) >>> q . prompt . startswith ( ... "Place the " ... ) and q . caption == q . prompt True >>> settings . clef_basics . question_type = ( ... "identification" ... ) >>> q = ClefBasics (). generate ( random . Random ( 3 )) >>> ( ... q . answer in q . choices , ... q . place_clef , ... q . caption , ... ) (True, '', 'Which clef is this?') >>> settings . clef_basics . question_type = ( ... "construction" ... )

title: alto.exercises.library
text: NotationIdentification class NotationIdentification ( ChoiceExercise ) [Source] Identify the highlighted part of a written phrase. Examples >>> q = NotationIdentification (). generate ( ... random . Random ( 2 ) ... ) >>> bool ( ... q . staff or q . notation_excerpt ... ) and q . answer in q . choices True

title: alto.exercises.library
text: NotationIdentification.settings_signature def settings_signature () -> str [Source] Use button preferences for reviews only when the learner answers with buttons. Returns str : The signature for the active question type. Examples Changing Button count leaves staff-placement reviews available.

title: alto.exercises.library
text: NotationIdentification.practice_signature def practice_signature () -> str [Source] Identify the terms eligible for review. Returns str : The selected terms, or the original empty signature when all terms are enabled. Examples >>> NotationIdentification (). settings_signature () ''

title: alto.exercises.library
text: NotationIdentification.instructions def instructions () -> str [Source] Explain how to answer the notation question. Returns str : Help for mouse and keyboard users. Examples >>> "number" in NotationIdentification (). instructions () True

title: alto.exercises.library
text: NotationIdentification.refresh def refresh ( question : Question ) -> Question [Source] Replace unchecked distractors in older practice questions before replay. Parameters question ( Question ): Stored question matching the current settings signature. Returns Question : The original notation with eligible answer buttons. Examples >>> ex = NotationIdentification () >>> q = ex . generate ( random . Random ( 1 )) >>> ex . refresh ( q ) == q True

title: alto.exercises.library
text: NotationIdentification.make_question def make_question ( rng : random . Random ) -> Question [Source] Choose a phrase and a single visible feature to highlight. Parameters rng ( random.Random ): Source for the phrase, feature, and its position. Returns Question : A short phrase with the selected marking and checked answer choices. Examples >>> q = NotationIdentification (). generate ( ... random . Random ( 0 ) ... ) >>> q . notation_target [ 0 ] == q . answer True

title: alto.exercises.library
text: NotationIdentification.card_groups def card_groups () -> dict [ str , str ] [Source] Group the active question type’s playable examples by the symbol being practiced. Returns dict of str to str : Map from each eligible example’s item key to its selected term. Examples >>> bool ( NotationIdentification (). card_groups ()) True

title: alto.exercises.library
text: NotationIdentification.daily_candidates def daily_candidates ( rng : random . Random ) -> Iterator [ Question ] [Source] Choose one example for each selected notation term. Parameters rng ( random.Random ): Randomizes term order, examples and distractors. Yields Question : A distinct playable card with the current answer controls. Examples >>> next ( ... NotationIdentification (). daily_candidates ( ... random . Random ( 4 ) ... ) ... ). answer in settings . notation . terms True

title: alto.exercises.library
text: NotationIdentification.review_question def review_question ( question : Question , * , same_settings : bool , ) -> Question | None [Source] Recover an eligible saved example under the current term and button selections. Parameters question ( Question ): Saved question. same_settings ( bool ): Whether the presentation settings still match. Returns Question or None : The current presentation of the card, or None if its term or example is outside the catalog. Examples >>> ex = NotationIdentification () >>> q = ex . generate ( random . Random ( 4 )) >>> ex . review_question ( ... q , same_settings = True ... ) == q True

title: alto.exercises.library
text: RythmicEquations class RythmicEquations ( ChoiceExercise ) [Source] Complete arithmetic equations with written note values. Examples >>> q = RythmicEquations (). generate ( ... random . Random ( 2 ) ... ) >>> "_" in q . prompt and q . answer in q . choices True

title: alto.exercises.library
text: RythmicEquations.instructions def instructions () -> str [Source] Explain how to complete the equation with a button or its shortcut. Returns str : Instructions for the exercise. Examples >>> "keys" in RythmicEquations (). instructions () True

title: alto.exercises.library
text: RythmicEquations.card_prompt def card_prompt ( question : Question ) -> str [Source] Ask for the missing symbol or number on an exported card. Parameters question ( Question ): The equation on the card. Returns str : The instruction shown above the equation. Examples >>> RythmicEquations (). card_prompt ( ... Question ( "" , choices = [], answer = "" ) ... ) 'Which note or rest balances the equation?'

title: alto.exercises.library
text: RythmicEquations.practice_signature def practice_signature () -> str [Source] Keep review questions tied to the options that generated them. Returns str : The selected operators and symbols, or an empty string for the original defaults. Examples >>> RythmicEquations (). practice_signature () ''

title: alto.exercises.library
text: RythmicEquations.make_question def make_question ( rng : random . Random ) -> Question [Source] Write a rhythm equation and hide a symbol or number. Parameters rng ( random.Random ): Chooses the note value, operation, and blank position. Returns Question : The equation and the note values available as answers. Examples >>> RythmicEquations (). make_question ( ... random . Random ( 0 ) ... ). prompt . count ( "_" ) 1

title: alto.exercises.packs
text: alto.exercises.packs Load third-party instrument packs from ZIP archives and authoring folders.

title: alto.exercises.packs
text: PackExercise class PackExercise ( ChoiceExercise ) [Source] A finite set of illustrated multiple-choice cards declared by an instrument pack. Examples The viola pack contributes one practice card for every eligible string and pitch.

title: alto.exercises.packs
text: PackExercise.options @ classmethod def options () -> settings . PackExerciseSettings [Source] Return the learner’s options for this exercise, creating the defaults the first time. Returns PackExerciseSettings : The shared, editable options, kept under the exercise’s class name. Examples >>> class Demo ( PackExercise ): ... span = ( 21 , 30 ) ... range_clef = "alto" >>> ( ... Demo . options (). range_for ( "alto" ), ... Demo . options (). sound , ... ) ((21, 30), None) >>> _ = settings . pack_exercises . pop ( "Demo" )

title: alto.exercises.packs
text: PackExercise.is_keyboard @ property def is_keyboard () -> bool [Source] Report whether this is a keyboard interval exercise. Returns bool : True when the pack declared the exercise with type keyboard-intervals . Examples >>> class Demo ( PackExercise ): ... spec = { "type" : "keyboard-intervals" } >>> Demo (). is_keyboard True

title: alto.exercises.packs
text: PackExercise.chosen_keys @ classmethod def chosen_keys () -> tuple [ int , int ] [Source] Find the lowest and highest key a keyboard exercise asks. Returns tuple of int : The learner’s range if the plugin offers one and it fits the exercise, otherwise the plugin’s default range. Examples >>> class Demo ( PackExercise ): ... key_span , key_default = ( ... ( 28 , 89 ), ... ( 48 , 72 ), ... ) >>> Demo . chosen_keys () (48, 72)

title: alto.exercises.packs
text: PackExercise.chosen_span @ classmethod def chosen_span () -> tuple [ str , str ] [Source] Name the lowest and highest key a keyboard exercise asks, for drawing the keyboards over that range. Returns tuple of str : The two keys, such as ("C3", "C5") . Examples >>> class Demo ( PackExercise ): ... key_span , key_default = ( ... ( 28 , 89 ), ... ( 48 , 72 ), ... ) >>> Demo . chosen_span () ('C3', 'C5')

title: alto.exercises.packs
text: PackExercise.chosen_intervals @ classmethod def chosen_intervals () -> tuple [ str , ...] [Source] Find the intervals a keyboard exercise asks. Returns tuple of str : The learner’s choice among the intervals the plugin lists, or all of them if the plugin offers no choice or the choice leaves none. Examples >>> class Demo ( PackExercise ): ... interval_names = ( "m2" , "M2" , "m3" ) >>> Demo . chosen_intervals () ('m2', 'M2', 'm3')

title: alto.exercises.packs
text: PackExercise.chosen_manuals @ classmethod def chosen_manuals () -> tuple [ str , ...] [Source] Find the keyboards a keyboard exercise puts its highlighted keys on. Returns tuple of str : The learner’s choice among the keyboards the exercise uses, or all of them if the plugin offers no choice or the choice leaves none. Examples >>> class Demo ( PackExercise ): ... manual_names = ( ... "Upper manual" , ... "Lower manual" , ... ) >>> Demo . chosen_manuals () ('Upper manual', 'Lower manual')

title: alto.exercises.packs
text: PackExercise.active_cards def active_cards () -> tuple [ Question , ...] [Source] Build the cards for the learner’s settings: the sharps and flats, the octave, and the range they chose. Returns tuple of Question : The cards, or all of the pack’s cards for an exercise with no settings, or when the range leaves none. Examples An exercise whose pack declares no settings always asks every card.

title: alto.exercises.packs
text: PackExercise.sound_instrument def sound_instrument ( key : str | None ) -> str | None [Source] Play the pack’s own sound unless the pack offers the choice and the learner chose another instrument. Parameters key ( str or None ): The key of the pack’s instrument. Returns str or None : The learner’s chosen instrument if there is one and it is installed, otherwise the pack’s own. Examples An exercise with no sound setting always plays the pack's instrument.

title: alto.exercises.packs
text: PackExercise.sound_options @ classmethod def sound_options () -> list [ tuple [ str , list [ tuple [ str , str ]]]] [Source] List the instruments a learner can choose to sound in this exercise, in the order they are offered. The instruments that came with the plugin come first, then other instruments of the same kind (other harpsichords for a harpsichord), then every other installed instrument, whatever its kind. An instrument with no recordings on disk is left out. Returns list of tuple of str and list of tuple of str and str : Each group’s heading and its instruments as (key, label), with empty groups left out. Examples >>> from alto.audio import INSTRUMENTS >>> class Demo ( PackExercise ): ... pack_name = "Demo pack" ... instruments = {} >>> [ ... heading ... for heading , _ in Demo . sound_options () ... ] ['Other instruments']

title: alto.exercises.packs
text: PackExercise.practice_signature def practice_signature () -> str [Source] Identify the pack settings used to generate this catalog. Returns str : Signature shared by cards from this exercise revision. Examples Adding an eligible pitch changes the signature, and so does asking sharps and flats or the octave.

title: alto.exercises.packs
text: PackExercise.refresh def refresh ( question : Question ) -> Question [Source] Restore the instrument reference on cards saved by the single-instrument prototype. Parameters question ( Question ): Saved question. Returns Question : Card with its pack-qualified instrument reference. Examples An existing D-string card keeps its original position when a pack is upgraded.

title: alto.exercises.packs
text: PackExercise.make_question def make_question ( rng : random . Random ) -> Question [Source] Pick one of the illustrated questions in the pack. Parameters rng ( random.Random ): Source of the question choice. Returns Question : The marked position, prompt, and answer choices. Examples An open D4 on a viola asks for D.

title: alto.exercises.packs
text: PackExercise.daily_candidates def daily_candidates ( rng : random . Random ) -> Iterator [ Question ] [Source] Visit each question in the pack once in shuffled order. Parameters rng ( random.Random ): Source of the order and button selection. Yields Question : Each distinct marked position. Examples Open G and G on the C string yield separate cards.

title: alto.exercises.packs
text: PackExercise.card_count def card_count () -> int [Source] Count the distinct questions in the exercise. Returns int : Number of cards in this exercise. Examples The viola example offers twenty positions.

title: alto.exercises.packs
text: read_controls def read_controls ( value : object , * , where : str , kinds : tuple [ str , ...] = CONTROL_KINDS , ) -> dict [ str , str | bool ] [Source] Validate the settings a pack offers for one of its exercises. Parameters value ( object ): The exercise’s settings entry: an object that may hold sound (the label of a switch that plays the pack’s own sound), range (a clef to draw a range selector on, or true for the keys of a keyboard exercise), accidentals and octave (true for a switch), intervals (true for a choice of intervals), manuals (true for a choice of keyboards), or None. where ( str ): The exercise id, for diagnostics. Keyword-only. kinds ( tuple of str, default CONTROL_KINDS ): The settings this kind of exercise can have. Keyword-only. Returns dict of str to str or bool : The declared settings by kind; empty when the pack declares none. Raises ValueError : If the entry has an unknown kind or a value of the wrong type. Examples >>> read_controls ( ... { "range" : "alto" , "octave" : True }, ... where = "pack.v.notes" , ... ) {'range': 'alto', 'octave': True} >>> read_controls ( ... { "range" : True , "intervals" : True }, ... where = "pack.v.keys" , ... kinds = KEYBOARD_CONTROL_KINDS , ... ) {'range': True, 'intervals': True} >>> read_controls ( None , where = "pack.v.notes" ) {}

title: alto.exercises.packs
text: read_pack def read_pack ( path : Path ) -> list [ type [ PackExercise ]] [Source] Read and validate every exercise before making any of them available. Parameters path ( Path ): A pack.json file or a ZIP containing it at the root. Returns list of type : Exercise classes with stable identifiers. Raises ValueError : If the file or one of its exercises has an invalid format. Examples The viola example contributes note identification and instrument anatomy exercises.

title: alto.exercises.packs
text: pack_manifests def pack_manifests ( folder : Path ) -> tuple [ list [ Path ], list [ str ]] [Source] Find each installed ZIP or folder manifest, including packs that failed validation. Parameters folder ( Path ): The plugins directory. Returns tuple of list of Path and list of str : ZIP files and pack.json files in discovery order, and any discovery errors. Examples An author can install either viola.zip or viola/pack.json.

title: alto.exercises.packs
text: installed_pack_info def installed_pack_info ( path : Path ) -> dict [Source] Read a pack’s manifest for display or duplicate detection without loading its media. Parameters path ( Path ): An installed ZIP or an editable pack.json. Returns dict : The manifest, or an empty dictionary for an invalid manifest or archive. Examples A damaged pack can still be listed for removal by filename.

title: alto.exercises.packs
text: InstalledPlugin InstalledPlugin ( title : str , path : Path , manifest : Path , snapshot : stat_result , ) [Source] One pack in the plugins folder, as listed for removal. Attributes title ( str ): The pack’s name, or its file name without the .zip extension when the manifest cannot be read. path ( Path ): The ZIP file or editable pack folder that removal moves to the trash. manifest ( Path ): The ZIP or the folder’s pack.json. snapshot ( stat_result ): The state of path when it was listed, used to notice a change before removal. Examples >>> from pathlib import Path >>> import os >>> plugin = InstalledPlugin ( ... title = "Viola" , ... path = Path ( "viola.zip" ), ... manifest = Path ( "viola.zip" ), ... snapshot = os . stat ( "." ), ... ) >>> plugin . title 'Viola'

title: alto.exercises.packs
text: installed_plugins def installed_plugins ( folder : Path ) -> tuple [ list [ InstalledPlugin ], list [ str ]] [Source] List the packs in the plugins folder, including damaged ones, so each can be removed. Parameters folder ( Path ): The plugins directory. Returns tuple of list of InstalledPlugin and list of str : The packs in discovery order, and any discovery errors. Examples >>> from pathlib import Path >>> installed_plugins ( ... Path ( "no-such-plugins-folder" ) ... ) ([], [])

title: alto.exercises.packs
text: install_pack def install_pack ( source : Path , * , folder : Path , expected_id : str | None = None , replacing : InstalledPlugin | None = None , ) -> str [Source] Validate a copy of the selected ZIP and install it for the next startup. Parameters source ( Path ): The downloaded instrument pack ZIP. folder ( Path ): The plugins directory used at startup. expected_id ( str or None ): The manifest ID assigned to a registered download. replacing ( InstalledPlugin or None ): The previously selected ZIP to replace after validation. Returns str : The installed pack’s display name. Raises ValueError : If the ZIP is invalid or conflicts with an existing installation. OSError : If the installation cannot be read or written. Examples Installing a downloaded viola.zip adds both of its exercises on the next launch.

title: alto.exercises.packs
text: load_packs def load_packs ( folder : Path ) -> list [ str ] [Source] Register valid packs and return readable errors for any packs that were skipped. Parameters folder ( Path ): The plugins folder containing pack ZIPs or editable pack folders. Returns list of str : File names and reasons for packs that could not be loaded. Examples A missing plugins folder yields an empty list.

title: alto.exercises.rhythm_equations
text: alto.exercises.rhythm_equations Build balanced rhythm equations with exact operator counts. Examples An equation with one operation per side can compare a sum to a product.

title: alto.exercises.rhythm_equations
text: equation_tokens def equation_tokens ( rng : random . Random , * , ordinary : dict [ float , list [ str ]], grouped : tuple [ dict [ float , list [ str ]], ...], left : int , right : int , operators : tuple [ str , ...], right_operators : tuple [ str , ...] | None = None , parentheses : bool = True , ) -> list [ str ] [Source] Choose a shared total, then build both sides backwards from it. Parameters rng ( random.Random ): Chooses the grouping, total, signs and symbols. ordinary ( dict ): Single note and rest names by duration in sixteenth notes. grouped ( tuple of dict ): Separate tables of tied and beamed names by duration. left ( int ): Operator count before the equals sign. right ( int ): Operator count after the equals sign. operators ( tuple of str ): Signs allowed on the left and, by default, on the right. right_operators ( tuple of str or None ): Separate selection of signs for the right side. parentheses ( bool ): Whether an expression can group operations with parentheses. Returns list of str : Equation tokens, or an empty list if no equation fits. Examples >>> equation_tokens ( random . Random ( 0 ), ordinary = { 4 : [ "q" ]}, ... grouped = (), left = 1 , right = 1 , operators = ( "+" ,)) ['q', '+', 'q', '=', 'q', '+', 'q']

title: alto.exercises.rhythm_equations
text: counted_operands def counted_operands ( ordinary : dict [ float , list [ str ]]) -> dict [ float , list [ str ]] [Source] Supply counts for totals without a selected single symbol. Parameters ordinary ( dict ): Selected symbols by duration. Returns dict : Count and unit tokens indexed by their combined duration. Examples >>> counted_operands ({ 4 : [ "quarter" ]})[ 12 ] ['3:quarter']

title: alto.exercises.rhythm_equations
text: number_question def number_question ( rng : random . Random , * , tokens : list [ str ], ordinary : dict [ float , list [ str ]], ) -> Question [Source] Hide a numeric factor, or count a duration in an explicit unit. Parameters rng ( random.Random ): Selects the blank and counting unit. tokens ( list of str ): Balanced equation. Each factor scales the preceding subtotal, with any additive prefix enclosed in parentheses. ordinary ( dict ): Selected note and rest symbols by duration. Returns Question : A numeric answer with a unit caption when counting durations. Examples >>> number_question ( random . Random ( 0 ), ... tokens = [ "half" , "÷" , "2" , "=" , "quarter" ], ... ordinary = { 4 : [ "quarter" ], 8 : [ "half" ]}). answer '2'

title: alto.instrument_info
text: alto.instrument_info What is known about each instrument’s recordings, for the summary shown in the instrument settings. The facts here come from the sources’ own pages (the University of Iowa Musical Instrument Samples, and the Salamander Grand Piano). What is on disk (how many notes, their range, their size) is worked out when the page is shown, not stored here. Pure Python, no Qt. Examples >>> coverage ( range ( 60 , 73 )). describe () '13 notes, C4 to C5, every semitone'

title: alto.instrument_info
text: InstrumentInfo InstrumentInfo ( summary : str , * , source : str , source_url : str , performer : str = '' , recorded : str = '' , includes : str = '' , terms : str = IOWA_TERMS , note : str = '' , ) [Source] The facts about where an instrument’s recordings came from. Attributes summary ( str ): One sentence on what the sound is. source ( str ): Who made the recordings. Keyword-only. source_url ( str ): Where the source describes them. Keyword-only. performer ( str, default ““ ): Who played. Keyword-only. recorded ( str, default ““ ): When and where it was recorded. Keyword-only. includes ( str, default ““ ): The articulation and dynamic that were used. Keyword-only. terms ( str ): The terms the recordings may be used under. Keyword-only. note ( str, default ““ ): Anything a user should know about how Alto prepared the recordings. Keyword-only. Examples >>> info = InstrumentInfo ( ... "A flute." , ... source = IOWA , ... source_url = "https://example.org/flute" , ... ) >>> info . terms == IOWA_TERMS True

title: alto.instrument_info
text: Coverage Coverage ( count : int , * , lowest : int | None = None , highest : int | None = None , gaps : int = 0 , ) [Source] Which notes an instrument has recordings for. Attributes count ( int ): How many notes have a recording. lowest ( int or None ): The lowest recorded note, as a MIDI number. Keyword-only. highest ( int or None ): The highest recorded note, as a MIDI number. Keyword-only. gaps ( int, default 0 ): How many semitones inside the range have no recording. Keyword-only. Examples >>> Coverage ( 0 ). describe () 'None installed'

title: alto.instrument_info
text: Coverage.installed @ property def installed () -> bool [Source] Report whether any recordings are on disk. Returns bool : True if at least one note has a recording. Examples >>> ( ... Coverage ( 0 ). installed , ... coverage ([ 60 ]). installed , ... ) (False, True)

title: alto.instrument_info
text: Coverage.describe def describe () -> str [Source] Describe the coverage in a sentence for the instrument settings. Returns str : The number of notes, the range, and how complete it is (the spacing, when the notes are well apart). Missing notes are shifted from a neighbor. Examples >>> coverage ( range ( 60 , 73 )). describe () '13 notes, C4 to C5, every semitone' >>> coverage ([ 60 , 62 , 64 , 65 ]). describe () '4 notes, C4 to F4, almost every semitone. The few missing notes are shifted from a neighbor.' >>> coverage ( range ( 48 , 73 , 2 )). describe () '13 notes, C3 to C5, about every second semitone. The other notes are shifted from a neighbor.' >>> coverage ( range ( 21 , 109 , 3 )). describe () '30 notes, A0 to C8, about every third semitone. The other notes are shifted from a neighbor.'

title: alto.instrument_info
text: coverage def coverage ( midis : Iterable [ int ]) -> Coverage [Source] Summarize the notes that have a recording. Parameters midis ( iterable of int ): The MIDI numbers of the recorded notes, in any order and with repeats allowed. Returns Coverage : The count, the range and the number of gaps. Examples >>> coverage ([ 64 , 60 , 62 ]) Coverage(count=3, lowest=60, highest=64, gaps=2)

title: alto.instrument_packs
text: alto.instrument_packs Media and fingerboard geometry supplied by third-party instrument packs.

title: alto.instrument_packs
text: PackString PackString ( pitch : str , nut : Point , bridge : Point , ) [Source] One open pitch with its nut and bridge locations in the original image pixels.

title: alto.instrument_packs
text: PackString.point def point ( half_steps : int ) -> Point [Source] Locate the pitch along the photographed string. Returns tuple of float : Image coordinates measured from the top left.

title: alto.instrument_packs
text: AnswerAnimation AnswerAnimation ( file : Path , anchor : str , ) [Source] An author-supplied animated overlay and its alignment on the instrument.

title: alto.instrument_packs
text: PackView PackView ( name : str , image : Path , size : tuple [ int , int ], ) [Source] Another picture of an instrument, such as its back, with its own pixel size.

title: alto.instrument_packs
text: PackKeyboard PackKeyboard ( name : str , lowest : str , highest : str , ) [Source] One keyboard of an instrument, drawn by Alto from the range of keys the plugin gives it. Attributes name ( str ): What the plugin calls this keyboard, such as “Lower manual”. lowest ( str ): The pitch of the lowest key, a natural such as “E1”. highest ( str ): The pitch of the highest key, a natural such as “F6”. Examples >>> keys = PackKeyboard ( "Manual" , "C4" , "E4" ) >>> keys . naturals 3 >>> keys . has ( "C#4" ), keys . has ( "E#4" ) (True, False)

title: alto.instrument_packs
text: PackKeyboard.naturals @ property def naturals () -> int [Source] Count the natural keys. Returns int : The number of natural keys from the lowest to the highest, both included. Examples >>> PackKeyboard ( "M" , "C4" , "C5" ). naturals 8

title: alto.instrument_packs
text: PackKeyboard.has def has ( name : str ) -> bool [Source] Report whether a pitch is a key on this keyboard. Parameters name ( str ): A pitch such as “F#3”. Returns bool : True when the keyboard has that key, natural or sharp. Examples >>> board = PackKeyboard ( "M" , "C4" , "E4" ) >>> ( ... board . has ( "C#4" ), ... board . has ( "E#4" ), ... board . has ( "F4" ), ... board . has ( "Db4" ), ... ) (True, False, False, False)

title: alto.instrument_packs
text: PackKeyboardStyle PackKeyboardStyle ( colors : tuple [ tuple [ str , str | tuple [ str , str ]], ...] = (), numbers : tuple [ tuple [ str , float ], ...] = (), ) [Source] How a plugin’s keyboards look: the colors of the keys and case, and the proportions of the keys. Attributes colors ( tuple of tuple of str and str or tuple of str ): Each color field the plugin set, with its value as #rrggbb . A natural or sharp key has two, for its top and bottom. numbers ( tuple of tuple of str and float ): Each numeric field the plugin set, with its value. Examples >>> style = PackKeyboardStyle ( ... (( "cap" , "#eee3c8" ),), ... (( "length" , 4.5 ),), ... ) >>> dict ( style . colors ), dict ( style . numbers ) ({'cap': '#eee3c8'}, {'length': 4.5})

title: alto.instrument_packs
text: read_keyboard_style def read_keyboard_style ( value : object , * , where : str , ) -> PackKeyboardStyle | None [Source] Validate the optional look of an instrument’s keyboards. Parameters value ( object ): The instrument’s keyboard_style entry, an object, or None. where ( str ): The instrument’s qualified key, used in messages. Keyword-only. Returns PackKeyboardStyle or None : The style, or None to draw the keyboards in the learner’s own keyboard style. Raises ValueError : If a field is unknown, or a color or number is invalid. Examples >>> read_keyboard_style ( ... None , where = "pack.v.va" ... ) is None True >>> # noinspection PyUnresolvedReferences >>> read_keyboard_style ( ... { ... "cap" : "#eee3c8" , ... "white" : [ "#2a211c" , "#120d0a" ], ... }, ... where = "pack.v.va" , ... ). colors [ 1 ] ('white', ('#2a211c', '#120d0a'))

title: alto.instrument_packs
text: PackInstrument PackInstrument ( key : str , image : Path , size : tuple [ int , int ], strings : tuple [ PackString , ...], sound : Instrument | None , correct_answer_animation : AnswerAnimation | None = None , sound_info : InstrumentInfo | None = None , positions : tuple [ tuple [ int , str ], ...] = (), views : tuple [ PackView , ...] = (), keyboards : tuple [ PackKeyboard , ...] = (), keyboard_style : PackKeyboardStyle | None = None , ) [Source] A pack-qualified identity and the resources shared by its exercises.

title: alto.instrument_packs
text: PackInstrument.keyboard def keyboard ( name : str ) -> PackKeyboard | None [Source] Find one of the instrument’s keyboards by name. Parameters name ( str ): The keyboard’s name as the plugin wrote it. Returns PackKeyboard or None : The keyboard, or None if the instrument has no keyboard with that name. Examples >>> keys = PackKeyboard ( "Manual" , "C4" , "E4" ) >>> board = PackInstrument ( ... "pack.x.y" , ... Path ( "a.png" ), ... ( 10 , 20 ), ... (), ... None , ... keyboards = ( keys ,), ... ) >>> ( ... board . keyboard ( "Manual" ) is keys , ... board . keyboard ( "Pedals" ), ... ) (True, None)

title: alto.instrument_packs
text: PackInstrument.picture def picture ( view : str = '' ) -> tuple [ Path , tuple [ int , int ]] | None [Source] Find the picture for a view: the instrument’s main picture for an empty name, otherwise the named extra picture. Parameters view ( str, default ““ ): The view’s name, or an empty string for the main picture. Returns tuple of Path and tuple of int, or None : The image file and its size in pixels, or None if the instrument has no such view. Examples >>> back = PackView ( ... "back" , Path ( "back.png" ), ( 30 , 40 ) ... ) >>> board = PackInstrument ( ... "pack.x.y" , ... Path ( "front.png" ), ... ( 10 , 20 ), ... (), ... None , ... views = ( back ,), ... ) >>> ( ... board . picture (), ... board . picture ( "back" ), ... board . picture ( "side" ), ... ) ((PosixPath('front.png'), (10, 20)), (PosixPath('back.png'), (30, 40)), None)

title: alto.instrument_packs
text: identifier def identifier ( value : object ) -> str [Source] Validate one component of a pack-qualified id. Returns str : The validated id. Raises ValueError : If the id includes an unsupported character.

title: alto.instrument_packs
text: pitch def pitch ( value : object ) -> Note [Source] Read a pitch spelled with an octave. Returns Note : The pitch used for playback and grading. Raises ValueError : If the pitch has an unsupported spelling.

title: alto.instrument_packs
text: PackFiles PackFiles ( manifest : Path , * , archive : ZipFile | None , ) [Source] Resolve only manifest-declared assets, from a folder or the root of a ZIP. Constructor Keep folder assets in place and give ZIP assets private, generated filenames. Raises ValueError : If the ZIP lacks a root manifest or repeats an entry name.

title: alto.instrument_packs
text: PackFiles.asset def asset ( name : object , * , extensions : tuple [ str , ...], ) -> Path [Source] Resolve a regular asset from this pack. Returns Path : A local file usable by the image and audio readers. Raises ValueError : If the path is missing, outside the pack, or has an unsupported type or size.

title: alto.instrument_packs
text: PackFiles.manifest def manifest () -> dict [Source] Read the API version and top-level pack object. Returns dict : Version two manifest. Raises ValueError : If the format is unsupported or the pack lacks a display name.

title: alto.instrument_packs
text: image_point def image_point ( value : object , * , width : int , height : int , ) -> Point [Source] Validate a marker or string endpoint against the image dimensions. Returns tuple of float : Coordinates in original image pixels. Raises ValueError : If either coordinate is missing or outside the picture.

title: alto.instrument_packs
text: read_sound_info def read_sound_info ( value : object , * , where : str , pack_name : str , ) -> InstrumentInfo | None [Source] Validate the optional facts a pack gives about where its recordings came from. Parameters value ( object ): The instrument’s sound_info entry, or None when it has none. where ( str ): The instrument’s qualified key, used in error messages. Keyword-only. pack_name ( str ): The pack’s display name, shown as the source when the entry gives none. Keyword-only. Returns InstrumentInfo or None : The facts for the Sound settings, or None when the instrument declared none. Raises ValueError : If an entry is not text, is too long, contains markup, or if the link is not an https address. Examples >>> info = read_sound_info ( ... { "summary" : "A viola." }, ... where = "pack.v.va" , ... pack_name = "Viola" , ... ) >>> info . source if info else None 'Viola' >>> read_sound_info ( ... None , ... where = "pack.v.va" , ... pack_name = "Viola" , ... ) is None True

title: alto.instrument_packs
text: plain_text def plain_text ( value : object , * , limit : int , ) -> bool [Source] Check that a manifest entry is nonblank plain text of a reasonable length. Parameters value ( object ): The manifest entry. limit ( int ): The most characters allowed. Keyword-only. Returns bool : True for a nonblank string with no markup characters and at most limit characters. Examples >>> ( ... plain_text ( "Name the note." , limit = 40 ), ... plain_text ( "Name" , limit = 40 ), ... plain_text ( None , limit = 40 ), ... ) (True, False, False)

title: alto.instrument_packs
text: read_text def read_text ( value : object , * , limit : int , what : str , where : str , ) -> str [Source] Check one piece of plain text and return it trimmed. Parameters value ( object ): The manifest entry. limit ( int ): The most characters allowed. Keyword-only. what ( str ): What the entry is, for the message. Keyword-only. where ( str ): Which lesson or step it belongs to, for the message. Keyword-only. Returns str : The entry without surrounding space. Raises ValueError : If it is not nonblank plain text within the limit. Examples >>> read_text ( ... " Hello " , ... limit = 10 , ... what = "title" , ... where = "lesson demo" , ... ) 'Hello'

title: alto.instrument_packs
text: read_focus def read_focus ( value : object , * , width : int , height : int , ) -> tuple [ float , float , float , float ] [Source] Validate a picture question’s region to show. Parameters value ( object ): The manifest entry: a list of left, top, width and height in picture pixels. width ( int ): The picture’s width in pixels. Keyword-only. height ( int ): The picture’s height in pixels. Keyword-only. Returns tuple of float : Left, top, width and height. Raises ValueError : If the entry is not four numbers describing a region of at least 40 pixels inside the picture. Examples >>> read_focus ( ... [ 0 , 10 , 200 , 100 ], width = 400 , height = 300 ... ) (0.0, 10.0, 200.0, 100.0)

title: alto.instrument_packs
text: read_marker_size def read_marker_size ( value : object ) -> float [Source] Validate a picture’s marker size. Parameters value ( object ): The manifest entry: a diameter in picture pixels, or 0 for the default size. Returns float : The diameter. Raises ValueError : If the entry is not 0 or a number from 6 to 200. Examples >>> read_marker_size ( 0 ), read_marker_size ( 24 ) (0.0, 24.0)

title: alto.instrument_packs
text: read_icon def read_icon ( files : PackFiles , * , name : object , ) -> str [Source] Read a plugin’s tile icon: a plain SVG of simple shapes, redrawn in the theme’s ink. Parameters files ( PackFiles ): The pack’s files. name ( object ): The manifest entry: a pack-relative path to an SVG file with the viewBox 0 0 24 24 . Keyword-only. Returns str : The shapes, with COLOR wherever the theme’s ink goes, ready for alto.ui.icons.svg_icon . Raises ValueError : If the file is missing, too large, not an SVG of the right box, or uses anything but simple shapes (no scripts, images, styles, or links). Examples The viola's icon is its own silhouette traced from the museum photograph.

title: alto.instrument_packs
text: read_picture_file def read_picture_file ( files : PackFiles , * , name : object , ) -> tuple [ Path , tuple [ int , int ]] [Source] Find and check a picture in the pack. Parameters files ( PackFiles ): The pack’s files. name ( object ): The manifest entry: a pack-relative path to a PNG, WebP, or JPEG picture. Keyword-only. Returns tuple of Path and tuple of int : The picture file and its width and height in pixels. Raises ValueError : If the picture is missing, unreadable, or larger than 16 megapixels.

title: alto.instrument_packs
text: read_views def read_views ( value : object , * , files : PackFiles , where : str , ) -> tuple [ PackView , ...] [Source] Validate the optional extra pictures of an instrument, such as a view of its back. Parameters value ( object ): The instrument’s views entry, an object from a view name to a pack-relative picture path, or None. files ( PackFiles ): The pack’s files. Keyword-only. where ( str ): The instrument’s qualified key, used in error messages. Keyword-only. Returns tuple of PackView : The views, in the order the manifest lists them. Empty when none were declared. Raises ValueError : If the entry is not a short object of valid names and readable pictures. Examples >>> # noinspection PyTypeChecker >>> read_views ( ... None , files = None , where = "pack.v.va" ... ) ()

title: alto.instrument_packs
text: read_keyboards def read_keyboards ( value : object , * , where : str , ) -> tuple [ PackKeyboard , ...] [Source] Validate the optional keyboards of an instrument, which Alto draws from their ranges. Parameters value ( object ): The instrument’s keyboards entry, a list of objects, or None. where ( str ): The instrument’s qualified key, used in messages. Keyword-only. Returns tuple of PackKeyboard : The keyboards in the order the manifest lists them, which is the order Alto draws them from top to bottom. Empty when none were declared. Raises ValueError : If the entry is not a short list of keyboards with distinct names and natural end keys. Examples >>> read_keyboards ( None , where = "pack.v.va" ) () >>> read_keyboards ( ... [ ... { ... "name" : "Manual" , ... "lowest" : "C4" , ... "highest" : "E4" , ... } ... ], ... where = "pack.v.va" , ... )[ 0 ]. naturals 3

title: alto.instrument_packs
text: read_positions def read_positions ( value : object , * , where : str , ) -> tuple [ tuple [ int , str ], ...] [Source] Validate the optional named positions along a string, which label the ruler beside the fingerboard. Parameters value ( object ): The instrument’s positions entry, a list of {"name": ..., "half_steps": ...} , or None when it has none. where ( str ): The instrument’s qualified key, used in error messages. Keyword-only. Returns tuple of (int, str) : Each position’s half steps above the open string and its name, in ascending order. Empty when none were declared. Raises ValueError : If the entry is not a short list of named, ascending positions with plain-text names. Examples >>> read_positions ( ... [ ... { "name" : "1st" , "half_steps" : 2 }, ... { "name" : "2nd" , "half_steps" : 3 }, ... ], ... where = "pack.v.va" , ... ) ((2, '1st'), (3, '2nd')) >>> read_positions ( None , where = "pack.v.va" ) ()

title: alto.instrument_packs
text: read_instrument def read_instrument ( row : object , * , pack : str , files : PackFiles , pack_name : str = '' , ) -> PackInstrument [Source] Validate one declared instrument against its own artwork and recordings. Returns PackInstrument : The calibrated instrument available to exercises in this pack. Raises ValueError : If a required field, string, image, or recording is invalid.

title: alto.learning.backup
text: alto.learning.backup Backup files: everything Alto keeps, in one file that can be read back into a clean install. Pure Python (no Qt). A backup is a zip file holding three things: the whole database (profiles, every answer, what is known about each question), the saved preferences (theme, fonts, instrument, every exercise’s settings, the last profile used) and a manifest that says which version of Alto made it and carries a checksum of each part. Reading a backup back checks the checksums and the database before anything is changed, so a damaged or foreign file is refused instead of half applied. Examples >>> import tempfile >>> from alto.learning.database import Database >>> db = Database () >>> ada = db . add_profile ( "Ada" ) >>> folder = Path ( tempfile . mkdtemp ()) >>> info = write_backup ( ... db , ... settings = { "ui/theme" : "dark" }, ... path = folder / "ada.altobackup" , ... ) >>> info . profiles , info . attempts (1, 0) >>> backup = read_backup ( ... folder / "ada.altobackup" ... ) >>> backup . settings {'ui/theme': 'dark'}

title: alto.learning.backup
text: BackupError class BackupError ( Exception ) [Source] A backup file could not be written or read: it is damaged, is not a backup, or was made by a newer Alto. Examples >>> str ( ... BackupError ( ... "This is not an Alto backup." ... ) ... ) 'This is not an Alto backup.'

title: alto.learning.backup
text: BackupInfo BackupInfo ( created : float , app_version : str , schema_version : int , profiles : int , attempts : int , ) [Source] What a backup says about itself. Attributes created ( float ): When it was made, as a timestamp. app_version ( str ): The version of Alto that made it. schema_version ( int ): The version of the database layout it holds. profiles ( int ): How many profiles it holds. attempts ( int ): How many answers it holds. Examples >>> BackupInfo ( ... 100.0 , ... app_version = "0.1.0" , ... schema_version = 1 , ... profiles = 2 , ... attempts = 30 , ... ). profiles 2

title: alto.learning.backup
text: Backup Backup ( info : BackupInfo , settings : dict [ str , object ], database : bytes , ) [Source] A backup that has been read and checked, ready to be applied. Attributes info ( BackupInfo ): What the backup says about itself. settings ( dict of str to object ): The saved preferences, by key. database ( bytes ): The database, as Database.snapshot returns it. Examples >>> Backup ( ... BackupInfo ( ... 1.0 , ... app_version = "0.1.0" , ... schema_version = 1 , ... profiles = 0 , ... attempts = 0 , ... ), ... settings = {}, ... database = b "" , ... ). settings {}

title: alto.learning.backup
text: app_version def app_version () -> str [Source] Return the version of Alto that is running. Returns str : The installed version, or “unknown” if Alto was not installed as a package. Examples >>> app_version (). count ( "." ) >= 1 True

title: alto.learning.backup
text: encode_value def encode_value ( value : object ) -> object [Source] Turn a saved preference into something JSON can hold. Text, numbers, true and false and lists of them are kept as they are. Bytes, which Qt settings can hold, become a small dictionary with the bytes in base64, so decode_value can bring them back. Parameters value ( object ): The value of a preference. Returns object : The same value, or its encoded form. Examples >>> ( ... encode_value ( "dark" ), ... encode_value ( 5 ), ... encode_value ([ "a" , "b" ]), ... ) ('dark', 5, ['a', 'b']) >>> encode_value ( b " \x00\x01 " ) {'bytes': 'AAE='}

title: alto.learning.backup
text: decode_value def decode_value ( value : object ) -> object [Source] Undo encode_value . Parameters value ( object ): A value read from a backup. Returns object : The preference’s value, with bytes restored. Examples >>> decode_value ({ "bytes" : "AAE=" }) b'\x00\x01' >>> decode_value ([ 1 , 2 ]) [1, 2]

title: alto.learning.backup
text: write_backup def write_backup ( db : Database , * , settings : Mapping [ str , object ], path : Path , now : float | None = None , ) -> BackupInfo [Source] Write a backup of the database and the saved preferences to a file. Parameters db ( Database ): The database to back up. It is not changed. settings ( mapping of str to object ): The saved preferences, by key. Keyword-only. path ( Path ): The file to write; it is replaced if it exists. Keyword-only. now ( float or None, default None ): The time to record, as a timestamp; the clock is used if None. Keyword-only. Returns BackupInfo : What the backup says about itself. Raises BackupError : If the file cannot be written. Nothing is left at path in that case. Examples >>> import tempfile >>> from alto.learning.database import Database >>> folder = Path ( tempfile . mkdtemp ()) >>> write_backup ( ... Database (), ... settings = {}, ... path = folder / "empty.altobackup" , ... now = 5.0 , ... ). created 5.0

title: alto.learning.backup
text: read_backup def read_backup ( path : Path ) -> Backup [Source] Read a backup file and check it all the way through, without changing anything. Parameters path ( Path ): The file. Returns Backup : The backup, ready to be applied. Raises BackupError : If the file cannot be read, is not an Alto backup, is damaged (a part does not match its checksum, or the database is not intact), or was made by a newer version of Alto. Examples >>> import tempfile >>> folder = Path ( tempfile . mkdtemp ()) >>> ( folder / "x.altobackup" ). write_bytes ( ... b "not a zip" ... ) 9 >>> read_backup ( folder / "x.altobackup" ) Traceback (most recent call last): ... alto.learning.backup.BackupError: This is not an Alto backup.

title: alto.learning.backup
text: restore_database def restore_database ( db : Database , * , backup : Backup , ) -> None [Source] Replace everything in the database with what a backup holds. Parameters db ( Database ): The database to replace the contents of. backup ( Backup ): A backup, as read_backup returns it. Keyword-only. Raises BackupError : If the database in the backup cannot be loaded. The database is not changed. Examples >>> import tempfile >>> from alto.learning.database import Database >>> source = Database () >>> _ = source . add_profile ( "Ada" ) >>> folder = Path ( tempfile . mkdtemp ()) >>> _ = write_backup ( ... source , ... settings = {}, ... path = folder / "a.altobackup" , ... ) >>> clean = Database () >>> restore_database ( ... clean , ... backup = read_backup ( ... folder / "a.altobackup" ... ), ... ) >>> [ p . name for p in clean . profiles ()] ['Ada']

title: alto.learning.calendar
text: alto.learning.calendar Daily exercise queues for SM-2 and FSRS. The scheduler controls when an introduced card is due. Each exercise supplies new questions under its current settings. Counting a prepared question does not introduce it.

title: alto.learning.calendar
text: ReviewInterval ReviewInterval ( seconds : int , identity : tuple [ int , str , str , str ], previous_state : str | None , rating : Rating = Rating . Good , graded_state : str | None = None , previous_due : float | None = None , ) [Source] A preview of one rating for a card in its current scheduling state. Examples >>> ReviewInterval ( ... 600 , ... ( 1 , "NoteNames" , "abc" , "FSRS" ), ... None , ... ). seconds 600

title: alto.learning.calendar
text: ReviewInterval.duration @ property def duration () -> str [Source] Format a review interval for display above a grade button or beside the music. Returns str : A whole-day interval or a short learning step in minutes and seconds. Examples >>> ReviewInterval ( ... 330 , ... ( 1 , "NoteNames" , "abc" , "FSRS" ), ... None , ... ). duration '5 min 30 s'

title: alto.learning.calendar
text: CalendarPractice CalendarPractice ( db : Database ) [Source] Prepare daily exercise queues and store each scheduler’s review dates. Examples >>> practice = CalendarPractice ( Database ()) >>> practice . db . profiles () [] Constructor Attach the queues to an Alto database. Parameters db ( Database ): Database containing the profile and its cards. Constructor examples >>> CalendarPractice ( Database ()). _batches {}

title: alto.learning.calendar
text: CalendarPractice.inherit_schedules def inherit_schedules ( profile : int , * , mode : str , ) -> None [Source] Initialize missing schedules for this profile from the other calendar scheduler. Parameters profile ( int ): Profile entering calendar practice. mode ( str ): Selected scheduler. Adaptive practice uses no calendar schedules. Examples Switching to FSRS carries over an SM-2 due date without consuming a review.

title: alto.learning.calendar
text: CalendarPractice.limits def limits ( profile : int , * , exercise : str = '' , ) -> tuple [ int , int ] [Source] Return the effective daily new-card and review limits. Parameters profile ( int ): Profile whose settings to read. exercise ( str ): Exercise class name, or an empty string for profile defaults. Returns tuple of int and int : New cards and completed reviews allowed per exercise per local day. UNLIMITED removes the cap. Examples >>> CalendarPractice ( Database ()). limits ( 1 ) (10, 200)

title: alto.learning.calendar
text: CalendarPractice.overrides def overrides ( profile : int , * , exercise : str , ) -> tuple [ int | None , int | None ] [Source] Read the two explicitly saved limits for an exercise. title: alto.learning.calendar
text: CalendarPractice.set_limits def set_limits ( profile : int , * , exercise : str = '' , new_cards : int | None , reviews : int | None , ) -> None [Source] Save the profile defaults or an exercise’s individual overrides. Parameters profile ( int ): Active profile. exercise ( str ): Exercise class name, or an empty string for the profile defaults. new_cards ( int or None ): Daily introductions, UNLIMITED for no cap, or None to inherit. reviews ( int or None ): Daily reviews, UNLIMITED for no cap, or None to inherit. Examples >>> db = Database () >>> practice = CalendarPractice ( db ) >>> profile = db . add_profile ( "Ada" ). id >>> practice . set_limits ( ... profile , new_cards = 5 , reviews = 30 ... ) >>> practice . limits ( ... profile , exercise = "NoteNames" ... ) (5, 30)

title: alto.learning.calendar
text: CalendarPractice.reset_limits def reset_limits ( profile : int ) -> None [Source] Restore the profile defaults and remove its exercise overrides. Parameters profile ( int ): Profile whose limits to reset. Examples Restoring defaults keeps the day's introductions and completed reviews.

title: alto.learning.calendar
text: CalendarPractice.queue def queue ( exercise : Exercise , * , profile : int , mode : str , now : float , ) -> tuple [ list [ Question ], list [ Question ]] [Source] Find due reviews and prepare the remaining new cards for this local day. Parameters exercise ( Exercise ): Exercise with its current settings. profile ( int ): Active profile ID. mode ( str ): Calendar scheduler whose due dates apply. now ( float ): Current timestamp. Returns tuple of list of Question and list of Question : Due reviews, oldest first, and new questions available for introduction. Examples >>> from alto.exercises.library import NoteNames >>> db = Database () >>> ada = db . add_profile ( "Ada" ) >>> due , new = CalendarPractice ( db ). queue ( ... NoteNames (), ... profile = ada . id , ... mode = "FSRS" , ... now = 1000 , ... ) >>> not due and len ( new ) == DAILY_NEW True

title: alto.learning.calendar
text: CalendarPractice.counts def counts ( exercise : Exercise , * , profile : int , mode : str , now : float , ) -> tuple [ int , int ] [Source] Count due reviews and unseen cards available with the selected settings. Parameters exercise ( Exercise ): Exercise shown on the tile. profile ( int ): Active profile. mode ( str ): Calendar scheduler. now ( float ): Current timestamp. Returns tuple of int and int : Due and new counts. Exact catalogs can be counted without rendering their cards. Examples >>> from alto.exercises.library import NoteNames >>> db = Database () >>> CalendarPractice ( db ). counts ( ... NoteNames (), ... profile = db . add_profile ( "Ada" ). id , ... mode = "SM-2" , ... now = 100 , ... )[ 1 ] > 0 True

title: alto.learning.calendar
text: CalendarPractice.tile_counts def tile_counts ( exercise : Exercise , * , profile : int , mode : str , now : float , ) -> tuple [ int , int , int ] [Source] Count available reviews, new cards, and missed cards awaiting a correct review. Parameters exercise ( Exercise ): Exercise with the current settings. profile ( int ): Active profile ID. mode ( str ): Active calendar scheduler. now ( float ): Current timestamp. Returns tuple of int, int, int : Due reviews, available new cards, and outstanding incorrect cards. A due retry counts in both review totals. Examples >>> from alto.exercises.library import NoteNames >>> db = Database () >>> CalendarPractice ( db ). tile_counts ( ... NoteNames (), ... profile = db . add_profile ( "Ada" ). id , ... mode = "SM-2" , ... now = 100 , ... )[ 2 ] 0

title: alto.learning.calendar
text: CalendarPractice.study_counts def study_counts ( exercise : Exercise , * , profile : int , mode : str , now : float , current_key : str | None = None , ) -> tuple [ tuple [ int , int , int ], str | None ] [Source] Count the exercise queues and identify the queue of the question on screen. Parameters exercise ( Exercise ): Exercise with the current settings. profile ( int ): Active profile ID. mode ( str ): Active calendar scheduler. now ( float ): Current timestamp. current_key ( str or None ): Item key of the question awaiting an answer. Returns tuple : The same review, new, and incorrect counts as the tiles, plus the current queue if a question is active. Examples A missed card that comes due again is underlined as incorrect during its retry.

title: alto.learning.calendar
text: CalendarPractice.take def take ( exercise : Exercise , * , profile : int , mode : str , now : float , ) -> Question | None [Source] Take the first eligible card, recording a new introduction only when served. Parameters exercise ( Exercise ): Exercise being opened or advanced. profile ( int ): Active profile ID. mode ( str ): Active calendar scheduler. now ( float ): Presentation timestamp. Returns Question or None : Next question, or None once the available work is finished. Examples >>> from alto.exercises.library import ( ... ChordQualities , ... ) >>> db = Database () >>> practice = CalendarPractice ( db ) >>> question = practice . take ( ... ChordQualities (), ... profile = db . add_profile ( "Ada" ). id , ... mode = "SM-2" , ... now = 1000 , ... ) >>> isinstance ( question , Question ) True

title: alto.learning.calendar
text: CalendarPractice.take_or_wait def take_or_wait ( exercise : Exercise , * , profile : int , mode : str , now : float , avoid : str | None = None , wait_learning : bool = False , ) -> tuple [ Question | None , float | None ] [Source] Draw an eligible card or return the time when a missed card can be reviewed. Parameters exercise ( Exercise ): Exercise with the current settings. profile ( int ): Active profile ID. mode ( str ): Active calendar scheduler. now ( float ): Presentation timestamp. avoid ( str or None ): Prefer another available card to the one just shown. wait_learning ( bool ): Also wake the exercise when a correctly answered learning card comes due. Returns tuple : The next question and, when the queue is waiting for a retry, its due timestamp. Examples A single missed card can wake the exercise when its learning step expires.
