text: CalendarPractice.introduce def introduce ( exercise : Exercise , * , profile : int , question : Question , now : float , ) -> None [Source] Register a calendar introduction once, in the caller’s draw or answer transaction. Parameters exercise ( Exercise ): Exercise that supplied this question. profile ( int ): Practicing profile. question ( Question ): New or previously introduced question. now ( float ): Time of introduction. Examples Answering a pending card keeps its original introduction day.

title: alto.learning.calendar
text: CalendarPractice.correct_interval def correct_interval ( exercise : str , * , profile : int , key : str , mode : str , now : float , ) -> ReviewInterval [Source] Preview the next correct answer without grading the card. Parameters exercise ( str ): Exercise class name. profile ( int ): Active profile ID. key ( str ): Card identity. mode ( str ): Calendar scheduler. now ( float ): Presentation timestamp. Returns ReviewInterval : Delay to display and reuse when the answer is submitted. Examples >>> CalendarPractice ( ... Database () ... ). correct_interval ( ... "NoteNames" , ... profile = 1 , ... key = "abc" , ... mode = "FSRS" , ... now = 1000 , ... ). seconds 600

title: alto.learning.calendar
text: CalendarPractice.passing_intervals def passing_intervals ( exercise : str , * , profile : int , key : str , mode : str , now : float , displayed : dict [ Rating , ReviewInterval ] | None = None , ) -> dict [ Rating , ReviewInterval ] [Source] Preview the three passing outcomes from one snapshot of this card. Parameters exercise ( str ): Exercise class name. profile ( int ): Active profile. key ( str ): Card identity. mode ( str ): Calendar scheduler. now ( float ): Presentation or answer timestamp. displayed ( dict or None ): Previously displayed outcomes to reuse while this card’s schedule is current. Returns dict : Passing grades and their previews, including the state to save. Examples >>> practice = CalendarPractice ( Database ()) >>> practice . passing_intervals ( ... "NoteNames" , ... profile = 1 , ... key = "abc" , ... mode = "SM-2" , ... now = 0 , ... )[ Rating . Good ]. seconds 600

title: alto.learning.calendar
text: CalendarPractice.grade def grade ( exercise : str , * , profile : int , key : str , mode : str , correct : bool , now : float , manual_rating : Rating | None = None , preview : ReviewInterval | None = None , ) -> None [Source] Reschedule a card from the first submission to this presentation. Parameters exercise ( str ): Exercise class name. profile ( int ): Active profile ID. key ( str ): Stable card identity. mode ( str ): Scheduler selected for this review. correct ( bool ): Whether the first submission was correct. manual_rating ( Rating or None ): Explicit grade from a button or response time. None uses the original automatic schedule. now ( float ): Answer timestamp. preview ( ReviewInterval or None ): Correct-answer interval shown for this presentation. Examples >>> from alto.exercises.library import NoteNames >>> db = Database () >>> ada = db . add_profile ( "Ada" ) >>> practice = CalendarPractice ( db ) >>> question = practice . take ( ... NoteNames (), ... profile = ada . id , ... mode = "SM-2" , ... now = 1000 , ... ) >>> practice . grade ( ... "NoteNames" , ... profile = ada . id , ... key = question . item_key (), ... mode = "SM-2" , ... correct = True , ... now = 1002 , ... ) >>> db . conn . execute ( ... "SELECT due FROM review_schedules" ... ). fetchone ()[ 0 ] 87402.0

title: alto.learning.database
text: alto.learning.database The SQLite store: profiles, every answer given, and what is known about each question. Pure Python (no Qt). Examples >>> db = Database () >>> ada = db . add_profile ( "Ada" ) >>> db . add_attempt ( ... ada . id , ... exercise = "NoteNames" , ... item_key = "k" , ... attempt_no = 1 , ... answer = "C" , ... correct = True , ... duration_ms = 2000 , ... answered_at = 100.0 , ... ) >>> db . count_attempts ( ada . id ) 1

title: alto.learning.database
text: check_snapshot def check_snapshot ( data : bytes ) -> tuple [ int , int , int ] [Source] Check that bytes are an intact Alto database that this version can read, and say what is in it. Parameters data ( bytes ): A snapshot, as Database.snapshot returns it. Returns tuple of (int, int, int) : The schema version, the number of profiles and the number of answers. Raises ValueError : If the data is not a SQLite database, is damaged, is not an Alto database, or has a newer schema than this version knows. Examples >>> check_snapshot ( Database (). snapshot ()) == ( ... SCHEMA_VERSION , ... 0 , ... 0 , ... ) True >>> check_snapshot ( b "not a database" ) Traceback (most recent call last): ... ValueError: This is not an Alto database.

title: alto.learning.database
text: Profile Profile ( id : int , * , name : str , ) [Source] A person who practices: their answers are kept apart from everyone else’s. Attributes id ( int ): The profile’s row number in the database. name ( str ): The name shown in the interface. Keyword-only. Examples >>> Profile ( 1 , name = "Ada" ) Profile(id=1, name='Ada')

title: alto.learning.database
text: ItemRecord ItemRecord ( strain : float , * , seen : int , first_try_right : int , wrong_attempts : int , total_first_ms : int , last_seen : float , signature : str , payload : str , item_key : str = '' , ) [Source] What a profile’s history says about one question. Attributes strain ( float ): How much practice the question needs; higher means it comes back sooner. seen ( int ): How many times the question was shown and answered. Keyword-only. first_try_right ( int ): How many of those showings were answered right on the first try. Keyword-only. wrong_attempts ( int ): How many wrong answers there have been in all. Keyword-only. total_first_ms ( int ): Time to the first answer, summed over the showings, in milliseconds. Keyword-only. last_seen ( float ): When the question was last answered, as a timestamp. Keyword-only. signature ( str ): The exercise settings it was asked under; it is only asked again while these are unchanged. Keyword-only. payload ( str ): The question itself as JSON, so it can be asked again. Keyword-only. item_key ( str, default ““ ): The question’s identity. Empty when the record is built to be saved, filled in when it is read back. Keyword-only. Examples >>> record = ItemRecord ( ... 2.0 , ... seen = 3 , ... first_try_right = 1 , ... wrong_attempts = 2 , ... total_first_ms = 9000 , ... last_seen = 100.0 , ... signature = "s" , ... payload = "{}" , ... ) >>> record . seen 3

title: alto.learning.database
text: Database Database ( path : str | Path = ':memory:' ) [Source] The SQLite database behind profiles, answers and per-question history. Attributes conn ( sqlite3.Connection ): The open connection, with rows returned as sqlite3.Row so columns can be read by name. Examples >>> db = Database () # in memory; give a path to keep it on disk >>> db . profiles () [] >>> db . add_profile ( "Ada" ) Profile(id=1, name='Ada') Constructor Open the database, creating it and its tables if they do not exist. Parameters path ( str or Path, default “:memory:” ): The file to use, whose folder is created if needed, or “:memory:” for a throwaway database. Constructor examples >>> db = Database () >>> db . conn . execute ( ... "PRAGMA user_version" ... ). fetchone ()[ 0 ] == SCHEMA_VERSION True

title: alto.learning.database
text: Database.write_transaction @ contextmanager def write_transaction () -> Iterator [ None ] [Source] Share the caller’s write transaction or begin one before reading the state to be updated. Yields None : Control while the transaction is active. Examples >>> db = Database () >>> with db . write_transaction (): ... print ( db . conn . in_transaction ) True >>> db . conn . in_transaction False

title: alto.learning.database
text: Database.close def close () -> None [Source] Close the connection. Examples >>> db = Database () >>> db . close ()

title: alto.learning.database
text: Database.snapshot def snapshot () -> bytes [Source] Return the whole database as bytes: every profile, answer and question record, exactly as they are now. Returns bytes : A complete SQLite database, which restore can load into another database. Examples >>> db = Database () >>> ada = db . add_profile ( "Ada" ) >>> check_snapshot ( db . snapshot ()) == ( ... SCHEMA_VERSION , ... 1 , ... 0 , ... ) True

title: alto.learning.database
text: Database.restore def restore ( data : bytes ) -> None [Source] Replace everything in the database with a snapshot, so it is exactly as it was when the snapshot was taken. Profiles, answers and question records that are here now are gone afterwards, and the ones in the snapshot take their place with the same ids. A snapshot made by an older version of Alto is brought up to date. Parameters data ( bytes ): A snapshot, as snapshot returns it. Raises ValueError : If the data is not an intact Alto database, or was made by a newer version of Alto. The database is not changed. Examples >>> source = Database () >>> ada = source . add_profile ( "Ada" ) >>> target = Database () >>> _ = target . add_profile ( "Someone else" ) >>> target . restore ( source . snapshot ()) >>> [ p . name for p in target . profiles ()] ['Ada']

title: alto.learning.database
text: Database.profiles def profiles () -> list [ Profile ] [Source] Return every profile, sorted by name without regard to case. Returns list of Profile : The profiles. Examples >>> db = Database () >>> _ = db . add_profile ( "ben" ) >>> _ = db . add_profile ( "Ada" ) >>> [ p . name for p in db . profiles ()] ['Ada', 'ben']

title: alto.learning.database
text: Database.profile def profile ( profile_id : int ) -> Profile | None [Source] Return one profile by its id. Parameters profile_id ( int ): The profile’s id. Returns Profile or None : The profile, or None if there is none with that id. Examples >>> db = Database () >>> ada = db . add_profile ( "Ada" ) >>> # noinspection PyUnresolvedReferences >>> db . profile ( ada . id ). name 'Ada' >>> db . profile ( 999 ) is None True

title: alto.learning.database
text: Database.add_profile def add_profile ( name : str ) -> Profile [Source] Create a profile. Parameters name ( str ): The name. Runs of spaces are collapsed to one, and case does not matter when checking for a duplicate. Returns Profile : The new profile. Raises ValueError : If the name is empty, or is already taken. Examples >>> db = Database () >>> db . add_profile ( " Ada Lovelace " ) Profile(id=1, name='Ada Lovelace') >>> db . add_profile ( "ada lovelace" ) Traceback (most recent call last): ... ValueError: There is already a profile called ada lovelace.

title: alto.learning.database
text: Database.delete_profile def delete_profile ( profile_id : int ) -> None [Source] Delete a profile together with all of its answers and question history. Parameters profile_id ( int ): The profile’s id. Examples >>> db = Database () >>> ada = db . add_profile ( "Ada" ) >>> db . delete_profile ( ada . id ) >>> db . profiles () []

title: alto.learning.database
text: Database.get_item def get_item ( profile_id : int , * , exercise : str , item_key : str , ) -> ItemRecord | None [Source] Return what is known about one question for a profile. Parameters profile_id ( int ): The profile’s id. exercise ( str ): The exercise’s class name. Keyword-only. item_key ( str ): The question’s identity. Keyword-only. Returns ItemRecord or None : The record, or None if the question has never been answered. Examples >>> db = Database () >>> ada = db . add_profile ( "Ada" ) >>> db . get_item ( ... ada . id , ... exercise = "NoteNames" , ... item_key = "k" , ... ) is None True

title: alto.learning.database
text: Database.save_item def save_item ( profile_id : int , * , exercise : str , item_key : str , item : ItemRecord , ) -> None [Source] Store what is known about a question, replacing any earlier record of it. Parameters profile_id ( int ): The profile’s id. exercise ( str ): The exercise’s class name. Keyword-only. item_key ( str ): The question’s identity. Keyword-only. item ( ItemRecord ): What to store. Keyword-only. Examples >>> db = Database () >>> ada = db . add_profile ( "Ada" ) >>> record = ItemRecord ( ... 2.0 , ... seen = 1 , ... first_try_right = 0 , ... wrong_attempts = 1 , ... total_first_ms = 3000 , ... last_seen = 100.0 , ... signature = "s" , ... payload = "{}" , ... ) >>> db . save_item ( ... ada . id , ... exercise = "NoteNames" , ... item_key = "k" , ... item = record , ... ) >>> # noinspection PyUnresolvedReferences >>> db . get_item ( ... ada . id , ... exercise = "NoteNames" , ... item_key = "k" , ... ). strain 2.0

title: alto.learning.database
text: Database.add_attempt def add_attempt ( profile_id : int , * , exercise : str , item_key : str , attempt_no : int , answer : str , correct : bool , duration_ms : int , answered_at : float , timing_valid : bool = True , ) -> None [Source] Log one answer, right or wrong. Parameters profile_id ( int ): The profile’s id. exercise ( str ): The exercise’s class name. Keyword-only. item_key ( str ): The question’s identity. Keyword-only. attempt_no ( int ): 1 for the first answer to this showing of the question, 2 for the second and so on. Keyword-only. answer ( str ): What was answered. Keyword-only. correct ( bool ): Whether it was right. Keyword-only. duration_ms ( int ): How long it took, in milliseconds. Keyword-only. answered_at ( float ): When it was answered, as a timestamp. Keyword-only. timing_valid ( bool ): Whether the question remained available for an uninterrupted response. Examples >>> db = Database () >>> ada = db . add_profile ( "Ada" ) >>> db . add_attempt ( ... ada . id , ... exercise = "NoteNames" , ... item_key = "k" , ... attempt_no = 1 , ... answer = "C" , ... correct = False , ... duration_ms = 1500 , ... answered_at = 50.0 , ... ) >>> [ ... ( r [ "answer" ], r [ "correct" ]) ... for r in db . attempts ( ada . id ) ... ] [('C', 0)]

title: alto.learning.database
text: Database.attempts def attempts ( profile_id : int , * , exercise : str | None = None , ) -> list [ sqlite3 . Row ] [Source] Return all of a profile’s answers in the order they were given. Parameters profile_id ( int ): The profile’s id. exercise ( str or None, default None ): Only answers to this exercise (its class name); every exercise if None. Keyword-only. Returns list of sqlite3.Row : Every column of each answer. Examples >>> db = Database () >>> ada = db . add_profile ( "Ada" ) >>> for i , name in enumerate ( ... [ "NoteNames" , "IntervalNames" ] ... ): ... db . add_attempt ( ... ada . id , ... exercise = name , ... item_key = "k" , ... attempt_no = 1 , ... answer = "x" , ... correct = True , ... duration_ms = 1000 , ... answered_at = float ( i ), ... ) >>> [ r [ "exercise" ] for r in db . attempts ( ada . id )] ['NoteNames', 'IntervalNames'] >>> [ ... r [ "exercise" ] ... for r in db . attempts ( ... ada . id , exercise = "IntervalNames" ... ) ... ] ['IntervalNames']

title: alto.learning.database
text: Database.attempts_in def attempts_in ( profile_ids : list [ int ] | None = None , * , exercise : str | None = None , since : float | None = None , item_key : str | None = None , ) -> list [ sqlite3 . Row ] [Source] Return answers given, oldest first, for some profiles, an exercise and a period. Parameters profile_ids ( list of int or None, default None ): The profiles to include; every profile if None. exercise ( str or None, default None ): Only this exercise (its class name); every exercise if None. Keyword-only. since ( float or None, default None ): Only answers from this timestamp on; the whole history if None. Keyword-only. item_key ( str or None, default None ): Only answers for this question key. Pass the exercise to identify the question. Keyword-only. Returns list of sqlite3.Row : Each answer’s exercise, attempt number, correctness, duration in milliseconds and time. Examples >>> db = Database () >>> ada = db . add_profile ( "Ada" ) >>> for t in ( 10.0 , 20.0 , 30.0 ): ... db . add_attempt ( ... ada . id , ... exercise = "NoteNames" , ... item_key = "k" , ... attempt_no = 1 , ... answer = "C" , ... correct = True , ... duration_ms = 1000 , ... answered_at = t , ... ) >>> [ ... r [ "answered_at" ] ... for r in db . attempts_in ( ... [ ada . id ], since = 15.0 ... ) ... ] [20.0, 30.0]

title: alto.learning.database
text: Database.first_attempts_per_day def first_attempts_per_day ( profile_ids : list [ int ] | None = None , * , exercise : str | None = None , since : float | None = None , ) -> dict [ str , int ] [Source] Count the questions first answered on each day, in local time, counting the days in the database. Parameters profile_ids ( list of int or None, default None ): The profiles to count; None for all of them. exercise ( str or None, default None ): Only this exercise’s questions; None for every exercise. Keyword-only. since ( float or None, default None ): Only answers from this time on, in seconds since the epoch. Keyword-only. Returns dict of str to int : The number of first answers on each day that has any, by the day as “YYYY-MM-DD”. Examples >>> db = Database () >>> ada = db . add_profile ( "Ada" ) >>> for attempt_no in ( 1 , 2 , 1 ): ... db . add_attempt ( ... ada . id , ... exercise = "NoteNames" , ... item_key = "k" , ... attempt_no = attempt_no , ... answer = "C" , ... correct = True , ... duration_ms = 900 , ... answered_at = 86_400.0 * 100 + 43_200 , ... ) >>> list ( ... db . first_attempts_per_day ( ... [ ada . id ] ... ). values () ... ) # the second try of a question is not counted [2]

title: alto.learning.database
text: Database.strained_items def strained_items ( profile_ids : list [ int ] | None = None , * , exercise : str | None = None , since : float | None = None , min_strain : float = 0.0 , limit : int = 10 , ) -> list [ sqlite3 . Row ] [Source] Return the questions that need most practice, the same question from different profiles counted together. Parameters profile_ids ( list of int or None, default None ): The profiles to include; every profile if None. exercise ( str or None, default None ): Only this exercise (its class name); every exercise if None. Keyword-only. since ( float or None, default None ): Only questions last seen from this timestamp on; the whole history if None. Keyword-only. min_strain ( float, default 0.0 ): Leave out questions with less strain than this. Keyword-only. limit ( int, default 10 ): The most questions to return. Keyword-only. Returns list of sqlite3.Row : Each question’s exercise, key, average strain, times seen, wrong attempts and stored payload, most strained first. Examples >>> db = Database () >>> ada = db . add_profile ( "Ada" ) >>> for key , strain in ( ... ( "easy" , 0.5 ), ... ( "hard" , 4.0 ), ... ): ... item = ItemRecord ( ... strain , ... seen = 1 , ... first_try_right = 0 , ... wrong_attempts = 1 , ... total_first_ms = 1000 , ... last_seen = 1.0 , ... signature = "s" , ... payload = "{}" , ... ) ... db . save_item ( ... ada . id , ... exercise = "NoteNames" , ... item_key = key , ... item = item , ... ) >>> [ ... r [ "item_key" ] ... for r in db . strained_items ( ... [ ada . id ], min_strain = 1.0 ... ) ... ] ['hard']

title: alto.learning.database
text: Database.count_attempts def count_attempts ( profile_id : int , * , exercise : str | None = None , since : float | None = None , until : float | None = None , ) -> int [Source] Return how many answers a profile has given, optionally of one exercise and within a period. Parameters profile_id ( int ): The profile’s id. exercise ( str or None, default None ): Count only answers to this exercise (a class name); all exercises if None. Keyword-only. since ( float or None, default None ): Count only answers given at or after this time (a timestamp). Keyword-only. until ( float or None, default None ): Count only answers given before this time (a timestamp). Keyword-only. Returns int : The number of answers, wrong ones included. Examples >>> db = Database () >>> ada = db . add_profile ( "Ada" ) >>> db . count_attempts ( ada . id ) 0 >>> for t in ( 1.0 , 5.0 , 9.0 ): ... db . add_attempt ( ... ada . id , ... exercise = "NoteNames" , ... item_key = "k" , ... attempt_no = 1 , ... answer = "C" , ... correct = True , ... duration_ms = 1000 , ... answered_at = t , ... ) >>> db . count_attempts ( ... ada . id , since = 2.0 , until = 9.0 ... # from the start of the period up to, not including, its end ... ) 1

title: alto.learning.database
text: Database.attempt_rows def attempt_rows ( profile_id : int , * , limit : int = 10000 , exercise : str | None = None , since : float | None = None , until : float | None = None , ) -> list [ sqlite3 . Row ] [Source] Return the newest answers first, each with the stored question it was an answer to (if that is still known). Parameters profile_id ( int ): The profile’s id. limit ( int, default 10000 ): The most rows to return. Keyword-only. exercise ( str or None, default None ): Return only answers to this exercise (a class name); all exercises if None. Keyword-only. since ( float or None, default None ): Return only answers given at or after this time (a timestamp). Keyword-only. until ( float or None, default None ): Return only answers given before this time (a timestamp). Keyword-only. Returns list of sqlite3.Row : Each answer’s time, exercise, question key, answer, correctness, attempt number, duration, question payload, and the question’s current due timestamp under the active scheduler (NULL if unscheduled). Examples >>> db = Database () >>> ada = db . add_profile ( "Ada" ) >>> for t in ( 1.0 , 2.0 ): ... db . add_attempt ( ... ada . id , ... exercise = "NoteNames" , ... item_key = "k" , ... attempt_no = 1 , ... answer = "C" , ... correct = True , ... duration_ms = 1000 , ... answered_at = t , ... ) >>> [ ... r [ "answered_at" ] ... for r in db . attempt_rows ( ada . id ) ... ] [2.0, 1.0] >>> [ ... r [ "answered_at" ] ... for r in db . attempt_rows ( ... ada . id , since = 1.5 ... ) ... ] [2.0]

title: alto.learning.database
text: Database.item_rows def item_rows ( profile_id : int , * , limit : int = 10000 , ) -> list [ sqlite3 . Row ] [Source] Return what is known about each of a profile’s questions, the most strained first. Parameters profile_id ( int ): The profile’s id. limit ( int, default 10000 ): The most rows to return. Keyword-only. Returns list of sqlite3.Row : Every column of each question’s record and the active scheduler’s due timestamp, or NULL if unscheduled. Examples >>> db = Database () >>> ada = db . add_profile ( "Ada" ) >>> db . item_rows ( ada . id ) []

title: alto.learning.database
text: Database.profile_rows def profile_rows () -> list [ sqlite3 . Row ] [Source] Return every profile with how many answers and questions it has. Returns list of sqlite3.Row : Each profile’s id, name, creation time, number of answers and number of questions, sorted by name. Examples >>> db = Database () >>> _ = db . add_profile ( "Ada" ) >>> [ ... ( ... r [ "name" ], ... r [ "attempts" ], ... r [ "questions" ], ... ) ... for r in db . profile_rows () ... ] [('Ada', 0, 0)]

title: alto.learning.database
text: Database.replay_candidates def replay_candidates ( profile_id : int , * , exercise : str , signature : str , hardest : int = 25 , random_extra : int = 10 , ) -> list [ ItemRecord ] [Source] Return questions asked before under these same settings: the ones that need most practice, plus a few at random. Parameters profile_id ( int ): The profile’s id. exercise ( str ): The exercise’s class name. Keyword-only. signature ( str ): The exercise’s current settings signature; only questions asked under it qualify. Keyword-only. hardest ( int, default 25 ): How many of the most strained questions to include. Keyword-only. random_extra ( int, default 10 ): How many more to pick at random. Keyword-only. Returns list of ItemRecord : The questions, each at most once. Examples >>> db = Database () >>> ada = db . add_profile ( "Ada" ) >>> item = ItemRecord ( ... 3.0 , ... seen = 1 , ... first_try_right = 0 , ... wrong_attempts = 1 , ... total_first_ms = 1000 , ... last_seen = 1.0 , ... signature = "s1" , ... payload = "{}" , ... ) >>> db . save_item ( ... ada . id , ... exercise = "NoteNames" , ... item_key = "k" , ... item = item , ... ) >>> [ ... row_ . item_key ... for row_ in db . replay_candidates ( ... ada . id , ... exercise = "NoteNames" , ... signature = "s1" , ... ) ... ] ['k'] >>> db . replay_candidates ( ... ada . id , ... exercise = "NoteNames" , ... signature = "other settings" , ... ) []

"abc" , ... source = "SM-2" , ... state = "[8, 180, 2.5]" , ... due = 200 * DAY , ... rating = Rating . Good , ... ) >>> Card . from_json ( result ). stability 180.0

title: alto.learning.grading
text: review_options def review_options ( key : str , * , mode : str , previous : str | None , due : float , now : float , ) -> dict [ Rating , tuple [ int , str ]] [Source] Calculate a consistent set of answer-button intervals from one scheduling state. Returns dict : Delay in seconds and serialized successor state for each grade. Examples >>> review_options ( ... "abc" , ... mode = "SM-2" , ... previous = None , ... due = 0 , ... now = 0 , ... )[ Rating . Again ][ 0 ] 60

title: alto.learning.learner
text: alto.learning.learner Ties the profile, the database and the scheduler together for the exercise screen. Examples >>> from alto.exercises.library import NoteNames >>> db = Database () >>> learner = Learner ( ... db , profile = db . add_profile ( "Ada" ) ... ) >>> question = learner . pick ( ... NoteNames (), rng = random . Random ( 1 ) ... ) >>> question . answer in question . choices True

title: alto.learning.learner
text: PracticeComplete PracticeComplete ( retry_at : float | None = None ) [Source] Bases: Exception The current exercise has no scheduled cards available. Examples >>> issubclass ( PracticeComplete , Exception ) True Constructor Carry the next missed card’s due time to the exercise screen. Parameters retry_at ( float or None ): Scheduled timestamp, or None when practice is finished for now. Constructor examples >>> PracticeComplete (). retry_at is None True

title: alto.learning.learner
text: Learner Learner ( db : Database , * , profile : Profile , ) [Source] Chooses what a profile is asked next and records how it was answered. Attributes FRESH ( int ): How many new questions are generated for each pick, alongside the ones asked before. db ( Database ): Where answers and what is known about each question are stored. profile ( Profile ): Whose answers these are. Examples >>> from alto.exercises.library import NoteNames >>> db = Database () >>> learner = Learner ( ... db , profile = db . add_profile ( "Ada" ) ... ) >>> rng = random . Random ( 2 ) >>> question = learner . pick ( ... NoteNames (), rng = rng ... ) >>> learner . record ( ... NoteNames (), ... question = question , ... answer = question . answer , ... correct = True , ... attempt_no = 1 , ... seconds = 2.5 , ... ) >>> db . count_attempts ( learner . profile . id ) 1 Constructor Create a learner for one profile. Parameters db ( Database ): The database to read and write. profile ( Profile ): The profile that is practicing. Keyword-only. Constructor examples >>> database = Database () >>> learner = Learner ( ... database , ... profile = database . add_profile ( "Ada" ), ... ) >>> learner . profile . name 'Ada'

text: Learner.pick def pick ( exercise : Exercise , * , rng : random . Random , avoid : str | None = None , now : float | None = None , ) -> Question [Source] Return the next eligible question using the profile’s selected scheduler. Parameters exercise ( Exercise ): The exercise being practiced. rng ( random.Random ): The random number generator used to make new questions and to draw one. Keyword-only. avoid ( str or None, default None ): The item_key of the question just asked, so it does not come straight back. Keyword-only. now ( float or None, default None ): The current time as a timestamp; the clock is used if None. Keyword-only. Returns Question : The question to ask. Random ( 3 ), ... avoid = first . item_key (), ... ) >>> second . item_key () != first . item_key () True

title: alto.learning.learner
text: Learner.record def record ( exercise : Exercise , * , question : Question , answer : str , correct : bool , attempt_no : int , seconds : float , now : float | None = None , preview : ReviewInterval | None = None , passing_previews : dict [ Rating , ReviewInterval ] | None = None , self_grading : bool = False , timing_valid : bool = True , ) -> ReviewInterval | None [Source] Log one answer and update what is known about the question. Parameters exercise ( Exercise ): The exercise being practiced. question ( Question ): The question that was answered. Keyword-only. answer ( str ): What was answered. Keyword-only. correct ( bool ): Whether the answer was right. Keyword-only. attempt_no ( int ): 1 for the first answer to this showing of the question, 2 for the second and so on. Keyword-only. seconds ( float ): How long the answer took. Keyword-only. now ( float or None, default None ): When it was answered, as a timestamp; the clock is used if None. Keyword-only. preview ( ReviewInterval or None ): Correct-answer interval displayed for this question. passing_previews ( dict or None ): Hard, Good, and Easy intervals shown during speed grading. self_grading ( bool ): Defer scheduling a correct calendar answer until the learner rates it. timing_valid ( bool ): Whether the presentation was uninterrupted. False excludes it from timing. Returns ReviewInterval or None : The interval chosen by speed grading, once enough earlier answers exist. Examples >>> from alto.exercises.library import NoteNames >>> db = Database () >>> learner = Learner ( ... db , profile = db . add_profile ( "Ada" ) ... ) >>> q = learner . pick ( ... NoteNames (), rng = random . Random ( 4 ) ... ) >>> learner . record ( ... NoteNames (), ... question = q , ... answer = "?" , ... correct = False , ... attempt_no = 1 , ... seconds = 3.0 , ... ) >>> learner . record ( ... NoteNames (), ... question = q , ... answer = q . answer , ... correct = True , ... attempt_no = 2 , ... seconds = 1.0 , ... ) >>> [ ... row [ "correct" ] ... for row in db . attempts ( ... learner . profile . id ... ) ... ] [0, 1] >>> # noinspection PyUnresolvedReferences >>> db . get_item ( ... learner . profile . id , ... exercise = "NoteNames" , ... item_key = q . item_key (), ... ). wrong_attempts 1

title: alto.learning.response_times

Parameters percent ( int ): Percentile from zero to 100. Returns float : Elapsed milliseconds at the requested percentile. Examples >>> ResponseTimes ( ... ( 1000 , 2000 ), 15 , 15 ... ). percentile ( 25 ) 1250.0

title: alto.learning.response_times
text: ResponseTimes.grade def grade ( milliseconds : int ) -> Rating [Source] Grade a correct first answer against earlier answers to this exercise. Parameters milliseconds ( int ): Eligible duration, or zero if the timing is unavailable. Returns Rating : Hard for slow answers, Easy for fast answers, and Good for ties or missing timings. Examples >>> ResponseTimes (( 1000 ,) * 40 , 15 , 15 ). grade ( ... 1000 ... ). name 'Good'

title: alto.learning.scheduler
text: alto.learning.scheduler How a question’s history turns into how soon it comes back. Pure Python, no database and no Qt. Every question carries a strain : how much practice it needs. A new question starts at NEW_STRAIN. Each answer moves it, and the chance of being asked is exp(WEIGHT_SLOPE * strain), so strained questions come back sooner and more often while well-known ones fade into the background. A wrong answer adds WRONG_PENALTY, so every extra attempt pushes the question further up. A right answer on the first try takes CORRECT_REWARD off. A right answer after misses earns only RETRY_REWARD. The first answer’s speed, against the exercise’s par_seconds , adds or removes strain on top: very quick answers take off up to FAST_BONUS, and slow ones add up to SLOW_PENALTY. Examples >>> strain = update_strain ( ... NEW_STRAIN , ... correct = False , ... attempt_no = 1 , ... seconds = 4.0 , ... par_seconds = 4.0 , ... ) >>> strain # a miss pushes the question up 3.0 >>> update_strain ( ... strain , ... correct = True , ... attempt_no = 2 , ... seconds = 2.0 , ... par_seconds = 4.0 , ... ) # a retry earns little 2.8

title: alto.learning.scheduler
text: arts_priority def arts_priority ( intervening : int , * , correct : bool , duration_ms : int , ) -> float [Source] Score a previously answered item for Adaptive Response-Time-based Sequencing. Parameters intervening ( int ): Other first submissions since the last first submission to this item. correct ( bool ): Whether the last first submission was correct. duration_ms ( int ): Response time of that submission, in milliseconds. Returns float : Priority for the next trial. A new item starts at 1.0. Examples >>> arts_priority ( ... 1 , correct = False , duration_ms = 200 ... ) 2.0 >>> arts_priority ( ... 0 , correct = True , duration_ms = 3000 ... ) 0.0

title: alto.learning.scheduler
text: speed_term def speed_term ( seconds : float , * , par_seconds : float , ) -> float [Source] Return the strain change for how long the first answer took. Parameters seconds ( float ): How long the first answer took. par_seconds ( float ): How long a good first answer takes for this exercise. Keyword-only. Returns float : Negative when the answer was quick (down to -FAST_BONUS ), zero at par, and positive when it was slow (up to SLOW_PENALTY ). Examples >>> speed_term ( ... 1.0 , par_seconds = 10.0 ... ) # at or under half of par: the full bonus -0.6 >>> round ( speed_term ( 7.5 , par_seconds = 10.0 ), 2 ) -0.3 >>> round ( speed_term ( 25.0 , par_seconds = 10.0 ), 2 ) 0.5 >>> speed_term ( ... 100.0 , par_seconds = 10.0 ... ) # four times par or more: the full penalty 1.0

title: alto.learning.scheduler
text: update_strain def update_strain ( strain : float , * , correct : bool , attempt_no : int , seconds : float , par_seconds : float , ) -> float [Source] Return the question’s strain after one more answer. Parameters strain ( float ): The strain before this answer. correct ( bool ): Whether the answer was right. Keyword-only. attempt_no ( int ): 1 for the first answer to this showing of the question, 2 for the second and so on. Keyword-only. seconds ( float ): How long the answer took. Only the first attempt’s speed matters. Keyword-only. par_seconds ( float ): How long a good first answer takes for this exercise. Keyword-only. Returns float : The new strain, kept between 0 and STRAIN_MAX . Examples >>> update_strain ( ... 1.5 , ... correct = False , ... attempt_no = 1 , ... seconds = 5.0 , ... par_seconds = 5.0 , ... ) 3.0 >>> round ( ... update_strain ( ... 1.5 , ... correct = True , ... attempt_no = 1 , ... seconds = 1.0 , ... par_seconds = 5.0 , ... ), ... 2 , ... ) # right, and quick 0.4 >>> update_strain ( ... 5.9 , ... correct = False , ... attempt_no = 1 , ... seconds = 5.0 , ... par_seconds = 5.0 , ... ) # capped 6.0

title: alto.learning.scheduler
text: weight def weight ( strain : float | None , * , last_seen : float | None , now : float , ) -> float [Source] Return how likely a question is to be picked, relative to the others. A question just seen is held back for a while, long for an easy one and short for a hard one, so what you have learned is not repeated right away but what you struggle with returns within the minute. Parameters strain ( float or None ): The question’s strain, or None for one never answered. last_seen ( float or None ): When it was last answered (a timestamp), or None if never. Keyword-only. now ( float ): The current time (a timestamp). Keyword-only. Returns float : A positive number; a larger one means the question is more likely to come up. Examples >>> round ( ... weight ( None , last_seen = None , now = 0.0 ), 2 ... ) # a new question 2.46 >>> round ( ... weight ( 3.0 , last_seen = 0.0 , now = 1e9 ), 2 ... ) # a hard question, long unseen 6.05 >>> round ( ... weight ( 3.0 , last_seen = 100.0 , now = 100.0 ), ... 3 , ... ) # the same, just seen: held back 0.121

title: alto.learning.scheduler
text: choose def choose ( options : Sequence [ T ], * , weights : Sequence [ float ], rng : random . Random , ) -> T [Source] Pick one option at random, in proportion to its weight. Parameters options ( sequence of T ): The things to choose from. weights ( sequence of float ): One weight per option; a larger weight makes it more likely. Keyword-only. rng ( random.Random ): The random number generator to draw with. Keyword-only. Returns T : The chosen option. Examples >>> choose ( ... [ "a" , "b" ], ... weights = [ 1.0 , 0.0 ], ... rng = random . Random ( 0 ), ... ) 'a'

title: alto.learning.stats
text: alto.learning.stats Numbers and series for the statistics screen, worked out from the answers in the database. Pure Python, no Qt. A “question” here is one showing of a question, scored by its first answer: it is right if that answer was right. Later attempts at the same showing show up as extra attempts per question, not as extra questions. Examples >>> db = Database () >>> ada = db . add_profile ( "Ada" ) >>> for i , ok in enumerate (( True , True , False )): ... db . add_attempt ( ... ada . id , ... exercise = "NoteNames" , ... item_key = str ( i ), ... attempt_no = 1 , ... answer = "C" , ... correct = ok , ... duration_ms = 2000 , ... answered_at = 1000.0 + i , ... ) >>> stats = collect ( ... db , profile_ids = [ ada . id ], now = 1010.0 ... ) >>> stats . questions , stats . first_right (3, 2) >>> # noinspection PyTypeChecker >>> round ( stats . accuracy ) 67

title: alto.learning.stats
text: Bucket Bucket ( start : datetime , * , label : str , questions : int = 0 , first_right : int = 0 , times : list [ float ] = field ( default_factory = list ), ) [Source] The answers given in one period (an hour, day, week or month), for the charts. Attributes start ( datetime ): When the period begins. label ( str ): What to call the period on a chart axis. Keyword-only. questions ( int, default 0 ): How many questions were answered in it. Keyword-only. first_right ( int, default 0 ): How many of those were right on the first answer. Keyword-only. times ( list of float ): Seconds to the first answer, one per question. Keyword-only. Examples >>> bucket = Bucket ( ... datetime ( 2026 , 1 , 5 ), ... label = "Jan 5" , ... questions = 2 , ... first_right = 1 , ... times = [ 2.0 , 4.0 ], ... ) >>> bucket . accuracy , bucket . median_seconds (50.0, 3.0)

title: alto.learning.stats
text: Stats Stats ( questions : int = 0 , * , first_right : int = 0 , attempts : int = 0 , median_seconds : float | None = None , practice_seconds : float = 0.0 , days_practiced : int = 0 , granularity : str = 'day' , buckets : list [ Bucket ] = field ( default_factory = list ), volume_buckets : list [ Bucket ] = field ( default_factory = list ), by_exercise : list [ ExerciseStats ] = field ( default_factory = list ), hardest : list [ HardQuestion ] = field ( default_factory = list ), ) [Source] Everything the statistics screen shows. Attributes questions ( int, default 0 ): How many questions were answered, each counted once. first_right ( int, default 0 ): How many were right on the first answer. Keyword-only. attempts ( int, default 0 ): How many answers were given in all, including repeats. Keyword-only. median_seconds ( float or None ): The typical time to a first answer. Keyword-only. practice_seconds ( float, default 0.0 ): Time spent practicing, with a cap on each answer so leaving the app open does not inflate it. Keyword-only. granularity ( str, default “day” ): The size of the chart periods: “hour”, “day”, “week” or “month”. Keyword-only. buckets ( list of Bucket ): One per period, oldest first. Keyword-only. volume_buckets ( list of Bucket ): Period counts for the questions answered chart. These share the trend buckets when their periods match. Examples >>> Stats (). accuracy is None # nothing answered yet True >>> Stats ( ... 4 , first_right = 3 , attempts = 6 ... ). attempts_per_question 1.5

text: period_end def period_end ( start : datetime , * , granularity : str , ) -> datetime [Source] Return the moment a chart period ends, which is when the next one begins. title: alto.learning.stats
text: daily_counts def daily_counts ( db : Database , * , profile_ids : list [ int ] | None , exercise : str | None = None , weeks : int = 53 , now : float | None = None , ) -> dict [ date , int ] [Source] Return how many questions were answered on each day, for the review heatmap. Looks back over the last weeks calendar weeks up to today, in local time. Days with no answers are left out. It counts questions (first attempts), not attempts, like everything else here. Parameters db ( Database ): Where the answers are. profile_ids ( list of int or None ): The profiles to include; every profile if None. Keyword-only. exercise ( str or None, default None ): Only this exercise (its class name); every exercise if None. Keyword-only. weeks ( int, default 53 ): How many calendar weeks to look back, counting this one. Keyword-only. now ( float or None, default None ): The current time as a timestamp; the clock is used if None. Keyword-only. Returns dict of date to int : The number of questions answered on each day that had any. Examples >>> database = Database () >>> ada = database . add_profile ( "Ada" ) >>> noon = datetime ( ... 2026 , 11 , 13 , 12 ... ). timestamp () >>> for i in range ( 3 ): ... database . add_attempt ( ... ada . id , ... exercise = "NoteNames" , ... item_key = str ( i ), ... attempt_no = 1 , ... answer = "C" , ... correct = True , ... duration_ms = 1000 , ... answered_at = noon + i , ... ) >>> daily_counts ( ... database , ... profile_ids = [ ada . id ], ... now = noon + 60 , ... ) {datetime.date(2026, 11, 13): 3}

title: alto.learning.stats
text: collect def collect ( db : Database , * , profile_ids : list [ int ] | None , exercise : str | None = None , since : float | None = None , now : float | None = None , hardest : int = 8 , volume_granularity : str | None = None , ) -> Stats [Source] Work out everything the statistics screen shows. Parameters db ( Database ): Where the answers are. profile_ids ( list of int or None ): The profiles to include; every profile if None. Keyword-only. exercise ( str or None, default None ): Only this exercise (its class name); every exercise if None. Keyword-only. since ( float or None, default None ): Only answers from this timestamp on; the whole history if None. Keyword-only. now ( float or None, default None ): The current time as a timestamp; the clock is used if None. Keyword-only. hardest ( int, default 8 ): How many questions to list as needing practice. Keyword-only. volume_granularity ( str or None, default None ): Group question counts by hour, day, week or month. None follows the timeframe. Keyword-only. Returns Stats : The totals, the per-period buckets, the per-exercise figures and the hardest questions. Examples >>> database = Database () >>> ada = database . add_profile ( "Ada" ) >>> database . add_attempt ( ... ada . id , ... exercise = "NoteNames" , ... item_key = "k" , ... attempt_no = 1 , ... answer = "C" , ... correct = True , ... duration_ms = 4000 , ... answered_at = 1000.0 , ... ) >>> stats = collect ( ... database , ... profile_ids = [ ada . id ], ... now = 1060.0 , ... ) >>> ( ... stats . questions , ... stats . median_seconds , ... stats . practice_seconds , ... ) (1, 4.0, 4.0) >>> collect ( ... database , profile_ids = [ 999 ], now = 1060.0 ... ). questions # nobody has answered anything 0

title: alto.lessons.base
text: alto.lessons.base What a lesson is made of: steps, and the small tasks inside them. A task is a soft exercise. It cannot be failed: a wrong answer gets a hint, a second wrong answer gets the answer, and nothing is scored or recorded. Examples >>> task = Task ( ... prompt = "Click the key." , ... cells = frozenset ({( "outer" , 1 )}), ... hint = "Count." , ... explanation = "One step." , ... ) >>> ( ... task . check (( "outer" , 1 )), ... task . check (( "outer" , 2 )), ... ) (True, False)

title: alto.lessons.base
text: Task Task ( prompt : str , hint : str , explanation : str , cells : frozenset [ tuple [ str , int ]] = frozenset (), choices : tuple [ str , ...] = (), correct : str = '' , clef : str = '' , key : int = 0 , targets : tuple [ tuple [ float , float , float ], ...] = (), ) [Source] One small question inside a lesson step. It is answered either by clicking a cell of the circle ( cells ) or by pressing one of choices . Attributes prompt ( str ): The question, as simple HTML. hint ( str ): What to say after a wrong answer. explanation ( str ): What to say after the right answer, or once the answer has been given away. cells ( frozenset of tuple of (str, int) ): The cells that are right, each a ring (“outer” or “inner”) and a place clockwise from the top. choices ( tuple of str ): The buttons to choose from, for a question that is not answered on the circle. correct ( str ): The right button, if there are choices. clef ( str ): For a step that shows a staff beside a task, the clef to draw on it; empty for a blank staff. key ( int ): Sharps (positive) or flats (negative) on the task staff. targets ( tuple of tuple of (float, float, float) ): For a question answered by clicking the step’s instrument picture: each right place as the x and y of its centre and its radius, in the picture’s own pixels. Examples >>> Task ( ... prompt = "Which?" , ... hint = "Count." , ... explanation = "Five." , ... choices = ( "A" , "B" ), ... correct = "B" , ... ). check ( "B" ) True >>> Task ( ... prompt = "Click it." , ... hint = "" , ... explanation = "" , ... targets = (( 10.0 , 10.0 , 5.0 ),), ... ). hits ( 12.0 , y = 11.0 ) True

title: alto.lessons.base
text: Task.hits def hits ( x : float , * , y : float , ) -> bool [Source] Say whether a click on the instrument picture is on one of the right places. Parameters x ( float ): The click’s x in the picture’s pixels. y ( float ): The click’s y in the picture’s pixels. Keyword-only. Returns bool : True if the click is within the radius of a target. Examples >>> Task ( ... prompt = "?" , ... hint = "" , ... explanation = "" , ... targets = (( 10.0 , 10.0 , 5.0 ),), ... ). hits ( 30.0 , y = 10.0 ) False

title: alto.lessons.base
text: Task.check def check ( answer : tuple [ str , int ] | str ) -> bool [Source] Say whether an answer is right. Parameters answer ( tuple of (str, int) or str ): A cell that was clicked, or the text of a button that was pressed. Returns bool : True for a right answer. Examples >>> Task ( ... prompt = "?" , ... hint = "" , ... explanation = "" , ... cells = frozenset ({( "inner" , 0 )}), ... ). check (( "inner" , 0 )) True >>> Task ( ... prompt = "?" , ... hint = "" , ... explanation = "" , ... choices = ( "A" , "B" ), ... correct = "A" , ... ). check (( "outer" , 0 )) False

title: alto.lessons.base
text: Staff Staff ( clef : str , note : str = '' , caption : str = '' , key : int = 0 , ) [Source] A staff to show beside the words of a step: a clef, and perhaps a note, with a line of words under it. Attributes clef ( str ): The clef to draw, any of alto.settings.CLEF_BASICS_CLEFS . note ( str ): A note to write on the staff, such as “C4”; empty for none. Only the seven clefs that have a lowest line for notes can have one, not the French violin and subbass clefs. caption ( str ): The words under the staff. key ( int ): Sharps (positive) or flats (negative) after the clef. Examples >>> Staff ( ... clef = "alto" , ... note = "C4" , ... caption = "Alto clef" , ... ). note 'C4'

title: alto.lessons.base
text:
Step Step ( title : str , text : str , circle : str = 'none' , hear : tuple [ tuple [ str , ...], ...] = (), hear_label : str = 'Hear it' , make_task : Callable [[ random . Random ], Task ] | None = field ( default = None , compare = False ), closing : bool = False , staves : tuple [ Staff , ...] = (), task_staff : bool = False , scale : str = '' , scale_tonic : str = 'C4' , scale_explore : bool = True , keyboard_note : str = '' , hear_display : Literal [ '' , 'staff' , 'keyboard' ] = '' , picture : PicturePosition | FingerboardPosition | None = None , hear_instrument : str = '' , single_question : bool = False , label_middle_c : bool = False , rhythm : tuple [ str , ...] = (), rhythm_meter : tuple [ int , int ] = ( 4 , 4 ), ) [Source] One page of a lesson. Attributes title ( str ): The heading. text ( str ): What to read, as simple HTML. circle ( str ): How the circle of fifths is shown: “none” for no circle, “rest” for a picture that does not respond, “explore” for one that can be clicked, or “walk” for one that can also be walked around with two buttons. hear ( tuple of tuple of str ): Notes to play from a Hear it button, as columns of note names such as “C4”; empty for no button. hear_label ( str ): What the Hear it button says. make_task ( callable or None ): Makes a fresh task from a random generator each time one is wanted; None for a step with no task. single_question ( bool ): True when the knowledge check repeats the same question on every attempt. closing ( bool ): True for the last step, which offers to practice. staves ( tuple of Staff ): Captioned staves in reading order. Adjacent examples share a panel and wrap when space is limited. task_staff ( bool ): Show one staff beside the words that follows the task: it draws the task’s clef and key signature. scale ( str ): Scale type for an interactive notation diagram; empty for none. scale_tonic ( str ): Starting note of the diagram, including its octave. scale_explore ( bool ): Allow changing the example. False hides the selectors for identification tasks. hear_display ( str ): Show the playback pitches on a treble staff or keyboard (“staff” or “keyboard”). Empty hides this diagram. keyboard_note ( str ): A named pitch to highlight on the lesson keyboard, which spans middle C to the C above it. picture ( PicturePosition or FingerboardPosition or None ): An instrument picture to show beside the words, such as one supplied by a plugin. Alto draws it with the same widget the exercises use. None for no picture. hear_instrument ( str ): The key of the instrument that plays the Hear it notes, such as one supplied by a plugin. Empty for the learner’s own choice of sound. rhythm ( tuple of str ): Written note and rest values to count with a metronome. rhythm_meter ( tuple of int ): Numerator and denominator for the rhythm example. label_middle_c ( bool ): Label middle C and bracket the pair of black keys beside it. Examples >>> Step ( ... title = "Hello" , text = "

Hi.

" ... ). circle 'none'

title: alto.lessons.base
text: Lesson Lesson ( key : str , title : str , about : str , summary : str , category : str , steps : tuple [ Step , ...], exercise : str , related_exercises : tuple [ str , ...] = (), icon : str = '' , ) [Source] A lesson: a title, a line about it, and its steps. Attributes key ( str ): A short name to save progress under. title ( str ): The title. about ( str ): A line or two saying what the lesson covers. summary ( str ): A short line for its card. category ( str ): The group it belongs to on the list, such as “Scales & Keys”. steps ( tuple of Step ): The pages, in order. exercise ( str ): The primary exercise offered on the last page and used for the lesson icon. related_exercises ( tuple of str ): Additional exercises offered on the last page, in display order. icon ( str ): SVG shapes for the lesson’s tile, in a 24 by 24 box with COLOR where the theme’s ink goes. Empty uses the icon of the primary exercise. Examples >>> steps = ( Step ( title = "One" , text = "" ),) >>> lesson = Lesson ( ... key = "demo" , ... title = "Demo" , ... about = "A demo." , ... summary = "Demo." , ... category = "Demos" , ... steps = steps , ... exercise = "NoteNames" , ... ) >>> lesson . steps [ 0 ]. title 'One'

title: alto.lessons.circle_of_fifths
text: alto.lessons.circle_of_fifths The lesson on the circle of fifths, taught from nothing. It covers what a key is, what a fifth is, how the circle counts sharps and flats, and what the inner ring and the neighbors of a key mean. Examples >>> len ( CIRCLE_OF_FIFTHS . steps ) 8 >>> summary ( "outer" , place = 2 ) 'D major: 2 sharps (F♯, C♯)'

title: alto.lessons.circle_of_fifths
text: key_name def key_name ( ring : str , * , place : int , ) -> str [Source] Return the first name of the key in a cell, written out. Parameters ring ( str ): “outer” for the major key, “inner” for the minor. place ( int ): The place on the circle, clockwise from the top. Keyword-only. Returns str : “G major” or “E minor”. Examples >>> ( ... key_name ( "outer" , place = 1 ), ... key_name ( "inner" , place = 1 ), ... ) ('G major', 'E minor')

title: alto.lessons.circle_of_fifths
text: summary def summary ( ring : str , * , place : int , ) -> str [Source] Say a key and its key signature in one line. Parameters ring ( str ): “outer” or “inner”. place ( int ): The place on the circle. Keyword-only. Returns str : Simple HTML such as “ A major : 3 sharps (F♯, C♯, G♯)”. Examples >>> ( ... summary ( "outer" , place = 0 ), ... summary ( "inner" , place = 11 ), ... ) ('C major: no sharps or flats', 'D minor: 1 flat (B♭)')

title: alto.lessons.circle_of_fifths
text: fifth_task def fifth_task ( rng : random . Random ) -> Task [Source] Ask for the letter a fifth above a random letter, answered with buttons. Parameters rng ( random.Random ): The random number generator. Returns Task : The question. Examples >>> task = fifth_task ( random . Random ( 1 )) >>> task . correct in LETTERS and len ( ... task . choices ... ) == 4 and task . correct in task . choices True

title: alto.lessons.circle_of_fifths
text: sharps_task def sharps_task ( rng : random . Random ) -> Task [Source] Ask for the major key with a given number of sharps, answered on the circle. Parameters rng ( random.Random ): The random number generator. Returns Task : The question. Examples >>> task = sharps_task ( random . Random ( 2 )) >>> ring , at = next ( iter ( task . cells )) >>> ( ... ring , ... SIGNATURES [ at ] ... == int ( ... task . prompt . split ( "<b>" )[ 1 ]. split ()[ ... 0 ... ] ... ), ... ) ('outer', True)

title: alto.lessons.circle_of_fifths
text: flats_task def flats_task ( rng : random . Random ) -> Task [Source] Ask for the major key with a given number of flats, answered on the circle. Parameters rng ( random.Random ): The random number generator. Returns Task : The question. Examples >>> task = flats_task ( random . Random ( 3 )) >>> ring , at = next ( iter ( task . cells )) >>> ( ... ring , ... - SIGNATURES [ at ] ... == int ( ... task . prompt . split ( "<b>" )[ 1 ]. split ()[ ... 0 ... ] ... ), ... ) ('outer', True)

title: alto.lessons.circle_of_fifths
text: relative_task def relative_task ( rng : random . Random ) -> Task [Source] Ask for the relative minor of a major key, answered on the circle. Parameters rng ( random.Random ): The random number generator. Returns Task : The question. Examples >>> task = relative_task ( random . Random ( 4 )) >>> task . cells <= { ... ( "inner" , at ) for at in range ( 12 ) ... } True

title: alto.lessons.circle_of_fifths
text: neighbor_task def neighbor_task ( rng : random . Random ) -> Task [Source] Ask for the key a fifth above or below a random key, answered on the circle. Parameters rng ( random.Random ): The random number generator. Returns Task : The question. Examples >>> task = neighbor_task ( random . Random ( 5 )) >>> ring , at = next ( iter ( task . cells )) >>> ring , at in range ( 12 ) ('outer', True)

title: alto.lessons.clef_basics
text: alto.lessons.clef_basics The lesson on clefs, taught from nothing. It covers what a clef does, the three symbols (the G, C and F clef) and the line each clef puts them on, the way every C clef points at middle C, and the rarer clefs. Examples >>> len ( CLEF_BASICS . steps ) 10 >>> symbol_task ( random . Random ( 1 )). choices ('G clef', 'C clef', 'F clef')

title: alto.lessons.clef_basics
text: symbol_task def symbol_task ( rng : random . Random ) -> Task [Source] Ask which of the three symbols a clef is made with. Parameters rng ( random.Random ): Chooses the clef. Returns Task : A clef drawn on a staff, and a button for each symbol. Examples >>> task = symbol_task ( random . Random ( 2 )) >>> task . correct == CLEF_SYMBOL_NAMES [ ... SYMBOLS [ task . clef ] ... ] True

title: alto.lessons.clef_basics
text: identify_task def identify_task ( rng : random . Random ) -> Task [Source] Ask which clef is drawn on a staff. Parameters rng ( random.Random ): Chooses the clef. Returns Task : A clef drawn on a staff, and a button for each of the four everyday clefs. Examples >>> task = identify_task ( random . Random ( 3 )) >>> task . correct in task . choices and task . clef != "" True

title: alto.lessons.clef_basics
text: line_task def line_task ( rng : random . Random ) -> Task [Source] Ask which line of a blank staff a named clef is written on. Parameters rng ( random.Random ): Chooses the clef. Returns Task : A blank staff, and a button for each line. Examples >>> task = line_task ( random . Random ( 4 )) >>> task . correct in LINES and task . clef == "" True

title: alto.lessons.packs
text: alto.lessons.packs Turn the lessons that an instrument plugin declares into Lesson s that Alto lists and shows. A plugin describes each lesson in its manifest as plain text and small objects: paragraphs, an optional picture of its own instrument, notes to hear, and a question with buttons. This module checks all of that and builds the same Lesson and Step objects the built-in lessons use, so the lesson pages need to know nothing about any particular plugin or instrument. Examples >>> inline ( "A **scroll** is the carved end." ) 'A scroll is the carved end.'

title: alto.lessons.packs
text: inline def inline ( text : str ) -> str [Source] Escape plain text for a lesson page, turning **word** into bold type for a term being defined. Parameters text ( str ): Plain text from a manifest. Returns str : Simple HTML. Examples >>> inline ( "The **nut** & the bridge." ) 'The nut & the bridge.'

title: alto.lessons.packs
text: read_lessons def read_lessons ( value : object , * , pack_id : str , pack_name : str , instruments : Mapping [ str , PackInstrument ], exercises : Mapping [ str , str ], icons : Mapping [ str , str ] | None = None , ) -> tuple [ Lesson , ...] [Source] Validate the optional lessons list of a plugin manifest and build its lessons. Parameters value ( object ): The manifest’s lessons entry, or None when the plugin has no lessons. pack_id ( str ): The plugin’s id, which qualifies each lesson’s key. Keyword-only. pack_name ( str ): The plugin’s display name, used as a lesson’s category when it names none. Keyword-only. instruments ( mapping of str to PackInstrument ): The plugin’s instruments by qualified key, which pictures and sounds refer to. Keyword-only. exercises ( mapping of str to str ): The plugin’s exercises, from the id the manifest uses to the key Alto registers it under. Keyword-only. icons ( mapping of str to str or None, default None ): The plugin’s icons by the file name the manifest uses, already read. Keyword-only. Returns tuple of Lesson : The lessons, in the order the manifest lists them. Raises ValueError : If a lesson, step, picture, or question is malformed, or refers to something the plugin does not declare. Examples >>> read_lessons ( ... None , ... pack_id = "demo" , ... pack_name = "Demo" , ... instruments = {}, ... exercises = {}, ... ) ()

title: alto.lessons.packs
text: read_picture def read_picture ( spec : object , * , where : str , pack_id : str , instruments : Mapping [ str , PackInstrument ], ) -> PicturePosition | FingerboardPosition [Source] Build a step’s instrument picture: a note on a string, or a marked place on the picture. Parameters spec ( object ): The picture’s manifest object. Give string and note for a note on a string, or point for a place. where ( str ): Which lesson and step this is, for messages. Keyword-only. pack_id ( str ): The plugin’s id. Keyword-only. instruments ( mapping of str to PackInstrument ): The plugin’s instruments by qualified key. Keyword-only. Returns PicturePosition or FingerboardPosition : What the step’s picture shows. Raises ValueError : If the picture is malformed or refers to something the plugin does not declare.

title: alto.location
text: alto.location Where Alto keeps its practice history and its settings, and how to keep them somewhere else with ALTO_HOME . Without ALTO_HOME they are in the usual places for the system. With it, both are in that folder instead, so a copy of Alto that is being worked on can have its own history and settings, apart from the copy that is used for practicing. Examples >>> database_path ( ... environ = { "ALTO_HOME" : "/tmp/alto-dev" } ... ). as_posix () '/tmp/alto-dev/data/alto.db'

title: alto.location
text: alto_home def alto_home ( * , environ : Mapping [ str , str ] = os . environ , ) -> Path | None [Source] Give the folder named by ALTO_HOME , if there is one. Parameters environ ( mapping of str to str ): The environment to read. Keyword-only. Returns Path or None : The folder, with ~ expanded and made absolute, or None if ALTO_HOME is not set or is empty. Examples >>> alto_home ( environ = {}) is None True >>> alto_home ( environ = { "ALTO_HOME" : "" }) is None True >>> str ( ... alto_home ( ... environ = { ... "ALTO_HOME" : "/tmp/alto-dev" ... } ... ) ... ) '/tmp/alto-dev' >>> alto_home ( ... environ = { "ALTO_HOME" : "~/alto-dev" } ... ) == Path . home () / "alto-dev" True

title: alto.location
text: database_path def database_path ( * , environ : Mapping [ str , str ] = os . environ , ) -> Path [Source] Give the file that holds the practice history. Parameters environ ( mapping of str to str ): The environment to read. Keyword-only. Returns Path : data/alto.db in the ALTO_HOME folder if there is one, otherwise alto.db in the system’s data folder for Alto. The folder need not exist yet. Examples >>> database_path ( ... environ = { "ALTO_HOME" : "/tmp/alto-dev" } ... ). as_posix () '/tmp/alto-dev/data/alto.db' >>> database_path ( environ = {}). name 'alto.db'

title: alto.location
text: settings_folder def settings_folder ( * , environ : Mapping [ str , str ] = os . environ , ) -> Path | None [Source] Give the folder that holds the settings when ALTO_HOME moves them. Parameters environ ( mapping of str to str ): The environment to read. Keyword-only. Returns Path or None : config in the ALTO_HOME folder, or None if the settings are in the system’s usual place. Examples >>> settings_folder ( environ = {}) is None True >>> str ( ... settings_folder ( ... environ = { ... "ALTO_HOME" : "/tmp/alto-dev" ... } ... ) ... ) '/tmp/alto-dev/config'

title: alto.location
text: desktop_name def desktop_name ( * , environ : Mapping [ str , str ] = os . environ , ) -> str [Source] Give the name the desktop uses to match Alto’s window to its menu entry, and so to its icon in the dock. Parameters environ ( mapping of str to str ): The environment to read. Keyword-only. Returns str : “alto”, or “alto-dev” when ALTO_HOME keeps a second copy apart, so that the two copies are separate in the dock. Examples >>> ( ... desktop_name ( environ = {}), ... desktop_name ( ... environ = { ... "ALTO_HOME" : "/tmp/alto-dev" ... } ... ), ... ) ('alto', 'alto-dev')
