title: alto.plugin_registry
text: install_registered def install_registered ( code : str , * , folder : Path , selected : InstalledPlugin | None = None , ) -> str | None [Source] Install by registration code, or update a selected ZIP from its registered repository. Parameters code ( str ): The published code, including any leading zeros. Updates recover the code from the installation or its registered pack ID. folder ( Path ): The plugins directory. selected ( InstalledPlugin or None ): The installed ZIP to update. Editable directories stay under the author’s control. Returns str or None : The installed pack name and release tag, or None if the installed ZIP already matches the latest asset. Raises ValueError : If registration, release selection, integrity checks, or pack validation fails.

title: alto.selfupdate
text: alto.selfupdate Replacing a packaged copy of Alto with a newer release: whether it can, getting the update, checking it, and handing over. A packaged copy is Alto frozen with PyInstaller, in a folder the user owns: ~/.local/opt/alto on Linux, made by install.sh , and a folder under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs on Windows, made by the installer. Neither needs administrator rights, so Alto can fetch the new package, check it, and start the program that installs it. Nothing is installed unless the signature on the list of checksums verifies against a key that came with Alto, the list names the file, and the file’s hash is the one listed (see alto.updates ). This module has no Qt, so the interface runs it on a worker thread and shows its progress. Examples >>> self_update_target ( ... executable = Path ( "/nowhere/alto" ), ... system = "linux" , ... ) is None True

title: alto.selfupdate
text: UpdateError class UpdateError ( Exception ) [Source] Something went wrong in getting or checking an update. The message says what, in words for the person.

title: alto.selfupdate
text: UpdateCanceled class UpdateCanceled ( Exception ) [Source] The person canceled the update before it was ready.

title: alto.selfupdate
text: Target Target ( system : str , folder : Path , prefix : Path | None , ) [Source] A packaged copy that can replace itself, and where it is. Attributes system ( str ): “linux” or “windows”. folder ( Path ): The folder the program is in. prefix ( Path or None ): On Linux, the folder that holds opt/alto and bin/alto ( ~/.local by default); None on Windows. Examples >>> Target ( ... "windows" , ... folder = Path ( "C:/Alto" ), ... prefix = None , ... ). system 'windows'

title: alto.selfupdate
text: Prepared Prepared ( work : Path , installer : Path | None , root : Path | None , ) [Source] An update that has been downloaded and checked, and is ready to be handed over. Attributes work ( Path ): The temporary folder that holds it, which is removed after the update. installer ( Path or None ): On Windows, the installer to run. root ( Path or None ): On Linux, the unpacked download, with its install.sh . Examples >>> Prepared ( ... Path ( "/tmp/x" ), ... installer = None , ... root = Path ( "/tmp/x/unpacked/alto-0.1.0" ), ... ). installer is None True

title: alto.selfupdate
text: self_update_target def self_update_target ( * , executable : Path | None = None , system : str | None = None , ) -> Target | None [Source] Say whether the running copy can replace itself, and if so where it is. On Linux a copy can if it was put in <prefix>/opt/alto by install.sh , which links <prefix>/bin/alto to it; a folder that someone unpacked and ran from cannot. On Windows a copy can if the installer made it, which leaves unins000.exe beside it. Parameters executable ( Path or None, default None ): The running program; the one that is running if None. Keyword-only. system ( str or None, default None ): “linux” or “windows”; this computer’s if None. Keyword-only. Returns Target or None : Where the copy is, or None if it cannot replace itself. Examples >>> self_update_target ( ... executable = Path ( "/usr/bin/python3" ), ... system = "linux" , ... ) is None True >>> self_update_target ( ... executable = Path ( "/nowhere/alto.exe" ), ... system = "windows" , ... ) is None True

title: alto.selfupdate
text: download def download ( url : str , * , destination : Path , allowed : str , max_bytes : int , progress : Callable [[ int , int ], None ], canceled : Callable [[], bool ], seconds : int = 30 , ) -> str [Source] Fetch a file, checking the address, the size and the connection, and give its SHA-256 hash. Parameters url ( str ): The address. It must start with allowed . destination ( Path ): Where to write the file. Nothing is left there if the download fails or is canceled. Keyword-only. allowed ( str ): What the address must start with, which is where a release keeps its files. Keyword-only. max_bytes ( int ): The most to accept, by the size the server states and by what actually arrives. Keyword-only. progress ( Callable ): Called with the bytes received so far and the size the server states (0 if it does not say). Keyword-only. canceled ( Callable ): Asked now and then; True stops the download. Keyword-only. seconds ( int, default 30 ): How long to wait for the server at a time. Keyword-only. Returns str : The SHA-256 hash of what was written, in hexadecimal. Raises UpdateError : If the address is not allowed, the file is too large, the connection is not secure, or the download fails. UpdateCanceled : If canceled said so.

title: alto.selfupdate
text: extract_tarball def extract_tarball ( archive : Path , * , destination : Path , ) -> Path [Source] Unpack the Linux download, refusing anything that would land outside the folder. Parameters archive ( Path ): The .tar.gz . destination ( Path ): The folder to unpack it in. Keyword-only. Returns Path : The one folder the download unpacks to, which holds install.sh and the program. Raises UpdateError : If it cannot be unpacked safely, or is not what an update needs.

title: alto.selfupdate
text: ignore_progress def ignore_progress ( done : int , total : int , ) -> None [Source] Take a note of progress and do nothing with it, for a download whose progress nobody watches. Parameters done ( int ): The bytes received so far. total ( int ): The total the server states. Examples >>> ignore_progress ( 1 , 2 )

title: alto.selfupdate
text: prepare_update def prepare_update ( release : updates . Release , * , target : Target , work : Path , keys : tuple [ str , ...], machine : str , base : str = updates . DOWNLOAD_BASE , status : Callable [[ str ], None ], progress : Callable [[ int , int ], None ], canceled : Callable [[], bool ], ) -> Prepared [Source] Download a release for this copy and check it: its signed list of checksums, then the file against its listed hash. Parameters release ( updates.Release ): The release to install. target ( Target ): The copy that will be replaced. work ( Path ): An empty folder to work in. keys ( tuple of str ): The public keys (base64) a signature may be made with. Keyword-only. machine ( str ): The processor, as platform.machine() says it. Keyword-only. base ( str, default updates.DOWNLOAD_BASE ): Where the release keeps its files. Keyword-only. status ( Callable ): Called with what is being done, in words for the person. Keyword-only. progress ( Callable ): Called with the bytes received so far and the total, while the file downloads. Keyword-only. canceled ( Callable ): Asked now and then; True stops. Keyword-only. Returns Prepared : The checked update, ready to be handed over. Raises UpdateError : If anything is missing or does not check out. Nothing is installed. UpdateCanceled : If canceled said so.

title: alto.selfupdate
text: clean_environment def clean_environment ( env : Mapping [ str , str ]) -> dict [ str , str ] [Source] Undo what PyInstaller did to the environment, for a program that this one starts. A packaged program puts its own libraries first on the library path, which would make the system’s sh , tar and the next Alto load them. PyInstaller keeps the original in LD_LIBRARY_PATH_ORIG , and asks a program that restarts itself to reset what it passed on. The desktop’s start-up token is for this launch only, so it is dropped too. Parameters env ( Mapping ): The environment of this program. Returns dict of str to str : The environment to give the other. Examples >>> clean_environment ( ... { ... "LD_LIBRARY_PATH" : "/app/lib" , ... "LD_LIBRARY_PATH_ORIG" : "/usr/lib" , ... "_PYI_ARCHIVE_FILE" : "x" , ... } ... ) {'LD_LIBRARY_PATH': '/usr/lib', 'PYINSTALLER_RESET_ENVIRONMENT': '1'} >>> clean_environment ( ... { ... "LD_LIBRARY_PATH" : "/app/lib" , ... "LD_LIBRARY_PATH_ORIG" : "" , ... } ... ) {'PYINSTALLER_RESET_ENVIRONMENT': '1'} >>> clean_environment ({ "HOME" : "/home/me" }) {'HOME': '/home/me', 'PYINSTALLER_RESET_ENVIRONMENT': '1'}

title: alto.selfupdate
text: log_path def log_path () -> Path [Source] Give the file the Linux helper writes to, so that a failed update can be looked into. Returns Path : update.log in Alto’s folder of the user’s cache. Examples >>> log_path (). name 'update.log'

title: alto.selfupdate
text: windows_handoff_command def windows_handoff_command ( installer : Path , * , pid : int , alto : Path , ) -> list [ str ] [Source] Give the command that waits for Alto to end, runs the installer, and starts the old Alto again if the installer fails. The installer must not start while Alto is still closing: it would find Alto’s files in use and, with no one to answer, give up. So Alto starts this command and quits, and the command waits for Alto’s process to be gone before it begins. Parameters installer ( Path ): The downloaded installer. pid ( int ): Alto’s process, which is waited for (for at most a minute). Keyword-only. alto ( Path ): The installed alto.exe , which is started again if the installer fails, so that the person is not left with no Alto. When it succeeds, the installer starts Alto itself ( /RELAUNCH=1 ). Keyword-only. Returns list of str : The program and its arguments. Examples >>> command = windows_handoff_command ( ... Path ( "C:/Temp/setup.exe" ), ... pid = 42 , ... alto = Path ( "C:/Alto/alto.exe" ), ... ) >>> ( ... command [ 0 ], ... command [ 1 : - 1 ] ... == list ( POWERSHELL_ARGUMENTS ), ... ) ('powershell.exe', True) >>> text = base64 . b64decode ( command [ - 1 ]). decode ( ... "utf-16-le" ... ) >>> "Wait-Process -Id 42" in text and "/RELAUNCH=1" in text True

title: alto.selfupdate
text: start_handoff def start_handoff ( prepared : Prepared , * , target : Target , pid : int | None = None , log : Path | None = None , environ : Mapping [ str , str ] | None = None , ) -> None [Source] Start the program that installs the update, and return at once so that Alto can quit. Parameters prepared ( Prepared ): The checked update. target ( Target ): The copy that is replaced. pid ( int or None, default None ): The process to wait for, which is Alto; this one if None. Keyword-only. log ( Path or None, default None ): Where the Linux helper writes; log_path() if None. Keyword-only. environ ( Mapping or None, default None ): The environment to start from; this program’s if None. Keyword-only. Raises UpdateError : If the update is missing what the system needs.

title: alto.selfupdate
text: new_work_folder def new_work_folder () -> Path [Source] Make a new temporary folder for an update, whose name says what it is for. Returns Path : The empty folder. Examples >>> folder = new_work_folder () >>> folder . is_dir () and folder . name . startswith ( ... LEFTOVER_PREFIX ... ) True >>> folder . rmdir ()

title: alto.selfupdate
text: remove_leftovers def remove_leftovers ( * , older_than : float = 86400.0 , now : float | None = None , root : Path | None = None , ) -> int [Source] Remove the temporary folders of earlier updates that were never cleaned up, such as a Windows installer that was run and left. Parameters older_than ( float, default 86400.0 ): How old, in seconds, a folder must be. Keyword-only. now ( float or None, default None ): The time to measure from; the clock’s if None. Keyword-only. root ( Path or None, default None ): The folder to look in; the system’s temporary folder if None. Keyword-only. Returns int : How many folders were removed. Examples >>> remove_leftovers ( ... root = Path ( "/no/such/folder" ) ... ) 0

title: alto.settings
text: alto.settings User settings. Pure Python (no Qt); persistence lives in ui/exercise_settings.py. Each exercise with settings has a small dataclass here ( NoteNameSettings , KeyboardSettings and so on) and one shared instance of it ( note_names , keyboard …) that the exercise and its settings panel both read and write. Examples >>> NoteNameSettings (). active_clefs () ['treble', 'bass'] >>> spell ( Note . parse ( "F#4" )) 'F♯'

title: alto.settings
text: spell def spell ( note : Note , * , naming : str = 'letters' , key : int = 0 , octave : bool = False , minor : bool = False , ) -> str [Source] Return a note name in the chosen naming system, optionally including its octave. Parameters note ( Note ): The note. naming ( str, default “letters” ): “letters” for C D E, “solfege” for Do Re Mi, “degrees” for caret scale degrees, or “functions” for function names. Keyword-only. key ( int, default 0 ): The major key signature for scale degrees: sharps if positive, flats if negative. Zero means C major. Keyword-only. octave ( bool, default False ): Include the note’s octave, separated from a scale degree by “ / “. Keyword-only. minor ( bool, default False ): Use the relative natural minor as the scale degree reference. Keyword-only. Returns str : The name and, if requested, octave. Carets use accidental prefixes; function names use Raised or Lowered prefixes. Examples >>> spell ( Note . parse ( "F#4" )) 'F♯' >>> spell ( Note . parse ( "F#4" ), naming = "solfege" ) 'Fa♯' >>> spell ( ... Note . parse ( "F#4" ), ... naming = "degrees" , ... key = 1 , ... ) '7̂' >>> spell ( ... Note . parse ( "F4" ), ... naming = "degrees" , ... key = 1 , ... ) '♭7̂' >>> spell ( Note . parse ( "Eb4" ), naming = "degrees" ) '♭3̂' >>> spell ( ... Note . parse ( "G4" ), ... naming = "functions" , ... key = 1 , ... ) 'Tonic' >>> spell ( ... Note . parse ( "F4" ), ... naming = "functions" , ... key = 1 , ... ) 'Lowered Leading tone' >>> spell ( ... Note . parse ( "G4" ), ... naming = "degrees" , ... key = 1 , ... octave = True , ... ) '1̂ / 4'

title: alto.settings
text: diatonic_name def diatonic_name ( d : int ) -> str [Source] Return the name and octave of the natural note on a staff step. Parameters d ( int ): The staff-step index (see Note.diatonic ). Returns str : For example ‘E4’. Examples >>> diatonic_name ( 30 ) 'E4'

title: alto.settings
text: ClefChoice class ClefChoice [Source] Settings with a set of chosen clefs, which are always used in the same order. Attributes CLEF_ORDER ( tuple of str ): Every clef the settings may hold, in the order they are offered and used. Each subclass sets it. clefs ( set of str ): The chosen clefs. The dataclass that uses this mixin declares the field and its default. Examples >>> ArpeggioSettings ( ... clefs = { "tenor" , "alto" } ... ). active_clefs () ['alto', 'tenor']

title: alto.settings
text: ClefChoice.active_clefs def active_clefs () -> list [ str ] [Source] Return the clefs to use, in canonical order. Returns list of str : The chosen clefs in the order of CLEF_ORDER , or the treble clef if none are chosen. Examples >>> NoteNameSettings ( ... clefs = { "grand" , "tenor" } ... ). active_clefs () ['tenor', 'grand'] >>> ClefBasicsSettings ( ... clefs = { "subbass" , "treble" } ... ). active_clefs () ['treble', 'subbass'] >>> NoteNameSettings ( clefs = set ()). active_clefs () ['treble']

title: alto.settings
text: KeyChoice class KeyChoice [Source] Settings with a set of chosen key signatures. Attributes keys ( set of int ): The chosen key signatures, as sharps (positive) or flats (negative). The dataclass that uses this mixin declares the field and its default. Examples >>> KeyboardSettings ( keys = { 3 , - 2 }). active_keys () [-2, 3]

title: alto.settings
text: KeyChoice.active_keys def active_keys () -> list [ int ] [Source] Return the key signatures to draw from, lowest first. Returns list of int : Sharps (positive) or flats (negative); no sharps or flats if none are chosen. Examples >>> ConstructionSettings ( ... keys = { 2 , - 1 } ... ). active_keys () [-1, 2] >>> KeySignatureSettings ( ... keys = set () ... ). active_keys () [0]

title: alto.settings
text: StaffRangeSettings StaffRangeSettings ( clefs : set [ str ] = field ( default_factory = lambda : { 'treble' , 'bass' }), * , ranges : dict [ str , tuple [ int , int ]] = field ( default_factory = dict ), note_values : set [ str ] = field ( default_factory = lambda : { 'whole' }), ) [Source] Bases: ClefChoice Selected clefs and inclusive pitch limits for each staff. Examples >>> StaffRangeSettings (). active_clefs () ['treble', 'bass']

title: alto.settings
text: StaffRangeSettings.active_values def active_values () -> list [ str ] [Source] Return the note values to draw, from longest to shortest. Returns list of str : The chosen values in the order of NOTE_VALUES , or whole notes if none are chosen. Examples >>> NoteNameSettings ( ... note_values = { "half" , "whole" } ... ). active_values () ['whole', 'half']

title: alto.settings
text: StaffRangeSettings.range_for def range_for ( clef : str ) -> tuple [ int , int ] [Source] Return the range of notes that may be asked on a clef. Parameters clef ( str ): A key of DEFAULT_RANGES . Returns tuple of (int, int) : The lowest and highest staff step, inclusive; the user’s override if there is one, otherwise the default. Examples >>> NoteNameSettings (). range_for ( "treble" ) (22, 52) >>> NoteNameSettings ( ... ranges = { "treble" : ( 40 , 30 )} ... ). range_for ( ... "treble" ... ) # given in the wrong order (30, 40)

title: alto.settings
text: NoteNameSettings NoteNameSettings ( * , key_signatures : set [ int ] = field ( default_factory = lambda : { 0 }), naming : str = 'letters' , minor_degrees : bool = False , accidentals : bool = False , require_octave : bool = False , ) [Source] Bases: StaffRangeSettings The settings of the note identification exercise. Attributes clefs ( set of str ): The clefs to ask on, any of RANGE_KEYS , so “grand” is allowed. ranges ( dict of str to tuple of (int, int) ): Overrides of DEFAULT_RANGES , as inclusive staff-step ranges. Keyword-only. key_signatures ( set of int ): The keys to use, as sharps (positive) or flats (negative). Keyword-only. note_values ( set of str ): The note values to draw, from NOTE_VALUES . Keyword-only. naming ( str, default “letters” ): A key of NAMINGS . Keyword-only. accidentals ( bool, default False ): Also ask notes with explicit sharps, flats and naturals. Keyword-only. require_octave ( bool, default False ): Also require the written octave as part of the answer. Keyword-only. Examples >>> cfg = NoteNameSettings ( ... clefs = { "bass" }, key_signatures = { 2 } ... ) >>> cfg . active_clefs (), cfg . active_keys () (['bass'], [2])

title: alto.settings
text: NoteNameSettings.active_keys def active_keys () -> list [ int ] [Source] Return the key signatures to draw from, lowest first. The field is named key_signatures rather than keys , as in KeyChoice , because the name is part of the practice signature that stored questions are matched by; renaming it would orphan every learner’s saved questions. Returns list of int : Sharps (positive) or flats (negative); no sharps or flats if none are chosen. Examples >>> NoteNameSettings ( ... key_signatures = { 2 , - 1 } ... ). active_keys () [-1, 2]

title: alto.settings
text: PackExerciseSettings PackExerciseSettings ( * , sound : str | None = None , accidentals : bool = False , require_octave : bool = False , keys : tuple [ int , int ] | None = None , intervals : frozenset [ str ] | None = None , manuals : frozenset [ str ] | None = None , ) [Source] Bases: StaffRangeSettings The options a plugin’s exercise offers the learner, such as its range and whether to ask accidentals. Only the options the plugin declares for the exercise are shown and used; the rest keep their defaults. Attributes clefs ( set of str ): The one clef the exercise’s range is drawn on. ranges ( dict of str to tuple of (int, int) ): The range of notes asked, as staff steps, under the clef. sound ( str or None, default None ): The key of the instrument that sounds in this exercise instead of the plugin’s own, or None for the plugin’s own. Keyword-only. accidentals ( bool, default False ): Also ask the notes between the listed ones, written with sharps or flats. Keyword-only. require_octave ( bool, default False ): The answer also includes the note’s written octave. Keyword-only. keys ( tuple of int or None, default None ): For a keyboard interval exercise, the lowest and highest key asked, as MIDI numbers. None asks the plugin’s own default range. Keyword-only. intervals ( frozenset of str or None, default None ): For a keyboard interval exercise, the names of the intervals asked. None asks every interval the plugin lists. Keyword-only. manuals ( frozenset of str or None, default None ): For a keyboard interval exercise, the names of the keyboards the highlighted keys may sit on. None uses them all. Keyword-only. Examples >>> PackExerciseSettings ( ... clefs = { "alto" } ... ). sound is None True >>> PackExerciseSettings ( ... clefs = { "alto" } ... ). keys is None True

title: alto.settings
text: IntervalSettings IntervalSettings ( * , staff_keys : set [ int ] = field ( default_factory = lambda : { 0 }), displays : set [ str ] = field ( default_factory = lambda : { 'Harmonic' }), directions : set [ str ] = field ( default_factory = lambda : { 'ascending' }), button_mode : str = 'limited' , button_count : int = 6 , accidentals : set [ int ] = field ( default_factory = lambda : set ( DEFAULT_INTERVAL_ACCIDENTALS )), quality_mode : str = 'combined' , inversions : bool = False , consonance : bool = False , intervals : set [ str ] = field ( default_factory = lambda : { name for name , iv in WRITTEN_INTERVALS . items () if 2 <= iv . number <= 7 or name == 'P8' }), ) [Source] Bases: StaffRangeSettings Staff signatures, presentations, answer format and spelled intervals for Interval Identification. Examples >>> IntervalSettings (). quality_mode 'combined'

title: alto.settings
text: IntervalSettings.staff_span def staff_span ( clef : str ) -> int [Source] Count the written staff positions in a clef’s selected range, including both endpoints. Parameters clef ( str ): The clef whose range to measure. Returns int : The largest diatonic interval number that fits. Examples >>> IntervalSettings ( ... ranges = { "treble" : ( 28 , 30 )} ... ). staff_span ( "treble" ) 3

title: alto.settings
text: key_name def key_name ( midi : int ) -> str [Source] Return the name of a MIDI note with its octave, black keys as sharps. Parameters midi ( int ): The MIDI note number. Returns str : For example ‘C4’ for 60 and ‘C♯4’ for 61. Examples >>> key_name ( 60 ), key_name ( 61 ) ('C4', 'C♯4')

title: alto.settings
text: KeyboardSettings KeyboardSettings ( black_keys : bool = True , * , naming : str = 'letters' , require_octave : bool = False , low : int = KEYBOARD_DEFAULT [ 0 ], high : int = KEYBOARD_DEFAULT [ 1 ], key_signature : bool = False , keys : set [ int ] = field ( default_factory = lambda : { - 3 , - 2 , - 1 , 0 , 1 , 2 , 3 }), ) [Source] Bases: KeyChoice The settings of the keyboard identification exercise. Attributes naming ( str, default “letters” ): Naming system for the highlighted key. Keyword-only. black_keys ( bool, default True ): Also ask the black keys, answered by either enharmonic name. require_octave ( bool, default False ): The answer must include the octave number as well. Keyword-only. low ( int ): The lowest key asked, as a MIDI number. Keyword-only. high ( int ): The highest key asked, as a MIDI number, inclusive. Keyword-only. key_signature ( bool, default False ): Show a key signature, and require the name that fits it (no enharmonic spelling). Keyword-only. keys ( set of int ): The key signatures to draw from, as sharps (positive) or flats (negative). Keyword-only. Examples >>> cfg = KeyboardSettings () >>> key_name ( cfg . low ), key_name ( cfg . high ) ('C3', 'C5')

title: alto.settings
text: keyboard_interval_name def keyboard_interval_name ( distance : int ) -> str [Source] Name a keyboard interval by its distance, including compound intervals. Parameters distance ( int ): The distance in half steps, from 1 through the full piano span. Returns str : A conventional interval name, with both spellings for tritones. Raises ValueError : If the distance cannot occur between two distinct piano keys. Examples >>> ( ... keyboard_interval_name ( 13 ), ... keyboard_interval_name ( 18 ), ... keyboard_interval_name ( 24 ), ... ) ('m9', 'A11 / d12', 'P15') >>> keyboard_interval_name ( 87 ) 'm52'

title: alto.settings
text: KeyboardIntervalSettings KeyboardIntervalSettings ( low : int = KEYBOARD_DEFAULT [ 0 ], high : int = KEYBOARD_DEFAULT [ 1 ], intervals : set [ int ] = field ( default_factory = lambda : set ( range ( 1 , 13 ))), all_interval_buttons : bool = False , compact_buttons : bool = False , button_count : int = 6 , ) [Source] The keyboard range and interval distances used for keyboard interval identification. Attributes low ( int ): The lowest key, as a MIDI number. Keyword-only. high ( int ): The highest key, inclusive. Keyword-only. intervals ( set of int ): Selected distances in half steps, up to the full piano span. Keyword-only. button_count ( int, default 6 ): Maximum answer buttons in limited mode. Keyword-only. compact_buttons ( bool, default False ): Answer with separate quality-letter and interval-number buttons. Keyword-only. all_interval_buttons ( bool, default False ): Show a fixed answer button for every selected interval instead of a limited number of choices. Keyword-only. Examples >>> KeyboardIntervalSettings (). bounds () (48, 72)

title: alto.settings
text: KeyboardIntervalSettings.answer_button_limit def answer_button_limit () -> int [Source] Return the requested count within the supported range of 1 to 87 buttons. Returns int : The bounded maximum number of answer buttons in limited mode. Examples >>> KeyboardIntervalSettings (). answer_button_limit () 6 >>> KeyboardIntervalSettings ( ... button_count = 0 ... ). answer_button_limit () 1

title: alto.settings
text: KeyboardIntervalSettings.bounds def bounds () -> tuple [ int , int ] [Source] Return a piano range containing at least two distinct keys. Returns tuple of (int, int) : Sorted bounds within the full piano range, widened by one key if necessary. Examples >>> KeyboardIntervalSettings ( ... low = 60 , high = 60 ... ). bounds () (60, 61)

title: alto.settings
text: KeyboardIntervalSettings.active_intervals def active_intervals () -> list [ int ] [Source] Return selected interval distances that fit the keyboard range. Returns list of int : Sorted positive distances that fit; empty if none are selected. Invalid nonempty selections use a minor second. Examples >>> KeyboardIntervalSettings ( ... low = 60 , high = 64 , intervals = { 3 , 4 , 12 } ... ). active_intervals () [3, 4] >>> KeyboardIntervalSettings ( ... intervals = set () ... ). active_intervals () []

title: alto.settings
text: ConstructionSettings ConstructionSettings ( clefs : set [ str ] = field ( default_factory = lambda : { 'treble' , 'bass' }), * , accidentals : bool = False , key_signature : bool = False , question_type : str = 'scale' , degrees : set [ int ] = field ( default_factory = lambda : set ( range ( 1 , 8 ))), octave : bool = True , staff_keys : set [ int ] | None = None , major : bool = True , minor : bool = False , keys : set [ int ] = field ( default_factory = lambda : { - 3 , - 2 , - 1 , 0 , 1 , 2 , 3 }), minor_keys : set [ int ] | None = None , ) [Source] Bases: ClefChoice, KeyChoice The settings of the note construction exercise. Attributes clefs ( set of str ): The clefs to ask on, any of RANGE_KEYS , so “grand” is allowed. accidentals ( bool, default False ): Also ask for sharps and flats, which the answer then has to include. Keyword-only. key_signature ( bool, default False ): Draw a key signature; it applies to the note unless the note is given its own sign. Keyword-only. question_type ( str, default “scale” ): Use the selected scale keys or ask for notes without a scale key. Keyword-only. degrees ( set of int ): Scale degrees to ask for in Scale and Degree mode. Keyword-only. octave ( bool, default True ): Require the note to be placed in a specific octave. Keyword-only. staff_keys ( set of int or None ): Staff signatures chosen independently. None uses the question key. Keyword-only. major ( bool, default True ): Use major keys. With key signatures off, use C major. Keyword-only. minor ( bool, default False ): Use relative minor keys. With key signatures off, use A minor. Keyword-only. keys ( set of int ): The key signatures to draw from, as sharps (positive) or flats (negative). Keyword-only. minor_keys ( set of int or None ): Signatures selected for minor keys. None uses the original shared selection. Keyword-only. Examples >>> ConstructionSettings ( ... clefs = { "grand" } ... ). active_clefs () ['grand']

title: alto.settings
text: ArpeggioSettings ArpeggioSettings ( clefs : set [ str ] = field ( default_factory = lambda : { 'treble' , 'bass' }), * , types : set [ str ] = field ( default_factory = lambda : { 'major' , 'minor' , 'dominant 7th' , 'diminished 7th' }), inversions : set [ int ] = field ( default_factory = lambda : set ( INVERSIONS )), key_signature : bool = False , keys : set [ int ] = field ( default_factory = lambda : { - 3 , - 2 , - 1 , 0 , 1 , 2 , 3 }), ) [Source] Bases: ClefChoice, KeyChoice The settings of the arpeggio identification exercise. Attributes clefs ( set of str ): The clefs to draw on, any of CLEFS . types ( set of str ): The chord types to ask, from ARPEGGIO_TYPES . Keyword-only. inversions ( set of int ): The inversions to ask: 0 for root position up to 3 for the third inversion. Keyword-only. key_signature ( bool, default False ): Draw a key signature, so the arpeggio only gets signs where it differs from it. Keyword-only. keys ( set of int ): The key signatures to draw from, as sharps (positive) or flats (negative). Keyword-only. Examples >>> ArpeggioSettings (). active_types () ['major', 'minor', 'dominant 7th', 'diminished 7th']

title: alto.settings
text: ArpeggioSettings.active_types def active_types () -> list [ str ] [Source] Return the chord types to ask, triads first and then seventh chords. Returns list of str : The chosen types in the order of ARPEGGIO_TYPES , or “major” if none are chosen. Examples >>> ArpeggioSettings ( ... types = { "minor 7th" , "major" } ... ). active_types () ['major', 'minor 7th']

title: alto.settings
text: ArpeggioSettings.active_inversions def active_inversions () -> list [ int ] [Source] Return the inversions to ask, root position first. Returns list of int : The chosen inversions, or root position (0) if none are chosen. Examples >>> ArpeggioSettings ( ... inversions = { 2 , 0 } ... ). active_inversions () [0, 2]

title: alto.settings
text: ArpeggioSettings.inversions_for def inversions_for ( chord_type : str ) -> list [ int ] [Source] Return the inversions that can be asked for a chord type. A triad has no third inversion. If none of the chosen inversions applies (only the third, for a triad), root position is used. Parameters chord_type ( str ): A key of CHORDS , such as “major” or “dominant 7th”. Returns list of int : The inversions to choose from. Examples >>> cfg = ArpeggioSettings () >>> ( ... cfg . inversions_for ( "major" ), ... cfg . inversions_for ( "dominant 7th" ), ... ) ([0, 1, 2], [0, 1, 2, 3]) >>> ArpeggioSettings ( ... inversions = { 3 } ... ). inversions_for ( "major" ) [0]

title: alto.settings
text: KeySignatureSettings KeySignatureSettings ( * , clefs : set [ str ] = field ( default_factory = lambda : { 'treble' , 'bass' }), modes : set [ str ] = field ( default_factory = lambda : { 'Major (Ionian)' , 'Natural minor (Aeolian)' }), keys : set [ int ] = field ( default_factory = lambda : set ( range ( - 7 , 8 ))), ) [Source] Bases: ClefChoice, KeyChoice The settings of the key signature identification exercise. Attributes clefs ( set of str ): The clefs a signature is drawn on, any of CLEFS . Keyword-only. modes ( set of str ): The scales to ask about, from KEY_MODES . Keyword-only. keys ( set of int ): The key signatures asked, as sharps (positive) or flats (negative). Keyword-only. Examples >>> cfg = KeySignatureSettings () >>> cfg . active_clefs (), len ( cfg . active_keys ()) (['treble', 'bass'], 15)

title: alto.settings
text: KeySignatureSettings.active_modes def active_modes () -> list [ str ] [Source] Return the scales to ask about, in the order of KEY_MODES . Returns list of str : The chosen modes, or major if none are chosen. Examples >>> KeySignatureSettings (). active_modes () ['Major (Ionian)', 'Natural minor (Aeolian)']

title: alto.settings
text: OrderOfKeysSettings OrderOfKeysSettings ( * , starting_accidentals : set [ int ] = field ( default_factory = lambda : { 0 }), ) [Source] Bases: KeySignatureSettings Choose the starting signs for writing a key signature. Attributes starting_accidentals ( set of int ): Allowed counts of given signs. Negative counts represent flats and positive counts represent sharps. Examples >>> OrderOfKeysSettings ( ... keys = { - 2 , 4 } ... ). available_starts () range(-2, 5)

title: alto.settings
text: OrderOfKeysSettings.available_starts def available_starts () -> range [Source] Return starting counts that fit at least one selected signature. Returns range : Counts from the flattest eligible start through the sharpest, always including zero. Examples >>> list ( ... OrderOfKeysSettings ( ... keys = { - 2 } ... ). available_starts () ... ) [-2, -1, 0]

title: alto.settings
text: KeyConstructionSettings KeyConstructionSettings () [Source] Bases: KeySignatureSettings The settings of the key signature construction exercise: the same choices as key signature identification. Attributes clefs ( set of str ): The clefs the blank staff is drawn in, any of CLEFS . Keyword-only. modes ( set of str ): The scales to ask for, from KEY_MODES . Keyword-only. keys ( set of int ): The key signatures to build, as sharps (positive) or flats (negative). Keyword-only. Examples >>> cfg = KeyConstructionSettings ( keys = { - 2 }) >>> cfg . active_keys (), cfg . active_modes () ([-2], ['Major (Ionian)', 'Natural minor (Aeolian)'])

title: alto.settings
text: ScaleIdentificationSettings ScaleIdentificationSettings ( * , question_type : str = 'combined' , button_mode : str = 'limited' , button_count : int = 6 , minor_keys : set [ int ] | None = None , motion : str = 'ascending' , staff_keys : set [ int ] = field ( default_factory = lambda : { 0 }), ) [Source] Bases: KeySignatureSettings Choose the clefs, scale types and independent staff and scale key signatures for identification. Attributes staff_keys ( set of int ): Signatures drawn on the staff, independently of the scale’s own signature. Keyword-only. motion ( str, default “ascending” ): Direction of the scale, “ascending” or “descending”. Keyword-only. button_mode ( str, default “limited” ): Show a limited set of complete answers or separate tonic and mode buttons in “all” mode. Keyword-only. button_count ( int, default 6 ): Maximum number of answer buttons in limited mode. Keyword-only. question_type ( str, default “combined” ): Ask for the mode, the tonic (key), or both. Keyword-only. minor_keys ( set of int or None ): Signatures for natural minor. None uses the shared key selection. Keyword-only. Examples >>> cfg = ScaleIdentificationSettings ( ... keys = { 2 }, staff_keys = { - 3 } ... ) >>> cfg . active_keys (), cfg . active_staff_keys () ([2], [-3])

title: alto.settings
text: ScaleIdentificationSettings.active_staff_keys def active_staff_keys () -> list [ int ] [Source] Return the selected staff signatures, falling back to no signature. Returns list of int : Signature counts in ascending order. Examples >>> ScaleIdentificationSettings ( ... staff_keys = set () ... ). active_staff_keys () [0]

title: alto.settings
text: ScaleConstructionSettings ScaleConstructionSettings ( * , minor_keys : set [ int ] | None = None , motion : str = 'ascending' , steps : bool = False , octave : bool = False , staff_keys : set [ int ] = field ( default_factory = lambda : { 0 }), ) [Source] Bases: KeySignatureSettings The settings of the scale construction exercise: the same choices as key signature identification. Here “keys” chooses the scale by the signature it has: G major and E minor both have one sharp. staff_keys is a separate choice: the key signature drawn on the staff, which need not be the scale’s. On a staff with two flats a C major scale has to be placed with naturals where the staff would otherwise flatten the notes. Attributes clefs ( set of str ): The clefs the scale is placed on, any of CLEFS . Keyword-only. modes ( set of str ): The kinds of scale to ask for, from KEY_MODES . Keyword-only. keys ( set of int ): The key signatures the scales have, as sharps (positive) or flats (negative). Keyword-only. steps ( bool, default False ): Also mark the whole and half steps between the notes, once the notes are placed. Keyword-only. staff_keys ( set of int ): The key signatures that may be drawn on the staff, as sharps (positive) or flats (negative); 0 is none. Keyword-only. octave ( bool, default False ): Name the octave of the first note, such as “G2 Major”, and require the scale to start there; any scale asked then fits on the staff and its ledger lines. Without it any octave is accepted. Keyword-only. motion ( str, default “ascending” ): Direction of the scale, “ascending” or “descending”. Keyword-only. minor_keys ( set of int or None ): Signatures for natural minor. None uses the shared key selection. Keyword-only. Examples >>> cfg = ScaleConstructionSettings ( keys = { 3 }) >>> ( ... cfg . active_keys (), ... cfg . active_clefs (), ... cfg . steps , ... cfg . octave , ... cfg . active_staff_keys (), ... ) ([3], ['treble', 'bass'], False, False, [0])

title: alto.settings
text: ScaleConstructionSettings.active_staff_keys def active_staff_keys () -> list [ int ] [Source] Return the key signatures that may be drawn on the staff, lowest first. Returns list of int : Sharps (positive) or flats (negative); no sharps or flats if none are chosen. Examples >>> ScaleConstructionSettings ( ... staff_keys = { - 2 , 3 } ... ). active_staff_keys () [-2, 3] >>> ScaleConstructionSettings ( ... staff_keys = set () ... ). active_staff_keys () [0]

title: alto.settings
text: ClefBasicsSettings ClefBasicsSettings ( * , clefs : set [ str ] = field ( default_factory = lambda : { 'treble' , 'bass' }), question_type : str = 'construction' , ) [Source] Bases: ClefChoice The settings of the clef basics exercise: what kind of question is asked, and which clefs. Every clef is one of three symbols, the G, C or F clef, put on a line of the staff: the mezzo-soprano clef is the C clef on the second line. The three symbols can always be chosen from. Attributes clefs ( set of str ): The clefs that are asked for, any of CLEF_BASICS_CLEFS . Keyword-only. question_type ( str, default “construction” ): “construction” to put a named clef on a blank staff, or “identification” to name the clef shown on a staff by pressing a button. Keyword-only. Examples >>> ClefBasicsSettings ( ... clefs = { "subbass" , "alto" } ... ). active_clefs () ['alto', 'subbass'] >>> ClefBasicsSettings (). question_type 'construction'

title: alto.settings
text: ClefBasicsSettings.active_type def active_type () -> str [Source] Return the kind of question to ask. Returns str : “construction” or “identification”; construction if the setting is anything else. Examples >>> ClefBasicsSettings ( ... question_type = "identification" ... ). active_type () 'identification' >>> ClefBasicsSettings ( ... question_type = "nonsense" ... ). active_type () 'construction'

title: alto.settings
text: ClefBasicsSettings.answer_clefs def answer_clefs () -> list [ str ] [Source] Return the clefs to offer as buttons when a clef is to be named: those asked for, and enough others to have a choice. Returns list of str : In canonical order; at least two, the treble and bass clefs being added if only one is asked for. Examples >>> ClefBasicsSettings ( ... clefs = { "alto" , "tenor" } ... ). answer_clefs () ['alto', 'tenor'] >>> ClefBasicsSettings ( ... clefs = { "alto" } ... ). answer_clefs () ['treble', 'alto']

title: alto.settings
text: NotationSettings NotationSettings ( terms : set [ str ] = field ( default_factory = lambda : set ( NOTATION_TERMS )), question_type : str = 'button' , ) [Source] Terms eligible to be highlighted in Notation Identification. Examples >>> "Notehead" in NotationSettings (). terms True

title: alto.settings
text: CircleSettings CircleSettings ( questions : set [ str ] = field ( default_factory = lambda : set ( CIRCLE_QUESTIONS )), scheme : str = DEFAULT_SCHEME , customs : list [ CustomRecord ] = field ( default_factory = list ), ) [Source] The settings of the circle of fifths exercise. Attributes questions ( set of str ): The kinds of question to ask, keys of CIRCLE_QUESTIONS : the relative major of a minor key, the relative minor of a major key, and the Roman numeral of a chord of a key. scheme ( str ): The key of the color scheme the circle is drawn in: a preset of alto.circle_schemes or one of customs . customs ( list of CustomRecord ): The color schemes the user made. Examples >>> CircleSettings (). active_questions () ['major', 'minor', 'numeral'] >>> CircleSettings ( ... questions = { "numeral" } ... ). active_questions () ['numeral'] >>> CircleSettings (). active_scheme (). name 'Cyan to indigo'

title: alto.settings
text: CircleSettings.active_questions def active_questions () -> list [ str ] [Source] Return the kinds of question to ask, in the order they are listed. Returns list of str : The chosen kinds, or all of them if none is chosen. Examples >>> CircleSettings ( ... questions = set () ... ). active_questions () ['major', 'minor', 'numeral'] >>> CircleSettings ( ... questions = { "minor" , "nonsense" } ... ). active_questions () ['minor']

title: alto.settings
text: CircleSettings.active_scheme def active_scheme () -> Scheme [Source] Return the color scheme to draw the circle in. Returns Scheme : The chosen scheme, or the default if the saved choice is no longer available, such as a deleted custom scheme. Examples >>> CircleSettings ( ... scheme = "midnight" ... ). active_scheme (). name 'Midnight' >>> CircleSettings ( ... scheme = "deleted" ... ). active_scheme (). key 'cyan-indigo'

title: alto.terms
text: alto.terms Glossary entries that an installed plugin supplies, kept apart from the built-in ones. A plugin describes each entry in its manifest as plain text, and may show one of its own instrument pictures with it. The glossary page merges these with the built-in terms and lists them under their own names. Examples >>> entry = PluginTerm ( ... name = "scroll" , ... pack = "Demo" , ... definition = "The carved end." , ... lessons = ( "pack.demo.parts" ,), ... ) >>> register_term ( entry ) >>> PLUGIN_TERMS [ "scroll" ] is entry True >>> _ = PLUGIN_TERMS . pop ( "scroll" )

title: alto.terms
text: PluginTerm PluginTerm ( name : str , pack : str , definition : str , guide : str = '' , picture : PicturePosition | None = None , caption : str = '' , exercises : tuple [ str , ...] = (), lessons : tuple [ str , ...] = (), ) [Source] One glossary entry from a plugin. Attributes name ( str ): The term, as listed. pack ( str ): The plugin’s display name. definition ( str ): What the term means, as simple HTML. guide ( str ): How to recognize or use it, as simple HTML. May be empty. picture ( PicturePosition or None ): An instrument picture to show beside the text, with the term marked on it. None for none. caption ( str ): The words under the picture. May be empty. exercises ( tuple of str ): The registered keys of the exercises to offer as practice. lessons ( tuple of str ): The keys of the lessons to offer. Examples >>> PluginTerm ( ... name = "nut" , ... pack = "Demo" , ... definition = "It holds the strings." , ... ). exercises ()

title: alto.terms
text: register_term def register_term ( entry : PluginTerm ) -> None [Source] Add a plugin’s glossary entry. Parameters entry ( PluginTerm ): The entry. Raises ValueError : If another plugin already supplies the same term. Examples >>> register_term ( ... PluginTerm ( ... name = "bridge" , ... pack = "Demo" , ... definition = "It lifts the strings." , ... ) ... ) >>> register_term ( ... PluginTerm ( ... name = "bridge" , ... pack = "Other" , ... definition = "Again." , ... ) ... ) Traceback (most recent call last): ... ValueError: The term bridge is already supplied by Demo. >>> _ = PLUGIN_TERMS . pop ( "bridge" )

title: alto.terms
text: read_terms def read_terms ( value : object , * , pack_id : str , pack_name : str , instruments : Mapping [ str , PackInstrument ], exercises : Mapping [ str , str ], lessons : Mapping [ str , str ], ) -> tuple [ PluginTerm , ...] [Source] Validate the optional glossary list of a plugin manifest. Parameters value ( object ): The manifest’s glossary entry: a list of objects with a term and a definition , and optionally a guide , a picture with a caption , and the ids of related exercises and lessons . None when there is none. pack_id ( str ): The plugin’s id. Keyword-only. pack_name ( str ): The plugin’s display name. Keyword-only. instruments ( mapping of str to PackInstrument ): The plugin’s instruments by qualified key. Keyword-only. exercises ( mapping of str to str ): The plugin’s exercises, from the id the manifest uses to the key Alto registers it under. Keyword-only. lessons ( mapping of str to str ): The plugin’s lessons, from the id the manifest uses to the key Alto registers it under. Keyword-only. Returns tuple of PluginTerm : The entries, in the order the manifest lists them. Raises ValueError : If an entry is malformed, repeats a term, or links to an exercise or lesson the plugin does not declare. Examples >>> read_terms ( ... None , ... pack_id = "demo" , ... pack_name = "Demo" , ... instruments = {}, ... exercises = {}, ... lessons = {}, ... ) () >>> read_terms ( ... [ ... { ... "term" : "nut" , ... "definition" : "It holds the strings." , ... } ... ], ... pack_id = "demo" , ... pack_name = "Demo" , ... instruments = {}, ... exercises = {}, ... lessons = {}, ... )[ 0 ]. name 'nut'

title: alto.theory.fifths
text: alto.theory.fifths The circle of fifths: the twelve keys in order, each major with its relative minor. Going clockwise from C at the top, each key is a fifth above the one before, so it has one more sharp (or one fewer flat). The relative minor of a major key has the same key signature and starts on its sixth note: A minor goes with C major. A key has six chords that fit on the circle: the major triads I, IV and V on the outer ring, and the minor triads ii, iii and vi on the inner ring. They are the key’s own wedge and the wedge on each side of it, on both rings. (The seventh chord, vii°, is diminished and has no wedge.) Examples >>> MAJORS [ 3 ], MINORS [ 3 ], SIGNATURES [ 3 ] (('A',), ('F♯m',), 3) >>> relative_minor ( "A" ) 'F♯m' >>> numeral_chords ( 1 ) {'I': 'G', 'ii': 'Am', 'iii': 'Bm', 'IV': 'C', 'V': 'D', 'vi': 'Em'} >>> accidentals_of ( - 2 ) ['B♭', 'E♭']

title: alto.theory.fifths
text: place_of_major def place_of_major ( name : str ) -> int [Source] Return where a major key is on the circle, by either of its names. Parameters name ( str ): The key’s name, such as “A”, “B♭” or “C♭”. Returns int : The place, clockwise from C at 0. Raises ValueError : If no key has that name. Examples >>> ( ... place_of_major ( "A" ), ... place_of_major ( "C♭" ), ... place_of_major ( "G♭" ), ... ) (3, 5, 6)

title: alto.theory.fifths
text: relative_minor def relative_minor ( name : str ) -> str [Source] Return the relative minor of a major key. Parameters name ( str ): The major key’s name. Returns str : The first name of its relative minor, such as “F♯m” for A. Examples >>> ( ... relative_minor ( "C" ), ... relative_minor ( "E♭" ), ... relative_minor ( "C♯" ), ... ) ('Am', 'Cm', 'B♭m')

title: alto.theory.fifths
text: cells_of_key def cells_of_key ( place : int ) -> dict [ tuple [ str , int ], str ] [Source] Return the six wedges that hold the chords of a major key, and the Roman numeral of each. Parameters place ( int ): The key’s own place on the circle, clockwise from C at 0. Returns dict of tuple of (str, int) to str : For each of the six cells, its ring (“outer” or “inner”) and place, the numeral of its chord. Examples >>> cells = cells_of_key ( 0 ) >>> ( ... cells [( "outer" , 11 )], ... cells [( "inner" , 0 )], ... cells [( "inner" , 1 )], ... ) # F is IV; Am is vi; Em is iii ('IV', 'vi', 'iii') >>> cells [( "outer" , 1 )] # G is V 'V' >>> ( ... len ( cells_of_key ( 11 )), ... cells_of_key ( 11 )[( "outer" , 10 )], ... ) # in F major, B♭ is IV (6, 'IV')

title: alto.theory.fifths
text: numeral_chords def numeral_chords ( place : int ) -> dict [ str , str ] [Source] Return the six chords of a major key that are on the circle, spelled as that key spells them. A wedge with two names, such as D♭ and C♯, is the same chord, but the key decides which name is right: C♯ is the V of F♯. Parameters place ( int ): The key’s own place on the circle. Returns dict of str to str : The chord’s name for each numeral, in the order of NUMERALS : “G”, “Am” and so on. Examples >>> numeral_chords ( 0 ) {'I': 'C', 'ii': 'Dm', 'iii': 'Em', 'IV': 'F', 'V': 'G', 'vi': 'Am'} >>> ( ... numeral_chords ( 6 )[ "V" ], ... numeral_chords ( 7 )[ "IV" ], ... ) # in F♯ major the V is C♯; in D♭ major the IV is G♭ ('C♯', 'G♭')

title: alto.theory.fifths
text: display_major def display_major ( place : int ) -> str [Source] Return the major key of a place as it is written to ask about it: “A major”, or “B major / C♭ major”. Parameters place ( int ): The place on the circle. Returns str : The name, with both names when the wedge has two. Examples >>> display_major ( 3 ), display_major ( 5 ) ('A major', 'B major / C♭ major')

title: alto.theory.fifths
text: display_minor def display_minor ( place : int ) -> str [Source] Return the minor key of a place as it is written to ask about it: “F♯ minor”, or “G♯ minor / A♭ minor”. Parameters place ( int ): The place on the circle. Returns str : The name, with both names when the wedge has two. Examples >>> display_minor ( 3 ), display_minor ( 5 ) ('F♯ minor', 'G♯ minor / A♭ minor')

title: alto.theory.fifths
text: accidentals_of def accidentals_of ( signature : int ) -> list [ str ] [Source] Return the sharps or flats of a key signature, in the order they are written. Parameters signature ( int ): The number of sharps (positive) or flats (negative). Returns list of str : The notes that are altered: “F♯”, “C♯” and so on, or “B♭”, “E♭” and so on. Examples >>> accidentals_of ( 3 ), accidentals_of ( 0 ) (['F♯', 'C♯', 'G♯'], [])

title: alto.theory.fifths
text: explain def explain ( ring : str , * , place : int , ) -> str [Source] Explain a cell of the circle: its key signature, where it comes from, its relative key and its chords. Parameters ring ( str ): “outer” for the major key at the place, “inner” for its relative minor. place ( int ): The place on the circle, clockwise from C at 0. Keyword-only. Returns str : Simple HTML, a few short paragraphs. Examples >>> text = explain ( "outer" , place = 1 ) >>> ( ... "G major" in text ... and "1 sharp: F♯" in text ... and "a fifth above C" in text ... ) True >>> "relative major, C major" in explain ( ... "inner" , place = 0 ... ) True >>> "C♭ major" in explain ( ... "outer" , place = 5 ... ) and "7 flats" in explain ( "outer" , place = 5 ) True

title: alto.theory.key_signatures
text: alto.theory.key_signatures Staff positions for written key signatures.

title: alto.theory.key_signatures
text: key_signature_positions def key_signature_positions ( clef : str , * , sign : int , ) -> list [ str ] [Source] Return the notes the sharps or flats of a key signature are written on, in a clef. Each accidental is a fourth up or a fifth down from the one before (sharps: F C G D A E B, flats: B E A D G C F), and the pattern is chosen so that all seven stay on the staff, or one step above or below it. This gives the usual signatures for the treble, bass, alto and tenor clefs, and works out the rest. Parameters clef ( str ): A key of BOTTOM_LINE . sign ( int ): 1 for sharps, -1 for flats. Keyword-only. Returns list of str : Seven note names with octaves, in the order the accidentals appear. Raises ValueError : If no placement keeps all seven accidentals on the staff. Examples >>> key_signature_positions ( "treble" , sign = 1 ) ['F5', 'C5', 'G5', 'D5', 'A4', 'E5', 'B4'] >>> key_signature_positions ( "bass" , sign =- 1 ) ['B2', 'E3', 'A2', 'D3', 'G2', 'C3', 'F2']

title: alto.theory.key_signatures
text: written_signature def written_signature ( clef : str , * , key : int , ) -> list [ Note ] [Source] Spell a key signature at its conventional staff positions, from left to right. Parameters clef ( str ): The clef the signature is written in. key ( int ): Signed count of sharps or flats. Returns list of Note : Pitches of the printed accidentals, including their octaves and signs. Examples >>> [ ... str ( note ) ... for note in written_signature ( ... "bass" , key =- 2 ... ) ... ] ['B♭2', 'E♭3']

title: alto.theory.pitch
text: alto.theory.pitch Pitches and intervals, spelled correctly (C# is not Db). A Note is a pitch with its spelling (a letter, an accidental and an octave), so C♯4 and D♭4 are different notes even though they sound the same. An Interval is a distance between two spelled notes, such as a major third or a perfect fifth. Together they can transpose a note by an interval and work out the interval between two notes. Examples >>> c4 = Note . parse ( "C4" ) >>> str ( c4 . transpose ( Interval . parse ( "M3" ))) 'E4' >>> Interval . between ( c4 , high = Note . parse ( "G4" )) Interval(number=5, quality='P')

title: alto.theory.pitch
text: Note Note ( octave : int , * , letter : int , accidental : int = 0 , ) [Source] A spelled pitch: a letter name, an accidental and an octave. The spelling matters. C♯4 and D♭4 sound the same (they share a MIDI number) but are different notes, because they sit on different lines of the staff. Attributes octave ( int ): The octave in scientific pitch notation, where middle C is C4. letter ( int ): An index into LETTERS : 0 is C, 1 is D, 2 is E, 3 is F, 4 is G, 5 is A and 6 is B. Keyword-only. accidental ( int, default 0 ): -2 for a double flat, -1 for a flat, 0 for a natural, 1 for a sharp and 2 for a double sharp. Keyword-only. Examples >>> middle_c = Note ( 4 , letter = 0 ) >>> middle_c . midi 60 >>> str ( Note ( 4 , letter = 3 , accidental = 1 )) 'F♯4' >>> Note ( 4 , letter = 0 ) < Note ( 4 , letter = 1 ) True

title: alto.theory.pitch
text: Note.midi @ property def midi () -> int [Source] Return the MIDI note number, where middle C (C4) is 60. Returns int : The number of semitones above C-1. Examples >>> Note ( 4 , letter = 0 ). midi 60 >>> Note ( ... 4 , letter = 1 , accidental =- 1 ... ). midi # D♭4 sounds like C♯4 61

title: alto.theory.pitch
text: Note.diatonic @ property def diatonic () -> int [Source] Return the absolute staff-step index of the note, ignoring its accidental. Counting from C0 as 0, D0 as 1 and so on, each line or space of the staff is one step. The distance between two notes in staff steps is the difference of their indexes. Returns int : octave * 7 + letter . Examples >>> Note ( 4 , letter = 0 ). diatonic # C4 28 >>> Note ( ... 4 , letter = 2 , accidental = 1 ... ). diatonic # E♯4 is on the same step as E4 30

title: alto.theory.pitch
text: Note.pitch_class @ property def pitch_class () -> int [Source] Return the pitch class: the note’s MIDI number modulo 12. Returns int : A number from 0 (C) to 11 (B), the same for every octave and for enharmonic spellings. Examples >>> Note ( ... 4 , letter = 0 , accidental = 1 ... ). pitch_class # C♯4 1 >>> Note ( ... 3 , letter = 6 , accidental = 1 ... ). pitch_class # B♯3 sounds like C 0

title: alto.theory.pitch
text: Note.name @ property def name () -> str [Source] Return the pitch-class name with Unicode accidentals, without the octave. Returns str : The letter followed by ♭, ♯, 𝄫 or 𝄪 where the note has an accidental. Examples >>> Note ( 4 , letter = 3 , accidental = 1 ). name 'F♯' >>> Note ( 4 , letter = 3 ). name 'F'

title: alto.theory.pitch
text: Note.from_diatonic @ classmethod def from_diatonic ( diatonic : int , * , accidental : int = 0 , ) -> Note [Source] Build a note from an absolute staff-step index. Parameters diatonic ( int ): The index, counting C0 as 0 (see Note.diatonic ). accidental ( int, default 0 ): The accidental to give the note. Keyword-only. Returns Note : The note on that staff step with that accidental. Examples >>> Note . from_diatonic ( 30 ) Note(octave=4, letter=2, accidental=0) >>> str ( Note . from_diatonic ( 30 , accidental =- 1 )) 'E♭4'

title: alto.theory.pitch
text: Note.parse @ classmethod def parse ( text : str ) -> Note [Source] Parse a note with ASCII or musical accidentals, such as ‘F#4’, ‘B♭3’ or ‘E𝄫2’. Parameters text ( str ): A letter A-G (either case), then an accidental (‘#’ for a sharp, ‘b’ for a flat, ‘bb’ for a double flat, ‘x’ for a double sharp, or nothing for a natural), then the octave number. Returns Note : The spelled note. Raises ValueError : If the letter is not A-G, or the octave is missing. KeyError : If the accidental is not one of ‘’, ‘#’, ‘b’, ‘bb’ or ‘x’. Examples >>> Note . parse ( "F#4" ) Note(octave=4, letter=3, accidental=1) >>> Note . parse ( "Bb3" ) Note(octave=3, letter=6, accidental=-1) >>> str ( Note . parse ( "G𝄫4" )) 'G𝄫4' >>> Note . parse ( "H4" ) Traceback (most recent call last): ... ValueError: substring not found

title: alto.theory.pitch
text: Note.transpose def transpose ( interval : Interval , * , descending : bool = False , ) -> Note [Source] Move the note up or down by an interval, keeping the spelling correct. Parameters interval ( Interval ): How far to move. Its number decides the letter and its quality decides the accidental. descending ( bool, default False ): Move down instead of up. Keyword-only. Returns Note : The new note. For example a major third above C is E, and a minor third above C is E♭, never D♯. Examples >>> str ( ... Note . parse ( "C4" ). transpose ( ... Interval . parse ( "M3" ) ... ) ... ) 'E4' >>> str ( ... Note . parse ( "C4" ). transpose ( ... Interval . parse ( "m3" ) ... ) ... ) 'E♭4' >>> str ( ... Note . parse ( "C4" ). transpose ( ... Interval . parse ( "P5" ), ... descending = True , ... ) ... ) 'F3'

title: alto.theory.pitch
text: Interval Interval ( number : int , * , quality : str , ) [Source] A simple or compound interval between two spelled notes. Attributes number ( int ): The size counting both end notes: 1 is a unison, 3 a third, 8 an octave, 9 a ninth and so on. quality ( str ): One of ‘dd’ (doubly diminished), ‘d’ (diminished), ‘m’ (minor), ‘M’ (major), ‘P’ (perfect), ‘A’ (augmented) and ‘AA’ (doubly augmented). Keyword-only. Unisons, fourths, fifths and octaves are perfect, the others major or minor. Examples >>> Interval ( 3 , quality = "M" ). semitones 4 >>> str ( Interval . parse ( "P5" )) 'P5'

title: alto.theory.pitch
text: Interval.inversion @ property def inversion () -> Interval [Source] Invert the spelled interval within an octave. Returns Interval : The complementary number and quality. Reduce compounds first, keeping octaves as octaves. Examples >>> ( ... Interval . parse ( "M3" ). inversion . short , ... Interval . parse ( "A4" ). inversion . short , ... ) ('m6', 'd5') >>> ( ... Interval . parse ( "m10" ). inversion . short , ... Interval . parse ( "P15" ). inversion . short , ... ) ('M6', 'P1')

title: alto.theory.pitch
text: Interval.is_perfect_type @ property def is_perfect_type () -> bool [Source] Report whether this size of interval is “perfect type” (unison, fourth, fifth, octave) rather than major or minor type. Returns bool : True for unisons, fourths, fifths and octaves (and their compounds), False for seconds, thirds, sixths and sevenths. Examples >>> Interval . parse ( "P5" ). is_perfect_type True >>> Interval . parse ( "M3" ). is_perfect_type False

title: alto.theory.pitch
text: Interval.semitones @ property def semitones () -> int [Source] Return the size of the interval in semitones. Returns int : The distance in half steps, including whole octaves for compound intervals. Examples >>> Interval . parse ( "M3" ). semitones 4 >>> Interval . parse ( "d5" ). semitones 6 >>> Interval . parse ( ... "m9" ... # a minor ninth is an octave plus a minor second ... ). semitones 13

title: alto.theory.pitch
text: Interval.short @ property def short () -> str [Source] Return the interval in short form: its quality followed by its number. Returns str : For example ‘M3’, ‘P5’ or ‘d7’. Examples >>> Interval ( 7 , quality = "m" ). short 'm7'

title: alto.theory.pitch
text: Interval.between @ classmethod def between ( low : Note , * , high : Note , ) -> Interval [Source] Work out the interval from one note up to a higher one. Parameters low ( Note ): The lower note. high ( Note ): The higher note. It must not be below low . Keyword-only. Returns Interval : The spelled interval, such as a major third (C4 up to E4) or an augmented fourth (C4 up to F♯4). Examples >>> Interval . between ( ... Note . parse ( "C4" ), high = Note . parse ( "E4" ) ... ) Interval(number=3, quality='M') >>> Interval . between ( ... Note . parse ( "C4" ), high = Note . parse ( "F#4" ) ... ). short 'A4'

title: alto.theory.pitch
text: Interval.parse @ classmethod def parse ( text : str ) -> Interval [Source] Parse an interval written in short form, such as ‘M3’, ‘P5’ or ‘d7’. Parameters text ( str ): The quality (one of dd, d, m, M, P, A, AA) followed by the number. Returns Interval : The interval. Examples >>> Interval . parse ( "m7" ) Interval(number=7, quality='m') >>> Interval . parse ( "P8" ). semitones 12

title: alto.theory.pitch
text: key_accidental def key_accidental ( letter : int , * , count : int , ) -> int [Source] Return the accidental a key signature applies to a letter. Parameters letter ( int ): An index into LETTERS (0 is C, 6 is B). count ( int ): The key signature: that many sharps if positive, that many flats if negative. Keyword-only. Returns int : 1 if the signature sharpens the letter, -1 if it flattens it, 0 if it leaves it natural. Examples >>> key_accidental ( 3 , count = 1 ) # F in G major 1 >>> key_accidental ( 6 , count =- 1 ) # B in F major -1 >>> key_accidental ( 0 , count = 1 ) # C in G major 0

title: alto.theory.scales
text: alto.theory.scales Scales, modes, key signatures and chords, built from spelled intervals. SCALES and CHORDS map a name to the list of intervals above the tonic or root. build turns such a list into notes, and the other functions work out key signatures, mode tonics and arpeggios from them. Examples >>> [ ... str ( n ) ... for n in build ( ... Note . parse ( "D4" ), ... intervals = SCALES [ "Dorian" ], ... ) ... ] ['D4', 'E4', 'F4', 'G4', 'A4', 'B4', 'C5'] >>> [ ... str ( n ) ... for n in build ( ... Note . parse ( "C4" ), ... intervals = CHORDS [ "minor 7th" ], ... ) ... ] ['C4', 'E♭4', 'G4', 'B♭4']

title: alto.theory.scales
text: major_key_tonic def major_key_tonic ( count : int ) -> Note [Source] Return the tonic of the major key with a given number of sharps or flats. Parameters count ( int ): Sharps (positive) or flats (negative) in the key signature, from -7 to 7. Returns Note : The tonic, in octave 4. Raises KeyError : If count is outside -7..7. Examples >>> str ( ... major_key_tonic ( 2 ) ... ) # two sharps: D major 'D4' >>> str ( ... major_key_tonic ( - 3 ) ... ) # three flats: E♭ major 'E♭4'

title: alto.theory.scales
text: mode_tonic def mode_tonic ( count : int , * , mode : str , ) -> Note [Source] Return the note a scale in a given mode starts on, for a given key signature. The notes of a mode are those of a major scale started from another degree. D Dorian, for example, has the key signature of C major, started from its second note. Parameters count ( int ): Sharps (positive) or flats (negative) in the key signature, from -7 to 7. mode ( str ): A key of MODE_DEGREE , such as “Dorian” or “Natural minor (Aeolian)”. Keyword-only. Returns Note : The tonic of that mode, in octave 4 or 5. Examples >>> str ( ... mode_tonic ( 0 , mode = "Dorian" ) ... ) # no sharps or flats: D Dorian 'D4' >>> str ( ... mode_tonic ( ... 2 , mode = "Natural minor (Aeolian)" ... ) ... ) # two sharps: B minor 'B4'

title: alto.theory.scales
text: arpeggio def arpeggio ( root : Note , * , intervals : list [ Interval ], inversion : int = 0 , ) -> list [ Note ] [Source] Return a chord broken and rising from its lowest note, then that note again an octave higher. Parameters root ( Note ): The root of the chord. intervals ( list of Interval ): The intervals above the root that make the chord, such as CHORDS["major"] . Keyword-only. inversion ( int, default 0 ): How many of the lowest chord tones are moved up an octave first: 0 is root position, 1 puts the third at the bottom, 2 the fifth. Keyword-only. Returns list of Note : The chord tones from the lowest up, ending on the lowest note an octave higher. Examples >>> [ ... str ( n ) ... for n in arpeggio ( ... Note . parse ( "C4" ), ... intervals = CHORDS [ "major" ], ... ) ... ] ['C4', 'E4', 'G4', 'C5'] >>> [ ... str ( n ) ... for n in arpeggio ( ... Note . parse ( "C4" ), ... intervals = CHORDS [ "major" ], ... inversion = 1 , ... ) ... ] ['E4', 'G4', 'C5', 'E5']

title: alto.theory.scales
text: build def build ( tonic : Note , * , intervals : list [ Interval ], ) -> list [ Note ] [Source] Build the notes of a scale or chord above a tonic. Parameters tonic ( Note ): The first note. intervals ( list of Interval ): The intervals above the tonic, including the unison, such as a value of SCALES or CHORDS . Keyword-only. Returns list of Note : The tonic transposed by each interval, in order. Examples >>> [ ... str ( n ) ... for n in build ( ... Note . parse ( "G4" ), ... intervals = SCALES [ "Major (Ionian)" ], ... ) ... ] ['G4', 'A4', 'B4', 'C5', 'D5', 'E5', 'F♯5']

title: alto.theory.scales
text: key_signature def key_signature ( tonic_name : str , * , scale : str = 'Major (Ionian)' , ) -> int [Source] Return the key signature of a scale as a signed count of accidentals. text: alto.ui.app_settings The application-wide settings dialog. It holds the color theme, the notation font, the keyboard style, the transitions, instruments, metronome clicks and what updates follow. Changes apply as soon as they are made. Each style is a card that previews it. Examples >>> dialog = AppSettingsDialog () >>> dialog . windowTitle () 'Settings' >>> dialog . pages . count () # Appearance, Sound and Updates 3

title: alto.ui.app_settings
text: AppSettingsDialog AppSettingsDialog ( parent : QWidget | None = None , * , learner : Learner | None = None , ) [Source] Bases: QDialog Application-wide settings. Changes apply immediately, and the main window can be used while the dialog is open. Pages are built when first selected, so hidden previews do not slow down opening Settings or changing themes. Attributes theme_changed ( bool ): True once the theme has been changed, so the window can be rebuilt in it. categories ( QListWidget ): The list of pages on the left: Appearance sections, Sound and Updates. pages ( QStackedWidget ): The page for the chosen category. instruments ( InstrumentPicker ): The chooser, available after the Instruments page is selected. theme_list ( QListWidget ): The themes, on the Theme section, with the one in use in bold. theme_items ( dict of str to QListWidgetItem ): The rows of that list, by the key of the theme’s family. theme_pages ( QStackedWidget ): The card of the theme chosen in the list, or the editor. theme_editor ( ThemeEditor ): The form that makes a theme of the user’s own, or changes one. new_theme_item ( QListWidgetItem ): The row of the list that makes a new theme. theme_cards ( dict of str to ThemeCard ): The cards built so far, by the key of the theme’s family. A card is built when its row is first chosen, because every widget makes a change of theme slower; use card to get one. theme_scrolls ( dict of str to QScrollArea ): The scroll area each built card is in, which is what the stack shows; use scroll to get one. theme_thumbs ( dict of str to ThemeThumb ): The clickable pictures of every built card, by the key of the theme each chooses; use thumb to get one. transition_list ( QListWidget ): The choice of transition, available after the Transitions section is first selected. transition_items ( dict of str to QListWidgetItem ): The rows of that list, by the transition’s key. transition_preview ( TransitionPreview ): Plays the transition that is chosen, beside the choices. scheduler_list ( QListWidget ): The algorithms on the Practice page, with the current profile’s choice selected. scheduler_description ( QLabel ): Explanation of the selected algorithm beside the list. Examples >>> dialog = AppSettingsDialog () >>> dialog . theme_changed False Constructor Build the dialog with the Appearance page showing. Parameters parent ( QWidget or None, default None ): The widget that owns the dialog. learner ( Learner or None ): Profile whose practice preferences can be edited. Constructor examples >>> dialog = AppSettingsDialog () >>> dialog . categories . currentRow () 0

Returns ThemeCard : Its card. Examples >>> dialog = AppSettingsDialog () >>> "sage" in dialog . theme_cards False >>> ( ... dialog . card ( "sage" ) ... is dialog . card ( "sage" ), ... "sage" in dialog . theme_cards , ... ) (True, True)

Examples >>> dialog = AppSettingsDialog () >>> dialog . choose_theme ( "light" ) >>> dialog . theme_changed , saved_theme () (True, 'light') >>> dialog . choose_theme ( "system" )

title: alto.ui.background
text: alto.ui.background Run slow work, such as a download, on another thread, and hear how it went on the window’s thread. Examples >>> import time >>> heard = [] >>> owner = QObject () >>> _ = run_in_background ( ... lambda : 6 * 7 , ... owner = owner , ... done = heard . append , ... failed = heard . append , ... ) >>> deadline = time . monotonic () + 5 >>> while ( ... not heard ... and time . monotonic () < deadline ... ): ... app . processEvents () >>> heard [42]

title: alto.ui.background
text: run_in_background def run_in_background ( work : Callable [[], T ], * , owner : QObject , done : Callable [[ T ], None ], failed : Callable [[ Exception ], None ], ) -> threading . Thread [Source] Run work on another thread, then call done with its result, or failed with its exception, on the owner’s thread. The window stays responsive while the work runs. If the owner is deleted before the work ends, neither is called. The thread does not keep Alto from quitting. Parameters work ( callable ): The slow part. It must not touch widgets. owner ( QObject ): The object the work is for, such as the dialog that started it. Keyword-only. done ( callable ): Called with what work returned. Keyword-only. failed ( callable ): Called with the exception work raised. Keyword-only. Returns threading.Thread : The thread doing the work, already started. Callers need not keep it. Examples >>> import time >>> heard = [] >>> owner = QObject () >>> def broken (): ... raise OSError ( "offline" ) >>> _ = run_in_background ( ... broken , ... owner = owner , ... done = heard . append , ... failed = lambda error : heard . append ( ... str ( error ) ... ), ... ) >>> deadline = time . monotonic () + 5 >>> while ( ... not heard ... and time . monotonic () < deadline ... ): ... app . processEvents () >>> heard ['offline']

title: alto.ui.backup_flow
text: alto.ui.backup_flow Exporting a backup and importing one: the file dialogs, the questions asked, and the safety copy made before anything is replaced. Everything Alto keeps goes into a backup (the database and the saved preferences), and importing one replaces everything, so an import into a clean install leaves it as if nothing had changed. Before an import replaces what is there, a backup of that is saved next to the database, so a wrong choice can be undone. Examples >>> default_name ( now = 0.0 ). endswith ( ... ".altobackup" ... ) True

title: alto.ui.backup_flow
text: default_name def default_name ( * , now : float | None = None , ) -> str [Source] Suggest a file name for a backup made now. Parameters now ( float or None, default None ): The time as a timestamp; the clock is used if None. Keyword-only. Returns str : For example alto-backup-2026-11-13.altobackup . Examples >>> default_name ( ... now = datetime ( ... 2026 , 11 , 13 , 12 ... ). timestamp () ... ) 'alto-backup-2026-11-13.altobackup'

title: alto.ui.backup_flow
text: counted def counted ( number : int , * , noun : str , ) -> str [Source] Write a count with its noun, in the plural unless there is one. Parameters number ( int ): The count. noun ( str ): The singular noun. Keyword-only. Returns str : For example “1 profile” or “12,345 answers”. Examples >>> ( ... counted ( 1 , noun = "profile" ), ... counted ( 12345 , noun = "answer" ), ... ) ('1 profile', '12,345 answers')

title: alto.ui.backup_flow
text: describe def describe ( info : BackupInfo ) -> str [Source] Say what a backup holds and when it was made, for the question asked before importing it. Parameters info ( BackupInfo ): What the backup says about itself. Returns str : A sentence or two. Examples >>> text = describe ( ... BackupInfo ( ... datetime ( ... 2026 , 11 , 13 , 9 , 30 ... ). timestamp (), ... app_version = "0.1.0" , ... schema_version = 1 , ... profiles = 2 , ... attempts = 1500 , ... ) ... ) >>> text 'Made on 13 November 2026, 09:30 by Alto 0.1.0. It holds 2 profiles and 1,500 answers.'

title: alto.ui.backup_flow
text: export_backup def export_backup ( parent : QWidget , * , db : Database , ) -> Path | None [Source] Ask where to save a backup, and write it. Parameters parent ( QWidget ): The window the dialogs belong to. db ( Database ): The database to back up. Keyword-only. Returns Path or None : The file that was written, or None if the user canceled or the backup could not be written (which is explained). Examples >>> export_backup ( ... QWidget (), db = Database () ... ) # doctest: +SKIP PosixPath('/home/ada/alto-backup-2026-11-13.altobackup')

title: alto.ui.backup_flow
text: safety_copy def safety_copy ( db : Database ) -> Path | None [Source] Save a backup of what the database holds now, beside it, before it is replaced. Parameters db ( Database ): The database about to be replaced. Returns Path or None : The file written, or None for a throwaway in-memory database, which has no folder to keep a copy in. Raises BackupError : If the copy cannot be written. Examples >>> safety_copy ( Database ()) is None True

title: alto.ui.backup_flow
text: import_backup def import_backup ( parent : QWidget , * , db : Database , ) -> bool [Source] Ask for a backup file and, once the user has agreed, replace everything with what it holds. The file is read and checked completely first, so a damaged or foreign file changes nothing. After the user agrees, a backup of the current data is saved beside the database, then the database and the saved preferences are replaced. The caller has to reload what is on screen afterwards. Parameters parent ( QWidget ): The window the dialogs belong to. db ( Database ): The database to replace the contents of. Keyword-only. Returns bool : True if the backup was applied; False if the user canceled or the file was refused (which is explained). Examples >>> import_backup ( ... QWidget (), db = Database () ... ) # doctest: +SKIP True

title: alto.ui.charts
text: alto.ui.charts Small charts drawn with QPainter, in the application’s theme colors. Stacked bars, a line, horizontal bars and a calendar heatmap. Each has a title, draws a message when there is nothing to show, and explains the bar or square under the pointer in a tooltip. Examples >>> nice_ticks ( 13 ) [0, 5, 10, 15] >>> chart = StackedBarChart ( ... "Questions answered" ... ) >>> chart . set_data ( ... [ "Mon" , "Tue" ], ... right = [ 3 , 1 ], ... wrong = [ 1 , 0 ], ... ) >>> chart . right , chart . wrong ([3, 1], [1, 0])

title: alto.ui.charts
text: nice_ticks def nice_ticks ( top : float , * , count : int = 4 , ) -> list [ float ] [Source] Return round tick values from 0 up to just above a top value. Parameters top ( float ): The largest value to show. count ( int, default 4 ): Roughly how many ticks to aim for. Keyword-only. Returns list of float : Ticks at round steps (1, 2, 2.5, 5 or 10 times a power of ten), starting at 0 and reaching at least top . Just 0 and 1 when top is not positive. Examples >>> nice_ticks ( 13 ) [0, 5, 10, 15] >>> nice_ticks ( 8 )[ - 1 ] >= 8 True >>> nice_ticks ( 0 ) [0.0, 1.0]

text: LineChart LineChart ( title : str , * , fmt : Callable [[ float ], str ], fixed_top : float | None = None , parent : QWidget | None = None , ) [Source] Bases: _Chart A value per period joined by a line. Periods with no answers leave a gap rather than a zero. Attributes fmt ( callable ): Turns a value into its label, for the axis and the tooltip. fixed_top ( float or None ): The value at the top of the plot; the largest value, rounded up, if None. values ( list of float or None ): The value of each period, or None for a gap. Examples >>> chart = LineChart ( ... "Right on the first try" , ... fmt = lambda v : f " { v : . 0 f } %" , ... fixed_top = 100 , ... ) >>> chart . set_data ( ... Parameters title ( str ): Drawn at the top left. fmt ( callable ): Turns a value into its label. Keyword-only. fixed_top ( float or None, default None ): The value at the top of the plot (such as 100 for a percentage); the largest value, rounded up, if None. Keyword-only. parent ( QWidget or None, default None ): The widget that owns the chart. Keyword-only. Constructor examples >>> LineChart ( ... "Speed" , fmt = lambda v : f " { v : . 1 f } s" ... ). fixed_top is None True

Parameters labels ( sequence of str ): The label of each period. values ( sequence of float or None ): The value of each period; None leaves a gap. Keyword-only. Examples >>> chart = LineChart ( ... "Speed" , fmt = lambda v : f " { v : . 1 f } s" ... ) >>> chart . set_data ( ... [ "a" , "b" ], values = [ 2.5 , None ] ... ) >>> chart . labels ['a', 'b']

title: alto.ui.charts
text: LineChart.paintEvent def paintEvent ( _ : QPaintEvent ) -> None [Source] Draw the axes, the line (one run at a time, so gaps show) and a dot for each value. Parameters _ ( QPaintEvent ): The paint request; the whole widget is always redrawn. Examples >>> chart = LineChart ( ... "Speed" , fmt = lambda v : f " { v : . 1 f } s" ... ) >>> chart . resize ( 400 , 300 ) >>> chart . set_data ( ... [ "a" , "b" , "c" ], values = [ 2.0 , None , 3.0 ] ... ) >>> chart . grab (). isNull () False

title: alto.ui.charts
text: LineChart.mouseMoveEvent def mouseMoveEvent ( event : QMouseEvent ) -> None [Source] Say what the value under the pointer is in a tooltip. Parameters event ( QMouseEvent ): The mouse move. Examples >>> from PySide6.QtCore import QEvent >>> from PySide6.QtGui import QMouseEvent >>> chart = LineChart ( ... "Speed" , fmt = lambda v : f " { v : . 1 f } s" ... ) >>> chart . resize ( 400 , 300 ) >>> chart . set_data ( ...
