title: alto.ui.circle
text: alto.ui.circle The circle of fifths: twelve wedges, the major keys on the outside and their relative minors on the inside. C is at the top and each step clockwise is a fifth up, so the keys gather sharps on the right and flats on the left. The disc in the middle shows the staff and key signature of the key being talked about. In an exercise one wedge is the question and its name (or its Roman numeral) is blank until the answer is right. Examples >>> circle = FifthsCircle () >>> circle . show_question ( ... "major" , place = 3 , title = "F♯ minor" ... ) >>> circle . target ('outer', 3)

title: alto.ui.circle
text: wedge_path def wedge_path ( * , center : QPointF , inner : float , outer : float , index : int , ) -> QPainterPath [Source] Return the outline of one wedge of a ring. Parameters center ( QPointF ): The middle of the circle. inner ( float ): The radius of the wedge’s inner edge, in pixels. Keyword-only. outer ( float ): The radius of its outer edge. Keyword-only. index ( int ): Which wedge: 0 is the one at the top and they go clockwise. Keyword-only. Returns QPainterPath : A closed shape, a piece of a ring 30 degrees wide. Examples >>> shape = wedge_path ( ... center = QPointF ( 100 , 100 ), ... inner = 40 , ... outer = 90 , ... index = 0 , ... ) >>> ( ... shape . contains ( QPointF ( 100 , 30 )), ... shape . contains ( QPointF ( 100 , 170 )), ... ) # the top of the circle, and the bottom (True, False)

title: alto.ui.circle
text: wedge_middle def wedge_middle ( * , center : QPointF , radius : float , index : int , ) -> QPointF [Source] Return the point in the middle of a wedge, at a given distance from the center. Parameters center ( QPointF ): The middle of the circle. radius ( float ): How far out, in pixels. Keyword-only. index ( int ): Which wedge, clockwise from the top. Keyword-only. Returns QPointF : The point. Examples >>> wedge_middle ( ... center = QPointF ( 100 , 100 ), ... radius = 50 , ... index = 0 , ... ). toTuple () # straight up (100.0, 50.0) >>> round ( ... wedge_middle ( ... center = QPointF ( 100 , 100 ), ... radius = 50 , ... index = 3 , ... ). x () ... ) # a quarter of the way around: to the right 150

title: alto.ui.circle
text: wedge_color def wedge_color ( index : int , * , inner : bool , lift : float = 0.0 , scheme : Scheme | None = None , ) -> QColor [Source] Return the color of a wedge in a color scheme: quiet when it is not being talked about and bright when it is. Parameters index ( int ): Which wedge, clockwise from the top. inner ( bool ): Whether it is in the inner ring. Keyword-only. lift ( float, default 0.0 ): How bright it is, from 0 (quiet) to 1 (lit). Keyword-only. scheme ( Scheme or None, default None ): The color scheme; the one chosen in the circle of fifths settings if None. Keyword-only. Returns QColor : The color. Examples >>> from alto.circle_schemes import preset >>> spectrum = preset ( "spectrum" ) >>> ( ... wedge_color ( ... 0 , ... inner = False , ... lift = 1.0 , ... scheme = spectrum , ... ). hue (), ... wedge_color ( ... 6 , inner = False , scheme = spectrum ... ). hue (), ... ) (0, 180) >>> lit , quiet = ( ... wedge_color ( ... 0 , ... inner = False , ... lift = amount , ... scheme = spectrum , ... ) ... for amount in ( 1.0 , 0.0 ) ... ) >>> lit . lightness () > quiet . lightness () True >>> # no wedge looks too bright for white names >>> every = [ ... wedge_color ( ... i , ... inner = False , ... lift = 1.0 , ... scheme = spectrum , ... ) ... for i in range ( 12 ) ... ] >>> all ( ... 0.299 * c . redF () ... + 0.587 * c . greenF () ... + 0.114 * c . blueF () ... <= 0.44 ... for c in every ... ) True

title: alto.ui.circle
text: write_text def write_text ( p : QPainter , * , center : QPointF , text : str , pixels : float , weight : QFont . Weight , color : QColor , max_width : float | None = None , ) -> None [Source] Write a line of text centered on a point, with its sharps and flats drawn as the notation font draws them. The letters are in the app’s own font. Its ♭ is the shape of a small “b”, though, and does not look like a flat sign, so the sharps, flats and naturals are the glyphs of the notation style that the staff is drawn in, sized to the letters. Parameters p ( QPainter ): The painter to draw with. center ( QPointF ): The middle of the line. Keyword-only. text ( str ): What to write, such as “B♭m” or “F♯ major”. Keyword-only. pixels ( float ): The size of the letters. Keyword-only. weight ( QFont.Weight ): How heavy they are. Keyword-only. color ( QColor ): The color. Keyword-only. max_width ( float or None, default None ): The widest the line may be. A longer line is written smaller to fit. Keyword-only. Examples >>> from PySide6.QtGui import QImage >>> image = QImage ( ... 120 , 60 , QImage . Format . Format_ARGB32 ... ) >>> image . fill ( QColor ( "black" )) >>> painter = QPainter ( image ) >>> write_text ( ... painter , ... center = QPointF ( 60 , 30 ), ... text = "B♭m" , ... pixels = 24 , ... weight = QFont . Weight . Bold , ... color = QColor ( "white" ), ... ) >>> painter . end () True >>> any ( ... image . pixelColor ( x , 30 ). lightness () ... > 128 ... for x in range ( 20 , 100 ) ... ) True

title: alto.ui.circle
text: FifthsCircle FifthsCircle ( parent : QWidget | None = None ) [Source] Bases: QWidget The circle of fifths, drawn for an exercise. Attributes kind ( str ): What is being asked: “major”, “minor” or “numeral”, or “” for nothing. target ( tuple of (str, int) or None ): The cell asked about: its ring (“outer” or “inner”) and its place clockwise from the top. shown ( dict of str to set of int ): For each ring, the places whose key name is written. lit ( set of int ): The places of the chords of the key, in a Roman numeral question; both rings are lit there. numerals ( dict of tuple of (str, int) to str ): The Roman numeral written in each cell that has one. title ( str ): The big text in the middle. subtitle ( str ): The small text in the middle. signature ( int or None ): The key signature drawn on the staff in the middle, or None for no staff. Examples >>> circle = FifthsCircle () >>> circle . show_question ( ... "major" , place = 0 , title = "A minor" ... ) >>> circle . reveal ( animate = False ) >>> circle . shown [ "outer" ], circle . signature ({0}, 0) Constructor Build the circle, with nothing asked. Parameters parent ( QWidget or None, default None ): The widget that owns it. Constructor examples >>> FifthsCircle (). target is None True

title: alto.ui.circle

title: alto.ui.circle
text: FifthsCircle.show_question def show_question ( kind : str , * , place : int , title : str , ring : str | None = None , key : int | None = None , ) -> None [Source] Ask about a cell, showing what the question needs and leaving the answer blank. A “major” question shows the minor keys and asks for the major of one of them; a “minor” question shows the majors and asks for a minor; a “numeral” question shows every name, lights the six chords of a key with its staff in the middle, and asks for the Roman numeral of one of them. Parameters kind ( str ): “major”, “minor” or “numeral”. place ( int ): The place of the cell asked about, clockwise from the top. Keyword-only. title ( str ): The big text in the middle, such as “F♯ minor”. Keyword-only. ring ( str or None, default None ): The ring of the cell asked about; for “major” the outer one and for “minor” the inner one if None. Keyword-only. key ( int or None, default None ): For a “numeral” question, the place of the key whose chords they are. Keyword-only. Examples >>> circle = FifthsCircle () >>> circle . show_question ( ... "minor" , place = 3 , title = "A major" ... ) >>> ( ... circle . target , ... circle . shown [ "outer" ] == set ( range ( 12 )), ... circle . shown [ "inner" ], ... circle . signature , ... ) (('inner', 3), True, set(), None) >>> circle . show_question ( ... "numeral" , ... place = 11 , ... ring = "outer" , ... key = 0 , ... title = "C major" , ... ) >>> ( ... sorted ( circle . lit ), ... circle . signature , ... circle . numerals , ... ) ([0, 1, 11], 0, {})

title: alto.ui.circle
text: FifthsCircle.reset def reset () -> None [Source] Clear everything: no question, no names shown, no animation running. Examples >>> circle = FifthsCircle () >>> circle . show_question ( ... "major" , place = 2 , title = "B minor" ... ) >>> circle . reset () >>> ( ... circle . target is None ... and circle . title == "" ... and circle . lit == set () ... ) True

title: alto.ui.circle
text: FifthsCircle.reveal def reveal ( * , animate : bool = True , ) -> None [Source] Show the answer: the key’s name in its cell, brightened, and its staff and key signature in the middle. For a Roman numeral question every chord of the key shows its numeral, as the circle in the reference does. Parameters animate ( bool, default True ): Brighten the cell gradually; if False it is bright at once. Keyword-only. Examples >>> circle = FifthsCircle () >>> circle . show_question ( ... "minor" , ... place = 5 , ... title = "B major / C♭ major" , ... ) >>> circle . reveal ( animate = False ) >>> ( ... circle . shown [ "inner" ], ... circle . title , ... circle . subtitle , ... circle . signature , ... ) ({5}, 'G♯ minor', '5 sharps', 5)

title: alto.ui.circle
text: FifthsCircle.set_subtitle def set_subtitle ( text : str ) -> None [Source] Change the small text in the middle, for example to say that a second answer is wanted. title: alto.ui.circle
text: FifthsCircle.flash_wrong def flash_wrong () -> None [Source] Flash the cell asked about in the red of a wrong answer, striped as well so that it still shows on the red wedge. Examples >>> circle = FifthsCircle () >>> circle . show_question ( ... "major" , place = 0 , title = "A minor" ... ) >>> circle . flash_wrong () >>> circle . _warning is not None True

title: alto.ui.circle
text: FifthsCircle.lift_of def lift_of ( ring : str , * , place : int , ) -> float [Source] Return how bright a cell is drawn, from 0 (quiet) to 1 (fully lit). The cell asked about is half lit, and brightens when it is answered. The cell beside it on the other ring is a little lit, to show the pair; in a Roman numeral question the six chords of the key are lit instead. Parameters ring ( str ): “outer” or “inner”. place ( int ): The place clockwise from the top. Keyword-only. Returns float : The brightness. Examples >>> circle = FifthsCircle () >>> circle . show_question ( ... "major" , place = 0 , title = "A minor" ... ) >>> ( ... circle . lift_of ( "outer" , place = 0 ), ... circle . lift_of ( "inner" , place = 0 ), ... circle . lift_of ( "outer" , place = 5 ), ... ) (0.5, 0.3, 0.0) >>> circle . reveal ( animate = False ) >>> circle . lift_of ( "outer" , place = 0 ) 1.0

title: alto.ui.circle
text: FifthsCircle.geometry_of def geometry_of () -> tuple [ QPointF , float ] [Source] Return where the circle is drawn: its middle and its radius. Examples >>> circle = FifthsCircle () >>> circle . resize ( 400 , 300 ) >>> middle , radius = circle . geometry_of () >>> middle . toTuple (), radius < 150 ((200.0, 150.0), True) >>> circle . resize ( 2400 , 2000 ) >>> circle . geometry_of ()[ 1 ] == MAX_RADIUS True

text: SchemeEditor SchemeEditor ( parent : QWidget | None = None ) [Source] Bases: QWidget The editor for a color scheme of the user’s own: a name, how its colors are made, and the colors. The colors are what a cell looks like when lit; the quiet cells are made from them. A picture shows the result as it is edited. Attributes saved ( Signal ): Emitted with the record when Save is clicked. deleted ( Signal ): Emitted with the scheme’s key when Delete is clicked (only an existing scheme can be deleted). canceled ( Signal ): Emitted when Cancel is clicked. name ( QLineEdit ): The name. mode ( QComboBox ): How the colors are made: a key of MODES is each item’s data. wedges ( QComboBox ): Whether the wedges are dark, with light names, or light, with dark names. swatches ( list of QPushButton ): One button for each color the mode takes; the others are hidden. preview ( SchemeThumb ): The picture of the scheme as it is. text: alto.ui.colors Mixing colors. The interface blends palette colors to get its soft tints and highlights. Examples >>> blend_name ( ... QColor ( "#000000" ), ... b = QColor ( "#ffffff" ), ... t = 0.5 , ... ) '#808080'

text: blend def blend ( a : QColor , * , b : QColor , t : float , ) -> QColor [Source] Return the color a given fraction of the way from one color to another. Parameters a ( QColor ): The color at 0. b ( QColor ): The color at 1. Keyword-only. t ( float ): How far from a to b : 0 is a , 1 is b , 0.5 is halfway. Keyword-only. Returns QColor : The blended color. Examples >>> blend ( ... QColor ( "#000000" ), ... b = QColor ( "#ffffff" ), ... t = 0.0 , ... ). name () '#000000' >>> blend ( ... QColor ( "#ff0000" ), ... b = QColor ( "#0000ff" ), ... t = 1.0 , ... ). name () '#0000ff'

text: blend_name def blend_name ( a : QColor , * , b : QColor , t : float , ) -> str [Source] Return the hex name of a blended color, for use in a stylesheet. title: alto.ui.database_page
text: alto.ui.database_page A read-only look at what is stored: every answer, every question’s record, and the profiles. Examples >>> len ( ... _when ( 0.0 )[ 0 ] ... ) # a timestamp as 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' 19

title: alto.ui.database_page
text: RowsModel RowsModel ( headers : list [ str ], * , rows : list [ list [ tuple [ str , object ]]], numeric : Iterable [ int ] = (), extras : list [ dict ] | None = None , parent : QObject | None = None , ) [Source] Bases: QAbstractTableModel Rows of (text shown, value to sort by) cells, as a table model. Numbers are right-aligned. Attributes headers ( list of str ): The column headings. rows ( list of list of tuple of (str, object) ): The cells: for each, the text to show and the value to sort by. numeric ( set of int ): The columns to right-align. extras ( list of dict ): Something about each row that is not shown, such as the stored question (see ROW_ROLE ). Examples >>> model = RowsModel ( ... [ "Name" , "Count" ], ... rows = [[( "Ada" , "Ada" ), ( "3" , 3 )]], ... numeric = { 1 }, ... ) >>> model . rowCount (), model . columnCount () (1, 2) >>> ( ... model . data ( model . index ( 0 , 1 )), ... model . data ( ... model . index ( 0 , 1 ), SORT_ROLE ... ), ... ) ('3', 3) Constructor Create the model. Parameters headers ( list of str ): The column headings. rows ( list of list of tuple of (str, object) ): The cells. Keyword-only. numeric ( iterable of int, default () ): The columns to right-align. Keyword-only. extras ( list of dict or None, default None ): Something about each row that is not shown, such as the stored question; empty for each row if None. Keyword-only. parent ( QObject or None, default None ): The owner. Keyword-only. Constructor examples >>> RowsModel ( ... [ "Name" ], rows = [[( "Ada" , "Ada" )]] ... ). extras [{}]

title: alto.ui.database_page
text: RowsModel.rowCount def rowCount ( parent : QModelIndex | QPersistentModelIndex = QModelIndex ()) -> int [Source] Return the number of rows. Parameters parent ( QModelIndex or QPersistentModelIndex ): Only the top level has rows: an index that is valid gives 0. Returns int : The number of rows. Examples >>> RowsModel ( ... [ "Name" ], ... rows = [ ... [( "Ada" , "Ada" )], ... [( "Ben" , "Ben" )], ... ], ... ). rowCount () 2

title: alto.ui.database_page
text: RowsModel.columnCount def columnCount ( parent : QModelIndex | QPersistentModelIndex = QModelIndex ()) -> int [Source] Return the number of columns. Parameters parent ( QModelIndex or QPersistentModelIndex ): Only the top level has columns: an index that is valid gives 0. Returns int : The number of columns. Examples >>> RowsModel ( ... [ "Name" , "Count" ], rows = [] ... ). columnCount () 2

title: alto.ui.database_page
text: RowsModel.data def data ( index : QModelIndex | QPersistentModelIndex , role : int = Qt . ItemDataRole . DisplayRole , ) -> object [Source] Return one piece of a cell for a role. Parameters index ( QModelIndex or QPersistentModelIndex ): The cell. role ( int, default DisplayRole ): What is wanted: the text to show, the value to sort by ( SORT_ROLE ), the alignment, or the row’s hidden details ( ROW_ROLE ). Returns object : The requested data, or None for a role the model does not use. Examples >>> model = RowsModel ( ... [ "Name" , "Count" ], ... rows = [[( "Ada" , "Ada" ), ( "3" , 3 )]], ... numeric = { 1 }, ... ) >>> model . data ( model . index ( 0 , 0 )) 'Ada' >>> align = Qt . ItemDataRole . TextAlignmentRole >>> model . data ( ... model . index ( 0 , 1 ), align ... ) != model . data ( ... model . index ( 0 , 0 ), align ... ) # numbers are right-aligned True

title: alto.ui.database_page
text: RowsModel.headerData def headerData ( section : int , orientation : Qt . Orientation , role : int = Qt . ItemDataRole . DisplayRole , ) -> object [Source] Return a column heading. Returns object : The heading, or None for anything else. Examples >>> model = RowsModel ( ... [ "Name" , "Count" ], rows = [] ... ) >>> model . headerData ( ... 1 , Qt . Orientation . title: alto.ui.database_page
text: QuestionTexts QuestionTexts () [Source] Describes stored questions in words, remembering each one so it is worked out only once. Examples >>> texts = QuestionTexts () >>> texts ( "NoteNames" , key = "k" , payload = None ) '(no longer stored)' Constructor Create an empty memory. Constructor examples >>> QuestionTexts (). _described {}

title: alto.ui.database_page
text: answer_cells def answer_cells ( rows : Sequence [ sqlite3 . Row ], * , names : dict [ str , str ], texts : QuestionTexts , ) -> tuple [ list [ list [ tuple [ str , object ]]], list [ dict ]] [Source] Turn answers read from the database into the cells of a table, and the hidden details of each row. Parameters rows ( sequence of sqlite3.Row ): Answers, as Database.attempt_rows returns them. names ( dict of str to str ): The title of each exercise, by class name. Keyword-only. texts ( QuestionTexts ): Describes each question in words. Keyword-only. Returns tuple of (list, list of dict) : The cells, in the order of ANSWER_HEADERS , and for each row the exercise, the stored question and the lines the question preview shows about the answer. Examples >>> from alto.learning import Database >>> db = Database () >>> ada = db . add_profile ( "Ada" ) >>> db . add_attempt ( ... ada . id , ... exercise = "NoteNames" , ... item_key = "k" , ... attempt_no = 1 , ... answer = "C" , ... correct = True , ... duration_ms = 2500 , ... answered_at = 1000.0 , ... ) >>> table , hidden = answer_cells ( ... db . attempt_rows ( ada . id ), ... names = { ... "NoteNames" : "Note Identification" ... }, ... texts = QuestionTexts (), ... ) >>> [ text for text , _ in table [ 0 ]][ 1 :] ['Note Identification', '(no longer stored)', 'C', 'Right', '1', '2.5 s', '—'] >>> hidden [ 0 ][ "exercise" ] 'NoteNames'

title: alto.ui.database_page
text: open_preview def open_preview ( index : QModelIndex , * , names : dict [ str , str ], parent : QWidget , learner : Learner | None = None , ) -> None [Source] Show the question behind a row of an answers table, if its record is still stored. Parameters index ( QModelIndex ): A cell of the row, in a model whose rows carry ROW_ROLE details. names ( dict of str to str ): The title of each exercise, by class name. Keyword-only. parent ( QWidget ): The widget the popup belongs to. Keyword-only. learner ( Learner or None, default None ): The active profile, used to open this question’s statistics. Keyword-only. Examples >>> model = RowsModel ( ... [ "Name" ], rows = [[( "Ada" , "Ada" )]] ... ) >>> open_preview ( ... model . index ( 0 , 0 ), ... names = {}, ... parent = QWidget (), ... ) # a row with no stored question shows nothing

title: alto.ui.database_page
text: DatabasePage DatabasePage ( learner : Learner , * , parent : QWidget | None = None , ) [Source] Bases: QWidget The tables behind the app. Answers and questions are the active profile’s own; profiles lists everyone. Attributes back ( Signal ): Emitted by Escape; the main window provides the shared Back button. learner ( Learner ): Whose answers and questions are shown. tabs ( dict of str to QPushButton ): The buttons that choose the table: “answers”, “questions” and “profiles”. search ( QLineEdit ): Filters every column at once. view ( QTableView ): The table. proxy ( QSortFilterProxyModel ): Sorts and filters the rows. Examples >>> from alto.learning import Database >>> db = Database () >>> page = DatabasePage ( ... Learner ( ... db , profile = db . add_profile ( "Ada" ) ... ) ... ) >>> page . note . text () '0 answers by Ada.' Constructor Build the page, showing the answers table. Parameters learner ( Learner ): Whose data to show. parent ( QWidget or None, default None ): The widget that owns the page. Keyword-only. Constructor examples >>> from alto.learning import Database >>> db = Database () >>> page = DatabasePage ( ... Learner ( ... db , profile = db . add_profile ( "Ada" ) ... ) ... ) >>> page . tabs [ "answers" ]. isChecked () True

title: alto.ui.database_page
text: DatabasePage.show_table def show_table ( key : str , * , keep_sort : bool = False , ) -> None [Source] Show one of the tables. Parameters key ( str ): “answers”, “questions” or “profiles”. keep_sort ( bool ): Preserve the current column and order when refreshing the open table. Examples >>> from alto.learning import Database >>> db = Database () >>> page = DatabasePage ( ... Learner ( ... db , profile = db . add_profile ( "Ada" ) ... ) ... ) >>> page . show_table ( "profiles" ) >>> page . note . text () '1 profile.'

title: alto.ui.degree_text

text: draw_degree_text def draw_degree_text ( painter : QPainter , * , rect : QRectF , text : str , alignment : Qt . AlignmentFlag = Qt . AlignmentFlag . AlignCenter , ) -> None [Source] Draw text with each combining circumflex centered above its preceding digit. Parameters painter ( QPainter ): The active painter, with the desired font and color. rect ( QRectF ): The rectangle in which to align the text. Keyword-only. text ( str ): The text, retaining combining circumflexes for copying and accessibility. Keyword-only. alignment ( Qt.AlignmentFlag, default AlignCenter ): Horizontal and vertical alignment. Keyword-only. Examples >>> from PySide6.QtGui import QPixmap >>> pixmap = QPixmap ( 100 , 40 ) >>> painter_ = QPainter ( pixmap ) >>> draw_degree_text ( ... painter_ , ... rect = QRectF ( 0 , 0 , 100 , 40 ), ... text = "3̂" , ... ) >>> painter_ . end () True

title: alto.ui.engraving
text: alto.ui.engraving Drawing notation with SMuFL music fonts (Bravura, Leland, Petaluma, MuseJazz and others). A SMuFL font has the parts of a note rather than whole notes: the head, the flag, and the clef and accidental glyphs, all measured in staff spaces (four to the em). The stem is a plain rectangle that the code draws, placed using the stem anchors the font publishes for each head. Heights are measured upward, so they are flipped on screen. Examples >>> sorted ( HEADS ) ['breve', 'half', 'whole'] >>> ACCIDENTALS [ 1 ] 'accidentalSharp'

title: alto.ui.engraving
text: notation_glyph @ cache def notation_glyph ( font : str , * , codepoint : int , ) -> QPainterPath [Source] Read a score marking from a bundled font at four staff spaces per em. Parameters font ( str ): Preferred SMuFL font key. codepoint ( int ): Standard Music Font Layout code point. Returns QPainterPath : Outline at 100 pixels per em. Bravura supplies markings missing in the selected font. Examples >>> notation_glyph ( ... "bravura" , codepoint = 0xE260 ... ). isEmpty () False

title: alto.ui.engraving
text: staff_line_width def staff_line_width ( font : str , * , gap : float , ) -> float [Source] Return the thickness of a staff line, as the font specifies. Parameters font ( str ): A key of _FILES . gap ( float ): The distance between staff lines in pixels. Keyword-only. Returns float : The thickness in pixels, at least 1. Examples >>> staff_line_width ( "bravura" , gap = 16 ) >= 1.0 True

title: alto.ui.engraving
text: ledger_width def ledger_width ( font : str , * , gap : float , ) -> float [Source] Return the thickness of a ledger line, as the font specifies. Parameters font ( str ): A key of _FILES . gap ( float ): The distance between staff lines in pixels. Keyword-only. Returns float : The thickness in pixels, at least 1.2. Examples >>> ledger_width ( "bravura" , gap = 16 ) >= 1.2 True

title: alto.ui.engraving
text: fill_path def fill_path ( p : QPainter , * , path : QPainterPath , color : QColor , ) -> None [Source] Fill a path with a color and no outline. Parameters p ( QPainter ): The painter to draw with. path ( QPainterPath ): What to fill. Keyword-only. color ( QColor ): The color. Keyword-only. Examples >>> from PySide6.QtGui import QImage >>> image = QImage ( ... 20 , 20 , QImage . Format . Format_ARGB32 ... ) >>> image . fill ( QColor ( "white" )) >>> painter = QPainter ( image ) >>> square = QPainterPath () >>> square . addRect ( QRectF ( 5 , 5 , 10 , 10 )) >>> fill_path ( ... painter , ... path = square , ... color = QColor ( "black" ), ... ) >>> painter . end () True >>> image . pixelColor ( 10 , 10 ). lightness () < 128 True

title: alto.ui.engraving
text: draw_note def draw_note ( p : QPainter , * , font : str , value : str , x : float , y : float , gap : float , color : QColor , stem_down : bool = False , flag_color : QColor | None = None , ) -> None [Source] Draw a note with its head centered on a point. The head, then a stem and (for the short values) a flag, placed on the font’s anchors. Parameters p ( QPainter ): The painter to draw with. font ( str ): A key of _FILES . Keyword-only. value ( str ): “breve”, “whole”, “half”, “quarter”, “eighth”, “sixteenth” or “thirty_second”. Keyword-only. x ( float ): The head’s center, in pixels. Keyword-only. y ( float ): The head’s center, in pixels. Keyword-only. gap ( float ): The distance between staff lines in pixels. Keyword-only. color ( QColor ): The color. Keyword-only. flag_color ( QColor or None ): Optional highlight for the flag alone. Keyword-only. stem_down ( bool, default False ): Draw the stem down. Keyword-only. Examples >>> from PySide6.QtGui import QImage >>> image = QImage ( ... 100 , 100 , QImage . Format . Format_ARGB32 ... ) >>> image . fill ( QColor ( "white" )) >>> painter = QPainter ( image ) >>> draw_note ( ... painter , ... font = "bravura" , ... value = "eighth" , ... x = 50 , ... y = 60 , ... gap = 16 , ... color = QColor ( "black" ), ... ) >>> painter . end () True >>> image . pixelColor ( 50 , 60 ). lightness () < 128 True

title: alto.ui.engraving
text: draw_beamed_eighths def draw_beamed_eighths ( p : QPainter , * , font : str , heads : list [ QPointF ], colors : list [ QColor ], gap : float , middle : float , ink : QColor , ) -> None [Source] Draw one beat of eighth notes with stems joined to a common beam. Parameters p ( QPainter ): Score painter. font ( str ): Selected SMuFL font. heads ( list of QPointF ): Notehead centers in reading order. colors ( list of QColor ): Ink for each notehead and its stem. gap ( float ): Staff space in pixels. middle ( float ): Height of the middle staff line, for choosing stem direction. ink ( QColor ): Color of the shared beam. Examples >>> from PySide6.QtGui import QPicture >>> with QPainter ( QPicture ()) as painter : # doctest: +SKIP ... draw_beamed_eighths ( ... painter , font = "bravura" , gap = 8 , middle = 40 , ... heads = [ QPointF ( 20 , 48 ), QPointF ( 40 , 44 )], ... colors = [ QColor ( "black" )] * 2 , ink = QColor ( "black" ), ... )

title: alto.ui.engraving
text: draw_clef def draw_clef ( p : QPainter , * , font : str , clef : str , x : float , bottom : float , gap : float , color : QColor , ) -> None [Source] Draw a clef with its left edge at a point. Parameters p ( QPainter ): The painter to draw with. font ( str ): A key of _FILES . Keyword-only. clef ( str ): “treble”, “bass”, “alto”, “tenor”, “soprano”, “mezzo”, “baritone_c” or “baritone_f”. Keyword-only. x ( float ): The clef’s left edge, in pixels. Keyword-only. bottom ( float ): The y position of the staff’s bottom line, in pixels. Keyword-only. gap ( float ): The distance between staff lines in pixels. Keyword-only. color ( QColor ): The color. Keyword-only. Examples >>> from PySide6.QtGui import QImage >>> image = QImage ( ... 100 , 100 , QImage . Format . Format_ARGB32 ... ) >>> image . fill ( QColor ( "white" )) >>> painter = QPainter ( image ) >>> draw_clef ( ... painter , ... font = "bravura" , ... clef = "treble" , ... x = 10 , ... bottom = 70 , ... gap = 10 , ... color = QColor ( "black" ), ... ) >>> painter . end () True >>> any ( ... image . pixelColor ( x_ , y ). lightness () ... < 128 ... for x_ in range ( 10 , 40 ) ... for y in range ( 20 , 90 ) ... ) True

title: alto.ui.engraving
text: accidental_width def accidental_width ( * , font : str , sign : int , gap : float , ) -> float [Source] Return how wide a sharp, flat or natural is drawn, so that it can be placed beside other things. Parameters font ( str ): A key of _FILES . Keyword-only. sign ( int ): -2 for a double flat, -1 flat, 0 natural, 1 sharp or 2 double sharp. Keyword-only. gap ( float ): The distance between staff lines in pixels, which sets the size. Keyword-only. Returns float : The width of the glyph’s ink, in pixels. Examples >>> accidental_width ( ... font = "bravura" , sign = 1 , gap = 16 ... ) > accidental_width ( ... font = "bravura" , sign = 1 , gap = 8 ... ) True

title: alto.ui.engraving
text: draw_accidental def draw_accidental ( p : QPainter , * , font : str , sign : int , x : float , y : float , gap : float , color : QColor , fit : float | None = None , ) -> float [Source] Draw a sharp, flat or natural with its left edge at a point. Parameters p ( QPainter ): The painter to draw with. font ( str ): A key of _FILES . Keyword-only. sign ( int ): -2 for a double flat, -1 flat, 0 natural, 1 sharp or 2 double sharp. Keyword-only. x ( float ): The glyph’s left edge, in pixels. Keyword-only. y ( float ): The glyph’s reference line, in pixels. Keyword-only. gap ( float ): The distance between staff lines in pixels. Keyword-only. color ( QColor ): The color. Keyword-only. fit ( float or None, default None ): If given, shrink the glyph to be no wider than this many pixels. Keyword-only. Returns float : The width drawn, in pixels. Examples >>> from PySide6.QtGui import QImage >>> image = QImage ( ... 100 , 100 , QImage . Format . Format_ARGB32 ... ) >>> painter = QPainter ( image ) >>> normal = draw_accidental ( ... painter , ... font = "bravura" , ... sign = 1 , ... x = 10 , ... y = 50 , ... gap = 16 , ... color = QColor ( "black" ), ... ) >>> squeezed = draw_accidental ( ... painter , ... font = "bravura" , ... sign = 1 , ... x = 10 , ... y = 50 , ... gap = 16 , ... color = QColor ( "black" ), ... fit = 5.0 , ... ) >>> painter . end () True >>> squeezed <= 5.0 < normal True

title: alto.ui.engraving
text: draw_brace def draw_brace ( p : QPainter , * , font : str , x : float , y0 : float , y1 : float , color : QColor , width : float , ) -> bool [Source] Draw the font’s brace stretched between two heights, for a grand staff. Parameters p ( QPainter ): The painter to draw with. font ( str ): A key of _FILES . Keyword-only. x ( float ): The brace’s right edge, in pixels. Keyword-only. y0 ( float ): The top, in pixels. Keyword-only. y1 ( float ): The bottom, in pixels. Keyword-only. color ( QColor ): The color. Keyword-only. width ( float ): How wide to draw it, in pixels. Keyword-only. Returns bool : True if it was drawn; False (and nothing is drawn) if the font has no usable brace. Examples >>> from PySide6.QtGui import QImage >>> image = QImage ( ... 100 , 100 , QImage . Format . Format_ARGB32 ... ) >>> painter = QPainter ( image ) >>> draw_brace ( ... painter , ... font = "bravura" , ... x = 30 , ... y0 = 10 , ... y1 = 90 , ... color = QColor ( "black" ), ... width = 12 , ... ) True >>> painter . end () True

title: alto.ui.exercise_settings
text: alto.ui.exercise_settings Load and save each exercise’s settings. The settings themselves are plain dataclasses in alto.settings , one shared object per exercise. The functions here read them from the saved preferences when Alto starts ( load_exercise_settings ) and write them back when a settings panel changes them. Values saved by older versions are converted, and anything saved that is not valid any more is ignored. Examples >>> load_note_names () >>> settings . note_names . naming in NAMINGS True

title: alto.ui.exercise_settings
text: load_note_names def load_note_names () -> None [Source] Load the saved note identification settings into the shared settings object. Settings saved by an older version, which had a switch between the grand staff and single clefs, are converted. Anything in the saved data that is not valid is ignored. Examples >>> cfg_ = settings . note_names >>> cfg_ . clefs = { "alto" } >>> save_note_names () >>> cfg_ . clefs = { "treble" } >>> load_note_names () >>> cfg_ . clefs {'alto'} >>> cfg_ . clefs = { "treble" , "bass" } >>> save_note_names ()

title: alto.ui.exercise_settings
text: save_note_names def save_note_names () -> None [Source] Save the note identification settings. Examples >>> cfg_ = settings . note_names >>> cfg_ . naming = "solfege" >>> save_note_names () >>> str ( store (). value ( "noteNames/naming" )) 'solfege' >>> cfg_ . naming = "letters" >>> save_note_names ()

title: alto.ui.exercise_settings
text: load_keyboard def load_keyboard () -> None [Source] Load the saved keyboard exercise settings into the shared settings object. A saved range that is not a valid span of keys, or a key list with nothing usable in it, is ignored. Examples >>> cfg_ = settings . keyboard >>> cfg_ . require_octave = True >>> save_keyboard () >>> cfg_ . require_octave = False >>> load_keyboard () >>> cfg_ . require_octave True >>> cfg_ . require_octave = False >>> save_keyboard ()

title: alto.ui.exercise_settings
text: save_keyboard def save_keyboard () -> None [Source] Save the keyboard exercise settings. Examples >>> cfg_ = settings . keyboard >>> save_keyboard () >>> int ( ... store (). value ( "keyboard/low" ) ... ) == cfg_ . low True

title: alto.ui.exercise_settings
text: load_keyboard_intervals def load_keyboard_intervals () -> None [Source] Load keyboard interval settings, ignoring invalid values and intervals that cannot fit. Examples >>> load_keyboard_intervals () >>> settings . keyboard_intervals . bounds ()[ ... 0 ... ] < settings . keyboard_intervals . bounds ()[ 1 ] True

title: alto.ui.exercise_settings
text: save_keyboard_intervals def save_keyboard_intervals ( cfg : settings . KeyboardIntervalSettings ) -> None [Source] Save the keyboard interval range and selected distances. Parameters cfg ( KeyboardIntervalSettings ): The settings to save. Examples >>> save_keyboard_intervals ( ... settings . KeyboardIntervalSettings () ... ) >>> int ( store (). value ( "keyboardIntervals/low" )) 48

title: alto.ui.exercise_settings
text: load_construction def load_construction () -> None [Source] Load the saved note construction settings into the shared settings object. Examples >>> store (). setValue ( ... "construction/accidentals" , "true" ... ) >>> load_construction () >>> settings . construction . accidentals False

title: alto.ui.exercise_settings
text: save_construction def save_construction ( cfg : settings . ConstructionSettings ) -> None [Source] Save the note construction settings. Parameters cfg ( ConstructionSettings ): The settings to save. Examples >>> settings . construction . degrees = { 1 , 3 } >>> save_construction ( settings . construction ) >>> str ( store (). value ( "construction/degrees" )) '1,3' >>> settings . construction . degrees = set ( ... range ( 1 , 8 ) ... ) >>> save_construction ( settings . construction )

title: alto.ui.exercise_settings
text: load_arpeggio def load_arpeggio () -> None [Source] Load the saved arpeggio settings into the shared settings object. Anything in the saved data that is not valid is ignored, and a list with nothing valid in it leaves the setting as it was. Examples >>> store (). setValue ( "arpeggio/types" , "major" ) >>> load_arpeggio () >>> settings . arpeggio . types {'major'} >>> settings . arpeggio . types = { ... "major" , ... "minor" , ... "dominant 7th" , ... "diminished 7th" , ... } >>> store (). setValue ( ... "arpeggio/types" , ... "," . join ( ... settings . arpeggio . active_types () ... ), ... )

ScaleConstructionSettings () ... ) >>> _load_key_settings ( ... loaded_ , prefix = "doctestScales" ... ) >>> sorted ( loaded_ . modes ), loaded_ . steps (['Dorian', 'Major (Ionian)'], True) >>> store (). remove ( "doctestScales" )

title: alto.ui.exercise_view
text: alto.ui.exercise_view The exercise screen: a question, its answer buttons, the score, and a pane of settings that slides in from the right. One ExerciseView works for every exercise. It asks the exercise (or, with a profile, the learner) for the next Question , shows it as a staff, a keyboard or text, offers the answer buttons, and records each answer. Examples >>> from alto.exercises.library import NoteNames >>> view = ExerciseView ( ... NoteNames (), rng = random . Random ( 1 ) ... ) >>> # noinspection PyUnresolvedReferences >>> view . question . answer in [ ... button . text () for button in view . buttons ... ] True

title: alto.ui.exercise_view
text: choice_keys def choice_keys ( choices : list [ str ]) -> list [ str ] [Source] Choose a key for each answer button, so that every answer can be given from the keyboard. Nine answers or fewer take the digits 1 to 9. More than that, as on the piano keyboard, take the notes’ own names: the letter for a natural, Shift and the letter for a sharp, Ctrl and the letter for a flat. A minor key, such as F♯m, is typed the same way as the major key of its name. Any other long list takes 1 to 9 and then 0, and the rest can be reached with Tab. Scale-degree banks use the degree digit, with Shift for a sharp, Ctrl for a flat, and Alt added for double alterations. Parameters choices ( list of str ): The answers, in the order of their buttons. Returns list of str : A key for each answer, such as “3” or “Shift+C”; “” for an answer that has none. Examples >>> choice_keys ( ... [ "major" , "minor" , "diminished" ] ... ) ['1', '2', '3'] >>> choice_keys ( ... list ( "CDEFGAB" ) + [ "C♯" , "B♭" ] + [ "F♯" ] ... ) ['C', 'D', 'E', 'F', 'G', 'A', 'B', 'Shift+C', 'Ctrl+B', 'Shift+F'] >>> choice_keys ([ str ( n ) for n in range ( 12 )])[ 8 :] ['9', '0', '', '']

title: alto.ui.exercise_view
text: second_row_keys def second_row_keys ( first : list [ str ], * , labels : list [ str ], ) -> list [ str ] [Source] Choose a key for each button of the second row of a two-part answer, such as the octave or the inversion. They must not be keys that the first row has. When the first row uses the digits the second row takes the home row, A S D F and so on; when the first row uses letters (the notes’ names) it takes the digits, and an octave that is a single digit takes that digit. Parameters first ( list of str ): The keys of the first row, as choice_keys chose them. labels ( list of str ): The text of each button of the second row. Keyword-only. Returns list of str : A key for each button; “” for one that has none. Examples >>> second_row_keys ( ... [ "1" , "2" , "3" ], ... labels = [ ... "root position" , ... "1st inversion" , ... ], ... ) ['A', 'S'] >>> second_row_keys ( ... [ "C" , "Shift+C" ], labels = [ "3" , "4" , "5" ] ... ) ['3', '4', '5']

title: alto.ui.exercise_view
text: note_name def note_name ( note : Note , * , key : int | None = None , minor : bool = False , ) -> str [Source] Return a note’s name as it is written, with its octave: F♯4. Parameters note ( Note ): The note. key ( int or None, default None ): The major key signature for scale degrees. Without a key context, degrees fall back to letter names. Keyword-only. minor ( bool, default False ): Use natural minor scale degrees. Keyword-only. Returns str : The name in the naming the app is set to, then the octave number. Examples >>> note_name ( Note . parse ( "F#4" )) 'F♯4'

title: alto.ui.exercise_view
text: note_words def note_words ( note : Note , * , key : int | None = None , minor : bool = False , ) -> str [Source] Return a note’s name in words, for a screen reader: “F sharp 4”. Parameters note ( Note ): The note. key ( int or None, default None ): The major key signature for scale degrees. Without a key context, use letter names. Keyword-only. minor ( bool, default False ): Use natural minor scale degrees. Keyword-only. Returns str : The letter, then “sharp”, “flat” or “natural” if it has a sign, then the octave number. Examples >>> ( ... note_words ( Note . parse ( "F#4" )), ... note_words ( Note . parse ( "Bb3" )), ... note_words ( Note . parse ( "C4" )), ... ) ('F sharp 4', 'B flat 3', 'C 4')

title: alto.ui.exercise_view
text: ExerciseView ExerciseView ( exercise : Exercise , * , rng : random . Random | None = None , parent : QWidget | None = None , learner : Learner | None = None , ) [Source] Bases: QWidget The screen for practicing one exercise. Attributes PANE_WIDTH ( int ): The width of the settings pane when it is open, in pixels. REFERENCE_WIDTH ( int ): The width of the reference pane when it is open, in pixels. exercise ( Exercise ): The exercise being practiced. learner ( Learner or None ): Records every answer and chooses what to ask next; None asks at random. rng ( random.Random ): The random number generator for new questions. correct ( int ): Questions answered right on the first try. total ( int ): Questions answered. streak ( int ): Right answers in a row. question ( Question or None ): The question on screen. answered ( bool ): True once this showing is finished, including a miss in SM-2 or FSRS. missed ( bool ): True once the question has been answered wrong, so it no longer counts toward the score. buttons ( list of QPushButton ): The answer buttons on screen. settings_panel ( ExerciseSettingsPanel ): The exercise’s settings, including how to advance after a correct answer. staff ( StaffWidget ): Shows the notes of a question. keyboard ( KeyboardWidget ): Shows the key of a keyboard question. input_staff ( StaffInput ): The staff to click, for “place this note” questions. clef_input ( ClefInput ): The blank staff a clef is put on, for “place this clef” questions. scale_input ( ScaleInput ): The staff to click, for “place the notes of this scale” questions. fork ( KeyFork ): The fork to pick a key signature on, for “build this key signature” questions. answer_button ( QPushButton ): Hands in what was built with the fork or placed on the scale staff. book_btn ( QToolButton or None ): Opens the exercise’s reference in a pane on the right; None for an exercise that has none. reference_pane ( QFrame or None ): The pane that holds the reference. lesson_requested ( Signal ): Emitted with a lesson’s key when the reference pane’s lesson button is pressed. shuffle_requested ( Signal ): Emitted when answer feedback ends or Next is clicked during shuffled practice. Examples >>> from alto.exercises.library import NoteNames >>> view = ExerciseView ( ... NoteNames (), rng = random . Random ( 1 ) ... ) >>> view . score . text () '0/0 (–) streak 0' Constructor Build the screen and show the first question. Parameters exercise ( Exercise ): The exercise to practice. rng ( random.Random or None, default None ): The random number generator; a fresh one if None. Keyword-only. parent ( QWidget or None, default None ): The widget that owns the screen. Keyword-only. learner ( Learner or None, default None ): Where to record answers and what to ask next; None asks at random and records nothing. Keyword-only. Constructor examples >>> from alto.exercises.library import ( ... KeySignatures , ... ) >>> view = ExerciseView ( ... KeySignatures (), rng = random . Random ( 2 ) ... ) >>> # the exercise has settings behind the gear button >>> view . settings_panel is not None True

title: alto.ui.exercise_view
text: ExerciseView.eventFilter def eventFilter ( watched : QObject , event : QEvent , ) -> bool [Source] Handle staff clicks in notation questions and forward wheel turns to the fork or clef staff. Parameters watched ( QObject ): The staff or the Answer button. event ( QEvent ): The incoming pointer or widget event. Returns bool : True when the exercise handles the event. Examples >>> from PySide6.QtCore import QPoint , QPointF >>> from PySide6.QtGui import QWheelEvent >>> from alto.exercises.library import ( ... KeySignatureConstruction , ... ) >>> view = ExerciseView ( ... KeySignatureConstruction (), ... rng = random . Random ( 1 ), ... ) >>> view . show () >>> here = QPointF ( 5 , 5 ) >>> turn = QWheelEvent ( ... here , ... here , ... QPoint ( 0 , 0 ), ... QPoint ( 0 , 120 ), ... Qt . MouseButton . NoButton , ... Qt . KeyboardModifier . NoModifier , ... Qt . ScrollPhase . NoScrollPhase , ... False , ... ) >>> view . eventFilter ( view . answer_button , turn ) True >>> view . fork . value 1

title: alto.ui.exercise_view
text: ExerciseView.submit def submit ( choice : str , * , button : QPushButton | None , ) -> None [Source] Check an answer chosen with a button or by clicking the notation. A correct answer uses the selected Next Question setting. An incorrect button flashes red. In SM-2 and FSRS the card returns at its scheduled retry time. ASRS and ARTS allow another answer on the same showing. Parameters choice ( str ): The text of the button that was pressed. button ( QPushButton or None ): The pressed button, or None for a staff click. Keyword-only. Examples >>> from alto.exercises.library import NoteNames >>> sounds . enabled = False >>> view = ExerciseView ( ... NoteNames (), rng = random . Random ( 1 ) ... ) >>> question = view . question >>> # noinspection PyUnresolvedReferences >>> wrong = next ( ... b ... for b in view . buttons ... if b . text () != question . answer ... ) >>> view . submit ( wrong . text (), button = wrong ) >>> view . missed , wrong . isEnabled () (True, False) >>> # noinspection PyUnresolvedReferences >>> right = next ( ... b ... for b in view . buttons ... if b . text () == question . answer ... ) >>> # noinspection PyUnresolvedReferences >>> view . submit ( question . answer , button = right ) >>> view . answered True >>> view . _advance . stop () >>> sounds . enabled = True

title: alto.ui.fingerboard
text: alto.ui.fingerboard Render a pack’s instrument portrait using its calibrated string endpoints.

title: alto.ui.fingerboard
text: ruler_reach def ruler_reach ( model : PackInstrument ) -> int [Source] Find how many half steps the ruler covers: an octave, or further if the pack names a position beyond it. Parameters model ( PackInstrument ): The instrument whose positions, if any, the ruler labels. Returns int : The highest half step with a tick. Examples >>> from pathlib import Path >>> bare = PackInstrument ( ... "pack.x.y" , ... Path ( "a.png" ), ... ( 10 , 10 ), ... (), ... None , ... ) >>> ruler_reach ( bare ) 12 >>> ruler_reach ( ... PackInstrument ( ... "pack.x.y" , ... Path ( "a.png" ), ... ( 10 , 10 ), ... (), ... None , ... positions = (( 14 , "9th" ),), ... ) ... ) 14

title: alto.ui.fingerboard
text: ruler_base def ruler_base ( model : PackInstrument , * , step : int , ) -> tuple [ QPointF , QPointF , float ] [Source] Locate where a ruler tick for one half step starts, beside the fingerboard rather than on it. Parameters model ( PackInstrument ): The instrument whose string endpoints give the geometry. step ( int ): Half steps above the open string. Returns tuple of QPointF, QPointF and float : The tick’s starting point in image pixels, the unit vector pointing away from the strings, and the local distance between neighboring strings at that step. Examples >>> from pathlib import Path >>> from alto.instrument_packs import PackString >>> strings = ( ... PackString ( "C3" , ( 0 , 10 ), ( 100 , 10 )), ... PackString ( "G3" , ( 0 , 0 ), ( 100 , 0 )), ... ) >>> viola = PackInstrument ( ... "pack.x.y" , ... Path ( "a.png" ), ... ( 100 , 10 ), ... strings , ... None , ... ) >>> start , away , apart = ruler_base ( ... viola , step = 0 ... ) >>> ( start . x (), start . y (), away . y (), apart ) (0.0, -18.0, -1.0, 10.0)

title: alto.ui.fingerboard
text: neck_view def neck_view ( model : PackInstrument , * , gap : float , ) -> QRectF [Source] Choose the part of the picture a note question needs: the nut, the neck with its ruler, and the bridge. The scroll, the pegs and everything past the bridge are left out, since the question never refers to them. Parameters model ( PackInstrument ): The instrument whose string endpoints give the geometry. gap ( float ): The smallest distance between strings at the nut, in image pixels. Keyword-only. Returns QRectF : The region to show, in image pixels. It can extend past the picture, so intersect it with the picture’s rectangle. Examples >>> from pathlib import Path >>> from alto.instrument_packs import PackString >>> strings = ( ... PackString ( "C3" , ( 100 , 60 ), ( 900 , 60 )), ... PackString ( "G3" , ( 100 , 40 ), ( 900 , 40 )), ... ) >>> board = PackInstrument ( ... "pack.x.y" , ... Path ( "a.png" ), ... ( 1000 , 100 ), ... strings , ... None , ... ) >>> view = neck_view ( board , gap = 20.0 ) >>> ( ... view . left () < 100 ... and view . right () > 900 ... and view . top () < 40 ... and view . bottom () > 60 ... ) True

title: alto.ui.fingerboard
text: manual_style def manual_style ( model : PackInstrument ) -> tuple [ KeyboardStyle | None , float ] [Source] Build the look of an instrument’s drawn keyboards from its plugin’s keyboard_style . Parameters model ( PackInstrument ): The instrument whose keyboards are drawn. Returns tuple of KeyboardStyle or None and float : The style, or None to use the learner’s own keyboard style, and how long a natural key is, in key widths. Examples >>> from pathlib import Path >>> bare = PackInstrument ( ... "pack.x.y" , ... Path ( "a.png" ), ... ( 10 , 10 ), ... (), ... None , ... ) >>> manual_style ( bare ) (None, 4.5) >>> from alto.instrument_packs import ( ... PackKeyboardStyle , ... ) >>> look = PackKeyboardStyle ( ... (( "cap" , "#eee3c8" ),), ... (( "length" , 5.0 ),), ... ) >>> styled = PackInstrument ( ... "pack.x.y" , ... Path ( "a.png" ), ... ( 10 , 10 ), ... (), ... None , ... keyboard_style = look , ... ) >>> look_style , look_length = manual_style ( ... styled ... ) >>> # noinspection PyUnresolvedReferences >>> look_style . cap , look_length ('#eee3c8', 5.0)

text: GlossaryPage.hideEvent def hideEvent ( event : QHideEvent ) -> None [Source] End the example when leaving the glossary. Parameters event ( QHideEvent ): The notification that the glossary has been hidden.

title: alto.ui.home
text: alto.ui.home The start screen: a card for every exercise, or for every lesson, in rows. A switch at the top chooses between the exercises and the lessons. Examples >>> from alto.exercises import REGISTRY >>> page = HomePage ( REGISTRY ) >>> len ( page . cards ) == len ( REGISTRY ) True

title: alto.ui.home
text: category_tree def category_tree ( name : str ) -> QTreeWidget [Source] Build a navigation tree with themed checkboxes and right-aligned expansion arrows. Parameters name ( str ): Accessible name of the tree. Returns QTreeWidget : Empty tree ready for categories and exercises. Examples >>> category_tree ( "Decks" ). columnCount () 2

title: alto.ui.home
text: TileCard TileCard ( * , icon : str , category : str , name : str , about : str , progress : tuple [ int , int ] | None = None , parent : QWidget | None = None , ) [Source] Bases: QPushButton A big button: an icon on top, then a category, a name and a short description, and optionally a lesson’s progress. Progress takes no room in the layout: a strip along the bottom edge shows it, and “Step N/M” sits in the top-right corner, both only once the lesson has been begun. A card with or without progress therefore has the same size and the same icon. Examples >>> card = TileCard ( ... icon = icons . EXERCISE_CIRCLE , ... category = "Scales & Keys" , ... name = "Circle of Fifths" , ... about = "Find keys." , ... ) >>> ( card . width (), card . height ()) == ( ... CARD_W , ... CARD_H , ... ) True >>> card . accessibleName () 'Circle of Fifths, Scales & Keys' Constructor Build a card. Parameters icon ( str ): The inside of a 24 by 24 SVG, drawn in the text color. Keyword-only. category ( str ): The small heading above the name. Keyword-only. name ( str ): The name. Keyword-only. about ( str ): A line of description, which is also the tooltip. Keyword-only. progress ( tuple of int or None, default None ): The step you are on, counting from 0, and how many steps there are. The bar and “Step N/M” appear only once the first step has been passed; nothing is drawn if None or at step 0. Keyword-only. parent ( QWidget or None, default None ): The widget that owns the card. Keyword-only. Constructor examples >>> card = TileCard ( ... icon = icons . HELP , ... category = "Help" , ... name = "Help" , ... about = "Get help." , ... progress = ( 1 , 8 ), ... ) >>> card . toolTip (), card . accessibleDescription () ('Get help.', 'Get help. Continue at step 2 of 8.')

title: alto.ui.home
text: TileCard.changeEvent def changeEvent ( event : QEvent ) -> None [Source] Recolor the icon when the tile receives a new palette. Parameters event ( QEvent ): The widget change delivered by Qt. Examples >>> card = lesson_card ( LESSONS [ 0 ]) >>> card . changeEvent ( ... QEvent ( QEvent . Type . PaletteChange ) ... )

title: alto.ui.home
text: exercise_icon def exercise_icon ( name : str ) -> str [Source] Find the icon for an exercise: the one its plugin supplies, or Alto’s own. Parameters name ( str ): The exercise’s class name. Returns str : SVG shapes with COLOR where the theme’s ink goes. Examples >>> exercise_icon ( ... "NoteNames" ... ) == icons . EXERCISE_NOTE_NAMES True >>> exercise_icon ( ... "pack.nothing.here" ... ) == icons . EXERCISE_NOTE_NAMES True

title: alto.ui.home
text: lesson_icon def lesson_icon ( lesson : Lesson ) -> str [Source] Find the icon for a lesson’s tile: its own if a plugin gave it one, otherwise its primary exercise’s. Parameters lesson ( Lesson ): The lesson. Returns str : SVG shapes with COLOR where the theme’s ink goes. Examples >>> lesson_icon ( LESSONS [ 0 ]) == exercise_icon ( ... LESSONS [ 0 ]. exercise ... ) True

title: alto.ui.home
text: ExerciseCard ExerciseCard ( cls : type [ Exercise ], * , parent : QWidget | None = None , ) [Source] Bases: TileCard The card of an exercise: its icon on top, then its category, name and a one-line description. Examples >>> from alto.exercises.library import NoteNames >>> card = ExerciseCard ( NoteNames ) >>> card . toolTip () == NoteNames . description True >>> ( card . width (), card . height ()) == ( ... CARD_W , ... CARD_H , ... ) True Constructor Build the card for one exercise. Parameters cls ( type of Exercise ): The exercise class; its name, category and description are shown, and its class name picks the icon. parent ( QWidget or None, default None ): The widget that owns the card. Keyword-only. Constructor examples >>> from alto.exercises.library import ( ... IntervalNames , ... ) >>> ExerciseCard ( IntervalNames ). toolTip () 'Name the interval between two notes.'

title: alto.ui.home
text: ExerciseCard.set_counts def set_counts ( counts : tuple [ int , int ] | tuple [ int , int , int ] | None ) -> None [Source] Show due reviews, new cards, and outstanding incorrect cards in the upper right corner. Parameters counts ( tuple of int or None ): Reviews due, new cards available, and optionally the outstanding incorrect count. None hides the counts. Examples >>> from alto.exercises.library import NoteNames >>> card = ExerciseCard ( NoteNames ) >>> card . set_counts (( 2 , 3 , 1 )) >>> print ( card . counts . toolTip ()) Blue — 3 new cards available Red — 1 incorrect card awaiting a correct answer Green — 2 reviews due

title: alto.ui.home
text: lesson_card def lesson_card ( lesson : Lesson , * , parent : QWidget | None = None , ) -> TileCard [Source] Make the card of a lesson: the icon of the exercise that practices the same topic, and a bar for how far through it you are. Parameters lesson ( Lesson ): The lesson. parent ( QWidget or None, default None ): The widget that owns the card. Keyword-only. Returns TileCard : The card, with a progress bar and “Step N/M” in its corner once the lesson has been begun. Examples >>> card = lesson_card ( LESSONS [ 0 ]) >>> card . accessibleName () 'Pitches and Notes, Notation'

title: alto.ui.home
text: HomePage HomePage ( registry : Iterable [ type [ Exercise ]], * , parent : QWidget | None = None , learner : Learner | None = None , filter_layout : QHBoxLayout | None = None , ) [Source] Bases: QWidget The start screen: a row of exercise buttons for each category. Attributes exercise_chosen ( Signal ): Emitted with the Exercise class when a card is clicked. lesson_chosen ( Signal ): Emitted with a lesson’s key when its card is clicked. filters_changed ( Signal ): Emitted after a change to the search, tile selection or displayed section. cards ( list of ExerciseCard ): One per exercise, in registry order. lesson_cards ( list of TileCard ): One per lesson, with how far through it you are. canvas ( TransitionCanvas ): Where the transition between the exercises and the lessons is drawn. mode_control ( SegmentedControl ): The switch between the exercises and the lessons. The main window puts it in its top bar. resume_button ( QPushButton ): Returns to the retained activity. The main window places it beside search and shows it on tiles after an activity begins. category_filter ( QToolButton ): Shows or hides the filter sidebar from the right end of the search row. no_results ( QLabel ): Shown when no tiles match the search. mode ( str ): “exercises” or “lessons”: which cards are showing. scroll_area ( QScrollArea ): Scrolls the rows when the window is shorter than all of them. Examples >>> from alto.exercises import REGISTRY >>> page = HomePage ( REGISTRY ) >>> chosen = [] >>> _ = page . exercise_chosen . connect ( ... chosen . append ... ) >>> page . cards [ 0 ]. click () >>> chosen == [ REGISTRY [ 0 ]] True Constructor Build the page. Parameters registry ( iterable of type of Exercise ): The exercises to show, in the order to show them. parent ( QWidget or None, default None ): The widget that owns the page. Keyword-only. learner ( Learner or None ): Profile supplying the exercise tile counts. filter_layout ( QHBoxLayout or None ): Shared workspace layout for the filter sidebar. A standalone page places it beside its tiles. Constructor examples >>> from alto.exercises.library import NoteNames >>> len ( HomePage ([ NoteNames ]). cards ) 1

title: alto.ui.home
text: HomePage.set_search def set_search ( text : str ) -> None [Source] Show only tiles matching a title, description or category search. Parameters text ( str ): Case-insensitive search text. Empty text shows every tile in the selected category. Examples >>> from alto.exercises import REGISTRY >>> page = HomePage ( REGISTRY ) >>> page . set_search ( "keyboard" ) >>> page . _query 'keyboard'

title: alto.ui.home
text: HomePage.matches_filter def matches_filter ( card : TileCard , * , section : str , ) -> bool [Source] Check whether a tile matches the search text and the selection for its section. Examples >>> from alto.exercises.library import NoteNames >>> page = HomePage ([ NoteNames ]) >>> page . matches_filter ( ... page . cards [ 0 ], section = "exercises" ... ) True

title: alto.ui.home

title: alto.ui.home

title: alto.ui.home

None keeps its current state. Examples >>> HomePage ([]). restore_tile_filters ({})

title: alto.ui.home
text: HomePage.set_category def set_category ( category : str | None ) -> None [Source] Select the tiles of one category, or all tiles when the category is absent. title: alto.ui.home
text: HomePage.set_mode def set_mode ( mode : str , * , animate : bool = True , ) -> None [Source] Show the exercises or the lessons, and remember which. The cards change with the transition that is chosen in the settings. The new cards are in place at once, so nothing waits on it. Parameters mode ( str ): “exercises” or “lessons”. animate ( bool, default True ): Play the chosen transition; if False the new cards simply appear. Keyword-only. Examples >>> from alto.exercises import REGISTRY >>> page = HomePage ( REGISTRY ) >>> page . set_mode ( "lessons" ) >>> page . mode , page . mode_control . current () ('lessons', 1) >>> page . set_mode ( "exercises" )

title: alto.ui.home
text: HomePage.page_changed def page_changed () -> None [Source] Animate the tiles from an empty grid on return, or stop the animation when leaving. Examples >>> page = HomePage ([]) >>> page . page_changed () >>> page . canvas . running False

title: alto.ui.home
text: HomePage.refresh_counts def refresh_counts () -> None [Source] Refresh each exercise tile and the totals for the current filters. Examples >>> HomePage ([]). refresh_counts ()

title: alto.ui.home
text: HomePage.showEvent def showEvent ( event : QShowEvent ) -> None [Source] Bring the lesson cards up to date each time the page is shown, so they say where each lesson was left.
