text: HomePage.resizeEvent def resizeEvent ( event : QResizeEvent ) -> None [Source] Lay the cards out again when the page changes size. Parameters event ( QResizeEvent ): The resize that happened. Examples >>> from alto.exercises import REGISTRY >>> page = HomePage ( REGISTRY ) >>> page . show () >>> page . resize ( 1000 , 600 ) >>> page . _columns >= 1 True

title: alto.ui.icons
text: alto.ui.icons Small monochrome icons drawn from SVG, tinted with the current theme’s text color. Each icon is the inside of a 24 by 24 SVG, written with the word COLOR where the theme color goes. svg_icon turns one into a QIcon . Examples >>> svg_icon ( ... HELP , color = QColor ( "black" ) ... ). isNull () False

title: alto.ui.icons
text: set_palette_icon def set_palette_icon ( target : QAbstractButton | QAction | QMenu , render : Callable [[ QPalette ], QIcon ], ) -> None [Source] Assign a native Qt icon and refresh it whenever the application palette changes. Parameters target ( QAbstractButton or QAction or QMenu ): Button, menu, or action to update. render ( Callable ): Draws the icon in the supplied palette. Examples >>> from PySide6.QtWidgets import QPushButton >>> button = QPushButton () >>> set_palette_icon ( ... button , ... lambda palette : svg_icon ( ... HELP , color = palette . text (). color () ... ), ... ) >>> button . icon (). isNull () False

title: alto.ui.icons
text: set_svg_icon def set_svg_icon ( target : QAbstractButton | QAction | QMenu , inner : str , * , role : QPalette . ColorRole = QPalette . ColorRole . WindowText , size : int = 24 , ) -> None [Source] Tint an SVG icon with the control’s current foreground or accent color. Parameters target ( QAbstractButton or QAction or QMenu ): Control that displays the icon. inner ( str ): SVG shapes using COLOR for the ink. role ( QPalette.ColorRole, default WindowText ): Color to take from the application palette. size ( int, default 24 ): Logical size in pixels. Examples >>> from PySide6.QtWidgets import QPushButton >>> button = QPushButton () >>> set_svg_icon ( button , HELP ) >>> button . icon (). isNull () False

title: alto.ui.icons
text: set_item_icons def set_item_icons ( view : QAbstractItemView , items : list [ tuple [ str , Callable [[ QIcon ], None ]]], ) -> None [Source] Recolor the current rows of a navigation list or tree without rebuilding it. Parameters view ( QAbstractItemView ): List or tree supplying the text color and icon size. items ( list of tuple ): SVG drawing and icon setter for each row in the current model. Examples A category tree keeps its checked and expanded items when the theme changes.

title: alto.ui.icons
text: svg_icon def svg_icon ( inner : str , * , color : QColor , size : int = 24 , scale : float = 2.0 , ) -> QIcon [Source] Render 24 by 24 SVG shapes into a crisp icon. Parameters inner ( str ): The SVG shapes, using COLOR wherever the color goes. color ( QColor ): The color to draw in. Keyword-only. size ( int, default 24 ): The icon’s size in logical pixels. Keyword-only. scale ( float, default 2.0 ): How many device pixels to render per logical pixel, so it stays sharp on high-resolution screens. Keyword-only. Returns QIcon : The icon. Examples >>> icon = svg_icon ( ... PLAY , color = QColor ( "#336699" ), size = 16 ... ) >>> icon . isNull () False

title: alto.ui.instrument_picker
text: alto.ui.instrument_picker Choosing the instrument that plays notes, with a summary of what each one is made from. Examples >>> format_size ( 2_500_000 ) '2.5 MB' >>> list ( PREVIEW ) [74, 75, 72, 71]

title: alto.ui.instrument_picker
text: sound_picker_layout def sound_picker_layout ( picker : QWidget , * , choices : QListWidget , card : QFrame , ) -> None [Source] Place sound choices beside their detail card in Settings. Parameters picker ( QWidget ): The instrument or metronome picker. choices ( QListWidget ): The list of sounds. card ( QFrame ): The selected sound’s details and preview. Examples Resizing the picker gives extra width to the detail card.

title: alto.ui.instrument_picker
text: load_instrument def load_instrument () -> None [Source] Apply the saved instrument. The piano is used if nothing is saved or the saved key is not an instrument. Examples >>> store (). setValue ( ... "audio/instrument" , "flute" ... ) >>> load_instrument () >>> sounds . instrument 'flute' >>> store (). setValue ( ... "audio/instrument" , "not an instrument" ... ) >>> load_instrument () >>> sounds . instrument 'piano'

title: alto.ui.instrument_picker
text: save_instrument def save_instrument () -> None [Source] Remember the instrument in use. Examples >>> sounds . instrument = "marimba" >>> save_instrument () >>> str ( store (). value ( "audio/instrument" )) 'marimba' >>> sounds . instrument = "piano" >>> save_instrument ()

title: alto.ui.instrument_picker
text: tokens def tokens ( widget : QWidget ) -> dict [ str , str ] [Source] Return the summary page’s colors. All are mixed from the system palette so they follow its light or dark theme. Parameters widget ( QWidget ): The widget whose palette to use. Returns dict of str to str : Color name to ‘#rrggbb’: accent, accent_soft, muted, line, panel and well, and for each of good, warn and bad a text color and a soft background (such as good and good_soft). Examples >>> colors = tokens ( QWidget ()) >>> sorted ( colors )[: 3 ] ['accent', 'accent_soft', 'bad'] >>> colors [ "panel" ]. startswith ( "#" ) True

title: alto.ui.instrument_picker
text: format_size def format_size ( nbytes : int ) -> str [Source] Write a file size the way the instrument page shows it. Parameters nbytes ( int ): The size in bytes. Returns str : Megabytes with one decimal from a million bytes, otherwise whole kilobytes (at least 1). Examples >>> ( ... format_size ( 2_500_000 ), ... format_size ( 500_000 ), ... format_size ( 10 ), ... ) ('2.5 MB', '500 KB', '1 KB')

title: alto.ui.instrument_picker
text: InstrumentPicker InstrumentPicker ( parent : QWidget | None = None ) [Source] Bases: QWidget The instruments in a box on the left; on the right, what the selected one is made from. An instrument that can be played in more than one way (the viola, arco or pizzicato) is one entry, and its page has a ‘Use this instrument’ and a ‘Hear it’ for each way. ‘Hear it’ plays a short arpeggio even while sound is muted. Attributes chosen ( Signal ): Emitted with the key of the instrument that is now in use. groups ( dict of str to list of Instrument ): The entries in the list, each with the instruments (ways of playing) it holds. list ( QListWidget ): The box of entries. shown ( str or None ): The entry whose page is showing. Examples >>> picker = InstrumentPicker () >>> picker . select ( "viola_plucked" ) >>> picker . shown 'Viola' Constructor Build the picker, showing the page of the instrument in use. Parameters parent ( QWidget or None, default None ): The widget that owns the picker. Constructor examples >>> picker = InstrumentPicker () >>> picker . list . count () == len ( picker . groups ) True

title: alto.ui.instrument_picker
text: InstrumentPicker.select def select ( key : str ) -> None [Source] Show the page of the entry an instrument belongs to. Parameters key ( str ): An instrument’s key. Examples >>> picker = InstrumentPicker () >>> picker . select ( "marimba" ) >>> picker . shown 'Marimba'

title: alto.ui.instrument_picker
text: InstrumentPicker.show_group def show_group ( group : str ) -> None [Source] Fill the summary page for an entry from what is known about it and what is on disk. Parameters group ( str ): An entry in the list, such as “Flute” or “Viola”. Examples >>> picker = InstrumentPicker () >>> picker . show_group ( "Flute" ) >>> picker . shown 'Flute'

title: alto.ui.instrument_picker
text: InstrumentPicker.changeEvent def changeEvent ( event : QEvent ) -> None [Source] Redraw the summary page when the palette changes, so its colors follow the theme. Parameters event ( QEvent ): The change. Examples >>> picker = InstrumentPicker () >>> picker . show_group ( "Flute" ) >>> picker . changeEvent ( ... QEvent ( QEvent . Type . PaletteChange ) ... ) >>> picker . shown 'Flute'

title: alto.ui.instrument_picker
text: InstrumentPicker.use def use ( key : str ) -> None [Source] Make an instrument the one for notes and the correct-answer chime. Nothing happens if it has no recordings installed. Parameters key ( str ): The instrument’s key. Examples >>> picker = InstrumentPicker () >>> chosen = [] >>> _ = picker . chosen . connect ( chosen . append ) >>> picker . use ( "marimba" ) >>> sounds . instrument , chosen ('marimba', ['marimba']) >>> picker . use ( "piano" )

title: alto.ui.instrument_picker
text: InstrumentPicker.preview def preview ( key : str ) -> None [Source] Play the DSCH motif in an instrument, even if sound is muted. Parameters key ( str ): The instrument’s key. Examples >>> InstrumentPicker (). preview ( ... "flute" ... ) # doctest: +SKIP

title: alto.ui.interval_range
text: alto.ui.interval_range A two-handle slider for selecting interval distances without changing the keyboard range. Examples >>> slider = IntervalRangeSlider () >>> slider . set_range ( 3 , high = 12 , maximum = 24 ) >>> slider . low , slider . high (3, 12)

title: alto.ui.interval_range
text: IntervalRangeSlider IntervalRangeSlider ( parent : QWidget | None = None ) [Source] Bases: QWidget A draggable interval range with keyboard controls for either endpoint. Attributes edited ( Signal ): Emits the selected lower and upper distances in half steps. low, high ( int ): The selected distances, inclusive. minimum, maximum ( int ): The smallest and largest available interval distances. active ( bool ): Whether the current selection contains any intervals. Examples >>> slider = IntervalRangeSlider () >>> slider . low , slider . high , slider . maximum (1, 12, 24) Constructor Create the slider with a one-octave selection. Parameters parent ( QWidget or None, default None ): The widget that owns the slider. Constructor examples >>> IntervalRangeSlider (). height () 36

title: alto.ui.interval_range
text: IntervalRangeSlider.set_range def set_range ( low : int , * , high : int , maximum : int , minimum : int = 1 , active : bool = True , ) -> None [Source] Synchronize the slider without emitting an edit. Parameters low ( int ): The lowest selected interval distance. high ( int ): The highest selected interval distance. Keyword-only. maximum ( int ): The largest available distance. Keyword-only. minimum ( int, default 1 ): The smallest available distance. Keyword-only. active ( bool, default True ): Whether any intervals are selected. Keyword-only. Examples >>> slider = IntervalRangeSlider () >>> slider . set_range ( 3 , high = 7 , maximum = 12 ) >>> slider . low , slider . high (3, 7)

title: alto.ui.interval_range
text: IntervalRangeSlider.move_endpoint def move_endpoint ( which : str , * , delta : int , ) -> None [Source] Move an endpoint by a number of half-step distances. Parameters which ( str ): The endpoint, “low” or “high”. delta ( int ): The number of interval distances to move. Keyword-only. Examples >>> slider = IntervalRangeSlider () >>> slider . move_endpoint ( "low" , delta = 2 ) >>> slider . low 3

title: alto.ui.interval_range
text: IntervalRangeSlider.paintEvent def paintEvent ( event : QPaintEvent ) -> None [Source] Draw the track, selected span, and both handles. Parameters event ( QPaintEvent ): The repaint request. Examples >>> IntervalRangeSlider (). grab (). isNull () False

title: alto.ui.interval_range
text: IntervalRangeSlider.mousePressEvent def mousePressEvent ( event : QMouseEvent ) -> None [Source] Choose the nearest handle and start dragging it. Parameters event ( QMouseEvent ): The mouse press. Examples >>> IntervalRangeSlider (). _dragging False

title: alto.ui.interval_range
text: IntervalRangeSlider.mouseMoveEvent def mouseMoveEvent ( event : QMouseEvent ) -> None [Source] Move the active handle while dragging. Parameters event ( QMouseEvent ): The pointer movement. Examples >>> IntervalRangeSlider (). maximum 24

title: alto.ui.interval_range
text: IntervalRangeSlider.mouseReleaseEvent def mouseReleaseEvent ( event : QMouseEvent ) -> None [Source] Finish dragging a handle. Parameters event ( QMouseEvent ): The mouse release. Examples >>> IntervalRangeSlider (). _dragging False

title: alto.ui.interval_range
text: IntervalRangeSlider.keyPressEvent def keyPressEvent ( event : QKeyEvent ) -> None [Source] Adjust the active endpoint with arrow keys, Home, or End. Parameters event ( QKeyEvent ): The keyboard input. Up selects the upper handle and Down the lower handle. Examples >>> ( ... IntervalRangeSlider (). focusPolicy () ... == Qt . FocusPolicy . StrongFocus ... ) True

title: alto.ui.key_fork
text: alto.ui.key_fork The fork: a picker for a key signature, shaped like a tuning fork lying on its side. The stem on the left ends in a natural sign (no sharps or flats, C major). At the right the stem opens into two tines: the top one has the sharps, 1 to 7, and the bottom one the flats, 1 to A circle marks the chosen signature. Click a number to choose it, drag the circle along the fork, or turn the mouse wheel to move it. Examples >>> fork = KeyFork () >>> fork . set_value ( - 3 ) >>> fork . value -3

title: alto.ui.key_fork
text: node_position def node_position ( value : int ) -> QPointF [Source] Return where a signature sits on the fork. Parameters value ( int ): The signature: that many sharps if positive (top tine), flats if negative (bottom tine), 0 for the stem’s end. Returns QPointF : The center of its number, in the widget’s coordinates. Examples >>> node_position ( 0 ). x () < node_position ( ... 1 ... ). x () < node_position ( 2 ). x () True >>> node_position ( 3 ). y () < node_position ( ... 0 ... ). y () < node_position ( - 3 ). y () True

title: alto.ui.key_fork
text: route def route ( value : int ) -> list [ QPointF ] [Source] Return the way along the fork from the end of the stem to a signature. Parameters value ( int ): The signature, as for node_position . Returns list of QPointF : The points to pass through: the stem’s end, around the bend of the U to the tine and then each number up to the one asked. Examples >>> ( ... len ( route ( 0 )), ... len ( route ( 2 )) ... > len ( route ( 1 )) ... > len ( route ( 0 )), ... ) (1, True) >>> route ( - 1 )[ - 1 ] == node_position ( - 1 ) True >>> round ( route ( 3 )[ 1 ]. x ()) == round ( ... APEX_X ... ) # it leaves the stem at the apex of the U True

title: alto.ui.key_fork
text: path_between def path_between ( a : int , * , b : int , ) -> list [ QPointF ] [Source] Return the way along the fork from one signature to another. The circle goes back along the tine it is on, around the U and out along the other, never across the gap between the tines. Parameters a ( int ): The signature to start from. b ( int ): The signature to end at. Keyword-only. Returns list of QPointF : The points to pass through, from a to b . Examples >>> path_between ( 2 , b = 2 ) == [ node_position ( 2 )] True >>> path_between ( 1 , b =- 1 )[ 0 ] == node_position ( ... 1 ... ) and path_between ( 1 , b =- 1 )[ ... - 1 ... ] == node_position ( - 1 ) True >>> any ( ... abs ( p . x () - APEX_X ) < 1e-9 ... for p in path_between ( 1 , b =- 1 ) ... ) # it goes around the U, through its apex True

title: alto.ui.key_fork
text: point_along def point_along ( points : list [ QPointF ], * , t : float , ) -> QPointF [Source] Return the point a fraction of the way along a path made of short straight pieces. Parameters points ( list of QPointF ): The corners of the path; at least one. t ( float ): How far along, from 0 (the first point) to 1 (the last). Keyword-only. Returns QPointF : The point that far along. Examples >>> point_along ( ... [ ... QPointF ( 0 , 0 ), ... QPointF ( 10 , 0 ), ... QPointF ( 10 , 10 ), ... ], ... t = 0.75 , ... ). toTuple () (10.0, 5.0) >>> point_along ( ... [ QPointF ( 0 , 0 ), QPointF ( 3 , 4 )], t = 0.5 ... ). toTuple () # slanting pieces are measured along their length (1.5, 2.0)

title: alto.ui.key_fork
text: nearest_on_fork def nearest_on_fork ( point : QPointF ) -> QPointF [Source] Return the point on the fork’s line that is closest to a point. Parameters point ( QPointF ): Any position in the widget, such as the mouse while the circle is dragged. Returns QPointF : The closest point on the way from the last sharp, around the U, to the last flat. Examples >>> nearest_on_fork ( ... QPointF ( node_position ( 2 ). x (), 0 ) ... ) == node_position ( ... 2 ... ) # straight above the number True >>> nearest_on_fork ( ... QPointF ( - 50 , node_position ( 0 ). y ()) ... ) == node_position ( ... 0 ... ) # past the end of the stem True

title: alto.ui.key_fork
text: fork_path def fork_path () -> QPainterPath [Source] Return the outline of the fork: the stem, a half circle for the U, and the two tines. Returns QPainterPath : One smooth line, drawn from the end of the stem. Examples >>> outline = fork_path () >>> ( ... outline . boundingRect (). left () == STEM_X ... and outline . boundingRect (). top () == TOP_Y ... ) True

title: alto.ui.key_fork
text: draw_natural def draw_natural ( p : QPainter , * , center : QPointF , height : float , color : QColor , ) -> None [Source] Draw a natural sign: two upright lines joined by two slanting bars. Parameters p ( QPainter ): The painter to draw with. center ( QPointF ): The middle of the sign. Keyword-only. height ( float ): How tall it is, in pixels. Keyword-only. color ( QColor ): The color of the lines. Keyword-only. Examples >>> from PySide6.QtGui import QPixmap >>> canvas = QPixmap ( 20 , 20 ) >>> painter = QPainter ( canvas ) >>> draw_natural ( ... painter , ... center = QPointF ( 10 , 10 ), ... height = 14 , ... color = QColor ( "black" ), ... ) >>> _ = painter . end ()

title: alto.ui.key_fork
text: KeyFork KeyFork ( * , parent : QWidget | None = None , ) [Source] Bases: QWidget A tuning fork on its side, for choosing how many sharps or flats a key signature has. Attributes value ( int ): The chosen signature: sharps if positive, flats if negative, 0 for none. locked ( bool ): While True the fork ignores the mouse and the keyboard. changed ( Signal ): Emitted with the new value whenever it changes. Examples >>> fork = KeyFork () >>> got = [] >>> _ = fork . changed . connect ( got . append ) >>> fork . set_value ( 2 ) >>> fork . set_value ( 2 ) # no change, nothing said >>> got [2] Constructor Build the fork, set to no sharps or flats. Parameters parent ( QWidget or None, default None ): The widget that owns the fork. Keyword-only. Constructor examples >>> KeyFork (). value 0

title: alto.ui.key_fork
text: KeyFork.set_value def set_value ( value : int , * , slide : bool = True , ) -> None [Source] Choose a signature and move the circle to it. Parameters value ( int ): The signature, kept between 7 flats and 7 sharps. slide ( bool, default True ): Move the circle along the fork; if False it jumps. Keyword-only. Examples >>> fork = KeyFork () >>> fork . set_value ( 99 ) >>> fork . value 7 >>> fork . set_value ( 0 , slide = False ) >>> fork . value , fork . _marker == node_position ( 0 ) (0, True)

title: alto.ui.key_fork
text: KeyFork.set_marker_color def set_marker_color ( color : QColor | None ) -> None [Source] Color the circle, for a right or wrong answer. Parameters color ( QColor or None ): The color to use, or None for the highlight color. Examples >>> fork = KeyFork () >>> fork . set_marker_color ( QColor ( "#2e7d32" )) >>> fork . _marker_color == QColor ( "#2e7d32" ) True

title: alto.ui.key_fork
text: KeyFork.value_at @ staticmethod def value_at ( point : QPointF ) -> int | None [Source] Return the signature whose number is under a point. Parameters point ( QPointF ): A position in the widget. Returns int or None : The signature there, or None if the point is not near a number. Examples >>> fork = KeyFork () >>> ( ... fork . value_at ( node_position ( 3 )), ... fork . value_at ( node_position ( - 4 )), ... fork . value_at ( node_position ( 0 )), ... ) (3, -4, 0) >>> fork . value_at ( QPointF ( 5 , 130 )) is None True

title: alto.ui.key_fork
text: KeyFork.mousePressEvent def mousePressEvent ( event : QMouseEvent ) -> None [Source] Pick up the circle if it was pressed, or choose the number that was clicked. Parameters event ( QMouseEvent ): The press. Only the left button does anything. Examples >>> from PySide6.QtCore import QEvent >>> fork = KeyFork () >>> point = node_position ( - 2 ) >>> fork . mousePressEvent ( ... QMouseEvent ( ... QEvent . Type . MouseButtonPress , ... point , ... point , ... Qt . MouseButton . LeftButton , ... Qt . MouseButton . LeftButton , ... Qt . KeyboardModifier . NoModifier , ... ) ... ) >>> fork . value -2

title: alto.ui.key_fork
text: KeyFork.mouseMoveEvent def mouseMoveEvent ( event : QMouseEvent ) -> None [Source] Carry the circle along the fork while it is held, and light the number under the mouse otherwise. The signature changes to the nearest number as the circle passes it. Parameters event ( QMouseEvent ): The move. Examples >>> from PySide6.QtCore import QEvent >>> fork = KeyFork () >>> here = node_position ( 0 ) >>> there = node_position ( 3 ) >>> fork . mousePressEvent ( ... QMouseEvent ( ... QEvent . Type . MouseButtonPress , ... here , ... here , ... Qt . MouseButton . LeftButton , ... Qt . MouseButton . LeftButton , ... Qt . KeyboardModifier . NoModifier , ... ) ... ) >>> fork . mouseMoveEvent ( ... QMouseEvent ( ... QEvent . Type . MouseMove , ... there , ... there , ... Qt . MouseButton . NoButton , ... Qt . MouseButton . LeftButton , ... Qt . KeyboardModifier . NoModifier , ... ) ... ) >>> fork . value 3

title: alto.ui.key_fork
text: KeyFork.mouseReleaseEvent def mouseReleaseEvent ( event : QMouseEvent ) -> None [Source] Let go of the circle, which slides to the number it is nearest. Parameters event ( QMouseEvent ): The release. Examples >>> from PySide6.QtCore import QEvent >>> fork = KeyFork () >>> fork . _dragging = True >>> fork . _marker = node_position ( 0 ) + QPointF ( ... 9 , 0 ... ) >>> fork . mouseReleaseEvent ( ... QMouseEvent ( ... QEvent . Type . MouseButtonRelease , ... fork . _marker , ... fork . _marker , ... Qt . MouseButton . LeftButton , ... Qt . MouseButton . NoButton , ... Qt . KeyboardModifier . NoModifier , ... ) ... ) >>> fork . _dragging False

title: alto.ui.key_fork
text: KeyFork.leaveEvent def leaveEvent ( event : QEvent ) -> None [Source] Stop lighting a number when the mouse leaves the fork. Parameters event ( QEvent ): The leave event. Examples >>> fork = KeyFork () >>> fork . _hover = 3 >>> fork . leaveEvent ( QEvent ( QEvent . Type . Leave )) >>> fork . _hover is None True

title: alto.ui.key_fork
text: KeyFork.wheelEvent def wheelEvent ( event : QWheelEvent ) -> None [Source] Move the circle one number along the fork for each notch of the wheel. Rolling up goes toward more sharps and down toward more flats, passing through the natural sign. Parameters event ( QWheelEvent ): The wheel turn. Examples >>> from PySide6.QtCore import QPoint >>> fork = KeyFork () >>> point = QPointF ( 100 , 50 ) >>> fork . wheelEvent ( ... QWheelEvent ( ... point , ... point , ... QPoint ( 0 , 0 ), ... QPoint ( 0 , - 120 ), ... Qt . MouseButton . NoButton , ... Qt . KeyboardModifier . NoModifier , ... Qt . ScrollPhase . NoScrollPhase , ... False , ... ) ... ) >>> fork . value -1

title: alto.ui.key_fork
text: KeyFork.keyPressEvent def keyPressEvent ( event : QKeyEvent ) -> None [Source] Move the circle with the arrow keys: up or right for a sharp, down or left for a flat. Parameters event ( QKeyEvent ): The key press. Examples >>> from PySide6.QtCore import QEvent >>> fork = KeyFork () >>> fork . keyPressEvent ( ... QKeyEvent ( ... QEvent . Type . KeyPress , ... Qt . Key . Key_Up , ... Qt . KeyboardModifier . NoModifier , ... ) ... ) >>> fork . value 1

title: alto.ui.key_fork
text: KeyFork.paintEvent def paintEvent ( _ : QPaintEvent ) -> None [Source] Draw the fork, its numbers and the circle on the chosen one. Parameters _ ( QPaintEvent ): The paint request; the whole widget is always redrawn. Examples >>> KeyFork (). grab (). isNull () False

title: alto.ui.keyboard
text: alto.ui.keyboard The on-screen piano keyboard, drawn to real proportions, and a miniature of the whole piano for choosing a span of keys. KeyboardWidget shows a range of keys and can highlight one. KeyboardSpan shows all 88 keys in miniature, shades the range that will be asked, and can be dragged to change it. Colors and materials come from keyboard_styles . Examples >>> keyboard = KeyboardWidget () >>> keyboard . show_key ( 60 ) >>> keyboard . highlight 60

title: alto.ui.keyboard
text: KeyboardWidget KeyboardWidget ( parent : QWidget | None = None , * , label_middle_c : bool = False , ) [Source] Bases: QWidget A piano keyboard drawn to real proportions that can highlight one or more keys. Attributes lo ( int ): The lowest key shown, as a MIDI number. hi ( int ): The highest key shown, as a MIDI number. highlight ( int or None ): The key to highlight. additional_highlights ( set of int ): Other keys highlighted together with highlight . style_override ( KeyboardStyle or None ): A fixed style, for the preview cards in the settings; otherwise the style chosen in the settings is used. pad ( float ): The frame padding, in pixels. max_key_width ( float ): The widest a key may be, in pixels. Smaller when something else (the key signature) shares the page. highlight_color ( QColor ): The color of the highlighted key. key_length ( float ): How long a natural key is drawn, in key widths. A piano’s is 6.2, and a harpsichord’s keys can be shorter. Examples >>> keyboard = KeyboardWidget () >>> ( ... keyboard . lo , ... keyboard . hi , ... ) # C3 to C5, until another range is shown (48, 72) Constructor Create a keyboard showing the default range, with no key highlighted. Parameters parent ( QWidget or None, default None ): The widget that owns the keyboard. label_middle_c ( bool, default False ): Mark middle C and its neighboring pair of black keys for an introductory lesson. Constructor examples >>> KeyboardWidget (). highlight is None True

title: alto.ui.keyboard
text: KeyboardWidget.style @ property def style () -> KeyboardStyle [Source] Return the style the keyboard is drawn in. Returns KeyboardStyle : The fixed style if one is set, otherwise the style chosen in the settings. Examples >>> keyboard = KeyboardWidget () >>> keyboard . style_override = ( ... keyboard_styles . BY_KEY [ "modern" ] ... ) >>> keyboard . style . label 'Modern piano'

title: alto.ui.keyboard
text: KeyboardWidget.refit def refit () -> None [Source] Size and redraw the keyboard after the style changes. Some styles have a taller strip above the keys. Examples >>> keyboard = KeyboardWidget () >>> keyboard . refit () >>> keyboard . height () > 0 True

title: alto.ui.keyboard
text: KeyboardWidget.full_width def full_width () -> int [Source] Measure the keyboard case when its keys reach their maximum width. Returns int : Width of the case in pixels, including padding. Examples >>> KeyboardWidget (). full_width () 590

title: alto.ui.keyboard
text: KeyboardWidget.resizeEvent def resizeEvent ( event : QResizeEvent ) -> None [Source] Change the height to match the new width, since keys are drawn to real proportions. Parameters event ( QResizeEvent ): The resize that happened. Examples >>> keyboard = KeyboardWidget () >>> keyboard . show () >>> keyboard . resize ( 300 , 300 ) >>> keyboard . height () # narrower, so shorter 143

title: alto.ui.keyboard
text: KeyboardWidget.show_key def show_key ( midi : int | None , * , span : tuple [ int , int ] | None = None , ) -> None [Source] Highlight a key, and optionally choose the range of keys to show. Parameters midi ( int or None ): The key to highlight, or None for no highlight. span ( tuple of (int, int) or None, default None ): The lowest and highest key to show; it is widened to whole white keys. Keyword-only. Examples >>> keyboard = KeyboardWidget () >>> keyboard . show_key ( ... 60 , span = ( 49 , 71 ) ... ) # C#3 is widened to C3 >>> ( ... keyboard . lo , ... keyboard . hi , ... keyboard . highlight , ... ) (48, 71, 60)

title: alto.ui.keyboard
text: KeyboardWidget.show_keys def show_keys ( midis : list [ int ], * , span : tuple [ int , int ] | None = None , ) -> None [Source] Highlight several keys together, clearing highlights from the previous question. Parameters midis ( list of int ): The MIDI numbers to highlight; an empty list clears all highlights. span ( tuple of (int, int) or None, default None ): The inclusive range to display, widened to white keys. Keyword-only. Examples >>> keyboard = KeyboardWidget () >>> keyboard . show_keys ([ 60 , 66 ], span = ( 48 , 72 )) >>> ( ... keyboard . highlight , ... keyboard . additional_highlights , ... ) (60, {66}) >>> keyboard . show_key ( 62 ) >>> keyboard . additional_highlights set()

title: alto.ui.keyboard
text: KeyboardWidget.set_highlight_color def set_highlight_color ( color : QColor ) -> None [Source] Choose the color of the highlighted key and redraw. Parameters color ( QColor ): The color. Examples >>> keyboard = KeyboardWidget () >>> keyboard . set_highlight_color ( ... QColor ( "#2e7d32" ) ... ) >>> keyboard . highlight_color . name () '#2e7d32'

title: alto.ui.keyboard
text: KeyboardWidget.paintEvent def paintEvent ( _ : QPaintEvent ) -> None [Source] Draw the case, the keys, the highlighted key and the style’s extras. Parameters _ ( QPaintEvent ): The paint request; the whole widget is always redrawn. Examples >>> keyboard = KeyboardWidget () >>> keyboard . show_key ( 60 ) >>> keyboard . grab (). isNull () False

title: alto.ui.keyboard
text: KeyboardSpan KeyboardSpan ( parent : QWidget | None = None , * , compact : bool = False , size : tuple [ int , int ] = ( 124 , 26 ), ) [Source] Bases: QWidget The whole 88-key piano in miniature, with the keys that will be asked shaded. The full-size one can be dragged across to choose the span: dragged is emitted with the lowest and highest key as it changes. Attributes dragged ( Signal ): Emitted with the lowest and highest key (MIDI numbers) as the span is dragged. lo ( int ): The lowest key shaded. hi ( int ): The highest key shaded. full ( tuple of int ): The lowest and highest key the miniature draws. All 88 keys, unless a plugin’s keyboard has fewer. Examples >>> span = KeyboardSpan () >>> span . set_span ( 60 , hi = 72 ) >>> ( span . lo , span . hi ) (60, 72) Constructor Create the miniature, shading the default range. Parameters parent ( QWidget or None, default None ): The widget that owns it. compact ( bool, default False ): Make a fixed-size version that ignores the mouse, for a summary in a menu row. Keyword-only. size ( tuple of (int, int), default (124, 26) ): The width and height of the compact version, in pixels. Keyword-only. Constructor examples >>> KeyboardSpan ( ... compact = True , size = ( 100 , 20 ) ... ). size (). width () 100

title: alto.ui.keyboard
text: KeyboardSpan.key_at def key_at ( pos : QPointF ) -> int [Source] Return the key under a point. Parameters pos ( QPointF ): The position in the widget. Returns int : The MIDI number: a black key where one is drawn there, else the white key (clamped to the ends of the piano). Examples >>> span = KeyboardSpan () >>> span . resize ( 500 , 64 ) >>> ( ... span . key_at ( QPointF ( 0 , 50 )), ... span . key_at ( QPointF ( 499 , 50 )), ... ) # the lowest and highest keys (21, 108) >>> span . key_at ( QPointF ( 250 , 50 )) 64

title: alto.ui.keyboard
text: KeyboardSpan.mousePressEvent def mousePressEvent ( event : QMouseEvent ) -> None [Source] Start choosing a span: grab an edge, pick the span up, or start a new one. Parameters event ( QMouseEvent ): The press. Only the left button does anything. Examples >>> from PySide6.QtCore import QEvent >>> span = KeyboardSpan () >>> span . resize ( 500 , 64 ) >>> got = [] >>> _ = span . dragged . connect ( ... lambda lo , hi : got . append (( lo , hi )) ... ) >>> point = QPointF ( 5 , 50 ) >>> span . mousePressEvent ( ... QMouseEvent ( ... QEvent . Type . MouseButtonPress , ... point , ... point , ... Qt . MouseButton . LeftButton , ... Qt . MouseButton . LeftButton , ... Qt . KeyboardModifier . NoModifier , ... ) ... ) >>> got # a press outside the span starts a new one on that key [(21, 21)]

title: alto.ui.keyboard
text: KeyboardSpan.mouseMoveEvent def mouseMoveEvent ( event : QMouseEvent ) -> None [Source] Drag the span, or (with no button held) show the cursor for what a press here would do. Parameters event ( QMouseEvent ): The move. Examples >>> from PySide6.QtCore import QEvent >>> span = KeyboardSpan () >>> span . resize ( 500 , 64 ) >>> middle = QPointF ( sum ( span . _edges ()) / 2 , 50 ) >>> span . mouseMoveEvent ( ... QMouseEvent ( ... QEvent . Type . MouseMove , ... middle , ... middle , ... Qt . MouseButton . NoButton , ... Qt . MouseButton . NoButton , ... Qt . KeyboardModifier . NoModifier , ... ) ... ) >>> # inside the span: it can be picked up >>> span . cursor (). shape () == Qt . CursorShape . OpenHandCursor True

title: alto.ui.keyboard
text: KeyboardSpan.mouseReleaseEvent def mouseReleaseEvent ( event : QMouseEvent ) -> None [Source] Finish a drag and refresh the cursor for where the pointer now is. Parameters event ( QMouseEvent ): The release. Examples >>> from PySide6.QtCore import QEvent >>> span = KeyboardSpan () >>> span . resize ( 500 , 64 ) >>> point = QPointF ( 5 , 50 ) >>> span . mouseReleaseEvent ( ... QMouseEvent ( ... QEvent . Type . MouseButtonRelease , ... point , ... point , ... Qt . MouseButton . LeftButton , ... Qt . MouseButton . NoButton , ... Qt . KeyboardModifier . NoModifier , ... ) ... ) >>> span . _mode is None True

title: alto.ui.keyboard
text: KeyboardSpan.set_span def set_span ( lo : int , * , hi : int , ) -> None [Source] Choose which keys are shaded and redraw. Parameters lo ( int ): The lowest key asked, as a MIDI number. hi ( int ): The highest key asked. Keyword-only. Examples >>> span = KeyboardSpan () >>> span . set_span ( 48 , hi = 72 ) >>> ( span . lo , span . hi ) (48, 72)

title: alto.ui.keyboard
text: KeyboardSpan.paintEvent def paintEvent ( _ : QPaintEvent ) -> None [Source] Draw the whole piano in miniature with the asked keys shaded and the span’s edges marked. Parameters _ ( QPaintEvent ): The paint request; the whole widget is always redrawn. Examples >>> span = KeyboardSpan () >>> span . grab (). isNull () False

title: alto.ui.keyboard_styles
text: alto.ui.keyboard_styles Keyboard styles: the colors and materials the on-screen piano keys are drawn in. There are ready-made styles ( STYLES ) and a custom one built from colors chosen part by part. Examples >>> BY_KEY [ "classic" ]. label 'Classic' >>> style_for ( "no such style" ). key == DEFAULT True

title: alto.ui.keyboard_styles
text: KeyboardStyle KeyboardStyle ( key : str , * , label : str , note : str , white : tuple [ str , str ], white_edge : str , black : tuple [ str , str ], black_edge : str , case : str | None = DEFAULT_CASE , felt : str | None = None , cap : str | None = None , narrow : float = 1.0 , gap : float = 1.0 , rail : float = 8.0 , thick : bool = False , hue : bool = False , glow : bool = False , ink : bool = False , knobs : bool = False , reverse_below : int | None = None , dot : str | None = None , round : float = 7.0 , ) [Source] How a keyboard looks: the colors of the keys and the case, and a few details of the drawing. Attributes key ( str ): The identifier saved in the settings. label ( str ): The name shown in the interface. Keyword-only. note ( str ): A few words on what it is modeled on. Keyword-only. white ( tuple of (str, str) ): The natural keys’ color at the top and at the bottom. Keyword-only. white_edge ( str ): The outline color of the natural keys. Keyword-only. black ( tuple of (str, str) ): The sharps’ color at the top and at the bottom. Keyword-only. black_edge ( str ): The outline color of the sharps. Keyword-only. case ( str or None ): The body around the keys; None draws no body. Keyword-only. felt ( str or None ): A strip of felt under the fallboard. Keyword-only. cap ( str or None ): A bone cap on top of each sharp. Keyword-only. narrow ( float, default 1.0 ): How wide the sharps are, compared with a piano’s. Keyword-only. gap ( float, default 1.0 ): Pixels between neighboring naturals. Keyword-only. rail ( float, default 8.0 ): The height of the strip above the keys. Keyword-only. thick ( bool, default False ): Heavy outlines. Keyword-only. hue ( bool, default False ): Color each key by its note name. Keyword-only. glow ( bool, default False ): A soft halo around the outlines. Keyword-only. ink ( bool, default False ): Hatched sharps, like an engraving. Keyword-only. knobs ( bool, default False ): A row of organ stop knobs in the strip above the keys. Keyword-only. reverse_below ( int or None ): Keys under this MIDI number swap colors (an organ’s preset keys). Keyword-only. dot ( str or None ): The color of a dot that marks every C. Keyword-only. round ( float, default 7.0 ): The most the lower corners of a natural are rounded, in pixels. Keyword-only. Examples >>> style = BY_KEY [ "modern" ] >>> style . label , style . case ('Modern piano', '#0d0d0f')

title: alto.ui.keyboard_styles
text: custom_colors def custom_colors () -> dict [ str , str | None ] [Source] Return the color of each part of the custom keyboard. Returns dict of str to str or None : Part name (“naturals”, “sharps”, “case”, “felt” or “caps”) to its color, or None where an optional part is left out. Examples >>> sorted ( custom_colors ()) ['caps', 'case', 'felt', 'naturals', 'sharps']

title: alto.ui.keyboard_styles
text: custom_style def custom_style () -> KeyboardStyle [Source] Build the style from the custom colors. Gradients and outlines are worked out from each part’s color. Returns KeyboardStyle : The custom style, with the key “custom”. Examples >>> custom_style (). key , custom_style (). label ('custom', 'Custom')

title: alto.ui.keyboard_styles
text: style_for def style_for ( key : str ) -> KeyboardStyle [Source] Return the style with a given key. Parameters key ( str ): A key of BY_KEY , or “custom”. Returns KeyboardStyle : That style; the default (Classic) if the key is not known. Examples >>> style_for ( "modern" ). label 'Modern piano' >>> style_for ( "nonsense" ). label 'Classic'

title: alto.ui.keyboard_styles
text: current def current () -> KeyboardStyle [Source] Return the keyboard style in use. Returns KeyboardStyle : The style chosen in the settings (Classic until another is chosen). Examples >>> current (). key in BY_KEY or current (). key == CUSTOM True

title: alto.ui.keyboard_styles
text: load_style def load_style () -> None [Source] Apply the saved style (Classic if none is saved or it is unknown), and the saved custom colors. Examples >>> store (). setValue ( "ui/keyboard" , "modern" ) >>> load_style () >>> current (). key 'modern' >>> set_style ( DEFAULT )

title: alto.ui.keyboard_styles
text: set_style def set_style ( key : str ) -> None [Source] Choose and save a style, and redraw every keyboard already on screen. Parameters key ( str ): A key of BY_KEY , or “custom”. Examples >>> set_style ( "modern" ) >>> current (). label 'Modern piano' >>> set_style ( DEFAULT )

title: alto.ui.keyboard_styles
text: set_custom_color def set_custom_color ( part : str , * , color : str | None , ) -> None [Source] Color one part of the custom keyboard and switch to the custom style. Parameters part ( str ): One of “naturals”, “sharps”, “case”, “felt” or “caps”. color ( str or None ): A color such as ‘#336699’, or None to leave an optional part (case, felt or caps) out. Keyword-only. Examples >>> set_custom_color ( ... "naturals" , color = "#ffffff" ... ) >>> current (). key , custom_colors ()[ "naturals" ] ('custom', '#ffffff') >>> set_custom_color ( ... "naturals" , ... color = DEFAULT_CUSTOM [ "naturals" ], ... ) >>> set_style ( DEFAULT )

title: alto.ui.keyboard_styles
text: on_redraw def on_redraw ( hook : Callable [[], None ]) -> None [Source] Register a function to call whenever the keyboard style changes. The keyboard widgets live in a module that imports this one, so they register themselves here instead of being found by this module. Parameters hook ( Callable ): A function with no arguments that lays out and repaints what depends on the style. Examples >>> calls = [] >>> def repaint () -> None : ... calls . append ( 1 ) >>> on_redraw ( repaint ) >>> _redraw () >>> calls [1] >>> _redraw_hooks . remove ( repaint )

title: alto.ui.keyboard_styles
text: reversed_key def reversed_key ( style : KeyboardStyle , * , midi : int , ) -> bool [Source] Report whether a key has swapped colors, as the low preset keys of an organ do. Parameters style ( KeyboardStyle ): The style. midi ( int ): The key’s MIDI number. Keyword-only. Returns bool : True if the style swaps colors below some key and this key is below it. Examples >>> from dataclasses import replace >>> reversed_key ( BY_KEY [ "classic" ], midi = 40 ) False >>> reversed_key ( ... replace ( ... BY_KEY [ "classic" ], reverse_below = 50 ... ), ... midi = 40 , ... ) True

title: alto.ui.keyboard_styles
text: key_brush def key_brush ( style : KeyboardStyle , * , midi : int , black : bool , y : float , height : float , ) -> QBrush [Source] Return the fill for a key. Parameters style ( KeyboardStyle ): The style. midi ( int ): The key’s MIDI number. Keyword-only. black ( bool ): True for a sharp or flat, False for a natural. Keyword-only. y ( float ): The key’s top edge, in pixels. Keyword-only. height ( float ): The key’s height, in pixels. Keyword-only. Returns QBrush : A solid color, a top-to-bottom gradient, or (for styles that color keys by note) a color that depends on the note. Examples >>> key_brush ( ... BY_KEY [ "classic" ], ... midi = 60 , ... black = False , ... y = 0 , ... height = 100 , ... ). color (). name () '#fbfbfc' >>> key_brush ( ... BY_KEY [ "modern" ], ... midi = 60 , ... black = False , ... y = 0 , ... height = 100 , ... ). gradient () is not None True

title: alto.ui.keyboard_styles
text: edge_color def edge_color ( style : KeyboardStyle , * , midi : int , black : bool , ) -> QColor [Source] Return the outline color for a key. Parameters style ( KeyboardStyle ): The style. midi ( int ): The key’s MIDI number. Keyword-only. black ( bool ): True for a sharp or flat, False for a natural. Keyword-only. Returns QColor : The outline color. Examples >>> edge_color ( ... BY_KEY [ "classic" ], midi = 60 , black = False ... ). name () '#9a9a9f' >>> edge_color ( ... BY_KEY [ "classic" ], midi = 61 , black = True ... ). name () '#111114'

title: alto.ui.lesson
text: alto.ui.lesson The lesson pages: a page that walks through one lesson step by step. A step has some words, sometimes a sound to hear, sometimes the circle of fifths to explore, and sometimes a small task. The tasks cannot be failed and are not recorded. Examples >>> LessonsPage ( ... "circle-of-fifths" , step = 0 ... ). view . counter . text () 'Step 1 of 8'

title: alto.ui.lesson
text: saved_step def saved_step ( lesson : Lesson ) -> int [Source] Return the step a lesson was left at, from the saved settings. Parameters lesson ( Lesson ): The lesson. Returns int : The step number from 0, or 0 if none is saved or it no longer exists. Examples >>> saved_step ( LESSONS [ 0 ]) in range ( ... len ( LESSONS [ 0 ]. steps ) ... ) True

title: alto.ui.lesson
text: save_step def save_step ( lesson : Lesson , * , step : int , ) -> None [Source] Remember the step a lesson is at. Parameters lesson ( Lesson ): The lesson. step ( int ): The step number from 0. Keyword-only. Examples >>> save_step ( LESSONS [ 0 ], step = 0 ) >>> saved_step ( LESSONS [ 0 ]) 0

title: alto.ui.lesson
text: StepView StepView ( step : Step , * , rng : random . Random | None = None , parent : QWidget | None = None , ) [Source] Bases: QWidget One step of a lesson: its words, a sound to hear, the circle, and a task. Attributes step ( Step ): The step. circle ( ExplorableCircle or None ): The circle, for a step that has one. staves ( list of StaffWidget ): The staves beside the words, for a step that has them: one for each of its staves , or the one that follows the task. left_scroll ( QScrollArea ): Holds the words and controls on the left, so they scroll if the window is too short for them. task ( Task or None ): The task now being asked, for a step that has them. feedback ( QLabel ): What is said about the last answer. info ( QLabel ): What is said about the key last picked on the circle. again ( QPushButton ): Repeats a fixed question or draws another question after the answer is explained. practice ( Signal ): Emitted by the Practice button on the last step. Examples >>> from alto.lessons.circle_of_fifths import ( ... CIRCLE_OF_FIFTHS , ... ) >>> view = StepView ( ... CIRCLE_OF_FIFTHS . steps [ 1 ], ... rng = random . Random ( 1 ), ... ) >>> view . task is not None and len ( ... view . choice_buttons ... ) == 4 True Constructor Build the step and ask its first task. Parameters step ( Step ): What to show. rng ( random.Random or None, default None ): Chooses the tasks; None for a new one. Keyword-only. parent ( QWidget or None, default None ): The widget that owns it. Keyword-only. Constructor examples >>> from alto.lessons.circle_of_fifths import ( ... CIRCLE_OF_FIFTHS , ... ) >>> StepView ( ... CIRCLE_OF_FIFTHS . steps [ 0 ] ... ). circle is not None True
