title: alto.ui.motion
text: alto.ui.motion Animations and feedback delays, run in one place so that tests decide when they happen. The interface moves: pages slide, feedback stays on screen for a moment and the next question follows. Each of those goes through this module: play starts an animation, later runs a step after a delay and start_timer starts a timer that does. In the app they take their real time. A button is given its key with set_shortcut . Tests switch to instant motion with set_instant . Then nothing moves on by itself: animations hold still and delayed steps and timers wait in a queue, however long the test takes, until it calls settle . That runs everything waiting, in the order it was asked for, at once. So a test can look at the state just after an action (the feedback showing, a page about to slide), and the motion happens only when the test says so, never during some other wait. A button’s key clicks it at once, since its pressed look is all there is to see in the meantime. Examples >>> set_instant ( True ) >>> owner = QObject () >>> done = [] >>> later ( ... 900 , ... owner = owner , ... step = lambda : done . append ( "cleared" ), ... ) >>> QCoreApplication . processEvents () # nothing happens by itself >>> done , busy () ([], True) >>> settle () >>> done , busy () (['cleared'], False) >>> set_instant ( False )

title: alto.ui.motion
text: instant def instant () -> bool [Source] Say whether motion waits for settle , as it does in tests. Returns bool : True if animations and delays hold until a test settles them. Examples >>> instant () False

title: alto.ui.motion
text: set_instant def set_instant ( on : bool ) -> None [Source] Make motion wait for settle , for tests, or give it back its real time. Parameters on ( bool ): True for instant motion. Examples >>> set_instant ( True ) >>> instant () True >>> set_instant ( False )

title: alto.ui.motion
text: later def later ( delay : int , * , owner : QObject , step : Callable [[], object ], ) -> None [Source] Run a step after a delay, such as clearing wrong-answer feedback so the learner can try again. Parameters delay ( int ): How long to wait, in milliseconds. With instant motion the step waits for settle instead. owner ( QObject ): The object the step belongs to. If it is deleted first, the step does not run. Keyword-only. step ( callable ): What to run. Keyword-only. Examples >>> set_instant ( True ) >>> owner = QObject () >>> done = [] >>> later ( ... 450 , ... owner = owner , ... step = lambda : done . append ( "retry" ), ... ) >>> settle () >>> done ['retry'] >>> set_instant ( False )

title: alto.ui.motion
text: start_timer def start_timer ( timer : QTimer , * , delay : int , ) -> None [Source] Start a single-shot timer whose timeout is part of the interface’s motion, such as moving on to the next question. The timer can be stopped as usual, and then it does not fire. Parameters timer ( QTimer ): The timer, which fires once. delay ( int ): Its interval, in milliseconds. With instant motion it waits for settle instead. Keyword-only. Examples >>> set_instant ( True ) >>> timer = QTimer () >>> timer . setSingleShot ( True ) >>> fired = [] >>> _ = timer . timeout . connect ( ... lambda : fired . append ( 1 ) ... ) >>> start_timer ( timer , delay = 1200 ) >>> timer . isActive (), busy () (True, True) >>> settle () >>> fired , timer . isActive () ([1], False) >>> start_timer ( timer , delay = 1200 ) >>> timer . stop () # a stopped timer does not fire >>> settle () >>> fired [1] >>> set_instant ( False )

title: alto.ui.motion
text: play def play ( animation : QAbstractAnimation ) -> None [Source] Start an animation. With instant motion it holds still at its start until settle moves it to its end. Parameters animation ( QAbstractAnimation ): The animation, or a group of them. It finishes as usual, with its finished signal. Examples >>> from PySide6.QtCore import QVariantAnimation >>> set_instant ( True ) >>> animation = QVariantAnimation () >>> animation . setDuration ( 220 ) >>> animation . setStartValue ( 0.0 ) >>> animation . setEndValue ( 1.0 ) >>> play ( animation ) >>> ( ... animation . state () ... == QAbstractAnimation . State . Stopped , ... busy (), ... ) (False, True) >>> settle () >>> ( ... animation . currentValue (), ... animation . state () ... == QAbstractAnimation . State . Stopped , ... ) (1.0, True) >>> set_instant ( False )

title: alto.ui.motion
text: busy def busy () -> bool [Source] Say whether any motion is still to come: a delayed step, an active timer or a running animation. Returns bool : True if settle would run something. Examples >>> busy () False

title: alto.ui.motion
text: settle def settle ( * , rounds : int = 1000 , ) -> None [Source] Let every piece of motion happen: delayed steps run, timers fire and animations reach their end. With instant motion they happen at once, in the order they were asked for, and motion they start (feedback that leads to the next question, which slides in) happens too. In the app’s real time this waits for them instead. Parameters rounds ( int, default 1000 ): The most pieces of motion to go through or, in real time, about how many milliseconds to wait. Keyword-only. Raises RuntimeError : If motion is still going after that many, such as a step that keeps asking for itself again. Examples >>> settle () >>> busy () False A step that always asks for itself again never settles: >>> set_instant ( True ) >>> owner = QObject () >>> def again (): ... later ( 10 , owner = owner , step = again ) >>> later ( 10 , owner = owner , step = again ) >>> settle ( rounds = 3 ) Traceback (most recent call last): ... RuntimeError: Motion is still going after 3 rounds. >>> set_instant ( False )

title: alto.ui.motion
text: set_shortcut def set_shortcut ( button : QAbstractButton , * , key : QKeySequence | str , ) -> None [Source] Give a button a key that presses it. In the app Qt handles the key; with instant motion it clicks the button at once. Parameters button ( QAbstractButton ): The button. key ( QKeySequence or str ): The key, such as “Return” or “Shift+C”. Keyword-only. Examples >>> from PySide6.QtWidgets import QPushButton >>> button = QPushButton ( "Undo" ) >>> set_shortcut ( button , key = "Backspace" ) >>> button . shortcut (). toString () 'Backspace' >>> set_instant ( True ) >>> held = QPushButton ( "Answer" ) >>> set_shortcut ( ... held , key = "Return" ... ) # in a test: the key clicks it at once >>> set_instant ( False )

title: alto.ui.notation
text: alto.ui.notation Notation styles: which music font the staff, clefs, notes and accidentals are engraved in. Also holds the choice of how the baritone clef is written (an F clef or a C clef). Examples >>> BY_KEY [ "leland" ]. label 'Leland' >>> clef_shape ( "treble" ) 'treble'

title: alto.ui.notation
text: NotationStyle NotationStyle ( key : str , * , label : str , note : str , font : str | None , line : float = 1.4 , ) [Source] One look for the music: a font and how heavy the staff lines are. Attributes key ( str ): The identifier saved in the settings. label ( str ): The name shown in the interface. Keyword-only. note ( str ): A few words on where this look comes from. Keyword-only. font ( str or None ): A key in engraving.json, or None for the built-in Noto Music drawing. Keyword-only. line ( float, default 1.4 ): The staff line weight in pixels, for the built-in drawing (the SMuFL fonts state their own). Keyword-only. Examples >>> style = BY_KEY [ "noto" ] >>> style . label , style . font ('Noto Music', None)

title: alto.ui.notation
text: baritone_clef def baritone_clef () -> str [Source] Return which way the baritone clef is written. Returns str : “f” for an F clef on the middle line, or “c” for a C clef on the top line. Examples >>> baritone_clef () in BARITONE_CLEFS True

title: alto.ui.notation
text: clef_shape def clef_shape ( clef : str ) -> str [Source] Return the clef as it is drawn. Parameters clef ( str ): A clef name such as “treble” or “baritone”. Returns str : The same name, except that “baritone” becomes “baritone_f” or “baritone_c” by the chosen way of writing it. Examples >>> clef_shape ( "alto" ) 'alto' >>> set_baritone_clef ( "c" ) >>> clef_shape ( "baritone" ) 'baritone_c' >>> set_baritone_clef ( ... "f" ... ) # back to the default >>> clef_shape ( "baritone" ) 'baritone_f'

title: alto.ui.notation
text: set_baritone_clef def set_baritone_clef ( kind : str ) -> None [Source] Choose and save how the baritone clef is written, and redraw every staff already on screen. Parameters kind ( str ): “f” or “c”; anything else gives the default (F). Examples >>> set_baritone_clef ( "c" ) >>> baritone_clef () 'c' >>> set_baritone_clef ( ... "sideways" ... ) # not a choice: the default >>> baritone_clef () 'f'

title: alto.ui.notation
text: current def current () -> NotationStyle [Source] Return the notation style in use. Returns NotationStyle : The style chosen in the settings (Finale Maestro until another is chosen). Examples >>> current (). key in BY_KEY True

title: alto.ui.notation
text: load_style def load_style () -> None [Source] Apply the saved choices: the style (Finale Maestro if none is saved or it is unknown) and the baritone clef. Examples >>> store (). setValue ( "ui/notation" , "bravura" ) >>> load_style () >>> current (). key 'bravura' >>> set_style ( DEFAULT ) # back to the default

title: alto.ui.notation
text: set_style def set_style ( key : str ) -> None [Source] Choose and save a style, and redraw every staff already on screen. Parameters key ( str ): A key of BY_KEY ; an unknown key gives the default. Examples >>> set_style ( "leland" ) >>> current (). label 'Leland' >>> set_style ( DEFAULT )

title: alto.ui.notation
text: on_redraw def on_redraw ( hook : Callable [[], None ]) -> None [Source] Register a function to call whenever the notation style changes. The staff widgets live in a module that imports this one, so they register themselves here instead of being found by this module. Parameters hook ( Callable ): A function with no arguments that repaints what depends on the style. Examples >>> calls = [] >>> def repaint () -> None : ... calls . append ( 1 ) >>> on_redraw ( repaint ) >>> _redraw () >>> calls [1] >>> _redraw_hooks . remove ( repaint )

title: alto.ui.notes
text: alto.ui.notes Engraved notes built from the Noto Music font’s glyphs, the way notation software draws them. The font only has stem-up notes. A stem-down note is made from the same glyph turned half a turn (which puts the stem on the left of the head and keeps the head’s tilt), with the flags cut from the stem-up glyph and mirrored so they sweep up from the stem’s end, as an engraver would write them. All numbers are in glyph units at a font size of 100, where one staff space is STAFF_SPACE units. Examples >>> note_shape ( "quarter" ). isEmpty () False >>> note_shape ( ... "whole" , stem_down = True ... ) is note_shape ( ... "whole" ... ) # a whole note has no stem to turn True

title: alto.ui.notes
text: note_shape def note_shape ( value : str , * , stem_down : bool = False , ) -> QPainterPath [Source] Return the outline of a note of a value, with the stem up or down. Half notes and shorter values have stems, so a double whole note or whole note looks the same either way. Shapes are cached after their first use. Parameters value ( str ): “breve”, “whole”, “half”, “quarter”, “eighth”, “sixteenth” or “thirty_second”. stem_down ( bool, default False ): Turn the stem down. Keyword-only. Returns QPainterPath : The outline, in glyph units. Examples >>> up , down = ( ... note_shape ( "quarter" ), ... note_shape ( "quarter" , stem_down = True ), ... ) >>> up == down False

title: alto.ui.notes
text: draw_note def draw_note ( p : QPainter , * , value : str , x : float , y : float , gap : float , color : QColor , stem_down : bool = False , ) -> None [Source] Draw a note with its head centered on a point, in Noto Music. The note is drawn from the Noto Music font, so it is only drawn as it should be where that font is installed. The staff draws with Bravura, which comes with Alto, wherever Noto Music is missing. Parameters p ( QPainter ): The painter to draw with. value ( str ): The note value. Keyword-only. x ( float ): The head’s center, in pixels. Keyword-only. y ( float ): The head’s center, in pixels. Keyword-only. gap ( float ): The distance between staff lines, which is also the head’s height. Keyword-only. color ( QColor ): The color to draw in. Keyword-only. stem_down ( bool, default False ): Draw the stem down. Keyword-only. Examples >>> from PySide6.QtGui import QImage >>> image = QImage ( ... 100 , 100 , QImage . Format . Format_ARGB32 ... ) >>> image . fill ( QColor ( "white" )) >>> painter = QPainter ( image ) >>> draw_note ( ... painter , ... value = "quarter" , ... x = 50 , ... y = 50 , ... gap = 16 , ... color = QColor ( "black" ), ... ) >>> painter . end () True >>> from PySide6.QtGui import QFontDatabase >>> not QFontDatabase . hasFamily ( ... "Noto Music" ... ) or image . pixelColor ( ... 50 , 50 ... ). lightness () < 128 # the head is at the point True

title: alto.ui.pack_settings_panel
text: alto.ui.pack_settings_panel The settings panels of exercises that plugins add. A plugin exercise declares the controls it wants (a range, a sound, accidentals …) and gets a panel built from them, like the built-in exercises’ panels. Its options are saved under the exercise’s name. Examples >>> COMMIT_DELAY_MS 150

title: alto.ui.pack_settings_panel
text: PackSettingsPanel PackSettingsPanel ( exercise : type [ PackExercise ], * , parent : QWidget | None = None , ) [Source] Bases: NoteAnswerSettingsPanel The settings a plugin declared for one of its note exercises, drawn from a fixed set of controls. The plugin picks which controls appear: a switch for its own sound, a range selector on one clef, and switches for accidentals and for the octave. Edits are live: each changes the options, saves them and emits changed . Attributes exercise ( type of PackExercise ): The exercise whose options are edited. cfg ( PackExerciseSettings ): The options being edited. range_row ( MenuRow ): The Range row, present only if the plugin declared a range. sound_row ( ToggleRow or None ): The plugin sound switch, if declared. accidentals_row ( ToggleRow or None ): The accidentals switch, if declared. octave_row ( ToggleRow or None ): The octave switch, if declared. Examples >>> class Demo ( PackExercise ): ... controls = { "octave" : True } >>> panel = PackSettingsPanel ( Demo ) >>> panel . octave_row is not None and not hasattr ( ... panel , "range_row" ... ) True >>> _ = settings . pack_exercises . pop ( "Demo" ) Constructor Build the menu and, if the plugin offers a range, its page. Parameters exercise ( type of PackExercise ): The exercise to edit. parent ( QWidget or None, default None ): The widget that owns the panel. Keyword-only. Constructor examples >>> class Sounds ( PackExercise ): ... controls = { "sound" : "Demo sound" } >>> panel = PackSettingsPanel ( Sounds ) >>> panel . stack . count () 2 >>> _ = settings . pack_exercises . pop ( "Sounds" )

title: alto.ui.pack_settings_panel
text: PackKeyboardSettingsPanel PackKeyboardSettingsPanel ( exercise : type [ PackExercise ], * , parent : QWidget | None = None , ) [Source] Bases: KeyboardRangePanel The settings a plugin declared for a keyboard interval exercise: its sound, the range of keys, and the intervals. The plugin picks which controls appear. Edits are live: each changes the options, saves them and emits changed . Attributes exercise ( type of PackExercise ): The exercise whose options are edited. cfg ( PackExerciseSettings ): The options being edited. stack ( SlideStack ): The settings menu, then the range page and the intervals page, as the plugin offers them. sound_row ( ToggleRow or None ): The plugin sound switch, if declared. range_row ( MenuRow or None ): The Range row, if declared. span ( KeyboardSpan or None ): The draggable range selector, if a range is declared. interval_page ( ChoiceChecklist or None ): The interval checkboxes, keyed by interval name, if a choice of intervals is declared. manual_page ( ChoiceChecklist or None ): The keyboard checkboxes, keyed by keyboard name, if a choice of manuals is declared. Examples >>> class Demo ( PackExercise ): ... controls = { ... "range" : True , ... "intervals" : True , ... "manuals" : True , ... } ... spec = { "type" : "keyboard-intervals" } ... key_span , key_default = ( ... ( 28 , 89 ), ... ( 48 , 72 ), ... ) ... interval_names = ( "m2" , "M2" , "m3" ) ... manual_names = ( ... "Upper manual" , ... "Lower manual" , ... ) >>> panel = PackKeyboardSettingsPanel ( Demo ) >>> ( ... panel . stack . count (), ... panel . low_label . text (), ... panel . high_label . text (), ... ) (4, 'C3', 'C5') >>> _ = settings . pack_exercises . pop ( "Demo" ) Constructor Build the menu and the pages the plugin offers. Parameters exercise ( type of PackExercise ): The exercise to edit. parent ( QWidget or None, default None ): The widget that owns the panel. Keyword-only. Constructor examples >>> class Sounds ( PackExercise ): ... controls = { "sound" : "Demo sound" } ... spec = { "type" : "keyboard-intervals" } >>> panel = PackKeyboardSettingsPanel ( Sounds ) >>> panel . stack . count () 2 >>> _ = settings . pack_exercises . pop ( "Sounds" )

title: alto.ui.pack_settings_panel
text: PackKeyboardSettingsPanel.flush def flush () -> None [Source] Save the options and ask a new question now, if an edit is waiting. Examples >>> class Demo ( PackExercise ): ... controls = { "sound" : "Demo sound" } ... spec = { "type" : "keyboard-intervals" } >>> panel = PackKeyboardSettingsPanel ( Demo ) >>> panel . _sound_chosen ( "piano" ) >>> panel . flush () >>> panel . _commit_timer . isActive () False >>> _ = settings . pack_exercises . pop ( "Demo" )

title: alto.ui.pack_settings_panel
text: PackKeyboardSettingsPanel.hideEvent def hideEvent ( event : QHideEvent ) -> None [Source] Keep an edit that is still waiting when the panel closes. Parameters event ( QHideEvent ): The event. Examples >>> class Demo ( PackExercise ): ... controls = { "sound" : "Demo sound" } ... spec = { "type" : "keyboard-intervals" } >>> panel = PackKeyboardSettingsPanel ( Demo ) >>> panel . _sound_chosen ( "piano" ) >>> panel . show () >>> panel . hide () >>> panel . _commit_timer . isActive () False >>> _ = settings . pack_exercises . pop ( "Demo" )

title: alto.ui.package_update
text: alto.ui.package_update The window that updates a packaged copy of Alto: the download and its checks with their progress, then what happens next. The work is in alto.selfupdate , which has no Qt, and runs on another thread here so that the window keeps moving. Until the download has been checked nothing has been installed, and Cancel (or closing the window) throws it away. When it is ready the window says that Alto will close, install the update and open again, and OK hands over; the caller starts the installer and quits. Examples >>> from alto.updates import Release >>> PackageUpdateDialog # doctest: +ELLIPSIS <class '...PackageUpdateDialog'>

title: alto.ui.package_update
text: UpdatePreparer UpdatePreparer ( parent : QObject | None = None ) [Source] Bases: QObject Download and check an update on another thread, and report how it goes through signals. Attributes status ( Signal ): Emitted with what is being done (“Checking the signature…”). progress ( Signal ): Emitted with the bytes received so far and the total (0 if it is not known), while the file downloads. done ( Signal ): Emitted once at the end, with 0 if the update is ready (see prepared ) or 1 if it failed, and the reason. Nothing is emitted if the person canceled. prepared ( Prepared or None ): The checked update, once it is ready. Examples >>> UpdatePreparer (). prepared is None True Constructor Make a preparer that has not started. Parameters parent ( QObject or None, default None ): The object that owns it.

title: alto.ui.package_update
text: UpdatePreparer.start def start ( * , release : Release , target : Target , work : Path , keys : tuple [ str , ...], ) -> None [Source] Start downloading and checking. Parameters release ( Release ): The release to install. target ( Target ): The copy that will be replaced. work ( Path ): An empty folder to work in. keys ( tuple of str ): The public keys (base64) a signature may be made with.

title: alto.ui.package_update
text: UpdatePreparer.cancel def cancel () -> None [Source] Stop, at the next chance, and say nothing more.

title: alto.ui.package_update
text: UpdatePreparer.is_canceled def is_canceled () -> bool [Source] Say whether the person has canceled. Returns bool : True once cancel has been called. Examples >>> UpdatePreparer (). is_canceled () False

title: alto.ui.package_update
text: PackageUpdateDialog PackageUpdateDialog ( parent : QWidget | None , * , release : Release , target : Target , ) [Source] Bases: QDialog The window that downloads and checks an update for a packaged copy, and then says what happens next. Attributes status ( QLabel ): What is happening. bar ( QProgressBar ): The progress of the download; a bar that keeps moving while the size is not known. button ( QPushButton ): Cancel while the update is being prepared, then OK if it is ready or Close if it failed. ended ( bool ): Whether the preparing has ended, ready, failed or canceled. ready ( bool ): Whether the update is downloaded and checked. canceled ( bool ): Whether the person canceled. error ( str ): Why it failed, if it did. preparer ( UpdatePreparer ): What does the work. Constructor Build the window; nothing is downloaded until run is called. Parameters parent ( QWidget or None ): The window it belongs to. release ( Release ): The release to install. Keyword-only. target ( Target ): The copy that will be replaced. Keyword-only.

title: alto.ui.package_update
text: PackageUpdateDialog.run def run () -> Prepared | None [Source] Download and check the update, showing the window until the person has read how it went. Returns Prepared or None : The update, if it is ready and OK was pressed; None if it failed or was canceled, in which case nothing is left behind. Examples >>> here = Target ( ... "linux" , folder = Path ( "/x" ), prefix = None ... ) >>> # noinspection PyTypeChecker >>> PackageUpdateDialog ( ... None , ... release = Release ( ... "0.1.0" , tag = "v0.1.0" , url = "" ... ), ... target = here , ... ). ready False

title: alto.ui.package_update
text: PackageUpdateDialog.reject def reject () -> None [Source] Close the window; before the update is ready that cancels it.

title: alto.ui.pictures
text: alto.ui.pictures Small pictures of musical things (clefs, note values, key signatures, note ranges …) for the settings panes. Each picture is drawn in fixed units and then scaled, so the same picture serves as a summary in a menu row and, larger, as the label of a choice. Colors come from the palette, so they work in light and dark themes. Examples >>> ( ... CLEF_NAMES [ "treble" ], ... VALUE_NAMES [ "sixteenth" ], ... ) ('Treble', '16th') >>> ClefPictures ([ "treble" , "bass" ]). toolTip () 'Treble, Bass'

title: alto.ui.pictures
text: symbol_icon def symbol_icon ( symbol : str , * , color : QColor , height : int = 56 , ) -> QIcon [Source] Draw a clef symbol on its own, without a staff, as an icon. The G, C and F clefs are drawn the same size as they are on a staff, so the three look alike beside one another, and centered. Parameters symbol ( str ): “G”, “C” or “F”. color ( QColor ): The color to draw it in. Keyword-only. height ( int, default 56 ): The icon’s height in pixels, which is also as wide as it is. Keyword-only. Returns QIcon : The icon, in the notation font chosen in the settings. Examples >>> symbol_icon ( ... "F" , color = QColor ( "black" ) ... ). isNull () False

title: alto.ui.pictures
text: ClefPictures ClefPictures ( clefs : list [ str ] | None = None , * , scale : float = 1.0 , parent : QWidget | None = None , ) [Source] Bases: _Picture The selected clefs, each on its own five-line staff, and a two-stave picture with a brace for the grand staff. Showing each clef on its own staff lets alto and tenor, which share a symbol, look different. Attributes H, W, GAP, SPACING ( float ): The picture’s height, the width of one clef, the distance between staff lines and the space between clefs. NAMES ( dict of str to str ): The name of each clef. clefs ( list of str ): The clefs shown. Examples >>> ClefPictures ([ "alto" , "tenor" ]). toolTip () 'Alto, Tenor' Constructor Create the picture. Parameters clefs ( list of str or None, default None ): The clefs to show, any of CLEF_NAMES . scale ( float, default 1.0 ): How much to enlarge it. Keyword-only. parent ( QWidget or None, default None ): The widget that owns it. Keyword-only. Constructor examples >>> ClefPictures ([ "treble" ], scale = 2.0 ). width () 60

title: alto.ui.pictures
text: ClefPictures.set_clefs def set_clefs ( clefs : list [ str ]) -> None [Source] Show different clefs and size the picture for them. Parameters clefs ( list of str ): The clefs to show, any of CLEF_NAMES . Examples >>> pictures = ClefPictures () >>> pictures . set_clefs ( ... [ "treble" , "bass" , "alto" ] ... ) >>> pictures . width () # three clefs and the space between them 106 >>> pictures . toolTip () 'Treble, Bass, Alto'

title: alto.ui.pictures
text: ClefPictures.icon @ classmethod def icon ( clef : str , * , scale : float = 1.8 , ) -> QIcon [Source] Return one clef as an icon. Parameters clef ( str ): A key of CLEF_NAMES . scale ( float, default 1.8 ): How much to enlarge it. Keyword-only. Returns QIcon : The icon. Examples >>> ClefPictures . icon ( "grand" ). isNull () False

title: alto.ui.pictures
text: ClefPictures.paintEvent def paintEvent ( _ : QPaintEvent ) -> None [Source] Draw each clef on its staff, or the grand staff with its brace. Parameters _ ( QPaintEvent ): The paint request; the whole widget is always redrawn. Examples >>> ClefPictures ( ... [ "treble" , "grand" ] ... ). grab (). isNull () False

title: alto.ui.pictures
text: ValuePictures ValuePictures ( values : list [ str ] | None = None , * , scale : float = 1.0 , center_stemless : bool = False , parent : QWidget | None = None , ) [Source] Bases: _Picture Note values as engraved symbols (no staff), each with its head on the same baseline so they line up. Attributes values ( list of str ): The note values shown, keys of VALUE_NAMES . center_stemless ( bool ): Whether the double whole note and whole note sit at the picture’s vertical center. Examples >>> pictures = ValuePictures ( ... [ "whole" , "quarter" , "eighth" ] ... ) >>> pictures . values ['whole', 'quarter', 'eighth'] Constructor Create the picture. Parameters values ( list of str or None, default None ): The note values to show. scale ( float, default 1.0 ): How much to enlarge it. Keyword-only. center_stemless ( bool, default False ): Center double whole notes and whole notes vertically so they align with the middle of adjacent text. Other notes keep their heads low so their stems fit above. Keyword-only. parent ( QWidget or None, default None ): The widget that owns it. Keyword-only. Constructor examples >>> ValuePictures ( ... [ "half" ], center_stemless = True ... ). center_stemless True

title: alto.ui.pictures
text: ValuePictures.set_values def set_values ( values : list [ str ]) -> None [Source] Show different note values and size the picture for them. Parameters values ( list of str ): The note values to show. Examples >>> pictures = ValuePictures () >>> pictures . set_values ([ "breve" , "whole" ]) >>> pictures . values ['breve', 'whole']

title: alto.ui.pictures
text: ValuePictures.icon @ classmethod def icon ( value : str , * , scale : float = 1.7 , ) -> QIcon [Source] Return one note value as an icon. Parameters value ( str ): A key of VALUE_NAMES . scale ( float, default 1.7 ): How much to enlarge it. Keyword-only. Returns QIcon : The icon. Examples >>> ValuePictures . icon ( "quarter" ). isNull () False

title: alto.ui.pictures
text: ValuePictures.paintEvent def paintEvent ( _ : QPaintEvent ) -> None [Source] Draw each note value. Parameters _ ( QPaintEvent ): The paint request; the whole widget is always redrawn. Examples >>> ValuePictures ( ... [ "whole" , "half" , "quarter" ] ... ). grab (). isNull () False

title: alto.ui.pictures
text: rhythm_picture def rhythm_picture ( term : str ) -> ValuePictures | None [Source] Render a single note, rest, tied pair, or beamed pair from an equation term. Parameters term ( str ): The stored term, with a tilde between tied notes or a bar between beamed notes. Returns ValuePictures or None : The engraved term, or None for an operator, numeral, or blank. Examples >>> rhythm_picture ( "eighth|eighth" ). beam_count 1

title: alto.ui.pictures
text: KeySignaturePicture KeySignaturePicture ( key : int = 0 , * , scale : float = 1.0 , parent : QWidget | None = None , ) [Source] Bases: _Picture A key signature as a plain row of its sharps or flats, with no staff or clef. Each sign sits at the height it has after a treble clef, and C major, which has none, shows a natural sign. Attributes H, GAP, STEP ( float ): The picture’s height, the distance between staff lines and the space between signs. ORDER ( dict of int to str ): Where each sign is written, in order, for sharps (1) and flats (-1). key ( int ): The key signature: sharps if positive, flats if negative. Examples >>> KeySignaturePicture ( 2 ). toolTip () 'D major: 2 sharps' Constructor Create the picture. Parameters key ( int, default 0 ): The key signature: that many sharps if positive, flats if negative. scale ( float, default 1.0 ): How much to enlarge it. Keyword-only. parent ( QWidget or None, default None ): The widget that owns it. Keyword-only. Constructor examples >>> KeySignaturePicture ( 0 ). toolTip () 'C major: no sharps or flats' >>> KeySignaturePicture ( - 1 ). toolTip () 'F major: 1 flat'

title: alto.ui.pictures
text: KeySignaturePicture.icon @ classmethod def icon ( key : int , * , scale : float = 1.2 , ) -> QIcon [Source] Return a key signature as an icon. Parameters key ( int ): Sharps if positive, flats if negative. scale ( float, default 1.2 ): How much to enlarge it. Keyword-only. Returns QIcon : The icon. Examples >>> KeySignaturePicture . icon ( 3 ). isNull () False

title: alto.ui.pictures
text: KeySignaturePicture.paintEvent def paintEvent ( _ : QPaintEvent ) -> None [Source] Draw the row of sharps or flats, or a natural sign for C major. Parameters _ ( QPaintEvent ): The paint request; the whole widget is always redrawn. Examples >>> KeySignaturePicture ( - 3 ). grab (). isNull () False

title: alto.ui.pictures
text: RangePictures RangePictures ( items : list [ tuple [ str , int , int ]] | None = None , * , scale : float = 1.0 , max_width : float | None = None , parent : QWidget | None = None , ) [Source] Bases: _Picture For each clef, a staff with its lowest and highest note, so the range can be read off at a glance. Attributes H, W, SPACING ( float ): The picture’s height, the width of one staff and the space between staves. MAX_SCALE ( float ): The most the picture is enlarged to fit max_width . max_width ( float or None ): The width to enlarge the picture to, if any. items ( list of tuple of (str, int, int) ): Each clef with its lowest and highest note, as staff steps ( Note.diatonic ). Examples >>> pictures = RangePictures ( ... [( "treble" , 22 , 52 )] ... ) >>> pictures . toolTip () 'Treble: D3 to F7' Constructor Create the picture. Parameters items ( list of tuple of (str, int, int) or None, default None ): Each clef with its lowest and highest note. scale ( float, default 1.0 ): How much to enlarge it. Keyword-only. max_width ( float or None, default None ): Enlarge the picture to use this width (up to MAX_SCALE ) however many clefs there are. Keyword-only. parent ( QWidget or None, default None ): The widget that owns it. Keyword-only. Constructor examples >>> RangePictures ( ... [( "treble" , 22 , 52 )], max_width = 238 ... ). scale 1.9

title: alto.ui.pictures
text: RangePictures.set_items def set_items ( items : list [ tuple [ str , int , int ]]) -> None [Source] Show the ranges of some clefs and size the picture for them. Parameters items ( list of tuple of (str, int, int) ): Each clef with its lowest and highest note, as staff steps ( Note.diatonic ). Examples >>> pictures = RangePictures () >>> pictures . set_items ( ... [( "bass" , 10 , 40 ), ( "alto" , 21 , 35 )] ... ) >>> pictures . toolTip (). splitlines () ['Bass: F1 to A5', 'Alto: C3 to C5']

title: alto.ui.pictures
text: RangePictures.paintEvent def paintEvent ( _ : QPaintEvent ) -> None [Source] Draw a staff for each clef with its lowest and highest note. Parameters _ ( QPaintEvent ): The paint request; the whole widget is always redrawn. Examples >>> RangePictures ( ... [( "treble" , 22 , 52 ), ( "bass" , 10 , 40 )] ... ). grab (). isNull () False

title: alto.ui.pictures
text: NamePicture NamePicture ( naming : str = 'letters' , * , scale : float = 1.0 , parent : QWidget | None = None , ) [Source] Bases: _Picture How notes are named: C, D and E on a staff, labeled with letters, solfège syllables or scale degrees. Attributes H, W ( float ): The picture’s height and width. LETTERS, SYLLABLES ( tuple of str ): The two sets of labels. naming ( str ): “letters”, “solfege”, “degrees” (caret) or “functions”. Examples >>> NamePicture ( "solfege" ). toolTip () 'Solfège (Do Re Mi)' Constructor Create the picture. Parameters naming ( str, default “letters” ): “letters”, “solfege”, “degrees” (caret) or “functions”. scale ( float, default 1.0 ): How much to enlarge it. Keyword-only. parent ( QWidget or None, default None ): The widget that owns it. Keyword-only. Constructor examples >>> NamePicture (). naming 'letters'

title: alto.ui.pictures
text: NamePicture.set_naming def set_naming ( naming : str ) -> None [Source] Choose which labels are drawn. Parameters naming ( str ): “letters” for C D E, “solfege” for Do Re Mi, or “degrees” for 1̂ 2̂ 3̂, or “functions” for function names. Examples >>> picture = NamePicture () >>> picture . set_naming ( "solfege" ) >>> picture . toolTip () 'Solfège (Do Re Mi)'

title: alto.ui.pictures
text: NamePicture.icon @ classmethod def icon ( naming : str , * , scale : float = 1.6 , ) -> QIcon [Source] Return the picture as an icon. Parameters naming ( str ): “letters”, “solfege”, “degrees” (caret) or “functions”. scale ( float, default 1.6 ): How much to enlarge it. Keyword-only. Returns QIcon : The icon. Examples >>> NamePicture . icon ( "letters" ). isNull () False

title: alto.ui.pictures
text: NamePicture.paintEvent def paintEvent ( _ : QPaintEvent ) -> None [Source] Draw the staff, the clef, the three notes and their labels. Parameters _ ( QPaintEvent ): The paint request; the whole widget is always redrawn. Examples >>> NamePicture ( "letters" ). grab (). isNull () False

title: alto.ui.plugins_dialog
text: alto.ui.plugins_dialog The Plugins dialog: the installed plugins on the left, and the buttons that add or remove one on the right. Examples >>> from pathlib import Path >>> PluginsDialog ( ... Path ( "no-such-plugins-folder" ) ... ). windowTitle () 'Plugins'

title: alto.ui.plugins_dialog
text: PluginsDialog PluginsDialog ( folder : Path , * , parent : QWidget | None = None , ) [Source] Bases: QDialog List the installed plugins and offer to install one from a file or uninstall the selected one. Registered releases are downloaded in the background. The parent window handles local file installs, removal, and restarts. Attributes folder ( Path ): The plugins folder that is listed. list ( QListWidget ): The installed plugins, one row each. install_button ( QPushButton ): Asks for a plugin to install from a ZIP file. uninstall_button ( QPushButton ): Asks to remove the selected plugin. Disabled while nothing is selected. empty ( QLabel ): The message shown inside the list while no plugin is installed. problems ( QLabel ): Names any plugin that could not be read. install_requested ( Signal ): Emitted when Install is pressed. uninstall_requested ( Signal ): Emitted with the selected InstalledPlugin when Uninstall is pressed. Examples >>> from pathlib import Path >>> dialog = PluginsDialog ( ... Path ( "no-such-plugins-folder" ) ... ) >>> ( ... dialog . list . count (), ... dialog . uninstall_button . isEnabled (), ... ) (0, False) Constructor Build the dialog for the plugins in a folder. Parameters folder ( Path ): The plugins folder to list. parent ( QWidget or None, default None ): The widget that owns the dialog. Keyword-only. Constructor examples >>> from pathlib import Path >>> PluginsDialog ( ... Path ( "no-such-plugins-folder" ) ... ). minimumWidth () > 0 True

title: alto.ui.reference
text: alto.ui.reference The reference pane: an interactive circle of fifths to look things up on, with an explanation under it. Click a key on either ring, or move with the arrow keys, and the circle lights that key’s chords, shows its key signature in the middle, and the text underneath explains it. Examples >>> circle = ExplorableCircle () >>> circle . select ( "outer" , place = 2 ) >>> circle . title , circle . signature ('D major', 2)

title: alto.ui.reference
text: ExplorableCircle ExplorableCircle ( parent : QWidget | None = None ) [Source] Bases: FifthsCircle A circle of fifths that shows every key and lets you pick one. Attributes cell ( tuple of (str, int) or None ): The cell that is picked: its ring (“outer” or “inner”) and its place clockwise from the top; None for none. hover ( tuple of (str, int) or None ): The cell under the pointer. interactive ( bool ): Whether the circle answers the mouse and the keys. A picture of the circle that only the program changes has it off. picked ( Signal ): Emitted with the ring and place when a cell is picked, or with “” and -1 when the pick is cleared. Examples >>> circle = ExplorableCircle () >>> circle . cell , circle . title (None, 'Circle of fifths') Constructor Build the circle with every key named and none picked. Parameters parent ( QWidget or None, default None ): The widget that owns it. Constructor examples >>> ExplorableCircle (). shown [ "inner" ] == set ( ... range ( 12 ) ... ) True

title: alto.ui.reference
text: ExplorableCircle.set_interactive def set_interactive ( interactive : bool ) -> None [Source] Let the circle be clicked and moved with the keys, or make it a picture. Parameters interactive ( bool ): True to answer the mouse and the keys. Examples >>> circle = ExplorableCircle () >>> circle . set_interactive ( False ) >>> ( ... circle . interactive , ... circle . focusPolicy () ... == Qt . FocusPolicy . NoFocus , ... ) (False, True)

title: alto.ui.reference
text: ExplorableCircle.clear def clear () -> None [Source] Pick nothing: every key is named, none is lit and the middle says what to do. Examples >>> circle = ExplorableCircle () >>> circle . select ( "outer" , place = 4 ) >>> circle . clear () >>> circle . cell , circle . signature , circle . lit (None, None, set())

title: alto.ui.reference
text: ExplorableCircle.select def select ( ring : str , * , place : int , ) -> None [Source] Pick a cell: light the chords of its key, and show its name and key signature in the middle. A minor key has the key signature, and the chords, of its relative major. Parameters ring ( str ): “outer” for the major key at the place, “inner” for its relative minor. place ( int ): The place, clockwise from the top. Keyword-only. Examples >>> circle = ExplorableCircle () >>> circle . select ( "inner" , place = 3 ) >>> ( ... circle . title , ... circle . subtitle , ... sorted ( circle . lit ), ... circle . numerals [( "outer" , 4 )], ... ) ('F♯ minor', '3 sharps', [2, 3, 4], 'V')

title: alto.ui.reference
text: ExplorableCircle.cell_at def cell_at ( point : QPointF ) -> tuple [ str , int ] | None [Source] Return the cell under a point. Parameters point ( QPointF ): A position in the widget. Returns tuple of (str, int) or None : The ring and place, or None for the middle disc or outside the circle. Examples >>> circle = ExplorableCircle () >>> circle . resize ( 400 , 400 ) >>> middle , size = circle . geometry_of () >>> circle . cell_at ( ... QPointF ( ... middle . x (), middle . y () - 0.9 * size ... ) ... ) ('outer', 0) >>> circle . cell_at ( ... QPointF ( ... middle . x () + 0.6 * size , middle . y () ... ) ... ) ('inner', 3) >>> circle . cell_at ( middle ) is None True

title: alto.ui.reference
text: ExplorableCircle.lift_of def lift_of ( ring : str , * , place : int , ) -> float [Source] Return how bright a cell is drawn: as for any question, and a little brighter under the pointer. Parameters ring ( str ): “outer” or “inner”. place ( int ): The place clockwise from the top. Keyword-only. Returns float : The brightness, from 0 to 1. Examples >>> circle = ExplorableCircle () >>> circle . hover = ( "outer" , 5 ) >>> ( ... circle . lift_of ( "outer" , place = 5 ), ... circle . lift_of ( "outer" , place = 6 ), ... ) (0.2, 0.0)

title: alto.ui.reference
text: ExplorableCircle.mousePressEvent def mousePressEvent ( event : QMouseEvent ) -> None [Source] Pick the cell that is clicked; a click in the middle clears the pick. Parameters event ( QMouseEvent ): The click. Examples >>> from PySide6.QtCore import QPoint >>> from PySide6.QtTest import QTest >>> circle = ExplorableCircle () >>> circle . resize ( 400 , 400 ) >>> center , radius = circle . geometry_of () >>> QTest . mouseClick ( ... circle , ... Qt . MouseButton . LeftButton , ... pos = QPoint ( ... int ( center . x ()), ... int ( center . y () - 0.9 * radius ), ... ), ... ) >>> circle . cell ('outer', 0)

title: alto.ui.reference
text: ExplorableCircle.mouseMoveEvent def mouseMoveEvent ( event : QMouseEvent ) -> None [Source] Light the cell under the pointer, and show a hand over the ones that can be picked. Parameters event ( QMouseEvent ): The move. Examples >>> from PySide6.QtCore import QPoint >>> from PySide6.QtTest import QTest >>> circle = ExplorableCircle () >>> circle . resize ( 400 , 400 ) >>> circle . show () >>> center , radius = circle . geometry_of () >>> QTest . mouseMove ( ... circle , ... QPoint ( ... int ( center . x ()), ... int ( center . y () - 0.9 * radius ), ... ), ... ) >>> circle . hover ('outer', 0)

title: alto.ui.reference
text: ExplorableCircle.leaveEvent def leaveEvent ( event : QEvent ) -> None [Source] Stop lighting a cell once the pointer has left. Parameters event ( QEvent ): The event. Examples >>> circle = ExplorableCircle () >>> circle . hover = ( "outer" , 1 ) >>> circle . leaveEvent ( QEvent ( QEvent . Type . Leave )) >>> circle . hover is None True

title: alto.ui.reference
text: ExplorableCircle.keyPressEvent def keyPressEvent ( event : QKeyEvent ) -> None [Source] Move the pick with the arrow keys: Left and Right around the circle, Up and Down between the rings. Escape clears the pick, and Home picks C major. Parameters event ( QKeyEvent ): The key. Examples >>> circle = ExplorableCircle () >>> press = QKeyEvent ( ... QKeyEvent . Type . KeyPress , ... Qt . Key . Key_Right , ... Qt . KeyboardModifier . NoModifier , ... ) >>> circle . keyPressEvent ( press ) >>> circle . cell ('outer', 0) >>> circle . keyPressEvent ( press ) >>> circle . cell ('outer', 1)

title: alto.ui.reference
text: ReferencePanel ReferencePanel ( parent : QWidget | None = None ) [Source] Bases: QWidget The reference for the circle of fifths: a short description, the circle to explore, and what the picked key means. Attributes circle ( ExplorableCircle ): The circle to pick a key on. explanation ( QLabel ): The text under the circle, which follows the pick. lesson_button ( QPushButton ): Opens the lesson on the circle of fifths. lesson_requested ( Signal ): Emitted with the key of the lesson to open when that button is pressed. Examples >>> panel = ReferencePanel () >>> panel . circle . select ( "outer" , place = 1 ) >>> "G major" in panel . explanation . text () True Constructor Build the panel with nothing picked. Examples >>> panel = ClefReferencePanel () >>> "C clef" in panel . rows [ ... "mezzo" ... ]. text () and "bottom line" in panel . rows [ ... "french" ... ]. text () True Constructor Build the panel: the lesson button, a line of explanation and a row for each clef. Parameters parent ( QWidget or None, default None ): The widget that owns it. Constructor examples >>> len ( ClefReferencePanel (). rows ) == len ( ... settings . CLEF_BASICS_CLEFS ... ) True

title: alto.ui.settings_menu
text: alto.ui.settings_menu The building blocks of the settings panels that slide in beside an exercise. A panel is a menu of rows (Clefs, Range, Key signatures …) that each lead to a page, in a SlideStack . This module has the rows, switches, checklists and editors those pages are made of, and the panels’ shared base classes: ExerciseSettingsPanel (navigation and saving), ClefsPanel (a Clefs page) and StaffRangePanel (a Range page per clef). The panels themselves are in alto.ui.settings_panel and alto.ui.pack_settings_panel . Examples >>> _key_label ( 2 ) 'D · 2♯' >>> row = MenuRow ( "Clefs" ) >>> row . title . text () 'Clefs'

title: alto.ui.settings_menu
text: guard_last def guard_last ( boxes : Iterable [ QAbstractButton ], * , enabled : bool = True , ) -> None [Source] Disable the only checked box, so that at least one choice always stays selected. Parameters boxes ( iterable of QAbstractButton ): The checkboxes of one choice. enabled ( bool, default True ): False disables them all (for when the whole choice is switched off). Keyword-only. Examples >>> first , second = QCheckBox (), QCheckBox () >>> first . setChecked ( True ) >>> guard_last ([ first , second ]) >>> first . isEnabled (), second . isEnabled () (False, True) >>> second . setChecked ( True ) >>> guard_last ([ first , second ]) >>> first . isEnabled () True

title: alto.ui.settings_menu
text: arrow_button def arrow_button ( kind : Qt . ArrowType , * , tip : str , ) -> QToolButton [Source] Make a small arrow button that repeats while it is held. Parameters kind ( Qt.ArrowType ): Which way the arrow points. tip ( str ): The tooltip. Keyword-only. Returns QToolButton : The button. Examples >>> button = arrow_button ( ... Qt . ArrowType . UpArrow , ... tip = "Raise the lowest note" , ... ) >>> button . toolTip (), button . autoRepeat () ('Raise the lowest note', True)

title: alto.ui.settings_menu
text: RangeEditor RangeEditor ( key : str , * , low : int , high : int , limits : tuple [ int , int ] | None = None , parent : QWidget | None = None , ) [Source] Bases: QWidget A staff showing the lowest and highest note asked for a clef. Arrows on the left move the lower bound, arrows on the right move the upper bound. Attributes edited ( Signal ): Emitted with the clef key, the lowest note and the highest note (as staff steps) after a change. key ( str ): The clef. low ( int ): The lowest note asked, as a staff step ( Note.diatonic ). high ( int ): The highest note asked. limits ( tuple of (int, int) ): The furthest the bounds may go. staff ( StaffWidget ): Shows the two notes. Examples >>> editor = RangeEditor ( ... "treble" , low = 28 , high = 34 ... ) >>> editor . caption_text . text () 'C4 – B4' Constructor Build the editor for a clef’s range. Parameters key ( str ): The clef, a key of RANGE_LIMITS . low ( int ): The lowest note asked, as a staff step. Keyword-only. high ( int ): The highest note asked. Keyword-only. limits ( tuple of (int, int) or None, default None ): The furthest the bounds may go, as staff steps; None for the clef’s usual limits. Keyword-only. parent ( QWidget or None, default None ): The widget that owns the editor. Keyword-only. Constructor examples >>> RangeEditor ( ... "bass" , low = 14 , high = 28 ... ). limits == settings . RANGE_LIMITS [ "bass" ] True >>> RangeEditor ( ... "alto" , low = 21 , high = 30 , limits = ( 21 , 30 ) ... ). limits (21, 30)

title: alto.ui.settings_menu
text: KeyDiagram KeyDiagram ( keys : set [ int ] | None = None , * , parent : QWidget | None = None , ) [Source] Bases: QWidget A small fork showing which key signatures are selected. C major is on the left, then two rows of seven dots: 1 to 7 sharps on the top row and 1 to 7 flats on the bottom. Selected keys are filled, the rest are hollow. Attributes DOT, PITCH, ROW_GAP, PAD ( float ): The dot radius and the spacing, in pixels. keys ( set of int ): The selected key signatures: sharps if positive, flats if negative. Examples >>> KeyDiagram ({ 0 , 2 }). toolTip () 'C, D' Constructor Create the diagram. Parameters keys ( set of int or None, default None ): The key signatures to show as selected. parent ( QWidget or None, default None ): The widget that owns it. Keyword-only. Constructor examples >>> KeyDiagram (). keys set()

title: alto.ui.settings_menu
text: KeyDiagram.set_keys def set_keys ( keys : set [ int ]) -> None [Source] Choose which key signatures are shown as selected. Parameters keys ( set of int ): Sharps if positive, flats if negative. Examples >>> diagram = KeyDiagram () >>> diagram . set_keys ({ 2 , - 1 , 0 }) >>> diagram . toolTip () 'C, D, F'

title: alto.ui.settings_menu
text: KeyDiagram.paintEvent def paintEvent ( _ : QPaintEvent ) -> None [Source] Draw a dot for each key signature, filled when selected. Parameters _ ( QPaintEvent ): The paint request; the whole widget is always redrawn. Examples >>> KeyDiagram ({ 0 , 1 , - 1 }). grab (). isNull () False

title: alto.ui.settings_menu
text: label_with_picture def label_with_picture ( button : QAbstractButton , * , picture : _Picture , name : str , ) -> None [Source] Label a checkbox or radio button with a picture instead of text. The name stays as the tooltip and the accessible name. Parameters button ( QAbstractButton ): The button to label. picture ( _Picture ): The picture (a clef, a note value …). Keyword-only. name ( str ): What it is called. Keyword-only. Examples >>> box = QCheckBox () >>> label_with_picture ( ... box , ... picture = ClefPictures ([ "treble" ]), ... name = "Treble" , ... ) >>> box . toolTip (), box . accessibleName () ('Treble', 'Treble')

title: alto.ui.settings_menu
text: clef_choice_page def clef_choice_page ( choices : Iterable [ str ], * , selected : set [ str ], edited : Callable [[], object ], back : Callable [[], object ], title : str = 'Clefs' , hint : str = 'One of the checked clefs is picked at random.' , ) -> tuple [ dict [ str , QCheckBox ], QWidget ] [Source] Build the “Clefs” page that every exercise with a choice of clefs shares. Parameters choices ( iterable of str ): The clefs to offer, from settings.RANGE_KEYS ; “grand” is left out of exercises that cannot use the grand staff. selected ( set of str ): The clefs that start checked. Keyword-only. edited ( callable ): Called whenever a box is checked or unchecked. Keyword-only. back ( callable ): Called when the Back button is clicked. Keyword-only. title ( str, default “Clefs” ): The page’s title. Keyword-only. hint ( str, default “One of the checked clefs is picked at random.” ): The gray line above the list. Keyword-only. Returns dict of str to QCheckBox : The checkbox of each clef offered. QWidget : The page, with its title. The last checked clef cannot be unchecked. Examples >>> checked = [] >>> boxes_ , page_ = clef_choice_page ( ... ( "treble" , "bass" ), ... selected = { "bass" }, ... edited = lambda : checked . append ( 1 ), ... back = lambda : None , ... ) >>> boxes_ [ ... "bass" ... ]. isEnabled () # it is the only one checked, so it stays checked False >>> boxes_ [ "treble" ]. setChecked ( True ) >>> ( ... sorted ( ... c ... for c , ticked_box in boxes_ . items () ... if ticked_box . isChecked () ... ), ... checked , ... ) (['bass', 'treble'], [1])

title: alto.ui.settings_menu
text: show_keys def show_keys ( row : MenuRow , * , diagram : KeyDiagram , enabled : bool , keys : set [ int ], ) -> None [Source] Show the selected keys as a diagram in a menu row, or “Off” when key signatures are switched off. Parameters row ( MenuRow ): The menu row. diagram ( KeyDiagram ): The diagram to update. Keyword-only. enabled ( bool ): Whether key signatures are on. Keyword-only. keys ( set of int ): The selected key signatures. Keyword-only. Examples >>> row_ , diagram_ = ( ... MenuRow ( "Key signatures" ), ... KeyDiagram (), ... ) >>> show_keys ( ... row_ , ... diagram = diagram_ , ... enabled = False , ... keys = { 0 }, ... ) >>> row_ . value . text (), diagram_ . isHidden () ('Off', True)

title: alto.ui.settings_menu
text: MenuRow MenuRow ( title : str , * , chevron : bool = True , tall : bool = False , ) [Source] Bases: QPushButton A menu row: title on the left, current value and a chevron on the right. A tall row puts a picture on a second line of its own, using the full width, for summaries that need room to be readable. Attributes tall ( bool ): Whether the row has a second line. title ( QLabel ): The title. value ( QLabel ): The current value, shown on the right. Examples >>> row = MenuRow ( "Range" , tall = True ) >>> row . tall , row . title . text () (True, 'Range') Constructor Build the row. Parameters title ( str ): The row’s title. chevron ( bool, default True ): Show a chevron on the right, to say it opens a page. Keyword-only. tall ( bool, default False ): Give the row a second line for a picture. Keyword-only. Constructor examples >>> MenuRow ( "Clefs" ). minimumHeight () 48

title: alto.ui.settings_menu
text: MenuRow.attach def attach ( widget : QWidget ) -> None [Source] Put a widget in the row. Just after the value text, or (in a tall row) centered on its own line below. Parameters widget ( QWidget ): The widget, usually a small picture of the current choice. Examples >>> row = MenuRow ( "Clefs" ) >>> picture = ClefPictures ([ "treble" ]) >>> row . attach ( picture ) >>> # noinspection PyUnresolvedReferences >>> row . layout (). indexOf ( picture ) 2

title: alto.ui.settings_menu
text: MenuRow.fit def fit () -> None [Source] Make a tall row as high as its contents need. A button does not size itself to a layout inside it. Examples >>> row = MenuRow ( "Range" , tall = True ) >>> row . attach ( QLabel ( "a picture" )) >>> row . minimumHeight () > 0 True

title: alto.ui.settings_menu
text: Switch Switch ( parent : QWidget | None = None ) [Source] Bases: QAbstractButton A pill-shaped on/off switch whose knob slides across when toggled. Attributes W, H ( int ): The switch’s size, in pixels. Examples >>> switch = Switch () >>> switch . setChecked ( True ) >>> switch . isChecked () True Constructor Create a switch that is off. Parameters parent ( QWidget or None, default None ): The widget that owns it. Constructor examples >>> Switch (). isChecked () False

title: alto.ui.settings_menu
text: Switch.setChecked def setChecked ( on : bool ) -> None [Source] Turn the switch on or off without animating, as when a setting is loaded. Parameters on ( bool ): The new state. Examples >>> switch = Switch () >>> switch . setChecked ( True ) >>> switch . _pos 1.0

title: alto.ui.settings_menu
text: Switch.paintEvent def paintEvent ( _ : QPaintEvent ) -> None [Source] Draw the track, tinted between off and on, and the knob. Parameters _ ( QPaintEvent ): The paint request; the whole widget is always redrawn. Examples >>> Switch (). grab (). isNull () False

title: alto.ui.settings_menu
text: Switch.sizeHint def sizeHint () -> QSize [Source] Return the switch’s fixed size. Returns QSize : W by H . Examples >>> Switch (). sizeHint () PySide6.QtCore.QSize(42, 24)

title: alto.ui.settings_menu
text: ToggleRow ToggleRow ( title : str ) [Source] Bases: MenuRow A menu row with a switch that changes a setting in place instead of opening a page. Attributes switched ( Signal ): Emitted with the new state when the row is clicked. switch ( Switch ): The switch. Examples >>> row = ToggleRow ( "Accidentals" ) >>> changes = [] >>> _ = row . switched . connect ( changes . append ) >>> row . click () >>> changes , row . isOn () ([True], True) Constructor Build the row with its switch off. Parameters title ( str ): The row’s title. Constructor examples >>> ToggleRow ( "Accidentals" ). isOn () False

title: alto.ui.settings_menu
text: ToggleRow.isOn def isOn () -> bool [Source] Report whether the switch is on. Returns bool : True if on. Examples >>> ToggleRow ( "Accidentals" ). isOn () False

title: alto.ui.settings_menu
text: ToggleRow.setOn def setOn ( on : bool ) -> None [Source] Set the switch without announcing it, as when a setting is loaded. Parameters on ( bool ): The new state. Examples >>> row = ToggleRow ( "Accidentals" ) >>> row . setOn ( True ) >>> row . isOn () True

title: alto.ui.settings_menu
text: subpage def subpage ( title : str , * , body : QWidget , back : Callable [[], object ], fill : bool = False , ) -> QWidget [Source] Build a second-layer page: a Back button and title above a body. Parameters title ( str ): The page’s title. body ( QWidget ): What the page shows. Keyword-only. back ( callable ): Called when Back is clicked. Keyword-only. fill ( bool, default False ): Let the body take all the room (so a long page can scroll) instead of leaving space below it. Keyword-only. Returns QWidget : The page. Examples >>> calls = [] >>> page_ = subpage ( ... "Clefs" , ... body = QWidget (), ... back = lambda : calls . append ( "back" ), ... ) >>> next ( ... b ... for b in page_ . findChildren ( QToolButton ) ... if b . text () == "‹ Back" ... ). click () >>> calls ['back']

title: alto.ui.settings_menu
text: SlideStack SlideStack ( parent : QWidget | None = None ) [Source] Bases: QStackedWidget A stacked widget whose pages slide in from the right (going deeper) or the left (going back). Examples >>> stack = SlideStack () >>> _ = stack . addWidget ( QWidget ()) >>> _ = stack . addWidget ( QWidget ()) >>> stack . sliding False Constructor Create an empty stack. Parameters parent ( QWidget or None, default None ): The widget that owns it. Constructor examples >>> SlideStack (). count () 0

title: alto.ui.settings_menu
text: SlideStack.sliding @ property def sliding () -> bool [Source] Report whether a page is sliding in. Returns bool : True from the start of a slide until it finishes. Examples >>> SlideStack (). sliding False

title: alto.ui.settings_menu
text: SlideStack.slide_to def slide_to ( index : int ) -> None [Source] Slide to another page. Going to a later page slides it in from the right and going back slides it in from the left. A request made during a slide, or for the page already showing, is ignored. Parameters index ( int ): The page to go to. Examples >>> stack = SlideStack () >>> _ = stack . addWidget ( QWidget ()) >>> _ = stack . addWidget ( QWidget ()) >>> stack . slide_to ( 1 ) >>> stack . sliding True

title: alto.ui.settings_menu
text: ExerciseSettingsPanel class ExerciseSettingsPanel ( QWidget ) [Source] What every exercise’s settings pane has in common: it says when a setting has been edited. Attributes changed ( Signal ): Emitted after any setting is edited that changes what is asked, so the exercise asks a new question. restyled ( Signal ): Emitted after a setting is edited that changes only how the exercise looks, so the question stays and the picture is drawn again. Examples >>> panel = ExerciseSettingsPanel () >>> got = [] >>> _ = panel . changed . connect ( ... lambda : got . append ( 1 ) ... ) >>> panel . changed . emit () True >>> got [1]

ClefsPanel , ... ) True

title: alto.ui.settings_menu

text: KeySignaturePage KeySignaturePage ( enabled : bool , * , selected : set [ int ], allow_empty : bool = False , key_names : dict [ int , str ] | None = None , parent : QWidget | None = None , ) [Source] Bases: QWidget The key signature sub-page: a switch for using key signatures at all, and the keys to draw from. title: alto.ui.settings_menu
text: ChoiceChecklist ChoiceChecklist ( groups : list [ tuple [ str , list [ tuple [ object , str ]]]], * , selected : set , allow_empty : bool = False , positions : Mapping [ object , tuple [ int , int ]] | None = None , parent : QWidget | None = None , ) [Source] Bases: QWidget Checkboxes for a list of choices, optionally under headings and allowing an empty selection. Attributes changed ( Signal ): Emitted after a box is checked or unchecked. allow_empty ( bool ): Whether all choices may be unchecked. boxes ( dict ): The checkbox of each choice, by its key. Examples >>> groups = [ ... ( ... "Triads" , ... [ ... ( "major" , "Major" ), ... ( "minor" , "Minor" ), ... ], ... ), ... ( "" , [( "x" , "Other" )]), ... ] >>> checklist = ChoiceChecklist ( ... groups , selected = { "major" } ... ) >>> checklist . selected () {'major'} Constructor Build the checklist. Keyword-only. parent ( QWidget or None, default None ): The widget that owns it. Keyword-only. Constructor examples >>> checklist = ChoiceChecklist ( ... [( "" , [( 0 , "Root" ), ( 1 , "1st" )])], ... selected = { 0 }, ... ) >>> # noinspection PyTypeChecker >>> sorted ( checklist . boxes ) [0, 1]

title: alto.ui.settings_panel
text: alto.ui.settings_panel The settings panels of the built-in exercises, and settings_panel_for , which picks the panel for any exercise. Each exercise with settings has a panel: a menu of rows (Clefs, Range, Key signatures …) that each lead to a page. Edits are live: they change the shared settings object, are saved, and a changed signal tells the exercise to ask a new question. The widgets the panels are built from are in alto.ui.settings_menu , plugin exercises’ panels are in alto.ui.pack_settings_panel , and loading and saving the settings is in alto.ui.exercise_settings . Examples >>> panel = settings_panel_for ( ClefBasics ()) >>> type ( panel ). __name__ 'ClefBasicsSettingsPanel'

title: alto.ui.settings_panel
text: NoteNameSettingsPanel NoteNameSettingsPanel ( cfg : NoteNameSettings , * , parent : QWidget | None = None , ) [Source] Bases: NoteAnswerSettingsPanel The settings of the note identification exercise: a menu leading to a page for each group of settings. Two layers: the menu (Clefs, Range, Key signatures, Note values, Note names, Accidentals and Octave) and a page for each. Edits are live: each changes the settings, saves them and emits changed . Attributes cfg ( NoteNameSettings ): The settings being edited. stack ( SlideStack ): The menu and its pages. boxes ( dict of str to QCheckBox ): The clef checkboxes. key_boxes ( dict of int to QCheckBox ): The key signature checkboxes. value_boxes ( dict of str to QCheckBox ): The note value checkboxes. naming_radios ( dict of str to QRadioButton ): The letters and solfège choices, plus caret and function notation in the Scale degrees group. octave_row ( ToggleRow ): Whether the answer must include the written octave. range_editors ( dict of str to RangeEditor ): The range editor of each clef in use, built when the Range page opens. Examples >>> panel = NoteNameSettingsPanel ( ... NoteNameSettings () ... ) >>> panel . cfg . active_clefs () ['treble', 'bass'] Constructor Build the panel for a set of settings. Parameters cfg ( NoteNameSettings ): The settings to edit. parent ( QWidget or None, default None ): The widget that owns the panel. Keyword-only. Constructor examples >>> panel = NoteNameSettingsPanel ( ... NoteNameSettings () ... ) >>> panel . stack . count () # the menu and five pages 6

title: alto.ui.settings_panel

KeyboardSettings , * , parent : QWidget | None = None , ) [Source] Bases: KeyboardRangePanel The settings of the keyboard exercise: a menu with a page for the range of keys. The menu includes Range, Black keys, Octave number, Key signatures and Note names. Edits are live: each changes the settings, saves them and emits changed . Attributes cfg ( KeyboardSettings ): The settings being edited. stack ( SlideStack ): The menu and its pages. span ( KeyboardSpan ): The miniature piano on the Range page, which can be dragged to choose the keys. low_label, high_label ( QLabel ): The names of the lowest and highest key asked. key_page ( KeySignaturePage ): The key signature sub-page. Examples >>> panel = KeyboardSettingsPanel ( ... settings . KeyboardSettings () ... ) >>> ( ... panel . low_label . text (), ... panel . high_label . text (), ... ) ('C3', 'C5') Constructor Build the panel for a set of settings. Parameters cfg ( KeyboardSettings ): The settings to edit. parent ( QWidget or None, default None ): The widget that owns the panel. Keyword-only. Constructor examples >>> KeyboardSettingsPanel ( ... settings . KeyboardSettings () ... ). stack . count () # the menu, range, keys and note names 4

text: CircleSettingsPanel CircleSettingsPanel ( cfg : settings . CircleSettings , * , parent : QWidget | None = None , ) [Source] Bases: ExerciseSettingsPanel The settings of the circle of fifths exercise: which kinds of question to ask, and the colors of the circle.
