title: alto.ui.settings_panel
text: settings_panel_for def settings_panel_for ( exercise : Exercise , * , learner : Learner | None = None , ) -> ExerciseSettingsPanel [Source] Return the settings panel for an exercise. Parameters exercise ( Exercise ): The exercise. learner ( Learner or None ): Profile whose calendar limits can be overridden. Returns ExerciseSettingsPanel : A panel with the exercise options and the shared Next Question setting. Examples >>> from alto.exercises.library import ( ... IntervalNames , ... NoteNames , ... ) >>> type ( ... settings_panel_for ( NoteNames ()) ... ). __name__ 'NoteNameSettingsPanel' >>> type ( ... settings_panel_for ( IntervalNames ()) ... ). __name__ 'IntervalSettingsPanel'

title: alto.ui.staff
text: alto.ui.staff The staff: lines, clefs, key signatures and notes, drawn on a rounded white “paper”. StaffWidget draws one staff, or a grand staff with a brace, in any of the seven clefs. Notes and key signatures are placed by their staff step ( Note.diatonic ) measured from the bottom line of the clef, and are engraved in the notation font chosen in the settings. Examples >>> key_signature_positions ( "treble" , sign = 1 ) ['F5', 'C5', 'G5', 'D5', 'A4', 'E5', 'B4'] >>> staff = StaffWidget () >>> staff . show_notes ( ... [[ Note . parse ( "C4" )]], ... clef = "treble" , ... key = 2 , ... ) >>> staff . clef , staff . key ('treble', 2)

title: alto.ui.staff
text: clef_targets def clef_targets ( clef : str ) -> set [ tuple [ str , int ]] [Source] Return the ways a clef can be written: the symbol and where on the staff it goes. Parameters clef ( str ): A clef name such as “treble”, “mezzo” or “baritone”. Returns set of tuple of (str, int) : Each is a symbol, “G”, “C” or “F”, and the place of its reference line (the G, F or middle C) counted in lines and spaces up from the bottom line at 0: the bottom line is 0, the space above it 1, the second line 2, up to the top line at 8. Most clefs have one. The baritone clef has two: the F clef on the middle line and the C clef on the top line. Examples >>> clef_targets ( "treble" ) == { ... ( "G" , 2 ) ... } and clef_targets ( "mezzo" ) == {( "C" , 2 )} True >>> sorted ( clef_targets ( "baritone" )) [('C', 8), ('F', 4)] >>> sorted ( ... clef_targets ( "french" ) ... | clef_targets ( "subbass" ) ... ) [('F', 8), ('G', 0)]

title: alto.ui.staff
text: clef_target_of def clef_target_of ( shape : str ) -> tuple [ str , int ] [Source] Return the symbol and the place of one way of writing a clef. Parameters shape ( str ): A key of engraving.CLEF_SIGNS , such as “alto” or “baritone_c”. Returns tuple of (str, int) : The symbol and its place, as for clef_targets . Examples >>> ( ... clef_target_of ( "bass" ), ... clef_target_of ( "soprano" ), ... ) (('F', 6), ('C', 0))

title: alto.ui.staff
text: draw_key_signature def draw_key_signature ( p : QPainter , * , clef : str , key : int , x : float , bottom : float , gap : float , color : QColor , step : float = KEY_STEP , size : float = 2.0 , font : str | None = None , ) -> None [Source] Draw the sharps or flats of a key signature, left to right. Parameters p ( QPainter ): The painter to draw with. clef ( str ): The clef, which decides where on the staff each accidental goes. Keyword-only. key ( int ): The key signature: that many sharps if positive, flats if negative; nothing is drawn for 0. Keyword-only. x ( float ): The left edge of the first accidental, in pixels. Keyword-only. bottom ( float ): The y position of the staff’s bottom line, in pixels. Keyword-only. gap ( float ): The distance between staff lines, in pixels. Keyword-only. color ( QColor ): The color to draw in. Keyword-only. step ( float, default KEY_STEP ): The horizontal spacing between accidentals. Keyword-only. size ( float, default 2.0 ): The size of the built-in characters, in staff gaps. Keyword-only. font ( str or None, default None ): A SMuFL font to engrave them in; None uses the built-in sharp and flat characters. Keyword-only. Examples >>> from PySide6.QtGui import QImage >>> image = QImage ( ... 200 , 120 , QImage . Format . Format_ARGB32 ... ) >>> image . fill ( QColor ( "white" )) >>> painter = QPainter ( image ) >>> draw_key_signature ( ... painter , ... clef = "treble" , ... key = 3 , ... x = 10 , ... bottom = 80 , ... gap = 12 , ... color = QColor ( "black" ), ... font = "bravura" , ... ) >>> painter . end () True >>> any ( ... image . pixelColor ( x_ , y_ ). lightness () ... < 128 ... for x_ in range ( 10 , 60 ) ... for y_ in range ( 20 , 100 ) ... ) True

title: alto.ui.staff
text: draw_signature_sign def draw_signature_sign ( p : QPainter , * , sign : int , x : float , y : float , gap : float , color : QColor , step : float = KEY_STEP , size : float = 2.0 , font : str | None = None , ) -> None [Source] Draw one sharp or flat at its written position in a key signature. Parameters p ( QPainter ): Active staff painter. sign ( int ): Sharp (1) or flat (-1). x, y ( float ): Left edge and staff pitch position in pixels. gap ( float ): Distance between staff lines. color ( QColor ): Ink for this sign. step, size ( float ): Slot width in pixels and built-in glyph size in staff gaps. font ( str or None ): SMuFL font, or None for the built-in notation. Examples Both the printed signature and signs placed by the learner use this drawing.

title: alto.ui.staff
text: StaffWidget StaffWidget ( parent : QWidget | None = None , * , gap : float = 16.0 , side : float = 20.0 , note_offset : float = 100.0 , margin : float = 8.0 , compact : bool = False , max_step : float | None = None , lesson_layout : bool = False , ) [Source] Bases: QWidget A staff with notes, a clef, a key signature and, optionally, a caption. Attributes GAP ( float ): The distance between staff lines, in pixels. side ( float ): The space at the left and right edges. note_offset ( float ): Where the notes start, from the left edge. margin ( float ): The space kept above and below the staff for ledger lines, in gaps. compact ( bool ): Size the widget to fit instead of the 220 px default. max_step ( float or None ): The most width each column of notes may take. clef ( str ): The clef being drawn (“treble”, “bass”, “alto”, “tenor”, “soprano”, “mezzo”, “baritone” or “grand”). columns ( list of list of Note ): The notes drawn; each inner list is one chord or note. interval_voices ( bool ): Draw harmonic interval endpoints with their written duration and opposing stems. note_color ( QColor or None ): Feedback color for the highlighted notation component, or for the notes in other exercises. column_colors ( dict of int to QColor ): The color of particular columns of notes, by position from 0; they are drawn in these instead of note_color . wedges ( list of str ): The step between each column and the next, such as “W” or “H”, drawn as two lines rising from the notes to a point above them, with the letter over the point; “” for none there. wedge_colors ( dict of int to QColor ): The color of particular wedges, by position from 0. The others take the color of the note on their right, or note_color . notation_style ( NotationStyle or None ): A style to use instead of the one chosen in the settings. clef_hidden ( bool ): Draw the staff without its clef, for a clef the learner places. key ( int ): The key signature drawn: sharps if positive, flats if negative. key_room ( int ): How many sharps or flats’ worth of room to keep for the signature at least, so that a capped staff does not change width as the signature does. 0 keeps room only for the one drawn. value ( str ): The note value drawn. caption ( str ): Text written under the staff, inside the paper. Examples >>> staff = StaffWidget () >>> staff . show_notes ( ... [ ... [ Note . parse ( "E4" )], ... [ Note . parse ( "G4" )], ... ], ... clef = "treble" , ... ) >>> len ( staff . columns ) 2 Constructor Create an empty treble staff. Parameters parent ( QWidget or None, default None ): The widget that owns the staff. gap ( float, default 16.0 ): The distance between staff lines, in pixels. Keyword-only. side ( float, default 20.0 ): The space at the left and right edges. Keyword-only. note_offset ( float, default 100.0 ): Where the notes start, from the left edge. Keyword-only. margin ( float, default 8.0 ): The space kept above and below the staff for ledger lines, in gaps. Keyword-only. compact ( bool, default False ): Size the widget to fit instead of the 220 px default. Keyword-only. max_step ( float or None, default None ): The most width each column of notes may take: the staff then stops growing once its notes would be spread wider than that, so a few notes stay easy to read in a wide window. Keyword-only. lesson_layout ( bool, default False ): Space the excerpt by its printed symbols and wrap at note or chord boundaries. Keyword-only. Constructor examples >>> StaffWidget ( gap = 8.0 , compact = True ). GAP 8.0

title: alto.ui.staff
text: StaffWidget.show_notes def show_notes ( columns : list [ list [ Note ]], * , clef : str = 'treble' , key : int = 0 , value : str = 'whole' , caption : str = '' , notation_target : tuple [ str , int ] | None = None , locate_notation : bool = False , notation_excerpt : str | None = None , ) -> None [Source] Show some notes, with a clef and a key signature. Parameters columns ( list of list of Note ): The notes: each inner list is one note or chord, drawn left to right. clef ( str, default “treble” ): The clef, or “grand” for a grand staff. Keyword-only. key ( int, default 0 ): The key signature: that many sharps if positive, flats if negative. Keyword-only. value ( str, default “whole” ): The written duration for single notes and interval voices. Keyword-only. caption ( str, default ““ ): Text to write under the staff. Keyword-only. notation_target ( tuple of (str, int) or None ): Part and position to highlight in a notation question. Keyword-only. notation_excerpt ( str or None ): Versioned score to show for a repertoire question. Keyword-only. locate_notation ( bool, default False ): Render the target in ordinary ink for the learner to find. Keyword-only. Examples >>> staff = StaffWidget () >>> staff . show_notes ( ... [[ Note . parse ( "C4" )]], ... clef = "bass" , ... key =- 1 , ... value = "quarter" , ... caption = "_ Major" , ... ) >>> ( ... staff . clef , ... staff . key , ... staff . value , ... staff . caption , ... ) ('bass', -1, 'quarter', '_ Major')

title: alto.ui.staff
text: StaffWidget.sizeHint def sizeHint () -> QSize [Source] Return the size the staff would like. A capped staff asks for its full capped width, so a layout that centers it gives it that much. Returns QSize : The capped width and minimum height for a lesson or a staff with a max_step . Other staves use Qt’s default. Examples >>> staff = StaffWidget ( max_step = 120.0 ) >>> staff . show_notes ([[ Note . parse ( "C4" )]]) >>> staff . sizeHint (). width () 500

title: alto.ui.staff
text: StaffWidget.resizeEvent def resizeEvent ( event : QResizeEvent ) -> None [Source] Reflow a lesson excerpt when its available width changes. Parameters event ( QResizeEvent ): Previous and current widget size. Examples >>> staff = StaffWidget ( lesson_layout = True ) >>> staff . resize ( 300 , staff . height ())

title: alto.ui.staff
text: StaffWidget.highlight_column def highlight_column ( index : int | None ) -> None [Source] Highlight a sounding note or chord, preserving the staff’s other markings. Parameters index ( int or None ): The sounding column, or None to restore its usual ink. Examples >>> staff = StaffWidget () >>> staff . highlight_column ( 0 ) >>> staff . playback_column 0

title: alto.ui.staff
text: StaffWidget.set_note_color def set_note_color ( color : QColor | None ) -> None [Source] Apply feedback to the highlighted notation component or to the notes when there is no component target. Parameters color ( QColor or None ): The feedback color. None restores the usual ink and highlight colors. Examples >>> staff = StaffWidget () >>> staff . set_note_color ( QColor ( "#2e7d32" )) >>> # noinspection PyUnresolvedReferences >>> staff . note_color . name () '#2e7d32' >>> staff . set_note_color ( None ) >>> staff . note_color is None True

title: alto.ui.staff
text: StaffWidget.staff_bottoms def staff_bottoms () -> dict [ str , float ] [Source] Return where each staff is drawn. Returns dict of str to float : Clef name to the y position of that staff’s bottom line, in pixels. A grand staff has a “treble” and a “bass”. Examples >>> staff = StaffWidget () >>> staff . resize ( 400 , 400 ) >>> staff . staff_bottoms () {'treble': 232.0}

title: alto.ui.staff
text: StaffWidget.paintEvent def paintEvent ( _ : QPaintEvent ) -> None [Source] Draw the paper, the staff lines, the clef, the key signature, the notes and the caption. Parameters _ ( QPaintEvent ): The paint request; the whole widget is always redrawn. Examples >>> staff = StaffWidget () >>> staff . resize ( 400 , 400 ) >>> staff . show_notes ( ... [[ Note . parse ( "C4" )]], clef = "treble" ... ) >>> staff . grab (). toImage (). pixelColor ( ... 200 , 5 ... ). name () # the white paper '#ffffff'

title: alto.ui.staff
text: StaffWidget.mouseMoveEvent def mouseMoveEvent ( event : QMouseEvent ) -> None [Source] Preview the component under the pointer in Click on Staff questions. Parameters event ( QMouseEvent ): The pointer position relative to the score. Examples >>> StaffWidget (). hasMouseTracking () False

title: alto.ui.staff
text: StaffWidget.leaveEvent def leaveEvent ( event : QEvent ) -> None [Source] Clear the component preview when the pointer leaves the music. Parameters event ( QEvent ): The pointer leaving the staff. Examples >>> StaffWidget (). leaveEvent ( ... QEvent ( QEvent . Type . Leave ) ... )

title: alto.ui.staff
text: StaffWidget.hits_notation def hits_notation ( point : QPoint ) -> bool [Source] Check for target ink within four logical pixels of a click on the score. Parameters point ( QPoint ): Click position relative to the staff widget. Returns bool : Whether the clicked neighborhood contains the selected marking. Examples >>> StaffWidget (). hits_notation ( QPoint ( 0 , 0 )) False

title: alto.ui.staff
text: keyboard_key_staff def keyboard_key_staff () -> StaffWidget [Source] Build the compact key signature shown above a keyboard question. Returns StaffWidget : A fixed-width staff sized for the signature. Examples >>> keyboard_key_staff (). width () == px ( 210 ) True

title: alto.ui.staff_input
text: alto.ui.staff_input The staffs you click to place notes or a clef. One note for the note construction exercise, a row of them for scale construction, and a clef for the clef exercise. Examples >>> staff = StaffInput () >>> staff . accidental is None and not staff . locked True

title: alto.ui.staff_input
text: StaffInput StaffInput ( parent : QWidget | None = None ) [Source] Bases: StaffWidget A single staff you click to place a note, or place a note on with the keyboard. The note snaps to the nearest line or space and follows the pointer until you click. Without the mouse, a caret marks the note that would be placed: move_cursor and jump_to_letter move it, and place_caret places it. Attributes placed ( Signal ): Emitted with the Note when you click, using the current accidental . accidental_cycled ( Signal ): Emitted on a right click: the owner steps through natural, sharp and flat. caret_moved ( Signal ): Emitted when the caret moves. accidental ( int or None ): The sign you chose (-1 flat, 0 natural, 1 sharp); None follows the key signature. locked ( bool ): Ignore the mouse (while feedback is showing). caret ( int or None ): The staff step of the note that the keyboard would place, as Note.diatonic counts them; None until the keyboard or a click has put it somewhere. Once it has a place the note is shown in the preview color while the pointer is away. Examples >>> staff = StaffInput () >>> staff . reset ( "treble" , key = 0 ) >>> staff . resize ( 400 , 300 ) >>> str ( ... staff . note_at ( ... staff . staff_bottoms ()[ "treble" ] ... ) ... ) # the bottom line of the treble staff 'E4' Constructor Create the staff. Parameters parent ( QWidget or None, default None ): The widget that owns the staff. Constructor examples >>> StaffInput (). hasMouseTracking () True

title: alto.ui.staff_input
text: StaffInput.reset def reset ( clef : str , * , key : int = 0 , caption : str = '' , placement : Question | None = None , ) -> None [Source] Clear the staff for a new question, drawing a key signature. Parameters clef ( str ): The clef to draw. key ( int, default 0 ): The key signature: that many sharps if positive, flats if negative. Keyword-only. caption ( str, default ““ ): Text to write under the staff. Keyword-only. placement ( Question or None ): Written placement question with an optional fixed starting note. Examples >>> staff = StaffInput () >>> staff . accidental , staff . locked = 1 , True >>> staff . reset ( "bass" , key =- 2 ) >>> ( ... staff . accidental is None , ... staff . locked , ... staff . key , ... ) (True, False, -2)

title: alto.ui.staff_input
text: StaffInput.note_at def note_at ( y : float ) -> Note [Source] Return the note on the line or space nearest to a height on the staff. The note is kept within five ledger lines of the staff. On a grand staff, a click in the upper half is on the treble staff and the lower half on the bass staff. Parameters y ( float ): The height in the widget, in pixels from the top. Returns Note : The note, with the chosen accidental or, if none is chosen, the one the key signature gives it. Examples >>> staff = StaffInput () >>> staff . reset ( ... "treble" , key = 1 ... ) # G major: F is sharp >>> staff . resize ( 400 , 300 ) >>> bottom = staff . staff_bottoms ()[ "treble" ] >>> str ( ... staff . note_at ( ... bottom - 3 * staff . GAP / 2 ... ) ... ) # three steps above E4 'A4' >>> str ( ... staff . note_at ( bottom - staff . GAP / 2 ) ... ) # one step above E4: F, sharp in this key 'F♯4'

title: alto.ui.staff_input
text: StaffInput.note_for def note_for ( diatonic : int ) -> Note [Source] Return the note on a staff step, with the chosen sign or the one the key signature gives it. The step is kept within five ledger lines of the staff, as clicking is. Parameters diatonic ( int ): The staff step, as Note.diatonic counts them. Returns Note : The note. Examples >>> staff = StaffInput () >>> staff . reset ( ... "treble" , key = 1 ... ) # G major: F is sharp >>> str ( ... staff . note_for ( ... Note . parse ( "F4" ). diatonic ... ) ... ) 'F♯4' >>> staff . accidental = 0 >>> str ( ... staff . note_for ( ... Note . parse ( "F4" ). diatonic ... ) ... ) 'F4'

title: alto.ui.staff_input
text: StaffInput.caret_start def caret_start () -> int [Source] Return the staff step the caret starts from, when the keyboard first moves it. Returns int : The middle line of the staff, or middle C on a grand staff. Examples >>> staff = StaffInput () >>> staff . reset ( "treble" ) >>> str ( Note . from_diatonic ( staff . caret_start ())) 'B4' >>> staff . reset ( "grand" ) >>> str ( Note . from_diatonic ( staff . caret_start ())) 'C4'

title: alto.ui.staff_input
text: StaffInput.caret_note def caret_note () -> Note | None [Source] Return the note that the keyboard would place. Returns Note or None : The note at the caret, with the chosen sign; None if the caret has not been put anywhere. Examples >>> staff = StaffInput () >>> staff . reset ( "bass" ) >>> staff . caret_note () is None True >>> staff . move_cursor ( 0 ) >>> str ( staff . caret_note ()) 'D3'

title: alto.ui.staff_input
text: StaffInput.move_cursor def move_cursor ( steps : int ) -> None [Source] Move the caret up (positive) or down (negative) by staff steps, and show the note there. The first move starts from caret_start . The caret stays within the furthest ledger lines. Parameters steps ( int ): How many lines and spaces to move; 7 is an octave. Examples >>> staff = StaffInput () >>> staff . reset ( "treble" ) >>> staff . move_cursor ( 1 ) >>> str ( staff . caret_note ()) 'C5' >>> staff . move_cursor ( - 7 ) >>> str ( staff . caret_note ()) 'C4' >>> staff . move_cursor ( ... - 500 ... ) # no further than the ledger lines go >>> staff . caret == RANGE_LIMITS [ "treble" ][ 0 ] True

title: alto.ui.staff_input
text: StaffInput.jump_to_letter def jump_to_letter ( letter : int ) -> None [Source] Move the caret to the nearest note with a letter name, above or below where it is. Parameters letter ( int ): The letter, counting from C as 0: D is 1, E is 2, F is 3, G is 4, A is 5 and B is 6. Examples >>> staff = StaffInput () >>> staff . reset ( "treble" ) >>> staff . move_cursor ( 0 ) # B4, the middle line >>> staff . jump_to_letter ( 0 ) >>> str ( ... staff . caret_note () ... ) # the nearest C is the one just above 'C5' >>> staff . jump_to_letter ( 4 ) >>> str ( ... staff . caret_note () ... ) # and the nearest G is the one just below 'G4'

title: alto.ui.staff_input
text: StaffInput.place_caret def place_caret () -> None [Source] Place the note at the caret, as a click would. Examples >>> staff = StaffInput () >>> staff . reset ( "treble" ) >>> placed = [] >>> _ = staff . placed . connect ( placed . append ) >>> # the first press places the note at the start >>> staff . place_caret () >>> [ str ( n ) for n in placed ] ['B4']

title: alto.ui.staff_input
text: StaffInput.show_note def show_note ( note : Note | None , * , color : QColor | None = None , ) -> None [Source] Draw a single note on the staff, or clear it. Parameters note ( Note or None ): The note to draw; None clears the staff. color ( QColor or None, default None ): The color to draw it in; the notation’s own ink if None. Keyword-only. Examples >>> staff = StaffInput () >>> staff . show_note ( Note . parse ( "C4" )) >>> len ( staff . columns ) 1 >>> staff . show_note ( None ) >>> staff . columns []

title: alto.ui.staff_input
text: StaffInput.refresh_preview def refresh_preview () -> None [Source] Redraw the note that would be placed, for example after the accidental changes. It is the pointer’s note while the pointer is over the staff, and otherwise the note at the caret, once the keyboard has put the caret somewhere. Examples >>> staff = StaffInput () >>> # the pointer is not over the staff, and there is no caret: >>> # nothing to redraw >>> staff . refresh_preview () >>> staff . columns [] >>> staff . reset ( "treble" ) >>> staff . move_cursor ( 0 ) >>> len ( staff . columns ) # the note at the caret 1

title: alto.ui.staff_input
text: StaffInput.mouseMoveEvent def mouseMoveEvent ( event : QMouseEvent ) -> None [Source] Show the note under the pointer, in a lighter color. Parameters event ( QMouseEvent ): The mouse move. Examples >>> staff = StaffInput () >>> staff . reset ( "treble" ) >>> staff . resize ( 400 , 300 ) >>> from PySide6.QtCore import QPointF >>> point = QPointF ( ... 50 , staff . staff_bottoms ()[ "treble" ] ... ) >>> staff . mouseMoveEvent ( ... QMouseEvent ( ... QEvent . Type . MouseMove , ... point , ... point , ... Qt . MouseButton . NoButton , ... Qt . MouseButton . NoButton , ... Qt . KeyboardModifier . NoModifier , ... ) ... ) >>> str ( staff . columns [ 0 ][ 0 ]) 'E4'

title: alto.ui.staff_input
text: StaffInput.leaveEvent def leaveEvent ( event : QEvent ) -> None [Source] Remove the pointer’s note when the pointer leaves the staff, showing the note at the caret instead if there is one. Parameters event ( QEvent ): The leave event. Examples >>> staff = StaffInput () >>> staff . show_note ( Note . parse ( "C4" )) >>> staff . leaveEvent ( QEvent ( QEvent . Type . Leave )) >>> staff . columns []

title: alto.ui.staff_input
text: StaffInput.mousePressEvent def mousePressEvent ( event : QMouseEvent ) -> None [Source] Place the note on a left click, or step through the accidentals on a right click. Parameters event ( QMouseEvent ): The mouse press. Nothing happens while the staff is locked. Examples >>> staff = StaffInput () >>> staff . reset ( "treble" ) >>> staff . resize ( 400 , 300 ) >>> placed = [] >>> _ = staff . placed . connect ( placed . append ) >>> from PySide6.QtCore import QPointF >>> point = QPointF ( ... 50 , staff . staff_bottoms ()[ "treble" ] ... ) >>> staff . mousePressEvent ( ... QMouseEvent ( ... QEvent . Type . MouseButtonPress , ... point , ... point , ... Qt . MouseButton . LeftButton , ... Qt . MouseButton . LeftButton , ... Qt . KeyboardModifier . NoModifier , ... ) ... ) >>> [ str ( n ) for n in placed ] ['E4']

title: alto.ui.staff_input
text: ScaleInput ScaleInput ( parent : QWidget | None = None ) [Source] Bases: StaffInput A staff you click to place the notes of a scale one after another, left to right, and then, if asked, its steps. The next note follows the pointer, snapped to a line or space, in the place it will take. Each click puts it there and moves on to the next place. The places are all drawn from the start, so the notes do not move as more are placed. When steps are asked for, once all the notes are placed two lines rise from each pair of neighboring notes to a point above them (a wedge). The step to be marked next is shown there, in the preview color, as “W” (whole) or “H” (half). The mouse wheel or a right click changes it, and a left click marks it and moves on to the next pair. Attributes notes_changed ( Signal ): Emitted when a note or a step is placed or taken back. step_selected ( Signal ): Emitted with “W” or “H” when the step to be marked next changes. accidental_stepped ( Signal ): Emitted with 1 or -1 for each notch of the mouse wheel while notes are placed: the owner moves on to the next sign (1) or back to the one before (-1). notes ( list of Note ): The notes placed so far, left to right. steps ( list of str ): The steps marked so far, each “W” or “H”. slots ( int ): How many notes the scale has. with_steps ( bool ): Whether the steps are asked for too. pending_step ( str ): The step that a left click would mark next, “W” or “H”. Examples >>> from PySide6.QtCore import QPointF >>> staff = ScaleInput () >>> staff . reset_scale ( "treble" , slots = 8 ) >>> staff . resize ( 600 , 300 ) >>> point = QPointF ( ... 50 , staff . staff_bottoms ()[ "treble" ] ... ) >>> staff . mousePressEvent ( ... QMouseEvent ( ... QEvent . Type . MouseButtonPress , ... point , ... point , ... Qt . MouseButton . LeftButton , ... Qt . MouseButton . LeftButton , ... Qt . KeyboardModifier . NoModifier , ... ) ... ) >>> ( ... [ str ( n ) for n in staff . notes ], ... len ( staff . columns ), ... ) (['E4'], 8) Constructor Create the staff. Parameters parent ( QWidget or None, default None ): The widget that owns the staff. Constructor examples >>> ScaleInput (). notes []

title: alto.ui.staff_input
text: ScaleInput.reset_scale def reset_scale ( clef : str , * , slots : int , caption : str = '' , with_steps : bool = False , key : int = 0 , ) -> None [Source] Clear the staff for a new scale: a staff with room for its notes, and the key signature it is to have. Parameters clef ( str ): The clef to draw. slots ( int ): How many notes the scale has. Keyword-only. caption ( str, default ““ ): The name of the scale, written under the staff. Keyword-only. with_steps ( bool, default False ): Also ask for the steps between the notes. Keyword-only. key ( int, default 0 ): The key signature drawn on the staff: that many sharps if positive, flats if negative. It is the staff’s, not the scale’s: a note placed without a sign takes the sign the signature gives its letter. Keyword-only. Examples >>> staff = ScaleInput () >>> staff . notes , staff . slots = ( ... [ Note . parse ( "C4" )], ... 3 , ... ) >>> staff . reset_scale ( ... "bass" , slots = 8 , caption = "D Major" ... ) >>> ( ... staff . notes , ... staff . slots , ... staff . caption , ... staff . key , ... ) ([], 8, 'D Major', 0) >>> staff . reset_scale ( "bass" , slots = 8 , key =- 2 ) >>> staff . key -2

title: alto.ui.staff_input
text: ScaleInput.complete @ property def complete () -> bool [Source] Report whether every note of the scale has been placed. Returns bool : True when there are as many notes as places. Examples >>> staff = ScaleInput () >>> staff . reset_scale ( "treble" , slots = 1 ) >>> staff . complete False >>> staff . notes . append ( Note . parse ( "C4" )) >>> staff . complete True

title: alto.ui.staff_input
text: ScaleInput.placing_steps @ property def placing_steps () -> bool [Source] Report whether it is the turn of the steps: they are asked for, every note is placed and some step is still to mark. Returns bool : True while the next click marks a step. Examples >>> staff = ScaleInput () >>> staff . reset_scale ( ... "treble" , slots = 2 , with_steps = True ... ) >>> staff . notes . extend ( ... [ Note . parse ( "C4" ), Note . parse ( "D4" )] ... ) >>> staff . placing_steps True >>> staff . steps . append ( "W" ) >>> staff . placing_steps False

title: alto.ui.staff_input
text: ScaleInput.done @ property def done () -> bool [Source] Report whether everything asked for is placed: every note and, if they are asked for, every step. Returns bool : True when the scale can be handed in. Examples >>> staff = ScaleInput () >>> staff . reset_scale ( ... "treble" , slots = 2 , with_steps = True ... ) >>> staff . notes . extend ( ... [ Note . parse ( "C4" ), Note . parse ( "D4" )] ... ) >>> staff . done False >>> staff . steps . append ( "W" ) >>> staff . done True

title: alto.ui.staff_input
text: ScaleInput.show_note def show_note ( note : Note | None , * , color : QColor | None = None , ) -> None [Source] Show the pointer’s note in the next place, or take it away. Parameters note ( Note or None ): The note to show; None shows none. color ( QColor or None, default None ): Unused: the note under the pointer is always drawn in the preview color. Keyword-only. Examples >>> staff = ScaleInput () >>> staff . reset_scale ( "treble" , slots = 4 ) >>> staff . show_note ( Note . parse ( "G4" )) >>> staff . columns [ 0 ], staff . notes ([Note(octave=4, letter=4, accidental=0)], [])

title: alto.ui.staff_input
text: ScaleInput.set_pending_step def set_pending_step ( step : str ) -> None [Source] Choose the step that the next click marks. Parameters step ( str ): “W” for a whole step or “H” for a half step. Examples >>> staff = ScaleInput () >>> staff . reset_scale ( ... "treble" , slots = 3 , with_steps = True ... ) >>> chosen = [] >>> _ = staff . step_selected . connect ( ... chosen . append ... ) >>> staff . set_pending_step ( "H" ) >>> staff . pending_step , chosen ('H', ['H'])

title: alto.ui.staff_input
text: ScaleInput.toggle_step def toggle_step () -> None [Source] Switch the step that the next click marks between whole and half. Examples >>> staff = ScaleInput () >>> staff . reset_scale ( ... "treble" , slots = 3 , with_steps = True ... ) >>> staff . toggle_step () >>> staff . pending_step 'H' >>> staff . toggle_step () >>> staff . pending_step 'W'

title: alto.ui.staff_input
text: ScaleInput.undo def undo () -> None [Source] Take back the last thing placed: the last step if there is one, otherwise the last note. Examples >>> staff = ScaleInput () >>> staff . reset_scale ( "treble" , slots = 4 ) >>> staff . notes . append ( Note . parse ( "C4" )) >>> staff . undo () >>> staff . notes []

title: alto.ui.staff_input
text: ScaleInput.wheelEvent def wheelEvent ( event : QWheelEvent ) -> None [Source] Use the mouse wheel for what comes next: the sign of the note to place, or the step to mark. While notes are placed each notch asks the owner to move on to the next sign (up) or back to the one before (down). While steps are marked each notch switches between whole and half. Once everything is placed it does nothing. Parameters event ( QWheelEvent ): The wheel turn. Examples >>> from PySide6.QtCore import QPoint , QPointF >>> staff = ScaleInput () >>> staff . reset_scale ( ... "treble" , slots = 2 , with_steps = True ... ) >>> signs = [] >>> _ = staff . accidental_stepped . connect ( ... signs . append ... ) >>> here = QPointF ( 50 , 50 ) >>> turn = QWheelEvent ( ... here , ... here , ... QPoint ( 0 , 0 ), ... QPoint ( 0 , 120 ), ... Qt . MouseButton . NoButton , ... Qt . KeyboardModifier . NoModifier , ... Qt . ScrollPhase . NoScrollPhase , ... False , ... ) >>> staff . wheelEvent ( turn ) >>> signs , staff . pending_step ([1], 'W') >>> staff . notes . extend ( ... [ Note . parse ( "C4" ), Note . parse ( "D4" )] ... ) >>> staff . wheelEvent ( turn ) >>> signs , staff . pending_step ([1], 'H')

title: alto.ui.staff_input
text: ScaleInput.caret_start def caret_start () -> int [Source] Return the staff step the caret starts from: that of the last note placed, or the middle line. Returns int : Where the keyboard’s first move begins. Examples >>> staff = ScaleInput () >>> staff . reset_scale ( "treble" , slots = 8 ) >>> str ( ... Note . from_diatonic ( staff . caret_start ()) ... ) # the middle line 'B4' >>> staff . notes . append ( Note . parse ( "D4" )) >>> str ( ... Note . from_diatonic ( staff . caret_start ()) ... ) # the note before 'D4'

title: alto.ui.staff_input
text: ScaleInput.place_next def place_next ( note : Note | None = None ) -> None [Source] Place the next note, or mark the next step once the notes are placed. Parameters note ( Note or None, default None ): The note to place; the note at the caret if None. Ignored while steps are marked. Examples >>> staff = ScaleInput () >>> staff . reset_scale ( ... "treble" , slots = 2 , with_steps = True ... ) >>> staff . place_next ( Note . parse ( "C4" )) >>> staff . place_next ( Note . parse ( "D4" )) >>> # the notes are placed: this marks the first step >>> staff . place_next () >>> [ str ( n ) for n in staff . notes ], staff . steps (['C4', 'D4'], ['W'])

title: alto.ui.staff_input
text: ScaleInput.place_caret def place_caret () -> None [Source] Place the next note at the caret, or mark the next step, as a click would. Examples >>> staff = ScaleInput () >>> staff . reset_scale ( "treble" , slots = 2 ) >>> staff . move_cursor ( 2 ) >>> staff . place_caret () >>> [ str ( n ) for n in staff . notes ] ['D5']

title: alto.ui.staff_input
text: ScaleInput.mousePressEvent def mousePressEvent ( event : QMouseEvent ) -> None [Source] Place the next note or mark the next step on a left click; change the sign or the step on a right click. Parameters event ( QMouseEvent ): The mouse press. Nothing happens while the staff is locked or when everything is placed. Examples >>> from PySide6.QtCore import QPointF >>> staff = ScaleInput () >>> staff . reset_scale ( "treble" , slots = 1 ) >>> staff . resize ( 600 , 300 ) >>> point = QPointF ( ... 50 , staff . staff_bottoms ()[ "treble" ] ... ) >>> press = QMouseEvent ( ... QEvent . Type . MouseButtonPress , ... point , ... point , ... Qt . MouseButton . LeftButton , ... Qt . MouseButton . LeftButton , ... Qt . KeyboardModifier . NoModifier , ... ) >>> staff . mousePressEvent ( press ) >>> staff . mousePressEvent ( ... press ... ) # every place is taken >>> [ str ( n ) for n in staff . notes ] ['E4']

title: alto.ui.staff_input
text: SignatureInput class SignatureInput ( ScaleInput ) [Source] Place accidentals in consecutive key-signature slots immediately after the clef. Examples >>> staff = SignatureInput () >>> staff . reset_scale ( ... "treble" , slots = 7 , caption = "D major" ... ) >>> staff . place_next ( Note . parse ( "F#5" )) >>> staff . notes , staff . columns ([Note(octave=5, letter=3, accidental=1)], [])

title: alto.ui.staff_input
text: SignatureInput.reset_signature def reset_signature ( clef : str , * , key : int , caption : str , starting_slots : list [ int ], ) -> None [Source] Set the fixed signs for this question and clear the learner’s entries. Parameters clef ( str ): Clef used to read the positions. key ( int ): Target signature. caption ( str ): Name of the key under the staff. starting_slots ( list of int ): Positions to fill before the learner begins. Examples >>> staff = SignatureInput () >>> staff . reset_signature ( ... "treble" , ... key = 2 , ... caption = "D major" , ... starting_slots = [ 1 ], ... ) >>> len ( staff . template ), staff . template [ 1 ] (7, Note(octave=5, letter=0, accidental=1))

title: alto.ui.staff_input
text: SignatureInput.entered_signature def entered_signature () -> list [ Note | None ] [Source] Combine the fixed signs and the learner’s entries in staff order. Returns list of Note or None : One pitch per occupied slot, with None in each remaining gap. Examples >>> staff = SignatureInput () >>> staff . reset_signature ( ... "treble" , ... key = 2 , ... caption = "D major" , ... starting_slots = [ 1 ], ... ) >>> staff . place_next ( Note . parse ( "F#5" )) >>> [ ... str ( n ) ... for n in staff . entered_signature () ... if n is not None ... ] ['F♯5', 'C♯5']

title: alto.ui.staff_input
text: SignatureInput.paintEvent def paintEvent ( event : QPaintEvent ) -> None [Source] Draw the blank staff and caption, then the placed signs and the next sign under the pointer. Parameters event ( QPaintEvent ): The paint request. Examples >>> staff = SignatureInput () >>> staff . reset_scale ( "bass" , slots = 7 ) >>> staff . place_next ( Note . parse ( "Bb2" )) >>> staff . grab (). isNull () False

title: alto.ui.staff_input
text: ClefInput ClefInput ( parent : QWidget | None = None ) [Source] Bases: StaffWidget A blank staff on which you put a clef symbol: choose the G, C or F clef, then click where it goes. The symbol can go on any line or space of the staff and on the three ledger lines and spaces above and below it, and follows the pointer from place to place, in a lighter color, until you click. Without the mouse, move_caret moves it, step_symbol switches the symbol and place_caret places it. Attributes placed ( Signal ): Emitted with the symbol (“G”, “C” or “F”) and its place when you click: 0 is the bottom line, 1 the space above it, up to 8 for the top line, with -6 to 14 allowed. changed ( Signal ): Emitted when the symbol chosen or the place the keyboard would use changes. options ( list of str ): The symbols that can be chosen, in the order the wheel goes through them. selected ( str ): The symbol chosen now. locked ( bool ): Ignore the mouse and the wheel (while feedback is showing). caret ( int or None ): The place the keyboard would put the symbol; None until the keyboard has moved it. placed_symbol ( str or None ): The symbol that has been placed and is drawn solid, with placed_step its place; None until one is. Examples >>> staff = ClefInput () >>> staff . reset ([ "G" , "F" ]) >>> staff . step_symbol ( 1 ) >>> staff . selected 'F' Constructor Create the staff. Parameters parent ( QWidget or None, default None ): The widget that owns the staff. Constructor examples >>> ClefInput (). hasMouseTracking () True

title: alto.ui.staff_input
text: ClefInput.reset def reset ( options : list [ str ], * , caption : str = '' , ) -> None [Source] Clear the staff for a new question and offer some symbols to choose from. Parameters options ( list of str ): The symbols the wheel goes through, any of “G”, “C” and “F”; the first is chosen to begin with. caption ( str, default ““ ): The question, written under the staff. Keyword-only. Examples >>> staff = ClefInput () >>> staff . reset ( ... [ "C" , "F" ], ... caption = "Place the alto clef." , ... ) >>> ( ... staff . selected , ... staff . placed_symbol , ... staff . caption , ... ) ('C', None, 'Place the alto clef.')

title: alto.ui.staff_input
text: ClefInput.select def select ( symbol : str ) -> None [Source] Choose a symbol. Parameters symbol ( str ): “G”, “C” or “F”; one that is not among the options is ignored. Examples >>> staff = ClefInput () >>> staff . reset ([ "G" , "C" , "F" ]) >>> staff . select ( "F" ) >>> staff . selected 'F'

title: alto.ui.staff_input
text: ClefInput.step_symbol def step_symbol ( direction : int ) -> None [Source] Choose the next symbol of the options, or the one before, going around. Parameters direction ( int ): 1 for the next, -1 for the one before. Examples >>> staff = ClefInput () >>> staff . reset ([ "G" , "C" , "F" ]) >>> staff . step_symbol ( - 1 ) >>> staff . selected 'F'

title: alto.ui.staff_input
text: ClefInput.step_at def step_at ( y : float ) -> int [Source] Return the line or space nearest to a height in the widget. Parameters y ( float ): The height, in pixels. Returns int : The place, 0 for the bottom line and 1 for the space above it, up to 8 for the top line; from the first ledger line below the staff (-6) to the third above it (14). Examples >>> staff = ClefInput () >>> staff . reset ([ "G" ]) >>> staff . resize ( 400 , 300 ) >>> floor = staff . staff_bottoms ()[ "treble" ] >>> ( ... staff . step_at ( floor ), ... staff . step_at ( floor - 1.4 * staff . GAP ), ... staff . step_at ( 0 ), ... staff . step_at ( 10_000 ), ... ) (0, 3, 14, -6)

title: alto.ui.staff_input
text: ClefInput.move_caret def move_caret ( steps : int ) -> None [Source] Move the place the keyboard would put the symbol. Parameters steps ( int ): How many lines and spaces up (positive) or down, stopping at the last ledger lines; the first move starts from the middle line. Examples >>> staff = ClefInput () >>> staff . reset ([ "G" ]) >>> staff . move_caret ( 1 ) >>> staff . caret 5 >>> staff . move_caret ( 20 ) >>> staff . caret 14

title: alto.ui.staff_input
text: ClefInput.place def place ( step : int ) -> None [Source] Put the chosen symbol in a place, drawn solid, and say so. Parameters step ( int ): The place, 0 for the bottom line, 1 for the space above it and so on. Examples >>> staff = ClefInput () >>> staff . reset ([ "F" ]) >>> got = [] >>> _ = staff . placed . connect ( ... lambda symbol , where : got . append ( ... ( symbol , where ) ... ) ... ) >>> staff . place ( 6 ) >>> got , staff . placed_symbol , staff . placed_step ([('F', 6)], 'F', 6)

title: alto.ui.staff_input
text: ClefInput.place_caret def place_caret () -> None [Source] Place the symbol where the keyboard put it, or on the middle line if it has not moved. Examples >>> staff = ClefInput () >>> staff . reset ([ "G" ]) >>> staff . move_caret ( - 2 ) >>> staff . place_caret () >>> staff . placed_step 2

title: alto.ui.staff_input
text: ClefInput.clear_placed def clear_placed () -> None [Source] Take the placed symbol off the staff, so another can be tried. Examples >>> staff = ClefInput () >>> staff . place ( 1 ) >>> staff . clear_placed () >>> staff . placed_symbol is None True

title: alto.ui.staff_input
text: ClefInput.set_clef_color def set_clef_color ( color : QColor | None ) -> None [Source] Draw the placed symbol in a color, for feedback, or back in black. Parameters color ( QColor or None ): The color; None for black. Examples >>> staff = ClefInput () >>> staff . set_clef_color ( QColor ( "#2e7d32" )) >>> staff . clef_color == QColor ( "#2e7d32" ) True

title: alto.ui.staff_input
text: ClefInput.mouseMoveEvent def mouseMoveEvent ( event : QMouseEvent ) -> None [Source] Show the symbol in the place under the pointer, in a lighter color. Parameters event ( QMouseEvent ): The mouse move. Examples >>> staff = ClefInput () >>> staff . reset ([ "G" ]) >>> staff . resize ( 400 , 300 ) >>> from PySide6.QtCore import QPointF >>> point = QPointF ( ... 50 , ... staff . staff_bottoms ()[ "treble" ] ... - 2 * staff . GAP , ... ) >>> staff . mouseMoveEvent ( ... QMouseEvent ( ... QEvent . Type . MouseMove , ... point , ... point , ... Qt . MouseButton . NoButton , ... Qt . MouseButton . NoButton , ... Qt . KeyboardModifier . NoModifier , ... ) ... ) >>> staff . _hover 4

title: alto.ui.staff_input
text: ClefInput.leaveEvent def leaveEvent ( event : QEvent ) -> None [Source] Stop following the pointer when it leaves the staff. Parameters event ( QEvent ): The leave event. Examples >>> staff = ClefInput () >>> staff . _hover = 2 >>> staff . leaveEvent ( QEvent ( QEvent . Type . Leave )) >>> staff . _hover is None True

title: alto.ui.staff_input
text: ClefInput.mousePressEvent def mousePressEvent ( event : QMouseEvent ) -> None [Source] Place the symbol on a left click, or choose the next symbol on a right click. Parameters event ( QMouseEvent ): The mouse press. Nothing happens while the staff is locked. Examples >>> staff = ClefInput () >>> staff . reset ([ "G" , "F" ]) >>> staff . resize ( 400 , 300 ) >>> from PySide6.QtCore import QPointF >>> point = QPointF ( ... 50 , staff . staff_bottoms ()[ "treble" ] ... ) >>> staff . mousePressEvent ( ... QMouseEvent ( ... QEvent . Type . MouseButtonPress , ... point , ... point , ... Qt . MouseButton . RightButton , ... Qt . MouseButton . RightButton , ... Qt . KeyboardModifier . NoModifier , ... ) ... ) >>> staff . selected 'F'

title: alto.ui.staff_input
text: ClefInput.wheelEvent def wheelEvent ( event : QWheelEvent ) -> None [Source] Choose the next symbol for each notch of the wheel turned up, and the one before for each turned down. Parameters event ( QWheelEvent ): The wheel turn. Examples >>> from PySide6.QtCore import QPoint , QPointF >>> staff = ClefInput () >>> staff . reset ([ "G" , "F" ]) >>> here = QPointF ( 50 , 50 ) >>> staff . wheelEvent ( ... QWheelEvent ( ... here , ... here , ... QPoint ( 0 , 0 ), ... QPoint ( 0 , 120 ), ... Qt . MouseButton . NoButton , ... Qt . KeyboardModifier . NoModifier , ... Qt . ScrollPhase . NoScrollPhase , ... False , ... ) ... ) >>> staff . selected 'F'

title: alto.ui.staff_input
text: ClefInput.paintEvent def paintEvent ( _ : QPaintEvent ) -> None [Source] Draw the staff, then the symbol that was placed or, until one is, the one that would be placed. A symbol on a ledger line has the ledger lines it needs drawn behind it. Parameters _ ( QPaintEvent ): The paint request; the whole widget is always redrawn. Examples >>> staff = ClefInput () >>> staff . reset ([ "G" ]) >>> staff . place ( 1 ) >>> staff . grab (). isNull () False

title: alto.ui.staff_playback
text: alto.ui.staff_playback Connect a displayed music sample to the notes sounding on its staff.

title: alto.ui.staff_playback
text: StaffPlayback StaffPlayback ( parent : QWidget , * , highlight : Callable [[ int | None ], object ] | None = None , ) [Source] Bases: QObject Follow a sample’s audio onsets and end playback when its view closes. Constructor Attach playback to its view. Parameters parent ( QWidget ): The view containing the sample. highlight ( callable or None ): Draw the current step on the displayed staff or staves. Omit for audio-only playback.

title: alto.ui.staff_playback
text: StaffPlayback.play def play ( columns : Sequence [ Sequence [ Note ]], * , gap_ms : int = DEFAULT_NOTE_GAP_MS , force : bool = False , warmup : bool = False , instrument : str | None = None , ) -> None [Source] Play the displayed notes in order. Parameters columns ( sequence of sequence of Note ): Notes grouped by onset. gap_ms ( int ): Time between onsets in milliseconds. force ( bool ): Allow explicit auditions even when exercise sounds are muted. instrument ( str or None ): Sound registered by the active pack, or the learner’s default. warmup ( bool ): Prepare the audio streams before the first note.

title: alto.ui.staff_playback
text: StaffPlayback.play_rhythm def play_rhythm ( values : Sequence [ str ]) -> None [Source] Click at each note onset and leave rests silent. Parameters values ( sequence of str ): Written note and rest values. A quarter note gets one beat.
