title: alto.ui.stats_dialog
text: alto.ui.stats_dialog The statistics screen: a few numbers and charts about how practice is going. It shows the active profile’s own answers, filterable by exercise and by timeframe. Examples >>> since_for ( ... None , now = 1000.0 ... ) is None # all time: from the start True >>> format_duration ( 3600 ) '1 h 00 min'

title: alto.ui.stats_dialog
text: since_for def since_for ( span : str | int | None , * , now : float , ) -> float | None [Source] Return the timestamp a timeframe starts from. Parameters span ( str or int or None ): “today”, a number of days back, or None for all time. now ( float ): The current time as a timestamp. Keyword-only. Returns float or None : Midnight for “today”, now less that many days for a number, and None for all time. Examples >>> since_for ( 7 , now = 864000.0 ) 259200.0 >>> since_for ( None , now = 864000.0 ) is None True >>> 0 <= 864000.0 - since_for ( ... "today" , now = 864000.0 ... ) < 90000 # within a day of now True

title: alto.ui.stats_dialog
text: format_duration def format_duration ( seconds : float ) -> str [Source] Write a length of time the way the statistics show it. Parameters seconds ( float ): The time in seconds. Returns str : Seconds under half a minute, then minutes, then hours and minutes. Examples >>> ( ... format_duration ( 5 ), ... format_duration ( 90 ), ... format_duration ( 3000 ), ... ) ('5 s', '2 min', '50 min') >>> format_duration ( 3 * 3600 + 7 * 60 ) '3 h 07 min'

title: alto.ui.stats_dialog
text: period_title def period_title ( start : datetime , * , granularity : str , ) -> str [Source] Name a chart period in words, for the heading of its list of answers. Parameters start ( datetime ): The start of the period. granularity ( str ): “hour”, “day”, “week” or “month”, as Stats.granularity says. Keyword-only. Returns str : For example “Mon 5 Jan 2026”, “Week of Mon 5 Jan 2026” or “January 2026”. Examples >>> period_title ( ... datetime ( 2026 , 1 , 5 , 14 ), ... granularity = "hour" , ... ) 'Mon 5 Jan 2026, 14:00' >>> period_title ( ... datetime ( 2026 , 1 , 5 ), granularity = "day" ... ) 'Mon 5 Jan 2026' >>> period_title ( ... datetime ( 2026 , 1 , 5 ), granularity = "week" ... ) 'Week of Mon 5 Jan 2026' >>> period_title ( ... datetime ( 2026 , 1 , 1 ), ... granularity = "month" , ... ) 'January 2026'

title: alto.ui.stats_dialog
text: Tile Tile ( caption : str , * , parent : QWidget | None = None , ) [Source] Bases: QFrame One headline number with its caption. Attributes value ( QLabel ): The big number. caption ( QLabel ): What the number is. Examples >>> tile = Tile ( "Questions answered" ) >>> tile . value . text () '–' >>> tile . show_value ( "12" ) >>> tile . value . text () '12' Constructor Create a tile showing a dash until it is given a value. Parameters caption ( str ): What the number is, shown under it. parent ( QWidget or None, default None ): The widget that owns the tile. Keyword-only. Constructor examples >>> tile = Tile ( "Days practiced" ) >>> tile . caption . text () 'Days practiced'

title: alto.ui.stats_dialog
text: Tile.show_value def show_value ( text : str ) -> None [Source] Show a number (or any text) in the tile. Parameters text ( str ): What to show. Examples >>> tile = Tile ( "Typical first answer" ) >>> tile . show_value ( "7.6 s" ) >>> tile . value . text () '7.6 s'

title: alto.ui.stats_dialog
text: StatsPage StatsPage ( learner : Learner , * , parent : QWidget | None = None , ) [Source] Bases: QWidget The statistics, as a page of the main window. Attributes back ( Signal ): Emitted by Escape; the main window provides the shared Back button. learner ( Learner ): Whose answers are shown; only the active profile’s own. exercise ( FieldComboBox ): The exercise filter. timeframe ( FieldComboBox ): The timeframe filter. tiles ( dict of str to Tile ): The headline numbers, by name. detail ( QFrame ): The panel under the charts that lists the answers behind a clicked bar, point, row or day. Hidden until one is clicked. answers ( AnswerList ): The table in the detail panel. Examples >>> from alto.learning import Database >>> db = Database () >>> page = StatsPage ( ... Learner ( ... db , profile = db . add_profile ( "Ada" ) ... ) ... ) >>> page . note . text (). startswith ( ... "No answers recorded for Ada" ... ) True Constructor Build the page and fill it for the current filters. Parameters learner ( Learner ): Whose statistics to show. parent ( QWidget or None, default None ): The widget that owns the page. Keyword-only. Constructor examples >>> from alto.learning import Database >>> db = Database () >>> page = StatsPage ( ... Learner ( ... db , profile = db . add_profile ( "Ada" ) ... ) ... ) >>> # the last 30 days, until another is chosen >>> page . timeframe . currentText () 'Last 30 days'

title: alto.ui.stats_dialog
text: StatsPage.refresh def refresh () -> None [Source] Recalculate everything for the chosen exercise and timeframe and show it. Examples >>> from alto.learning import Database >>> db = Database () >>> page = StatsPage ( ... Learner ( ... db , profile = db . add_profile ( "Ada" ) ... ) ... ) >>> page . refresh () >>> page . tiles [ ... "questions" ... ]. value . text () # nothing answered yet '0'

title: alto.ui.store
text: alto.ui.store The application’s saved settings (a thin layer over QSettings ). Examples >>> settings = store () >>> settings . setValue ( "demo/count" , 3 ) >>> int_value ( ... settings , key = "demo/count" , default = 0 ... ) 3 >>> settings . remove ( "demo" )

title: alto.ui.store
text: store def store () -> QSettings [Source] Return the app’s saved settings. The first time it is opened under the name “alto” it brings across anything saved under the old name (“mtheory”), so a rename does not reset anyone’s preferences. If ALTO_HOME is set the settings are kept in a file in that folder instead, and nothing is brought across from the system’s own. Returns QSettings : The settings, kept in the user’s configuration folder or in ALTO_HOME . Examples >>> settings = store () >>> settings . setValue ( "demo/name" , "Ada" ) >>> str ( store (). value ( "demo/name" )) 'Ada' >>> settings . remove ( "demo" )

title: alto.ui.store
text: int_value def int_value ( settings : QSettings , * , key : str , default : int , ) -> int [Source] Read an integer setting. QSettings hands back whatever was saved, which may be a number or its text. Parameters settings ( QSettings ): The settings to read. key ( str ): The setting’s name. Keyword-only. default ( int ): What to return if nothing is saved. Keyword-only. Returns int : The saved value, or default if there is none (or it is not a number, text or similar). Raises ValueError : If the saved text is not a whole number. Examples >>> settings_ = store () >>> settings_ . setValue ( "demo/count" , "42" ) >>> int_value ( ... settings_ , key = "demo/count" , default = 0 ... ) 42 >>> int_value ( ... settings_ , key = "demo/missing" , default = 7 ... ) 7 >>> settings_ . setValue ( "demo/count" , "many" ) >>> int_value ( ... settings_ , key = "demo/count" , default = 0 ... ) Traceback (most recent call last): ... ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'many' >>> settings_ . remove ( "demo" )

title: alto.ui.store
text: text_value def text_value ( settings : QSettings , * , key : str , default : str , ) -> str [Source] Read a saved setting as text. Parameters settings ( QSettings ): The settings to read. key ( str ): The setting’s name. Keyword-only. default ( str ): What to return if nothing is saved. Keyword-only. Returns str : The saved text, or default if there is none (or it is not text). Examples >>> settings_ = store () >>> settings_ . setValue ( "demo/name" , "viola" ) >>> text_value ( ... settings_ , ... key = "demo/name" , ... default = "piano" , ... ) 'viola' >>> text_value ( ... settings_ , ... key = "demo/missing" , ... default = "piano" , ... ) 'piano' >>> settings_ . remove ( "demo" )

title: alto.ui.store
text: bool_value def bool_value ( settings : QSettings , * , key : str , default : bool , ) -> bool [Source] Read a switch saved as the text “true” or “false”. Parameters settings ( QSettings ): The settings to read. key ( str ): The setting’s name. Keyword-only. default ( bool ): What to return if nothing is saved, or if the saved text is neither “true” nor “false”. Keyword-only. Returns bool : The saved switch. Examples >>> settings_ = store () >>> save_bool ( ... settings_ , key = "demo/on" , value = True ... ) >>> ( ... bool_value ( ... settings_ , ... key = "demo/on" , ... default = False , ... ), ... bool_value ( ... settings_ , ... key = "demo/missing" , ... default = True , ... ), ... ) (True, True) >>> settings_ . setValue ( "demo/on" , "FALSE" ) >>> bool_value ( ... settings_ , key = "demo/on" , default = True ... ) False >>> settings_ . remove ( "demo" )

title: alto.ui.store
text: save_bool def save_bool ( settings : QSettings , * , key : str , value : bool , ) -> None [Source] Save a switch as the text “true” or “false”, the form bool_value reads. Parameters settings ( QSettings ): The settings to write. key ( str ): The setting’s name. Keyword-only. value ( bool ): The switch. Keyword-only. Examples >>> settings_ = store () >>> save_bool ( ... settings_ , key = "demo/on" , value = False ... ) >>> settings_ . value ( "demo/on" ) 'false' >>> settings_ . remove ( "demo" )

title: alto.ui.store
text: list_value def list_value ( settings : QSettings , * , key : str , separator : str = ',' , ) -> list [ str ] [Source] Read a saved list of words, such as “treble,bass”. QSettings may hand back text that contains commas as a list of its parts, so both forms are read. Parameters settings ( QSettings ): The settings to read. key ( str ): The setting’s name. Keyword-only. separator ( str, default “,” ): What separates the words in the saved text. Keyword-only. Returns list of str : The words in their saved order, without empty ones; empty if nothing is saved. Examples >>> settings_ = store () >>> settings_ . setValue ( ... "demo/clefs" , "treble,,bass" ... ) >>> ( ... list_value ( settings_ , key = "demo/clefs" ), ... list_value ( ... settings_ , key = "demo/missing" ... ), ... ) (['treble', 'bass'], []) >>> settings_ . setValue ( ... "demo/modes" , [ "major|minor" ] ... ) >>> list_value ( ... settings_ , ... key = "demo/modes" , ... separator = "|" , ... ) ['major', 'minor'] >>> settings_ . remove ( "demo" )

title: alto.ui.store
text: choices_value def choices_value ( settings : QSettings , * , key : str , allowed : Iterable [ str ], separator : str = ',' , ) -> set [ str ] [Source] Read a saved set of choices, keeping only the ones that are still offered. Parameters settings ( QSettings ): The settings to read. key ( str ): The setting’s name. Keyword-only. allowed ( iterable of str ): The choices that exist now. Keyword-only. separator ( str, default “,” ): What separates the choices in the saved text. Keyword-only. Returns set of str : The saved choices that are allowed; empty if nothing is saved or none of them exists any more. Examples >>> settings_ = store () >>> settings_ . setValue ( ... "demo/clefs" , "treble,gone,bass" ... ) >>> sorted ( ... choices_value ( ... settings_ , ... key = "demo/clefs" , ... allowed = ( "treble" , "bass" , "alto" ), ... ) ... ) ['bass', 'treble'] >>> settings_ . remove ( "demo" )

title: alto.ui.store
text: keys_value def keys_value ( settings : QSettings , * , key : str , ) -> set [ int ] [Source] Read a saved set of key signatures, each a number of sharps (positive) or flats (negative) up to seven. Parameters settings ( QSettings ): The settings to read. key ( str ): The setting’s name. Keyword-only. Returns set of int : The saved key signatures that exist; empty if nothing usable is saved. Examples >>> settings_ = store () >>> settings_ . setValue ( ... "demo/keys" , "-2,0,9,x,3" ... ) >>> sorted ( ... keys_value ( settings_ , key = "demo/keys" ) ... ) [-2, 0, 3] >>> settings_ . remove ( "demo" )

title: alto.ui.store
text: joined def joined ( values : Iterable [ object ], * , separator : str = ',' , ) -> str [Source] Write values as the text that list_value , choices_value and keys_value read back. Parameters values ( iterable of object ): The values, in the order to save them. separator ( str, default “,” ): What to put between them. Keyword-only. Returns str : The values as text, joined by the separator. Examples >>> ( ... joined ([ - 1 , 0 , 2 ]), ... joined ( ... [ "major" , "minor" ], separator = "|" ... ), ... ) ('-1,0,2', 'major|minor')

title: alto.ui.store
text: export_settings def export_settings () -> dict [ str , object ] [Source] Return every saved preference, by key, for a backup. Returns dict of str to object : Each key Alto has saved and its value. Qt byte arrays come back as bytes and lists as lists. Examples >>> settings_ = store () >>> settings_ . setValue ( "demo/name" , "Ada" ) >>> export_settings ()[ "demo/name" ] 'Ada' >>> settings_ . remove ( "demo" )

title: alto.ui.store
text: import_settings def import_settings ( values : Mapping [ str , object ]) -> None [Source] Replace every saved preference with the ones from a backup, so the preferences are exactly as they were. Preferences saved now that the backup does not have are removed. The marker that stops old “mtheory” preferences being brought across again is kept, so an old installation’s leftovers cannot leak back in. Parameters values ( mapping of str to object ): The preferences, by key, as export_settings returned them. Examples >>> import_settings ( ... { "demo/name" : "Ada" , "demo/count" : 3 } ... ) >>> ( ... store (). value ( "demo/name" ), ... int_value ( ... store (), key = "demo/count" , default = 0 ... ), ... ) ('Ada', 3) >>> store (). remove ( "demo" ) >>> store (). remove ( "" )

title: alto.ui.style
text: alto.ui.style Application-wide stylesheet: rounded corners on buttons, panes, lists and scroll bars. Colors come from the palette so it follows the system light/dark theme. Examples >>> RADIUS 10

title: alto.ui.style
text: navigation_heading_style def navigation_heading_style ( palette : QPalette ) -> tuple [ QFont , QColor ] [Source] Style category headings in the navigation pane and tile filters. Parameters palette ( QPalette ): The pane’s current palette. Returns tuple of QFont and QColor : The small, spaced capitals and muted foreground used for section headings. Examples >>> navigation_heading_style ( QPalette ())[ ... 0 ... ]. bold () True

title: alto.ui.style
text: app_style def app_style ( palette : QPalette , * , paper_palette : QPalette | None = None , ) -> str [Source] Build the stylesheet for a palette. Push buttons use rounded hairline borders. In dark mode, exercise tiles have near-black outlines and other standard buttons have graphite-gray outlines. Parameters palette ( QPalette ): The palette to take colors from, so the style follows the light or dark theme. paper_palette ( QPalette or None, default None ): The theme’s light variant for playback on white staff paper. Dark desktop themes use Qt light colors with the desktop accent when no light variant is supplied. Returns str : Qt style sheet text. Examples >>> from PySide6.QtWidgets import QApplication >>> sheet = app_style ( QApplication . palette ()) >>> "QPushButton" in sheet and "border-radius" in sheet True

title: alto.ui.theme
text: alto.ui.theme The color theme: follow the system, force light or dark, or use a theme with colors of its own. A theme with colors of its own is a CustomTheme : a fixed palette that is light or dark whatever the desktop is set to. Examples >>> [ key for key , label in THEMES ][: 4 ] ['system', 'light', 'dark', 'studio']

title: alto.ui.theme
text: CustomTheme CustomTheme ( key : str , family : str , label : str , note : str , dark : bool , window : str , panel : str , ink : str , muted : str , line : str , accent : str , track : str , ) [Source] A theme with colors of its own. Attributes key ( str ): What it is saved as. family ( str ): The key of the light version of the theme, which its dark version shares. label ( str ): What the settings call it. note ( str ): A short line about it, shown under its picture. dark ( bool ): True if it is a dark theme, so that Qt draws its own parts (such as the title bar) to match. window ( str ): The color of the window. panel ( str ): The color of lists, boxes and buttons. ink ( str ): The color of text. muted ( str ): The color of quiet text. line ( str ): The color of outlines. accent ( str ): The color of what is chosen, and of links. track ( str ): The color of the track behind a switch or a slider, a little off the window’s own. Examples >>> ( ... CUSTOM_THEMES [ 0 ]. key , ... CUSTOM_THEMES [ 0 ]. dark , ... len ( CUSTOM_THEMES ), ... ) ('studio', False, 50)

title: alto.ui.theme
text: hsl_hex def hsl_hex ( hue : float , * , saturation : float , lightness : float , ) -> str [Source] Turn a color given as hue, saturation and lightness into “#rrggbb”. Parameters hue ( float ): The hue, in degrees. saturation ( float ): The saturation, from 0 to 100. Keyword-only. lightness ( float ): The lightness, from 0 to 100. Keyword-only. Returns str : The color in hexadecimal. Examples >>> ( ... hsl_hex ( ... 0 , saturation = 100 , lightness = 50 ... ), ... hsl_hex ( ... 210 , saturation = 0 , lightness = 100 ... ), ... ) ('#ff0000', '#ffffff')

title: alto.ui.theme
text: seeded_themes def seeded_themes ( seed : tuple [ str , str , str , float , float , float , float ]) -> tuple [ CustomTheme , CustomTheme ] [Source] Make the light and the dark theme of a seed: neutrals tinted by one hue, and an accent of another. Parameters seed ( tuple ): The key, name and note, then the neutral hue and saturation and the accent hue and saturation. Returns tuple of (CustomTheme, CustomTheme) : The light theme and the dark theme. Examples >>> pale , deep = seeded_themes ( SEEDS [ 0 ]) >>> pale . key , deep . key , pale . dark , deep . dark ('parchment', 'parchment_dark', False, True)

title: alto.ui.theme
text: family_of def family_of ( key : str ) -> tuple [ str , str ] [Source] Split a theme’s key into its family and which version of it that is. Parameters key ( str ): The key of any theme. Returns tuple of (str, str) : The family’s key and “light”, “dark” or “system”. “system”, “light” and “dark” belong to the family “default”. Examples >>> ( ... family_of ( "sage_dark" ), ... family_of ( "sage" ), ... family_of ( "sage_auto" ), ... family_of ( "dark" ), ... family_of ( "system" ), ... ) (('sage', 'dark'), ('sage', 'light'), ('sage', 'system'), ('default', 'dark'), ('default', 'system'))

title: alto.ui.theme
text: variant_key def variant_key ( family : str , * , version : str , ) -> str [Source] Give the key of one version of a family. Parameters family ( str ): The family’s key. version ( str ): “light”, “dark” or “system”. Keyword-only. Returns str : The key. Examples >>> ( ... variant_key ( "sage" , version = "dark" ), ... variant_key ( "sage" , version = "system" ), ... variant_key ( "default" , version = "dark" ), ... ) ('sage_dark', 'sage_auto', 'dark')

title: alto.ui.theme
text: ThemeRecord class ThemeRecord ( TypedDict ) [Source] A theme the user made, as it is saved: its key, its name, and the colors of its light and dark versions. Examples >>> ThemeRecord ( ... id = "my_1" , ... name = "Mine" , ... light = {}, ... dark = {}, ... )[ "name" ] 'Mine'

title: alto.ui.theme
text: user_records def user_records () -> list [ ThemeRecord ] [Source] Read the themes the user has made, as they are saved. Returns list of ThemeRecord : One record for each theme: its “id”, its “name”, and its “light” and “dark” colors. A saved list that cannot be read, or has something else in it, gives only the records that can be used. Examples >>> store (). remove ( "ui/userThemes" ) >>> user_records () []

title: alto.ui.theme
text: save_user_records def save_user_records ( records : list [ ThemeRecord ]) -> None [Source] Save the themes the user has made. Parameters records ( list of ThemeRecord ): The records, as user_records gives them. Examples >>> save_user_records ([]) >>> user_records () []

title: alto.ui.theme
text: new_family_id def new_family_id () -> str [Source] Make the key for a new theme of the user’s. Returns str : A key that starts with “my_” and is not one that is in use. Examples >>> new_family_id (). startswith ( "my_" ) True

title: alto.ui.theme
text: upsert_user_theme def upsert_user_theme ( record : ThemeRecord ) -> None [Source] Save a theme the user made, replacing the one with the same key if there is one. Parameters record ( ThemeRecord ): The theme. Examples >>> store (). remove ( "ui/userThemes" ) >>> colors = { part : "#112233" for part in PARTS } >>> upsert_user_theme ( ... ThemeRecord ( ... id = "my_a" , ... name = "Mine" , ... light = colors , ... dark = colors , ... ) ... ) >>> upsert_user_theme ( ... ThemeRecord ( ... id = "my_a" , ... name = "Renamed" , ... light = colors , ... dark = colors , ... ) ... ) >>> [ ... ( r [ "id" ], r [ "name" ]) ... for r in user_records () ... ] [('my_a', 'Renamed')] >>> store (). remove ( "ui/userThemes" )

title: alto.ui.theme
text: delete_user_theme def delete_user_theme ( family : str ) -> None [Source] Remove a theme the user made. Parameters family ( str ): The theme’s key. Examples >>> store (). remove ( "ui/userThemes" ) >>> colors = { part : "#112233" for part in PARTS } >>> upsert_user_theme ( ... ThemeRecord ( ... id = "my_a" , ... name = "Mine" , ... light = colors , ... dark = colors , ... ) ... ) >>> delete_user_theme ( "my_a" ) >>> user_records () []

title: alto.ui.theme
text: theme_of def theme_of ( colors : dict [ str , str ], * , dark : bool , key : str = '' , family : str = '' , label : str = '' , note : str = '' , ) -> CustomTheme [Source] Build a custom theme from its saved or preview colors. Parameters colors ( dict of str to str ): A color for every part, as “#rrggbb”. dark ( bool ): True if it is the dark version. Keyword-only. key ( str ): Saved theme identifier, or empty for a preview. family ( str ): Identifier shared by the light and dark versions. label ( str ): Name displayed in settings. note ( str ): Description displayed with the theme. Returns CustomTheme : The theme with the supplied colors and identifiers. Examples >>> theme_of ( ... { part : "#102030" for part in PARTS }, ... dark = True , ... ). window '#102030'

title: alto.ui.theme
text: user_themes def user_themes () -> tuple [ CustomTheme , ...] [Source] Give the themes the user has made, light and dark versions of each. Returns tuple of CustomTheme : The light theme and then the dark theme of each record. Examples >>> store (). remove ( "ui/userThemes" ) >>> user_themes () ()

title: alto.ui.theme
text: families def families () -> tuple [ tuple [ str , str , str ], ...] [Source] List every theme there is to choose, the user’s own first. Returns tuple of tuple of (str, str, str) : The key of each theme’s family, its name and a line about it. Examples >>> store (). remove ( "ui/userThemes" ) >>> families () == FAMILIES True

title: alto.ui.theme
text: custom_theme def custom_theme ( key : str ) -> CustomTheme | None [Source] Find a theme with colors of its own, one of the built-in ones or one the user made. Parameters key ( str ): The theme’s key. Returns CustomTheme or None : The theme, or None for “system”, “light”, “dark” or anything that is not one. Examples >>> ( ... custom_theme ( "studio_dark" ) ... is CUSTOM_THEMES [ 1 ], ... custom_theme ( "dark" ), ... ) (True, None)

title: alto.ui.theme
text: scheme_of def scheme_of ( key : str ) -> Qt . ColorScheme | None [Source] Say which color scheme a theme uses: light, dark, or the desktop’s own. Parameters key ( str ): The theme’s key. Returns Qt.ColorScheme or None : The scheme; None if there is no theme with that key. Examples >>> ( ... scheme_of ( "dark" ) ... == Qt . ColorScheme . Dark , ... scheme_of ( "sage_auto" ) ... == Qt . ColorScheme . Unknown , ... scheme_of ( "nonsense" ), ... ) (True, True, None)

title: alto.ui.theme
text: preview_colors def preview_colors ( theme : CustomTheme ) -> dict [ str , str ] [Source] Pick the colors for the small picture of a theme in the settings. Parameters theme ( CustomTheme ): The theme. Returns dict of str to str : The window, panel, outline, text, faint and chosen colors, and a tint for the chosen row. Examples >>> ( ... preview_colors ( CUSTOM_THEMES [ 0 ])[ ... "window" ... ], ... sorted ( ... preview_colors ( CUSTOM_THEMES [ 0 ]) ... )[: 3 ], ... ) ('#eceef1', ['accent', 'faint', 'ink'])

title: alto.ui.theme
text: theme_palette def theme_palette ( theme : CustomTheme ) -> QPalette [Source] Build the Qt palette of a theme with colors of its own. Parameters theme ( CustomTheme ): The theme. Returns QPalette : The palette: the window, lists and buttons, text, the chosen row and links in the theme’s colors, with quiet text for what is switched off. Examples >>> colors = theme_palette ( CUSTOM_THEMES [ 0 ]) >>> ( ... colors . color ( ... QPalette . ColorRole . Window ... ). name (), ... colors . color ( ... QPalette . ColorRole . Highlight ... ). name (), ... ) ('#eceef1', '#2f7fc1')

title: alto.ui.theme
text: saved_theme def saved_theme () -> str [Source] Return the theme the user chose. Returns str : The key of the theme: “system”, “light”, “dark” or one of the themes with colors of its own; “system” if nothing valid is saved. Examples >>> save_theme ( "dark" ) >>> saved_theme () 'dark' >>> save_theme ( "system" )

title: alto.ui.theme
text: save_theme def save_theme ( key : str ) -> None [Source] Remember the theme the user chose. Parameters key ( str ): “system”, “light”, “dark” or the key of a theme with colors of its own. Examples >>> save_theme ( "light" ) >>> saved_theme () 'light' >>> save_theme ( "system" )

title: alto.ui.theme
text: system_is_dark def system_is_dark () -> bool [Source] Say whether the desktop is set to dark, as long as the app is not forcing a color scheme of its own. A theme that follows the desktop does not force one, so this is what it asks. Returns bool : True if the color scheme in use is dark. Examples >>> system_is_dark () in { True , False } True

title: alto.ui.theme
text: apply_theme def apply_theme ( key : str ) -> None [Source] Switch the application’s color scheme and rebuild the stylesheet from the new palette. Parameters key ( str ): “system” to follow the desktop, “light” or “dark”, or the key of a theme with colors of its own. Anything else follows the system. Examples >>> apply_theme ( "system" ) >>> # noinspection PyUnresolvedReferences >>> app . styleSheet () != "" True >>> apply_theme ( "studio" ) >>> QApplication . palette (). color ( ... QPalette . ColorRole . Window ... ). name () '#eceef1' >>> apply_theme ( "system" ) >>> QApplication . palette (). color ( ... QPalette . ColorRole . Window ... ). name () != "#eceef1" True

title: alto.ui.theme_cards
text: alto.ui.theme_cards The card of a theme in the settings. A card is one theme: its name, three pictures of the window one above another that can be clicked (light, dark, and System, which is cut through on a slant to show it is light or dark as the desktop is) and the squares of its colors. Examples >>> card = ThemeCard ( "sage" ) >>> sorted ( card . thumbs ) ['sage', 'sage_auto', 'sage_dark']

title: alto.ui.theme_cards
text: colors_of def colors_of ( key : str ) -> dict [ str , str ] [Source] Give the colors of a theme’s picture. Parameters key ( str ): A theme’s key: “light”, “dark”, or a theme with colors of its own, light or dark. Returns dict of str to str : The window, panel, outline, text, faint and chosen colors, and a tint for the chosen row. Examples >>> ( ... colors_of ( "dark" )[ "window" ], ... colors_of ( "studio" )[ "window" ], ... ) ('#2b2b2b', '#eceef1')

title: alto.ui.theme_cards
text: ThemeThumb ThemeThumb ( key : str , * , colors : dict [ str , str ], other : dict [ str , str ] | None = None , scale : float = 1.0 , parent : QWidget | None = None , ) [Source] Bases: QPushButton A small picture of the window in a theme, to click to choose the theme. Attributes theme_key ( str ): The key of the theme it chooses. colors ( dict of str to str ): The colors it is drawn in. other ( dict of str to str or None ): The colors of the dark half, for a picture that is cut through on a slant; None for a plain one. scale_by ( float ): How many times bigger than the smallest size it is drawn. Examples >>> ThemeThumb ( "dark" , colors = DARK ). theme_key 'dark' Constructor Build the picture. Parameters key ( str ): The theme it chooses. colors ( dict of str to str ): The colors of the picture, or of its light half. other ( dict of str to str or None, default None ): The colors of its dark half, for a picture cut through on a slant. Keyword-only. scale ( float, default 1.0 ): How many times bigger than the smallest size to draw it. Keyword-only. parent ( QWidget or None, default None ): The widget that owns it. Keyword-only. Constructor examples >>> ( ... ThemeThumb ( ... "system" , colors = LIGHT , other = DARK ... ). width (), ... ThemeThumb ( ... "light" , colors = LIGHT , scale = 2.0 ... ). width (), ... ) (116, 232)

title: alto.ui.theme_cards
text: ThemeThumb.paintEvent def paintEvent ( _ : QPaintEvent ) -> None [Source] Draw the window, cut through on a slant if it has two halves, with an outline that is heavier when it is chosen. Parameters _ ( QPaintEvent ): The paint request. Examples >>> ThemeThumb ( ... "light" , colors = LIGHT ... ). grab (). isNull () False

title: alto.ui.theme_cards
text: ThemeCard ThemeCard ( family : str , * , scale : float = 1.0 , parent : QWidget | None = None , ) [Source] Bases: QFrame The card of one theme: its name, three clickable pictures one above another, and with each the squares of its colors. The pictures are Light, Dark and System. The System one is cut through on a slant, light on one side and dark on the other, because that version is light or dark as the desktop is. Attributes family ( str ): The key of the theme’s family: “default” for System, Light and Dark. thumbs ( dict of str to ThemeThumb ): The three pictures, by the key of the theme each chooses. change_button ( QPushButton or None ): Opens the editor; only a theme the user made has one. chosen ( Signal ): Emitted with the key of the theme when one of the pictures is clicked. edit_requested ( Signal ): Emitted with the key of the theme when its Change colors button is pressed; only a theme the user made has one. Examples >>> card = ThemeCard ( "default" ) >>> list ( card . thumbs ) ['light', 'dark', 'system'] Constructor Build the card of a family. Parameters family ( str ): The key of the family: “default”, “studio” or one of the generated themes. scale ( float, default 1.0 ): How many times bigger than the smallest size to draw the pictures. Keyword-only. parent ( QWidget or None, default None ): The widget that owns it. Keyword-only. Constructor examples >>> ThemeCard ( "studio" ). family 'studio'

title: alto.ui.theme_cards
text: ThemeCard.show_current def show_current ( key : str ) -> None [Source] Mark the picture of the theme that is in use, and outline the card that has it. Parameters key ( str ): The key of the theme in use. Examples >>> card = ThemeCard ( "sage" ) >>> card . show_current ( "sage_dark" ) >>> [ ... k ... for k , picture in card . thumbs . items () ... if picture . isChecked () ... ] ['sage_dark']

title: alto.ui.theme_editor
text: alto.ui.theme_editor The editor for a theme of the user’s own: a name, and a color for every part of its light and dark versions. Examples >>> editor = ThemeEditor () >>> editor . load ( None ) >>> editor . record ()[ "name" ] 'My theme'

title: alto.ui.theme_editor
text: ThemeEditor ThemeEditor ( parent : QWidget | None = None ) [Source] Bases: QWidget A form to make a theme, or change one: its name, and the colors of its light and dark versions. A small picture of each version follows the colors as they are chosen. Choosing a theme in the “Start from” list takes its colors at once. Attributes name_edit ( QLineEdit ): The theme’s name. start_from ( FieldComboBox ): The themes whose colors can be taken; choosing one takes them. colors ( dict of str to dict of str to str ): The colors being made, by “light” or “dark”, and then by part. buttons ( dict of str to dict of str to QPushButton ): The button of each color, which opens the color picker, by version and part. pictures ( dict of str to ThemeThumb ): The picture of each version. save_button ( QPushButton ): Saves the theme. delete_button ( QPushButton ): Deletes the theme; it is only there for a theme that has been saved. saved ( Signal ): Emitted with the theme’s key when it is saved. canceled ( Signal ): Emitted when the editing is given up. deleted ( Signal ): Emitted with the theme’s key when it is deleted. Examples >>> ThemeEditor (). save_button . text () 'Save' Constructor Build the form, ready to make a new theme. Parameters parent ( QWidget or None, default None ): The widget that owns it. Constructor examples >>> sorted ( ThemeEditor (). colors ) ['dark', 'light']

title: alto.ui.theme_editor
text: ThemeEditor.eventFilter def eventFilter ( watched : QObject , event : QEvent , ) -> bool [Source] Light up the code written beside a color while the pointer is over the color. Parameters watched ( QObject ): The object the event is for. event ( QEvent ): The event. Returns bool : Always False: the color button still gets the event. Examples >>> editor = ThemeEditor () >>> button = editor . buttons [ "light" ][ "accent" ] >>> _ = editor . eventFilter ( ... button , QEvent ( QEvent . Type . Enter ) ... ) >>> "bold" in editor . _values [ "light" ][ ... "accent" ... ]. styleSheet () True >>> _ = editor . eventFilter ( ... button , QEvent ( QEvent . Type . Leave ) ... ) >>> "bold" in editor . _values [ "light" ][ ... "accent" ... ]. styleSheet () False

title: alto.ui.theme_editor
text: ThemeEditor.load def load ( record : ThemeRecord | None ) -> None [Source] Fill the form from a theme that was saved, or for a new one that starts as Studio. Parameters record ( ThemeRecord or None ): The theme to change; None for a new theme. Examples >>> editor = ThemeEditor () >>> editor . load ( None ) >>> ( ... editor . delete_button . isHidden (), ... editor . name_edit . text (), ... ) (True, 'My theme')

title: alto.ui.theme_editor
text: ThemeEditor.record def record () -> ThemeRecord [Source] Give the theme as it is now in the form. Returns ThemeRecord : The key, the name and the colors of both versions. Examples >>> editor = ThemeEditor () >>> editor . record ()[ "light" ][ ... "window" ... ] == editor . colors [ "light" ][ "window" ] True

title: alto.ui.transition_preview
text: alto.ui.transition_preview A preview of a transition for the settings. It is a mock of the home page, with the app’s own cards, that switches from the exercises to the lessons once. Examples >>> preview = TransitionPreview () >>> preview . show_transition ( "cascade" ) >>> preview . transition . key 'cascade'

title: alto.ui.transition_preview
text: make_sides def make_sides () -> tuple [ list [ TileCard ], list [ TileCard ]] [Source] Make the cards for the two sides of the preview: the app’s own exercise cards, and its lesson cards. The lessons side has the real lesson, and a few examples that are marked as such, so that a transition has more than one card to move. Returns tuple of (list of TileCard, list of TileCard) : The cards of the exercises side, and of the lessons side. Examples >>> first , second = make_sides () >>> len ( first ), len ( second ) > len ( LESSONS ) (6, True)

title: alto.ui.transition_preview
text: Stage Stage ( parent : QWidget | None = None ) [Source] Bases: QWidget The page of the mock window: it draws the cards that are resting, and the transition plays on a canvas over it. Attributes canvas ( TransitionCanvas ): Where a transition is drawn. resting ( list of Sprite ): The cards that are showing when no transition is playing. Examples >>> Stage (). resting [] Constructor Build the stage with nothing on it. Parameters parent ( QWidget or None, default None ): The widget that owns it. Constructor examples >>> Stage (). canvas . running False

title: alto.ui.transition_preview
text: Stage.resizeEvent def resizeEvent ( event : QResizeEvent ) -> None [Source] Keep the canvas the size of the stage. Parameters event ( QResizeEvent ): The resize. Examples >>> stage = Stage () >>> # a hidden widget is only told about its size once it is >>> # shown >>> stage . show () >>> stage . resize ( 300 , 200 ) >>> stage . canvas . geometry () == stage . rect () True

title: alto.ui.transition_preview
text: Stage.paintEvent def paintEvent ( _ : QPaintEvent ) -> None [Source] Draw the cards at rest, unless a transition is drawing them. Parameters _ ( QPaintEvent ): The paint request. Examples >>> stage = Stage () >>> stage . resize ( 100 , 100 ) >>> stage . grab (). isNull () False

title: alto.ui.transition_preview
text: TransitionPreview TransitionPreview ( parent : QWidget | None = None ) [Source] Bases: QFrame A mock home page that plays a transition between two sets of the app’s cards, once. It has a bar with the same Exercises and Lessons switch as the real window. It follows the side that is showing, and pressing it plays the transition to the other side, so the learner can try it as often as they like. Attributes transition ( Transition ): The transition being shown. side ( int ): Which set of cards is showing: 0 for the exercises, 1 for the lessons. stage ( Stage ): The page the cards are on. switch ( SegmentedControl ): The mock switch in the title bar. Examples >>> preview = TransitionPreview () >>> preview . side 0 Constructor Build the preview, showing the default transition. Parameters parent ( QWidget or None, default None ): The widget that owns it. Constructor examples >>> TransitionPreview (). transition . key 'cascade'

title: alto.ui.transition_preview

title: alto.ui.transitions
text: alto.ui.transitions The transitions between the exercises and the lessons on the home page. A transition moves between two sets of cards. Each card is photographed first, as a sprite, and a sprite can be faded, slid, scaled, blurred or cut away from one side. A transition is a function that sets how every sprite looks at each moment, so ten different ones share one player. Examples >>> [ ... transition . key ... for transition in TRANSITIONS ... ][: 3 ] ['none', 'cascade', 'fade'] >>> DEFAULT_TRANSITION 'cascade'

title: alto.ui.transitions
text: Sprite Sprite ( pixmap : QPixmap , rect : QRectF , opacity : float = 1.0 , dx : float = 0.0 , dy : float = 0.0 , sx : float = 1.0 , sy : float = 1.0 , blur : float = 0.0 , angle : float = 0.0 , reveal : float = 1.0 , reveal_from : int = 1 , ) [Source] A photograph of one card, and how it is drawn at this moment. Attributes pixmap ( QPixmap ): The photograph. rect ( QRectF ): Where the card is, in the canvas. opacity ( float ): 0 for invisible to 1 for solid. dx ( float ): How far it is moved right, in pixels. dy ( float ): How far it is moved down, in pixels. sx ( float ): How much it is stretched across, about its middle; 1 is as it was. sy ( float ): How much it is stretched down, about its middle. blur ( float ): 0 for sharp to 1 for fully blurred. angle ( float ): How far it is turned about its middle, in degrees, clockwise. reveal ( float ): How much of it shows, from 0 to 1. reveal_from ( int ): 1 to uncover it from the left, -1 from the right, 0 from the middle outwards. Examples >>> sprite = Sprite ( ... pixmap = QPixmap (), ... rect = QRectF ( 0 , 0 , 10 , 10 ), ... ) >>> sprite . opacity , sprite . reveal (1.0, 1.0)

title: alto.ui.transitions
text: Scene Scene ( time : float , old : Sequence [ Sprite ], new : Sequence [ Sprite ], direction : int , ) [Source] What a transition is given at each moment: the time, the two sets of sprites and the direction. Attributes time ( float ): The time since the transition began, in milliseconds. old ( sequence of Sprite ): The cards that are leaving. new ( sequence of Sprite ): The cards that are arriving. direction ( int ): 1 when going toward the lessons, -1 when coming back. Examples >>> Scene ( ... time = 0.0 , old = [], new = [], direction = 1 ... ). direction 1

title: alto.ui.transitions
text: ease_out def ease_out ( progress : float ) -> float [Source] Ease a progress from 0 to 1 so that it starts fast and slows to a stop. Parameters progress ( float ): How far along, from 0 to 1. Returns float : The eased progress. Examples >>> ease_out ( 0.0 ), ease_out ( 1.0 ), ease_out ( 0.5 ) (0.0, 1.0, 0.875)

title: alto.ui.transitions
text: ramp def ramp ( time : float , * , start : float , length : float , ) -> float [Source] Say how far along a part of a transition is, from 0 before it starts to 1 once it has finished. Parameters time ( float ): The time since the transition began, in milliseconds. start ( float ): When the part begins. Keyword-only. length ( float ): How long it lasts. Keyword-only. Returns float : The progress, from 0 to 1. Examples >>> ( ... ramp ( 50 , start = 100 , length = 200 ), ... ramp ( 200 , start = 100 , length = 200 ), ... ramp ( 900 , start = 100 , length = 200 ), ... ) (0.0, 0.5, 1.0)

title: alto.ui.transitions
text: hide def hide ( sprites : Sequence [ Sprite ]) -> None [Source] Make sprites invisible. Parameters sprites ( sequence of Sprite ): The sprites. Examples >>> card = Sprite ( ... pixmap = QPixmap (), rect = QRectF () ... ) >>> hide ([ card ]) >>> card . opacity 0.0

title: alto.ui.transitions
text: fade_in def fade_in ( scene : Scene ) -> None [Source] Set the sprites for a fade in: the new cards fade up from clear, and nothing of the old remains. Parameters scene ( Scene ): The time, the cards that are leaving and arriving, and the direction. Examples >>> new = [ ... Sprite ( pixmap = QPixmap (), rect = QRectF ()) ... ] >>> fade_in ( ... Scene ( ... time = 0 , old = [], new = new , direction = 1 ... ) ... ) >>> new [ 0 ]. opacity 0.0

title: alto.ui.transitions
text: crossfade def crossfade ( scene : Scene ) -> None [Source] Set the sprites for a crossfade: the old cards fade out as the new ones fade in. Parameters scene ( Scene ): The time, the cards that are leaving and arriving, and the direction. Examples >>> old , new = ( ... [ ... Sprite ( ... pixmap = QPixmap (), rect = QRectF () ... ) ... ], ... [ ... Sprite ( ... pixmap = QPixmap (), rect = QRectF () ... ) ... ], ... ) >>> crossfade ( ... Scene ( ... time = 300 , ... old = old , ... new = new , ... direction = 1 , ... ) ... ) >>> old [ 0 ]. opacity , new [ 0 ]. opacity (0.0, 1.0)

title: alto.ui.transitions
text: slide def slide ( scene : Scene ) -> None [Source] Set the sprites for a slide: both sets move sideways, toward the side of the switch that was pressed. Parameters scene ( Scene ): The time, the cards that are leaving and arriving, and the direction. Examples >>> new = [ ... Sprite ( pixmap = QPixmap (), rect = QRectF ()) ... ] >>> slide ( ... Scene ( ... time = 0 , old = [], new = new , direction = 1 ... ) ... ) >>> new [ 0 ]. dx 60.0

title: alto.ui.transitions
text: rise def rise ( scene : Scene ) -> None [Source] Set the sprites for a rise: the old cards sink and fade, and the new ones rise into place. Parameters scene ( Scene ): The time, the cards that are leaving and arriving, and the direction. Examples >>> new = [ ... Sprite ( pixmap = QPixmap (), rect = QRectF ()) ... ] >>> rise ( ... Scene ( ... time = 0 , old = [], new = new , direction = 1 ... ) ... ) >>> new [ 0 ]. dy , new [ 0 ]. opacity (22.0, 0.0)

title: alto.ui.transitions
text: cascade def cascade ( scene : Scene ) -> None [Source] Set the sprites for a cascade: the new cards arrive one after another, each rising a little as it appears. Parameters scene ( Scene ): The time, the cards that are leaving and arriving, and the direction. Examples >>> new = [ ... Sprite ( pixmap = QPixmap (), rect = QRectF ()) ... for _ in range ( 2 ) ... ] >>> cascade ( ... Scene ( ... time = 100 , ... old = [], ... new = new , ... direction = 1 , ... ) ... ) >>> new [ 0 ]. opacity > new [ 1 ]. opacity > 0.0 True

title: alto.ui.transitions
text: zoom def zoom ( scene : Scene ) -> None [Source] Set the sprites for a zoom: the old cards grow a little as they fade, and the new ones grow into place. Parameters scene ( Scene ): The time, the cards that are leaving and arriving, and the direction. Examples >>> new = [ ... Sprite ( pixmap = QPixmap (), rect = QRectF ()) ... ] >>> zoom ( ... Scene ( ... time = 0 , old = [], new = new , direction = 1 ... ) ... ) >>> new [ 0 ]. sx 0.92

title: alto.ui.transitions
text: flip def flip ( scene : Scene ) -> None [Source] Set the sprites for a flip: each old card turns edge on and goes, then each new one turns face on. Parameters scene ( Scene ): The time, the cards that are leaving and arriving, and the direction. Examples >>> new = [ ... Sprite ( pixmap = QPixmap (), rect = QRectF ()) ... ] >>> flip ( ... Scene ( ... time = 0 , old = [], new = new , direction = 1 ... ) ... ) >>> new [ 0 ]. opacity 0.0

title: alto.ui.transitions
text: blur def blur ( scene : Scene ) -> None [Source] Set the sprites for a blur: the old cards dissolve into a blur and the new ones come into focus. Parameters scene ( Scene ): The time, the cards that are leaving and arriving, and the direction. Examples >>> new = [ ... Sprite ( pixmap = QPixmap (), rect = QRectF ()) ... ] >>> blur ( ... Scene ( ... time = 0 , old = [], new = new , direction = 1 ... ) ... ) >>> new [ 0 ]. blur , new [ 0 ]. opacity (1.0, 0.0)

title: alto.ui.transitions

Scene ( ... time = 0 , ... old = [], ... new = new , ... direction =- 1 , ... ) ... ) >>> new [ 0 ]. reveal , new [ 0 ]. reveal_from (0.0, -1)

title: alto.ui.transitions
text: Transition Transition ( key : str , label : str , about : str , frame : Callable [[ Scene ], None ] | None = field ( default = None , compare = False ), length : Callable [[ Scene ], float ] = field ( default = lambda scene : 0.0 , compare = False ), ) [Source] One way of moving between the exercises and the lessons. Attributes key ( str ): What it is saved as. label ( str ): What the settings call it. about ( str ): A sentence saying what it looks like. frame ( callable or None ): Sets how every sprite looks in a scene; None for no transition at all. length ( callable ): Says how long it lasts, in milliseconds, from a scene that has the cards but no time. Examples >>> TRANSITIONS [ 0 ]. frame is None True

title: alto.ui.transitions
text: Motion Motion ( length : float = 320.0 , per_card : float = 0.0 , start : float = 0.0 , after : bool = False , order : str = 'index' , ease : str = 'out' , dx : float = 0.0 , dy : float = 0.0 , scale : float = 1.0 , sx : float = 1.0 , sy : float = 1.0 , angle : float = 0.0 , blur : float = 0.0 , fade : bool = True , reveal : str = '' , ) [Source] How one set of cards moves in a transition built from parts: when each card starts, how long it takes, and what it does. Every card goes between its resting look and a look given here, so the same description serves for cards arriving (from that look to rest) and leaving (from rest to that look). Attributes length ( float ): How long each card takes, in milliseconds. per_card ( float ): How much later each card starts than the one before it. start ( float ): When the first card starts. after ( bool ): True to wait until the cards that are leaving have all finished before starting; only for cards that are arriving. order ( str ): The order the cards start in: one of ORDERS . ease ( str ): How the motion is timed: one of EASES . dx ( float ): How far to the right the card is at the far look, in pixels; it follows the direction of the switch. dy ( float ): How far down the card is at the far look. scale ( float ): How big the card is at the far look, as a fraction of its size. sx ( float ): As well as scale , how wide, for a card that turns on its edge. sy ( float ): As well as scale , how tall. angle ( float ): How far the card is turned at the far look, in degrees; it follows the direction of the switch. blur ( float ): How blurred it is at the far look, from 0 to 1. fade ( bool ): True to fade between solid and clear; False to keep it solid, and hide it only once it is out of the way. reveal ( str ): “” for none, or “side” or “center” to uncover it from one side or from the middle. Examples >>> Motion (). order , Motion (). ease ('index', 'out')

title: alto.ui.transitions
text: eased def eased ( progress : float , * , how : str , ) -> float [Source] Time a progress from 0 to 1 in one of the ways a motion can be eased. Parameters progress ( float ): How far along, from 0 to 1. how ( str ): One of EASES : “out” slows to a stop, “in” speeds up, “back” overshoots a little and settles, “linear” does neither. Keyword-only. Returns float : The timed progress, which “back” takes a little past 1 on the way. Examples >>> ( ... eased ( 0.5 , how = "linear" ), ... eased ( 1.0 , how = "back" ), ... eased ( 0.5 , how = "in" ), ... ) (0.5, 1.0, 0.25) >>> eased ( 0.8 , how = "back" ) > 1.0 True

title: alto.ui.transitions
text: ranks def ranks ( sprites : Sequence [ Sprite ], * , order : str , ) -> list [ int ] [Source] Say where each sprite comes in an order: 0 for the first to start. Parameters sprites ( sequence of Sprite ): The cards of one side. order ( str ): One of ORDERS : “index” is as laid out, “reverse” backwards, “outward” from the middle of the cards to the edges, “inward” the other way, “diagonal” from the top left to the bottom right, and “random” in a fixed scrambled order. Keyword-only. Returns list of int : The rank of each sprite, in the sprites’ own order. Examples >>> row = [ ... Sprite ( ... pixmap = QPixmap (), ... rect = QRectF ( x , 0 , 10 , 10 ), ... ) ... for x in ( 0 , 20 , 40 ) ... ] >>> ( ... ranks ( row , order = "index" ), ... ranks ( row , order = "reverse" ), ... ranks ( row , order = "outward" ), ... ) ([0, 1, 2], [2, 1, 0], [1, 0, 2])

title: alto.ui.transitions
text: span def span ( motion : Motion , * , count : int , ) -> float [Source] Say how long a motion takes for a number of cards, from when it starts to when the last card has finished. Parameters motion ( Motion ): The motion. count ( int ): How many cards. Returns float : The time in milliseconds. Examples >>> span ( ... Motion ( ... length = 300.0 , ... per_card = 50.0 , ... start = 10.0 , ... ), ... count = 4 , ... ) 460.0

title: alto.ui.transitions
text: move def move ( scene : Scene , * , leaving : Motion | None , arriving : Motion , ) -> None [Source] Set the sprites for a transition built from a motion for the cards that leave and one for the cards that arrive. Parameters scene ( Scene ): The time, the cards and the direction. leaving ( Motion or None ): What the old cards do; None for them to be gone at once. arriving ( Motion ): What the new cards do. Examples >>> new = [ ... Sprite ( pixmap = QPixmap (), rect = QRectF ()) ... ] >>> move ( ... Scene ( ... time = 0 , old = [], new = new , direction = 1 ... ), ... leaving = None , ... arriving = Motion ( dy = 20 ), ... ) >>> new [ 0 ]. opacity , new [ 0 ]. dy (0.0, 20.0)

title: alto.ui.transitions
text: built def built ( * , leaving : Motion | None , arriving : Motion , ) -> tuple [ Callable [[ Scene ], None ], Callable [[ Scene ], float ]] [Source] Make the frame and length functions of a transition built from motions. Parameters leaving ( Motion or None ): What the old cards do. Keyword-only. arriving ( Motion ): What the new cards do. Keyword-only. Returns tuple of (callable, callable) : The frame function, and the length function. Examples >>> draw , lasts = built ( ... leaving = None , ... arriving = Motion ( ... length = 300 , per_card = 50 ... ), ... ) >>> lasts ( ... Scene ( ... time = 0 , ... old = [], ... new = [ ... Sprite ( ... pixmap = QPixmap (), ... rect = QRectF (), ... ) ... ] ... * 3 , ... direction = 1 , ... ) ... ) 400.0

Format_ARGB32 ... ) >>> brush = QPainter ( image ) >>> paint_sprites ( ... brush , ... sprites = [ ... TRANSITIONS [ 1 ], new = [], direction = 1 ... ) >>> canvas . running True >>> canvas . stop ()

title: alto.ui.update_flow
text: alto.ui.update_flow Checking for a newer Alto and installing it: the questions asked, the progress shown, and the restart afterwards. The menu’s “Check for updates…” follows one of two channels, chosen in Settings: the newest release (the default), or the newest commit on the main branch. A copy installed with scripts/alto-install.sh can replace itself, from either, with uv tool install , showing its output, and restarts when OK is pressed. A packaged copy cannot replace itself, so it is told that a newer release exists and offered the page where it can be downloaded; it always follows releases. A copy run from a source folder is told to update with git. Examples >>> brief ( ... "fatal: unable to access 'https://example.org/': Could not " ... "resolve host \n " ... ) "fatal: unable to access 'https://example.org/': Could not resolve host"

brief def brief ( text : str , * , limit : int = 400 , ) -> str [Source] Cut what a program printed down to what is worth showing in a message: the end of it, without the blank space around it. Parameters text ( str ): What the program printed. limit ( int, default 400 ): The most characters to keep. Keyword-only. Returns str : The end of the text, at most limit characters long. Examples >>> brief ( " one 
 two

two' >>> brief ( "x" * 10 , limit = 4 ) 'xxxx'

text: CommandRunner CommandRunner ( parent : QObject | None = None ) [Source] Bases: QObject Run one program without freezing the window, handing on what it prints as it prints it, and how it ended. Attributes output ( Signal ): Emitted with each piece of text the program prints, as it arrives. Its errors are mixed in with it. done ( Signal ): Emitted once, with the exit code and everything the program printed. The exit code is -1 if the program could not be started, was stopped for taking too long, or crashed. Examples >>> runner = CommandRunner () >>> runner . running False Constructor Make a runner that has not started anything. Parameters parent ( QObject or None, default None ): The object that owns it.

Parameters program ( str ): The program’s path. arguments ( list of str ): What to give it. Keyword-only. seconds ( int, default 0 ): Stop it if it has not ended by then; 0 lets it take as long as it takes. Keyword-only. Examples >>> import sys >>> runner = CommandRunner () >>> runner . start ( ... sys . executable , ... arguments = [ ... "-c" , ... "import time; time.sleep(30)" , ... ], ... ) >>> runner . stop () >>> runner . running False

title: alto.ui.update_flow
text: UpdateDialog UpdateDialog ( parent : QWidget | None , * , command : tuple [ str , list [ str ]], ) [Source] Bases: QDialog The window that shows an update being installed: a bar that keeps moving, what uv prints, and then what comes next. It cannot be closed while the update runs, because stopping it half way could leave the installed copy broken. When it has finished it says so, and its one button closes it. After a successful update the caller restarts Alto. Attributes status ( QLabel ): What is happening. bar ( QProgressBar ): A bar that keeps moving while the update runs, and fills when it has succeeded. log ( QPlainTextEdit ): What uv prints, as it prints it. button ( QPushButton ): Enabled when the update has ended. ended ( bool ): Whether the update has ended. succeeded ( bool ): Whether it ended well. runner ( CommandRunner ): The program that does the update. Constructor Build the window; the update does not start until run is called. title: alto.ui.warmup
text: alto.ui.warmup Get ready, while Alto sits idle just after it opens, what a first visit to a page would otherwise pay for. The music font of the notation style is loaded by drawing a small staff out of sight. And most of what makes a page slow to open the first time is not the page. Labels such as “F♯” and “B♭” use signs that the interface font does not have, so Qt looks for a font that does, and it does so again for every size and weight of text, about 40 ms each time on Linux. Pages show such labels in several sizes, so a first visit could spend a tenth of a second looking for fonts. Laying out a line with those signs once in each size the interface uses, a little at a time while nothing else is happening, makes the first visit to a page about as quick as the second. Notes the current instrument has no recording of are made by shifting the nearest recording the first time they play, which takes a few tens of milliseconds each. They are made here too, one per step, so that even a first play is quick. Examples >>> warmed = [] >>> owner = QObject () >>> start ( ... owner , ... steps = [ ... lambda : warmed . append ( 1 ), ... lambda : warmed . append ( 2 ), ... ], ... delay = 0 , ... ) >>> import time >>> deadline = time . monotonic () + 2 >>> while ( ... len ( warmed ) < 2 ... and time . monotonic () < deadline ... ): ... app . processEvents () >>> warmed [1, 2] >>> while ( ... any ( ... timer . isActive () ... for timer in owner . findChildren ( ... QTimer ... ) ... ) ... and time . monotonic () < deadline ... ): ... app . processEvents () >>> any ( ... timer . isActive () ... for timer in owner . findChildren ( QTimer ) ... ) # it stops once every step has run False

title: alto.ui.warmup
text: warmup_steps def warmup_steps () -> list [ Callable [[], None ]] [Source] List the steps of the warm-up. They draw a staff; lay out text in the application’s own font size and each style sheet size, plain and bold, at the zoom; and, while sound is on, make the notes the current instrument has no recording of. Returns list of callable : The steps, each a few tens of milliseconds at most. Examples >>> notes = ( ... len ( sounds . unrecorded ()) ... if sounds . enabled ... else 0 ... ) >>> len ( ... warmup_steps () ... # the staff, eleven sizes in two weights, and the notes ... ) == 1 + 22 + notes True

title: alto.ui.warmup
text: start def start ( owner : QObject , * , steps : list [ Callable [[], None ]] | None = None , delay : int = START_DELAY_MS , ) -> None [Source] Run the warm-up’s steps one at a time, each when the event loop has nothing else to do, beginning after a short delay. Input and painting are handled between the steps, so the window stays as responsive as it is without the warm-up. If the owner is deleted first (the window closed), the rest of the steps are dropped. Parameters owner ( QObject ): What the warm-up belongs to, usually the main window. steps ( list of callable or None, default None ): The steps; None for the usual ones ( warmup_steps() ). Keyword-only. delay ( int, default START_DELAY_MS ): How long to wait first, in milliseconds. Keyword-only. Examples >>> start ( ... QObject (), steps = [], delay = 0 ... ) # nothing to do

title: alto.ui.zoom
text: alto.ui.zoom Zoom: make everything in Alto larger or smaller together. The zoom is a percentage, 100 by default, that moves through a list of steps. It scales the application font, every pixel and point length in the stylesheet, and the sizes the interface fixes in pixels, which are written with px here so that they follow it. The notation that is drawn by hand takes its size from the same percentage. Pressing Ctrl and Plus or Ctrl and Minus, or turning the mouse wheel with Ctrl held, moves one step, and Ctrl and 0 goes back to 100%. The choice is saved. Examples >>> set_percent ( 100 ) False >>> px ( 20 ), px ( 0 ) (20, 0) >>> css ( ... "QLabel { font-size: 14pt; border: 1px solid; }" ... ) 'QLabel { font-size: 14pt; border: 1px solid; }'

title: alto.ui.zoom
text: percent def percent () -> int [Source] Give the zoom now in force. Returns int : The percentage, one of STEPS . Examples >>> percent () 100

title: alto.ui.zoom
text: factor def factor () -> float [Source] Give the zoom as a multiplier. Returns float : 1.0 at 100%. Examples >>> factor () 1.0

title: alto.ui.zoom
text: px def px ( value : float ) -> int [Source] Scale a length in pixels by the zoom. Parameters value ( float ): The length at 100%. Returns int : The length now, rounded, and never less than one pixel unless it was zero. Examples >>> px ( 20 ), px ( 0 ), px ( - 4 ) (20, 0, -4)

title: alto.ui.zoom
text: css def css ( text : str ) -> str [Source] Scale every pixel and point length in a stylesheet by the zoom. Parameters text ( str ): The stylesheet. Returns str : The same stylesheet with each length such as 12px or 14pt multiplied. A length of zero stays zero. Examples >>> css ( ... "QLabel { padding: 8px 12px; font-size: 14pt; margin: 0px;" ... " }" ... ) 'QLabel { padding: 8px 12px; font-size: 14pt; margin: 0px; }'

title: alto.ui.zoom
text: apply_font def apply_font () -> None [Source] Make the application font as large as the zoom says, from the size it had at 100%. Examples >>> apply_font ()

title: alto.ui.zoom
text: set_percent def set_percent ( value : int ) -> bool [Source] Zoom to the step nearest a percentage, save it and say so. Parameters value ( int ): The percentage wanted. Returns bool : True if the zoom changed, False if it was already there. Examples >>> set_percent ( 125 ) True >>> percent (), factor () (125, 1.25) >>> set_percent ( 125 ) False >>> set_percent ( 100 ) True

title: alto.ui.zoom
text: step def step ( direction : int ) -> bool [Source] Zoom in or out by one step. Parameters direction ( int ): Positive to zoom in, negative to zoom out. Returns bool : True if the zoom changed, False at the largest or smallest step. Examples >>> step ( 1 ), percent () (True, 110) >>> step ( - 1 ), percent () (True, 100) >>> while step ( - 1 ): ... pass >>> percent (), step ( - 1 ) (50, False) >>> reset (), percent () (True, 100)

title: alto.ui.zoom

title: alto.ui.zoom
text: load def load () -> None [Source] Take the saved zoom into force, without announcing it, ignoring anything that is not a step. Examples >>> store (). setValue ( SETTING , 150 ) >>> load () >>> percent () 150 >>> store (). setValue ( SETTING , "wide" ) >>> load () >>> percent () 100
