text: Everywhere Keys What it does Esc Go back from the statistics or database page. Ctrl + Alt + S Open the app settings. Ctrl + R Restart Alto. Ctrl + Q Quit. Ctrl + + Zoom in. Ctrl + = does the same, so no Shift is needed. Ctrl + - Zoom out. Ctrl + 0 Go back to 100%. On macOS, Qt shows these shortcuts with ⌘ in place of Ctrl . Zoom makes everything larger or smaller together: the text, the buttons, the lists, the notation, the keyboard and the icons. It moves through 50%, 67%, 75%, 80%, 90%, 100%, 110%, 125%, 150%, 175%, 200%, 250% and 300%. Alto draws the window again at each step, and remembers the zoom the next time it starts. The current percentage briefly appears to the left of the Glossary button. Windows that are already open, such as the settings, take the new zoom when you open them again.

title: Shortcuts
text: Mouse Action Where What it does Click the staff Note, Interval, and Scale Construction Place the note. Right-click the staff Note Construction, Scale Construction Step through no sign, sharp, flat and natural. Turn the wheel over the staff Scale Construction Step through the signs while notes are placed, then switch between whole and half steps. Double-click a row Database: Answers or Questions Preview that question. Click a column heading Database Sort by that column. Hover a chart Statistics Show the exact values for that period. Turn the wheel with Ctrl held Anywhere Zoom in or out one step for each click of the wheel. Drag the edge of the sidebar Exercise screens Resize the exercise list, or drag it narrower than its minimum to hide it.

title: Shortcuts
text: The menu Open the ☰ menu at the top left for Profile , Settings… , Tools , Help , Restart , or Quit . Under Help , About shows the installed version and development status. Report an issue opens Alto’s GitHub issues page. Under Tools , choose Import backup… , Export backup… , Anki Exporter , or Check for updates… . For deck selection, scheduling, and import instructions, see Anki decks .

title: Statistics and database
text: Statistics and database

title: Statistics and database
text: Statistics Open Statistics using the chart button at the upper right of the main window. They always show the active profile’s own answers. Use ← Back or Esc to return to the page you came from.

title: Statistics and database
text: Filters Exercise: all exercises, or any one of them. Timeframe: today, the last 7, 30 or 90 days, the last year, or all time. Each bar counts a week of questions. The neighboring accuracy chart still shows one point per day. Choose Response-time distribution… below the speed chart to see the recent times used for automatic grading. The tool opens on the selected exercise and uses its latest 100 eligible answers across timeframes. Response-time grading .

title: Statistics and database
text: What you see Summary tiles: questions answered, how often the first answer was right, the typical time to a first answer, attempts per question, days practiced, and time spent practicing. A single answer counts for at most two minutes of practice time, so leaving the app open does not inflate it. Questions answered shows first-try correct answers in green and misses in red. Use Granularity in the chart’s upper-right corner to choose Hour , Day , Week , or Month for each bar. Auto picks a period based on the timeframe. If your choice produces more than 48 bars, scroll left beneath the chart to see earlier periods. Right on the first try: your first-try accuracy over time. Days with no answers leave a gap. Typical time to first answer: the median, over time, so a single slow answer does not distort it. By exercise: accuracy, number of questions and typical time for each exercise. Reviews: a calendar of the last 12 months, a square per day (weeks run left to right, Monday at the top), darker the more questions you answered. Use the outward diagonal arrows to separate the months and the inward arrows to close the gaps. Hover a square for the exact count. It follows the exercise filter but ignores the timeframe. Questions that need practice: the questions with the highest strain, how often you missed them, and how many times you have answered them.

title: Statistics and database
text: Pointing and clicking Every chart responds to the pointer. Hover a bar, a point, an exercise row or a calendar day and it brightens while the rest of the chart fades back, with its numbers in a tooltip. Click one and the answers behind it are listed in a panel under the charts: a bar or point lists the answers given during its hour, day, week, or month within the selected timeframe; a row of the by-exercise chart lists the answers to that exercise within the timeframe; a square of the calendar lists the answers given on that day. The clicked element stays bright and the rest stay faded while the panel is open. Click it again, or press Close , to put the panel away; it also closes when you change the exercise or the timeframe, because its numbers would no longer match. Periods and days with no answers cannot be clicked. The list has the same columns as the database browser below, sorts when you click a heading, and double-clicking a row previews the question. It shows the newest 500 answers, and says when there are more. Double-click any cell in Questions that need practice to open the saved question and its answer. The Question Statistics button on the card opens that question’s speed and accuracy graphs. The Reviews calendar: a year of practice at a glance. Days without reviews use the lightest shade, and the darkest squares are your busiest days. A question counts as right only if your first answer was right. That is the same rule the practice scheduler uses, so the numbers match what Alto thinks about your progress.

title: Statistics and database
text: Browsing the database The database button next to the statistics button opens a read-only view of what is stored. It never changes anything. Three tables are available: Answers: every answer the active profile has given, newest first, with the question, your answer, whether it was right, the attempt number and the time. Questions shows each question’s strain, answer counts, typical response time, and last practice time. Profiles: everyone who has a profile, with how many answers and questions each has. In both Answers and Questions , Due shows the next review in local time for the selected SM-2 or FSRS schedule. All answers to the same question show its current due date. A dash means the question has no due date under the current scheduler. Last seen records when you practiced the question. Due shows when the scheduler wants to show it again. Click a column heading to sort, and use the search box to filter every column at once. Answers and questions are limited to the newest 10,000 rows each; the line above the table says when that applies.

title: Statistics and database
text: Previewing a question Double-click a row in Answers or Questions to see that question as the exercise showed it, with its answer. Choose the Question Statistics bar chart icon in the upper-right corner to graph your practice history for that question. Each point represents one time you were asked. The speed graph shows seconds to your first answer. The accuracy graph shows the percentage answered correctly on the first try up to that point. Hover over a point for its value. You can also open these graphs from an answer in Statistics. The preview shows the notes, the correct answer, what you answered and how long it took. Play sounds the notes.
